on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, as shadow rapporteur for the ppe group, i would like to start by saying that we welcome the increasing role of the eu as a trading power in every region of the world, including the pacific region. the agreement, as it is now, is not a perfect one, not least because it is not a comprehensive epa, but only an interim one. we hope that the commission will be in a position to negotiate, in due time, a comprehensive epa including a larger number of countries in the region. secondly, the current agreement concerns only a small part of eu trade, since the share of eu trade accounted for by the whole of the pacific region is just 0.06%, and yet some areas have caused us concern, most notably on the issue of the derogation from the rules of origin for fishery products. in our resolution we raise our concern that a number of countries, such as the philippines, thailand, china, the united states, australia and others, will be able to take advantage of this derogation and potentially export large quantities of processed fisheries products to the eu, potentially harming the interests of the eu fish processing and canning industry. we therefore encourage the commission to act on parliament’s request for it to conduct an impact assessment study and, in the event that the assessment demonstrates a destabilising effect on the eu’s fish processing and canning industry, for it to initiate the procedure leading to suspension of the exceptional arrangements in this agreement regarding rules of origin.
in view of the council conclusions on serbia's progress on reforms, serbia should be congratulated, but unfortunately there are some concerns. as serbia moves towards the european union, significant efforts must be made in certain areas, in particular the improvement of the business environment in serbia. the experience of lithuanian investors raises legitimate questions about the business environment and the protection of foreign investment in serbia. since the serbian government accused lithuanian companies, which had invested eur 34 million, of breach of their obligations and terminated the privatisation contract in violation of the agreement between serbia and lithuania providing for the promotion and mutual protection of investments. serbia needs to find ways to ensure a transparent and predictable business environment, to deal with bureaucratic constraints, legal uncertainty and the like. we support serbia's aspirations, of course, to join the european union and we are willing to deal with the problematic issues.
in writing. − i have supported this report and the european commission's proposal because i believe it is essential to make community law simpler and clearer, to make it more understandable and accessible to all citizens. this objective will not be achieved if many provisions, which have been amended in part and often substantially on several occasions, remain scattered among the various acts, and if the search for the rules in force at a given moment requires the work of comparing the various acts. the codification of legislation is of particular importance in the field of business, which is governed by a substantial body of community legislation in order to ensure the smooth and uninterrupted free movement of persons, goods and services. the consolidation of the legislation governing mergers of public limited companies is a welcome step towards improving community law.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the opinion of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, the proposal in question seeks only to codify the existing texts without changing their substance and, therefore, in the interests of clarity and rationality, the existing texts should be codified.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the community has exclusive competence in respect of various aspects of external aviation which have traditionally been regulated by bilateral air services agreements between member states and third countries, and as a result the community agreements need to replace certain provisions of the current bilateral agreements contained in the 47 existing bilateral air services agreements between the member states of the european union and the countries of the economic and monetary union of west africa. in order to avoid discrimination against eu air carriers, the traditional designation articles listing air carriers from member states that have signed a bilateral agreement are replaced by an eu designation article listing all eu air carriers. in addition, aviation fuel is generally exempt from taxation under traditional bilateral agreements, and such taxation is permitted under council directive 2003/96/ec amending the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity when activities are carried out within the territory of the european union. in addition, the clearly anti-competitive provisions of bilateral agreements (competitive commercial air carrier agreements) are compatible with eu competition law.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document. the construction sector is one of the most important industries in europe, accounting for 10% of gdp and 50.5% of total fixed capital. the sector directly employs 12 million eu citizens and creates an additional 26 million jobs in other sectors. the economic downturn has hit the eu construction industry hard, with many companies going bankrupt and workers losing their livelihoods across the eu. barriers to trade in the construction sector also persist in the union as member states still use national technical rules to prevent the free movement of goods and services in the construction sector in this context, the revision of the construction products directive is a much-needed boost that should help the sector to remove barriers to trade for manufacturers, thus helping businesses to stay in business and workers to keep their jobs. in order to remove administrative barriers, it is essential to ensure the independence and transparency of technical assessment bodies and i therefore support the proposal that transparency standards should be developed and that the participation of all stakeholders in the technical committees of the european standardisation bodies should be ensured in order to avoid conflicts of interest.
in writing. - i supported this proposal because the construction sector is one of europe's most important industries, generating 10% of gdp, directly employing 12 million eu citizens and dependent on 26 million workers. furthermore, around 92% of the companies producing construction materials are small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). as smes are the cornerstone of our economy, this proposal must recognise their role and needs. the revision of the construction products directive (89/106/eec) is a much-needed boost to the sector in removing barriers to trade for manufacturers, thus helping businesses to stay in business and workers to keep their jobs. the proposal for a regulation laying down harmonised conditions for the marketing of construction products (com (2008) 311) aims to update, simplify and amend the construction products directive in the light of changed circumstances. it is good that there is a focus and a particular concern on harmful substances in these products, and the ability to detect dangerous substances in products is very important. if we knew where asbestos was in buildings, construction workers and building occupants would not suffer from diseases such as mesothelioma. for the sake of health and safety and transparency in the future, it is important to re-introduce the amendments on hazardous substances (amendments 7, 17 and 49).

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document, which is of great importance for the effective delivery of humanitarian aid. the european consensus on humanitarian aid implementation is the first joint document on humanitarian aid policy since the 1996 regulation in this field. consensus is a key tool, especially in the rapidly changing context of humanitarian aid, such as the frequency of natural disasters, military conflicts that cause mass displacement, etc. i believe that the european consensus on humanitarian aid will be an important step forward in making the eu's humanitarian action as effective as possible and will contribute to the dissemination of humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law, to the coordination and coherence of eu humanitarian aid delivery, to a clearer use of military and civil protection resources and capabilities, to disaster risk reduction and to a stronger link between emergency aid, rehabilitation and development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european union is the largest humanitarian aid donor, providing more than 40% of official international humanitarian aid. the number and intensity of natural disasters worldwide have increased sharply as a result of the effects of climate change. the humanitarian aid landscape has therefore changed significantly in recent years, and it is necessary to strengthen the eu's capacity to respond to disasters. i believe that the european union must step up its efforts to reduce disaster risk and provide not only for emergency aid but also for support to local communities to make them better prepared for disasters. the worrisome trend is the increase in violations of international humanitarian law and the deterioration of the situation in the areas where humanitarian aid is delivered. i agree that the european union must take action to ensure that humanitarian aid is coordinated in a good way and that it is not misused in any way.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report by parliament on the implementation of the european consensus on humanitarian aid: mid-term review and future prospects of the action plan. the humanitarian aid agreement commits the european union to working closely together in this area to develop a common vision for humanitarian aid. the aim of this agreement is to enhance the effectiveness of the european union, to protect and promote the fundamental principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and to promote respect for international humanitarian law. the mid-term review found that there was a lack of information on specific actions taken or to be taken and that the agreement was not yet known even to representatives of humanitarian organisations. a major effort is needed to improve the visibility of the consensus and to better inform member states, other institutions and military actors. the humanitarian aid environment has changed significantly in recent years and calls for an even stronger and more active application of the humanitarian aid agreement. i would like to emphasise the need to strengthen disaster risk reduction efforts and to provide not only for emergency relief but also for support for communities' own disaster preparedness capabilities. more efforts should also be made to integrate gender and to protect victims of sexual violence, which is increasingly being used as a weapon of war, through humanitarian assistance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is not just a formality, but helps us to return to the issues of humanitarian aid. the humanitarian situation has changed considerably in recent years. as regards the change in circumstances, it should be noted in particular that the impact of climate change has led to a sharp increase in the number and intensity of natural disasters. efforts to reduce disaster risk should therefore be strengthened, providing not only for emergency assistance but also for support for the capacity of communities to prepare themselves for disasters. in addition, complex crises, in particular internal conflicts, have increased and the nature of conflicts has changed, often involving mass population displacement (refugees, internally displaced persons) and increased violence against the population. there is a growing number of violations of international humanitarian law and a deterioration of the situation in the areas where humanitarian aid is delivered. the most shocking aspect of violations of international humanitarian law is the increasing use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. much should be done to protect humanitarian aid from sexual violence. therefore, more specific attention should be paid to the most vulnerable groups, such as women, children and forcibly displaced persons (idps and refugees). the recent humanitarian disasters in haiti and pakistan have once again demonstrated the need to strengthen the eu's disaster response capacity in terms of effectiveness, coordination and visibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union, as the largest provider of humanitarian aid, needs to focus more on humanitarian aid in areas where it is urgently needed, given the sharp increase in the number of natural disasters and internal conflicts. member states should participate more effectively in the implementation of this consensus by integrating it into their national humanitarian strategies. in view of the need for humanitarian aid, it is necessary to increase its funding by ensuring the financing of operations in a timely and efficient manner. i agree with the proposal that there should be a clear separation of powers between military and humanitarian actors, so that military resources and capabilities, especially in regions where there is military conflict, are used only in strictly limited and extreme cases. in addition, a european civil protection and rapid response force should be established to ensure the proper and effective coordination and coherence of humanitarian aid.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which recognises that food security is a human right. this is achieved when all people have access at all times to sufficient safe and nutritious food to meet their daily nutritional needs for an active and healthy life. it is important to note that global stocks of staple foods are much smaller than in the past during the 2007 food crisis, they fell to a record low of 12 weeks of global food stocks. at the same time, global food production is becoming increasingly vulnerable to extreme weather events linked to climate change, which can lead to sudden, unpredictable food shortages. the eu should therefore provide for its contribution to the global food supply system. i think it is very important to promote both competitiveness in the agricultural sector and traditional farming, small farms, organic farming and local distribution. in addition, as rural communities age, i believe it is vital to ensure that young farmers have access to land and credit.
in writing. - i voted for this document. with the rapidly increasing number of people in the world, the agricultural sector must meet the growing demand for food despite the constraints of limited natural resources, high energy prices and climate change. the food and agriculture organization (fao) estimates that at least 70 percent more food will have to be produced to meet the needs of a world population expected to exceed 9 billion by 2050. in addition, around 900 million people worldwide are chronically hungry due to extreme poverty, and 2 billion people are food insecure for longer periods of time due to greater or lesser poverty, making food availability one of the most important issues to be addressed. i agree that the new cap, which will be implemented after 2013, should promote not only competitiveness but also traditional agriculture, small farms, organic farming and local distribution of products to contribute to food security. in addition, as rural communities age, i believe it is vital to ensure that young farmers have access to land and credit, and that food prices are affordable and farmers have sufficient income.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because food security is a human right that ensures an active and healthy life. around the world, large numbers of people are constantly hungry or cannot reliably obtain food for long periods of time. despite the apparent sufficiency of supply, a large proportion of the world's population cannot afford to buy the most essential food items, and food availability remains one of the most pressing issues to be addressed. it is important to ensure that food is accessible to people from all social categories. the goal of food security cannot be achieved without addressing two of the most pressing issues of our time: the volatility of markets and prices, which is strongly influenced by speculation in commodity markets, and the dwindling food supply. speculation on food prices shall not be permitted in any way. we need to promote not only competitiveness but also traditional farming, small farms, organic farming and local distribution of products, ensuring agricultural diversity across europe. in addition, as rural communities age, i believe it is vital to ensure that young farmers have access to land and credit. our goal is to keep food prices affordable and farmers' incomes decent. however, i am in no way opposed to the use, consumption, import and other activities of genetically modified material and to the authorisation of production methods used in third countries, as there is no evidence to suggest that this does not pose a risk to human health or the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector in relation to food supply, as the growing number of consumers, the high number of hungry people, the situation of farmers, the volatility of food prices and speculation in shares make it particularly important to regulate the agricultural sector by means of certain measures. in particular, every effort must be made, through financial incentives, to promote traditional, small-scale or organic farming in order to ensure a continuous food supply. in view of the public health risks of genetically modified substances, i am opposed to the proposal to allow the import of non-genetically modified products containing at least a minimum technical level of the genetically modified substance. we must take all measures to prevent the import of new types of genetically modified feed into the eu and the possibility of using production methods used in third countries. food accessibility problems cannot be solved by violating food safety requirements and putting human health at risk. in view of the increasingly ageing rural population and in order to attract and encourage young people to engage in agricultural activities, preferential access to loans for young farmers should be provided.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european tourism industry, like many other economic sectors, is facing the increasing challenge of globalisation. this is a challenge that the commission has already highlighted and addressed on several occasions, in particular with the communication 'an industrial policy in the era of globalisation'. on 30 june last year, the commission also adopted a specific communication on tourism, which proposes, in line with the lisbon treaty and the new europe 2020 strategy, a consolidated policy framework to strengthen the competitiveness of the sector, with the aim of making european tourism a truly competitive, modern, stable and responsible industry. the creation of a favourable environment for the development of medium-sized, small and very small enterprises in the tourism sector is the fundamental principle of this consolidated framework. to achieve this we have proposed three concrete actions aimed firstly at boosting the competitiveness of the tourism sector within our union, secondly at promoting the development of sustainable, responsible and quality tourism, and thirdly at consolidating the image and visibility of europe as a set of sustainable and quality tourist destinations and, of course, maximising the potential of the union's policies and financial instruments to develop tourism. the initiatives promoted should provide the sector with the tools to adapt to the challenges faced by its players and to undertake sustainable development in terms of competitiveness. concrete measures will certainly be taken to promote innovation in tourism, to improve the quality of tourist services and to improve the professional skills of staff, because we can no longer think of tourism as a purely family-run sector, but we must also think of a more modern and more competitive tourist organization. i will give a few examples of vocational training: a 'ict & tourism platform' to facilitate the adaptation of the tourism sector and businesses to the evolution of the new information technology market and to increase their competitiveness. these are all proposals, ideas, which are included in the text of the commission's communication, which was approved by the council and which we are debating in parliament, the rapporteur is present in the chamber. the mobilisation of industry actors to make better use of the various union programmes, such as leonardo, the framework programme for innovation and competitiveness, erasmus for young entrepreneurs, the european social fund and other programmes. in addition, a strategy for the promotion of a diversified tourist offer and the creation of a virtual observatory with electronic support for european tourism will make it possible to contribute equally to the creation of a favourable environment for the players in the sector. it should also be borne in mind that smes can benefit from other cross-cutting initiatives to access finance. i would mention the jeremie project, a joint initiative of the commission, the european investment fund and the european investment bank, which aims to improve access to finance for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, in particular through the channels of venture capital, loans, guarantees, microcredit and other forms of repayable aid. finally, i would like to point out that small and mediumsized enterprises in the tourism sector are fully benefiting from the measures proposed under the small business act which aims to facilitate the operational environment specific to small and mediumsized enterprises and that parliament will receive the updated text within a few weeks. the small business act is therefore also a tool for protecting small and mediumsized enterprises in the tourism sector, which represent an extraordinary potential for developing a sector which i hope to be able to strengthen in the coming year, because i am absolutely convinced that a european policy, as provided for in the treaty, can add value to the work already being done very well by the regions of the european union and the member states. i therefore believe i can reassure the honourable member who put the question that the commission and my staff are committed to ensuring that all small and mediumsized enterprises in the sector are supported and have easier access to community economic instruments, in the context of a political strategy which aims to make tourism one of the key sectors of economic and industrial policy.
i think that all of us here today hope that the forecasts you have made for the future development of tourism will be realised and that this sector will not only be developed but also attractive for investment. as you know, however, tourism has developed unevenly in the european union so far, for reasons both objective and subjective. i'd like to ask. the baltic sea strategy identifies the attractiveness and accessibility of the baltic region as one of its key objectives. what has been achieved in this area in the past year ?
vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank mr balčytis for giving me the opportunity to speak on a subject which is particularly close to my heart as a european commissioner and as the first european commissioner responsible for tourism, which i consider a priority, together with industrial policy and space policy. the key issue, however, in order to give a concrete answer, beyond the political initiatives which i have tried to implement since i became commissioner, is what mr fidanza said in his speech, because there was no community competence for tourism policy before the lisbon treaty, and in the current financial perspective there are no funds to contribute with community aid to a strong tourism action. we have interesting programmes such as calypso, which in spain have been enhanced by regional initiatives which i think are very positive, but if i have understood the message that mr fidanza has sent, in the report that will be presented by parliament there will be support for an increase in the funds allocated to tourism policy in the next financial perspective. this can be included in the eighth framework programme or in ad hoc budget lines. it is important, however, that parliament should raise the issue, because it is difficult to give concrete answers if the economic instruments are not available. that said, it does not mean that we will not act in a very determined way. as you know, there have been many initiatives, the belgian presidency has organised a major event in malta, the hungarian presidency has already announced that it will be organising a major event - that was the subject of discussion at the first meeting we had in budapest a few days ago - a major event devoted to tourism. i am also glad that mr balčytis has raised the problem of tourism in the baltic: tourism is not a problem which concerns only the economies of the mediterranean countries - spain, france, italy, greece and malta - it is a very important resource for the whole of the european union, including the countries of central and eastern europe, which have beauty and potential to develop. i think that one of the issues that is dealt with in the text adopted on 30 june last year is the relationship with the new emerging classes, with the new bourgeoisie of the russian federation, where there are millions and millions of citizens who want to do tourist work and therefore want to go outside the borders of their country. we have a problem with the visas. the same problem exists with china, i believe, and it is the will of the european commission and the ministers of tourism to try to solve this problem, both with regard to this potential of russian tourism and this potential of chinese tourism, to speed up and make it easier to receive in our countries, and the baltic countries, being closer to the russian federation, can benefit from a tourist presence also of the emerging middle class which can bring benefits to their economy. this is at the very heart of our work on tourism policy and i am also pleased that many ministers from different countries - i met the new british minister for tourism in london a few weeks ago - including britain, are strongly committed to supporting the european union's tourism policy, as is france. it would be important to identify some entry points, because europe must be an added value. i am pleased that commissioner vassiliou has wanted to include major sporting events in the text on sport adopted today. i think the london olympics are a great opportunity for the whole of the european union. we must ensure that each country in the union is a gateway for tourists who do not stop in that country but, after visiting that country, can go to visit other european countries. this is the additional action that the european commission can take and the support of parliament is crucial for me. i thank you for what you can do, not only in the debate on tourism policy but also in any debate on the next budgetary activities.
member of the commission. − mr president, education is one of the major factors that determines employability. the risk of being unemployed is 40% lower for higher education graduates than for people with only secondary education. however, youth unemployment and under-employment are unacceptably high today. too many graduates struggle to make the transition to the labour market and secure quality employment that corresponds to their educational background. of course, the efforts to improve employability begin well before higher education. the commission works with member states to identify the skills or key competences that young people need to learn at school. today, young people need a wider range of skills than ever before in order to flourish in a globalised economy. many will work in jobs that do not yet exist. many will need advanced linguistic, intercultural and entrepreneurial skills. technology will continue to change the world in ways we cannot imagine, so the ability to continue to learn and to innovate will become crucial factors for employability. guidance is also critical. young people are confronted with an increased number of educational choices. they need to be able to take informed decisions. this requires better information about education and training paths, including a clear picture of job opportunities. we need to develop quality career guidance services and vocational orientation with the strong involvement of labour market institutions. turning to higher education, the commission recently launched, as you know, youth on the move – a europe 2020 flagship initiative which sets out to make education and training more relevant to young people’s needs. we are now starting to implement the various parts of this strategy. later this year, the commission plans to present a new communication on the modernisation of higher education. we will take stock of progress in making higher education more relevant to the needs of the knowledge-based society, including the question of employability. we will identify the key challenges for the future and set out our response. as part of these efforts, the commission will reinforce the european platform for dialogue between universities and business, with a view to increasing the employability of students and to developing the role of education in the knowledge triangle. in a more global and mobile world, transparency regarding the performance of higher education institutions can stimulate both competition and cooperation, and be an incentive for further improvements and modernisation. however, existing international rankings can give an incomplete picture of the performance of universities. this year, the commission will present the results of a feasibility study to develop an alternative multi-dimensional ranking system which reflects the diversity of higher education institutions. europe needs to be better at anticipating the skill needs of tomorrow. this is why the commission has launched the agenda for new skills and jobs, which goes hand in hand with our youth on the move initiative. the agenda for new skills and jobs looks at how to help our young people to become more employable. above all, we need to give people the right mix of skills so that they can adapt to our fast-changing society. our new eu skills panorama, which will be operational in 2012, will help to forecast not only the skills that employers need today, but also those required in the future. in the spring of this year, the commission intends to propose new european benchmarks on learning mobility and on the role of education in preparing people to be employable in the knowledge-based labour market. finally, eu programmes to support education, training and youth, including mobility programmes such as erasmus, can help young people to improve their chances in the labour market by gaining valuable international experience and by developing their intellectual understanding.

member of the commission. − first of all, on the question of the disparities between higher education institutes: exactly! that is why we want to have transparency in the records of universities. that is why we are now completing the feasibility study on the basis of which we shall dare to look into the ranking of universities, the mapping of universities and the standards of universities in order to give students more informed choices. the aim is for them to know exactly where to study, what to study and what is the standard of the university that they want to enter. regarding fees, i think i agree with you that high fees need fair loans, but as i am sure you know this is the responsibility of the member states. we know that one thing that economists agree on is that investment in education is something which will produce long-term results, growth and jobs, so i always urge governments not to cut university investment or education investment in general. moreover, i agree with the honourable member who raised the question of the insufficiency of mobility grants like erasmus. that is why we are again completing a feasibility study – a study by the london school of economics, which i hope will be ready in a couple of months – on the basis of which we shall explore, with the european investment bank, the possibility of creating a european student loan for mobility. this, i am sure, will give all students, whether they are poor or rich, the possibility of taking advantage of these excellent mobility grants. with regard to mr papanikolaou’s question, he is talking about the structural development funds on the basis of which governments can build their education infrastructure. unfortunately the structural funds are not my responsibility, but i will find out from commissioner hahn whether there are any reports by member states as to the outcome of these grants and if so, i will certainly let you know.
member of the commission. − as you are aware, it is for each member state to decide how to organise its educational system. this is in accordance with article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. nevertheless, the commission works with member states to foster mutual learning and exchanges of good practice. as we stated in the europe 2020 strategy, it is vital for europe’s future as a knowledge-based and inclusive society that education systems are reformed and modernised to match the best in the world. the oecd’s pisa survey is an important resource for these exchanges. the latest pisa survey, published in december 2010, shows a mixed picture for eu member states. there are signs of considerable improvement in some systems but, overall, there is much progress still to be made. these results will provide an important input to future exchanges between the commission and the member states. the european benchmark, adopted by the council in may 2009, aims at an adequate level of basic skills in reading, mathematics and science by calling for the share of low-achievers aged 15 to be reduced to below 15% by the year 2020. now i would like to read something from the pisa report, which is very relevant. the share of low-achieving pupils in reading, which had increased from 21% in 2000 to 24% in 2006, improved to 20% in 2009. nevertheless, the oecd 2010 benchmark of reducing the 2000 share by 20% to reach 17% was not reached. the share of low-achieving pupils in maths and science has been declining since 2006. there was more progress in science than in maths and the share of low-achievers is today lower in science than in maths. if 2006 is used as a strong starting point, the eu is well on track as regards progress towards the 2020 low-achiever benchmark. on average, over the three disciplines in the 25 eu countries for which data is available, 22.5% were low-achievers in 2006 and by 2009 their share had declined to 19.6%. so we see that, on average, in the european union we have made progress. the commission will, of course, analyse the pisa results and publish its conclusions in its next annual progress report on benchmarks in 2011. in november 2010 the council invited the commission and member states to focus their joint work on the following areas: curriculum design, motivation for reading, literacy, maths, science and technology, the impact of new technologies on basic skills and their use in helping learners to acquire autonomy and maintain motivation, gender differences in performance and attitudes, the link between pupils’ background and their mastery of basic skills and, finally, issues around teachers and teacher trainers as well as around schools’ ethos and characteristics. in its conclusion the council also invited the commission to establish a high-level group on literacy and a thematic working group on maths, science and technology. i intend to launch the high-level group on literacy on 1 february. it will suggest policy measures based on best practices and research, which will help member states to improve the consistency and effectiveness of the provision of basic skills within their lifelong learning strategies and the group will conclude its work and publish its report in mid-2012. moreover, the thematic working group on maths, science and technology has already been established. it comprises national policymakers and experts on the basis of mutual learning and the exchange of good practices. the thematic working group will identify and disseminate policy measures to improve the situation of low-achievers in basic skills at national level. i should also underline that the comenius actions of the lifelong learning programme focuses among other priorities on increasing motivation in science and mathematics and on improving literacy skills.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document, which aims to establish patients' rights to crossborder healthcare. it should be noted that there is currently too much uncertainty on access to healthcare, compensation or responsibility for clinical care after treatment in other member states. this directive should enable all patients, not just the best informed or the most affluent, to benefit from many of the rights already recognised in this area by the court of justice of the european union. it should be stressed that this document does not in any way address the promotion of health services in other member states, but aims to make them feasible, safe and of high quality when they are judged to be useful or necessary. citizens of the european union must be given better and clearer information on the rules for travelling to receive healthcare in a member state other than the member state of the insured person. i agree that 'health tourism' must be tackled, but in order to protect patients' rights, a system of advance authorisation must be developed that is patient-friendly and that provides a reasonable advance warning to healthcare managers of the exceptional costs associated with travelling to healthcare facilities in other eu countries.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. citizens of the european union expect safe, high-quality and effective healthcare from their member states. member states are responsible for their own healthcare systems, and the availability and quality of services vary considerably. patients do not always have access to appropriate treatment in their own member state , which is fundamentally contrary to the freedoms enshrined in the eu treaty . the recognition of prescriptions in the union is also not resolved, which poses major problems for travellers. i do not think that the free movement of patients and the right to choose treatment in another member state will encourage medical tourism. i believe that this can be a positive sign for member states to undertake appropriate healthcare reforms and ensure that the highest quality and the widest range of healthcare services are provided so that patients can receive treatment in another member state if needed.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the situation in haiti one year after the earthquake, in which the european parliament once again expresses its solidarity with the people of haiti affected by the earthquake and cholera. i agree with the very important call for the international community, including the eu, to commit firmly and in the long term to immediately implement all the commitments made at the international donor conference in new york. it is important to take urgent action and coordinate as effectively as possible the provision of humanitarian assistance to the haitian people, of whom more than one million are still living in the camps that were supposed to be temporary. according to human rights groups, living conditions in these unprepared camps are appalling and women are "victimized by rape and sexual violence". however, in the longer term, it is clear that humanitarian aid providers are not obliged to continue to fill the gaps or to perform the functions of the state of haiti and that measures are needed to ensure sustainable development, in particular access to healthcare, drinking water and good sanitation. at the political level, the priority for the haitian state is to immediately acquire the capacity to ensure democracy and good governance in the country, as this is essential for the reconstruction of the country and the participation of civil society and the haitian people.
in writing. - i supported this resolution, which assesses the situation in haiti one year after the earthquake. the situation in the country remains complex and chaotic, with reconstruction efforts largely stalled, millions of people facing hunger and more than 800,000 children at risk of violence, sexual abuse, trafficking and exploitation. the situation in the country has deteriorated further following the political crisis following the presidential and parliamentary elections. although the international community has responded effectively to the tragedy in haiti with financial and humanitarian aid, only a fraction of the promised $10 billion has been delivered so far. the cholera epidemic in the country has demonstrated the failure of the haitian state to respond adequately to the situation and highlighted the shortcomings of the international aid system . the ongoing political unrest has prevented the resumption of reconstruction and assistance to the affected people, further exacerbating the situation. the european union, as the main provider of aid, must take a political leadership role in coordinating haiti's reconstruction efforts and ensuring that aid reaches those who need it most.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the situation in haiti, as the european parliament once again expresses its solidarity with the people of haiti affected by the earthquake and cholera. i support the very important call for the international community, including the eu, to commit firmly and long-term to the immediate implementation of all the pledges, given that more than a million people live in camps that were built by themselves and that were meant to be temporary, and given that human rights associations report that living conditions in these unprepared camps are appalling and that women are victims of rape and sexual violence. the population is currently suffering from food shortages, and 80 percent of haitians live in abject poverty. access to healthcare, drinking water and good sanitation is essential. measures are needed to ensure the long-term development of haiti. i therefore support the eu and member states' commitment to make the recovery and reconstruction of haiti a top priority, and that the time has come to help haiti become an economically and politically strong and independent state. the international community must seize this opportunity to end the root causes of poverty in haiti once and for all.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the negotiations on the eu-libya framework agreement. libya remains an authoritarian regime, its population does not enjoy basic human rights and capital punishment is regularly carried out. the state institutions are not democratically accountable and state power is not anchored in the rule of law. nevertheless, libya has expanding commercial and political relations with eu member states, and the country is strategically important for the eu. negotiations on an eu-libya framework agreement started in november 2008. however, the development of relations must ensure full respect for european values and principles, and it is important to request firmly that the council and the commission take necessary steps – such as strongly recommending that libya ratify and implement the geneva convention on refugees of 1951 and its 1967 protocol; requesting that the libyan authorities sign a memorandum of understanding granting unhcr a legal presence in the country; encouraging libya to commit to a moratorium on the death penalty, etcetera – in order to protect european values.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in belarus. in minsk, more than 700 people were detained for participating in the 19 december demonstration, most of whom were released after serving short administrative sentences, while 24 opposition activists and journalists, including six presidential candidates, facing up to 15 years in prison for inciting mass unrest with violent attacks and armed resistance. the brutal use of force by the police and kgb against protesters on election day is condemned. such behaviour is a flagrant violation of the fundamental principles of democracy, such as freedom of assembly and expression, and human rights. in view of the current situation in belarus, i would urge the european commission to continue to provide financial support to the european humanitarian university (ehu) in vilnius, lithuania, to provide more scholarships to belarusian students persecuted for their civic activities and expelled from universities, and to contribute to the support of the organisation 'solidarity with belarus'.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on a sustainable eu policy in the far north. i agree that a unified, coordinated eu policy for the arctic is necessary, with a clear definition of the eu's priorities, potential challenges and strategy, taking into account the arctic's renewable and non-renewable resources, the impact of climate change on the region and the differing geopolitical assessments of the arctic at large. the arctic is a sensitive region where the impacts of climate change are particularly pronounced and have serious implications for other regions of the world. the best way to protect the arctic is therefore to have a long-term and ambitious global climate agreement, but the rapid warming of the arctic requires exploring other possible short-term measures to limit warming in the arctic. this is particularly important in the light of the growing interest in arctic resource exploitation. local populations, whose economies are largely dependent on the sustainable use of natural resources, and therefore the mitigation of climate change and its impacts and the right of local populations to a clean natural environment are also human rights issues, should not be overlooked.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the eu black sea strategy. i agree with the rapporteur that, given the importance of the black sea region to the eu and the relatively low level of synergy in the black sea, a strategy should be put in place to increase the coherence and visibility of eu action in the region and that the eu black sea strategy should be an integral part of the broader vision of eu foreign and security policy. the analysis of the current situation three years after the establishment of the black sea synergy shows in particular the lack of a clear, understandable and updated picture of the results of the implementation of the black sea synergy. the implementation of the eu black sea strategy should therefore create a stronger policy framework and promote eu engagement in the black sea region. i am of the opinion that the main objectives of the black sea strategy must be the creation of an area of peace, the stability and prosperity of the black sea, and the ensuring of the eu's energy security. this is why security, good governance, energy, transport, environmental protection, social, economic and human development must be prioritised. it is essential to include in the black sea security dimension decisive action to strengthen democracy, good governance and state capacity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the eu black sea strategy. the strategic importance of the black sea region for the eu was recognised in 2007 following the accession of romania and bulgaria. as the development of this region, strategically located at the crossroads of europe, the middle east and central asia, began to have a direct impact on eu internal affairs, the eu recognised the need to provide for greater involvement in the region. this has led the eu to launch a new policy approach to the region, known as black sea synergy. the black sea synergy aims to develop regional cooperation between the eu and the region, as well as cooperation within the region itself. unfortunately, the strategy has been far less successful, with less progress on elements such as stability, democracy and good governance, due to the deterioration of democracy in the black sea countries and the 2008 russia-georgia war. in addition, the region is still plagued by persistent conflicts, a trend towards militarisation and proliferation, maritime surveillance, illicit trade and cross-border crime. i believe that the effective implementation of this strategy requires the establishment of mechanisms for regular reporting, monitoring, evaluation and follow-up. in addition, the main objectives of the black sea strategy must be the creation of an area of peace, the stability and prosperity of the black sea, and the ensuring of the eu's energy security. this is why security, good governance, energy, transport, environmental protection, social, economic and human development must be prioritised.

mr president, the european council is expected to approve that no eu member state should remain an energy island after 2015. as a rule, interconnections are absent in those member states where the natural gas sector is dominated by an incumbent operator. any progress on infrastructure that would allow new-party access is very slow because vertically integrated monopolies invest mainly to further consolidate their domination, while it is hard to attract new investors to a closed market. implementation of the eu gas directive – i.e. full ownership unbundling – is the only effective and reasonable way to encourage infrastructure investments (in this case in lithuania), introduce competition and speed up integration into the eu internal energy market. however, it is absurd that an eu member state is being threatened, or even discriminated against, for implementing the eu legislation while the eu itself seems to stand aside. therefore i would ask you, colleagues, the commission and the council, to use every opportunity openly to express disapproval of pressure being put on a member state to waive implementation of the eu acquis; and to consolidate support for it at the european council meeting. i should mention, too, that the implementation of the eu gas directive in lithuania is closely followed by other member states where conditions are similar. without this access, the goal of achieving a fully integrated and functioning eu internal energy market by 2014 will be undermined.
the next decade will be crucial for the european union as a whole, as member states will have to make serious choices: to replace existing sources and infrastructure and to meet the growing energy needs that will be necessary for the future development of the european economy. this energy council meeting is really important. it could become historic if the specific principles for the development of the common internal energy market are agreed. it will indeed allow all 27 member states of the european union to coordinate their actions and focus their efforts on creating a greater and more competitive environment for our economy, increasing employment and reducing social exclusion. i think it is very important that we actually set out specific timetables to reduce or eliminate the isolation in the member states. this requires a high degree of political will and solidarity, and the development of projects that are not only commercially attractive but also essential for the european union. it is also very important, i think, to set binding timetables for member states to meet their commitments to implement these projects in time. while investment decisions are often made by market participants, political decisions also play a crucial role in creating a stable and transparent investment environment.

in writing. − in order to improve the efficiency and transparency of community external assistance, a new framework for aid planning and delivery was established in 2006. it is composed of council regulation (ec) no 1085/2006 of 17 july 2006 establishing an instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa), regulation (ec) no 1638/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 24 october 2006 laying down general provisions establishing a european neighbourhood and partnership instrument, council regulation (ec) no 1934/2006 of 21 december 2006 establishing a financing instrument for cooperation with industrial and other high-income countries and territories, regulation (ec) no 1717/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 15 november 2006 establishing a stability instrument, council regulation (euratom) no 300/2007 of 19 february 2007 establishing a financing instrument for cooperation in the field of nuclear safety, regulation (ec) no 1889/2006 of 18 december 2006 and regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 of the european parliament and of the council establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation. the implementation of those regulations has revealed the existence of an exception to the principle of non-compliance with the union financing requirements for expenditure relating to taxes, levies, duties and other charges. it is therefore necessary to amend the relevant provisions of regulation (ec) no 1889/2006 to bring it into line with other measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of a recommendation establishing a financing instrument for cooperation with industrial and other high-income countries and territories. the main objective pursued by regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 is the reduction of poverty in the context of the millennium development goals. cooperation with developing countries and regions under the geographic programmes established by this regulation shall cover only the financing of measures which meet the official development assistance criteria (oda criteria) established by the development assistance committee of the organisation for economic cooperation and development (hereinafter referred to as the oecd/dac). it is important for the european union to further strengthen its relations with the developing countries concerned, which are important bilateral partners and participants in multilateral fora and global governance. the union has a strategic interest in developing a wide range of relations with those countries, in particular in areas such as the economy, trade, academia, business and scientific exchanges. it therefore needs a financial instrument to finance measures which are not in principle oda in the sense of the oda criteria, but which are essential to the establishment of relations and which make a significant contribution to the progress of the developing countries concerned. in cooperating, the union should take into account the efforts of beneficiary countries to comply with the international agreements of the international labour organisation and to contribute to the common objectives of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the conclusion of the agreement on trade in bananas. i am pleased that one of the most technically complex, politically sensitive and commercially significant legal disputes in the history of the wto has come to an end. i believe that the agreement reached is a solution, but it does not fully reconcile the legitimate interests of all parties and it is therefore necessary to call on the european commission to carry out an impact assessment on the impact of the agreements on banana-growing developing countries and the outermost regions of europe by 2020 without delay. i welcome the fact that the banana trade agreements are the eu's final commitments on banana market access and will be included in the final outcome of the future multilateral negotiations on agricultural market access successfully concluded during the wto doha round. i would stress that the agreements reached are progress in the doha round, albeit limited, given that the scale of the problems is much larger than the banana issue.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft agreement on the banana trade. bananas are the fourth most important food product in the world and play a major role in the food supply. however, many countries grow bananas only for domestic and sometimes regional markets, and only 20 percent of the world's total production is sold internationally. banana trade is controlled by a small number of companies, of which only five multinational companies control more than 80% of the total international banana trade. on 15 december 2009, the eu, a group of latin american countries and the united states reached an agreement on eu banana import duties, the subject of perhaps the longest and most bitter dispute in the recent history of the multilateral trading system. the agreement consists of three main elements: an agreed list of reduced customs tariffs for banana exporters from the most favoured nation (mfn) countries; an agreement on the removal of preferential treatment for tropical products and certain products in the context of wider wto negotiations; a financial support package of eur 190 million for acp banana exporters; or a programme of complementary measures in the banana sector. as the banana dispute continued, the banana production and trade situation of the countries concerned became unstable. the conclusion of this agreement will make the global banana market more predictable and stable, will stimulate investment and growth, and will give greater attention to the broader issues of conditions in the banana supply chain.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation repealing the council regulation on the tariff rates for bananas. under the eu's banana import regime, 775 000 tonnes of bananas were allowed to enter the eu each year duty-free from the acp countries, while bananas from all other exporting countries (suppliers of bananas from the most favoured nation (mfn) countries) were subject to a tariff of eur 176 per metric tonne. many latin american countries have long insisted that this import regime unlawfully discriminated against them and gave preference to bananas from acp countries and violated wto rules on quantitative restrictions. under the terms of the agreement, the eu will gradually reduce its customs duties on bananas exported from latin american countries until they reach an amount of eur 114 per metric tonne. the agreement provides that the banana-exporting countries of latin america shall cease all wto actions against the eu: once the wto has approved the new eu tariff schedule for bananas, the latin american banana-supplying countries will terminate all ongoing wto banana disputes with the eu and withdraw all complaints against the eu since the accession of new member states or since the eu changed its tariff for bananas in 2006 and will not seek further reductions in the tariff for bananas during the doha round.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment. the fact that waste electrical and electronic equipment is one of the fastest growing parts of the waste stream poses a number of challenges for us. according to the european commission's impact assessment, almost 85% of waste electrical and electronic equipment is now collected. a comparison of the amount of used equipment collected with the amount of equipment placed on the market shows that 65% of the equipment sold is collected. however, the amount of waste electrical and electronic equipment handled is not reported to public authorities and only a small proportion is properly treated: only 33% of waste electrical and electronic equipment is officially described in reports, collected and treated in accordance with the requirements of the directive. increasing the amount of waste recycled is becoming a challenge. the member states are the key players in the fight against illegal shipments of waste. they must ensure that the directive is transposed into national law, implemented and enforced. so far, there has been a large-scale illegal shipment of waste equipment outside the eu. waste equipment is too often declared as used but still functioning equipment and exported as such from the eu. it is therefore necessary to regulate the simplified disposal of waste electrical and electronic equipment and used equipment.
in writing. − i supported this proposal because waste electrical and electronic equipment is one of the fastest growing parts of the waste stream. on the one hand, attention should be paid to the environmental and health impacts of improper treatment or disposal of these equipment, while on the other hand, the loss of raw materials is another important issue. the efficient and innovative use of energy, materials and resources is the foundation of the global economy. therefore, increasing the collection and proper treatment of waste materials in accordance with the directive is a major challenge and a necessity. we must think about and promote the appropriate collection and treatment of waste electrical and electronic equipment, because strong measures help to promote economic growth with a balanced impact on the environment and a clean and healthy environment for our people. i agree that not only the producers, the member states, but also we ourselves, the consumers, must contribute to a clean and healthy environment, and we must take a large share of the responsibility for the proper management of waste equipment. too many appliances are forgotten or left unused on the shelves or thrown in the trash in violation of the rules. member states must pursue ambitious targets by all means available, even if the targets set will not be easy to achieve. but the fact that some countries have already achieved these goals proves that it is possible. to maintain high levels of consumption in the future, we need to treat and use the remaining natural resources more responsibly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this directive because i believe that the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment is another challenge we need to overcome. at the moment, my country, lithuania, is unfortunately very far behind the eu average in terms of the management of this waste. waste electronics and electronic equipment an excellent source of precious metals and other resources imported into the eu. if all this waste was properly managed, reused and recycled, we could save a lot of money on raw materials. i hope that the new directive, although it will take a long time to come into force, which should lead to a more perfect system for the collection, reuse and recycling of waste, will both open up new opportunities for business and reduce the burden on the end user.
in writing. − waste electrical and electronic equipment is one of the fastest growing waste types. the accelerating pace of life, the rapid development of technology, and the desire to have the latest and greatest equipment are to blame. in this cycle, we face two major problems: resources and waste. i voted in favour of this report because i support the aim of collecting as much of the waste as possible, recycling it and putting it back into the world. this is the only way to reduce the need for useful resources and the amount of waste going to landfill. i think that the goals that we set are achievable, but they are not easy. the new eu countries will need to make a special effort. unfortunately, we have no backup planets to spare. if we want to maintain high levels of consumption in the future, we need to be more responsible in the way we use and waste the remaining natural resources.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the tb vaccine initiative, as this disease is still one of the leading causes of death worldwide, killing nearly two million people every year. this initiative would target tuberculosis patients worldwide, and in particular those in the least developed countries. it would also contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 targets and the millennium development goals by 2015. in addition, the vaccination programme could enhance the union's strategic autonomy in the fight against tuberculosis and other communicable diseases. it should be noted that vaccines are the main tool to be used in conjunction with the best available tests for the detection of infection in order to combat tuberculosis. these tests must be reliable, inexpensive and accessible to all patients, and must be accompanied by more effective diagnosis and treatment. this requires a major reorientation of research and increased and sustainable funding of the vaccine package. the european commission and the member states should therefore respect their financial commitments and take all necessary steps to ensure that the funds allocated to healthcare services also reach the poorest and most vulnerable people in the country.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because we have to fight tuberculosis, because almost two million people die of it every year worldwide, and almost one in three of the world's population is infected. it is a major public health threat and the second leading cause of death from infectious diseases worldwide. tuberculosis is strongly associated with social and economic problems, such as poverty, unemployment, alcoholism, drug addiction, hiv/aids, as well as with inadequate and poor health care systems in poor countries and delayed diagnosis. i am pleased that the tb vaccine initiative has already been developed, as the results of research and work could be used by tb patients all over the world. i would also point out that the fight against tuberculosis is still underfunded, that specific funding measures are needed to contribute to the licensing of european tuberculosis vaccines, the availability of vaccines, clinical trials for tuberculosis and more effective diagnosis and treatment, and that funding for health services must reach the poorest and most vulnerable populations in countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the tb vaccine initiative. tb and its prevention often remain a challenge not only for the developing world but also for developed countries. the alarming annual death toll of around 2 million worldwide from tb should be reduced by a variety of measures, including sharing best practices and allocating funds for tb vaccination. on the other hand, some of the main risk and incidence factors are alcohol and drug use and high levels of poverty. it is therefore necessary to take into account not only the vaccination mentioned above but also long-term programmes to reduce the latter. so once again i welcome this eu initiative to contribute to the active eu support for vaccine programmes, which, as shown by the statistics of the eu member states, have been successful in significantly reducing the incidence of tuberculosis.
