in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conclusion of an eu-brazil agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of ordinary passports. this eu-brazil agreement establishes a reciprocal visa-free regime for all citizens of brazil and the eu travelling for tourism and business purposes as defined in the agreement, including citizens of the four member states estonia, latvia, cyprus and malta who are currently not able to travel to brazil without a visa. it should be noted that under the common visa policy and due to the exclusive competence of the european union in this area, only the union, and not individual member states, can negotiate and conclude a visa waiver agreement. it is important that, in order to ensure a level playing field for all eu citizens, the agreement includes a provision allowing brazil to suspend or withdraw its application only in respect of all eu member states. the union may, in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, suspend or terminate this agreement only on behalf of all member states. i agree with the rapporteur that we need to ensure the implementation of the principle of reciprocity in eu visa policy.
in writing. − under council regulation (ec) no 539/2001, brazilian citizens can travel to all eu member states without a visa for short stays. however, brazil still requires visas from citizens of four member states (estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia) to enter its territory. other member states have bilateral agreements with brazil on visas, under which their nationals may enter brazil without a visa for a short period. the european union has exclusive external competence in this area, which means that only the european union, and not individual member states, can negotiate and conclude an agreement on visa-free travel. on 18 april 2008 the council therefore adopted a decision authorising the commission to open negotiations for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and brazil on the short-stay visa waiver. following the negotiations, the agreement was ratified and formally signed on behalf of the union and brazil in brussels on 8 november 2010. i think it is necessary to approve this agreement on visa-free travel so that all eu citizens, including those from estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, can travel to brazil for tourism and business purposes without a visa, just as brazilian citizens can already travel to all eu member states without a visa. the common eu visa policy must therefore be strengthened without delay.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conclusion of an eu-brazil agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of ordinary passports. under council regulation (ec) no 539/2001, brazilian citizens can travel without a visa for short periods to all member states of the european union. however, brazil still requires visas from citizens of four member states (estonia, cyprus, malta and latvia) to enter its territory. other member states have bilateral agreements with brazil on visas, under which their nationals may enter brazil without a visa for a short period. in the context of a common visa policy and given the exclusive competence of the european union in this area, only the union, and not individual member states, can negotiate and conclude a visa waiver agreement. it is necessary to approve this visa-free agreement so that all eu citizens, including citizens of estonia, latvia, malta and cyprus, can travel to brazil for tourism and business purposes without a visa, in the same way that brazilian citizens can already travel to all eu member states without a visa. therefore, measures in this area should be taken without delay.
in writing. − this agreement establishes a reciprocal visa-free regime for short-stay travel for all citizens of the european union and of brazil holding diplomatic, service or official passports. in order to ensure a level playing field for all eu citizens with regard to the visa waiver regime, article 8 of the agreement provides that brazil may suspend or withdraw the agreement only in respect of all member states and, in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, the eu may suspend or withdraw the agreement only in respect of all member states. the agreement provides for the establishment of a committee of experts to settle any dispute arising from the interpretation or application of the provisions of the agreement. the agreement also provides for the exchange of models of passports between brazil and the member states. i believe that the preservation of the existing bilateral agreements should remain of paramount importance to the european union, as they provide for a short-term visa-free regime for those categories of travellers who are not covered by the eu-brazil agreement. in this context, it should be recalled that the european union could make a reservation to suspend the application of the eu-brazil visa waiver regime in the event of brazil's denunciation of bilateral agreements. this agreement on visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports is a step forward towards establishing a full reciprocal exemption from the visa regime under regulation no 539/2001.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document as it establishes a reciprocal visa-free regime for short-stay travel for all eu and brazilian citizens holding diplomatic, service or official passports. in order to ensure a level playing field for all eu citizens, article 8 of the agreement provides that brazil may suspend or withdraw the agreement only in respect of all member states of the union and, in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, the eu may suspend or withdraw the agreement only in respect of all member states. this agreement on visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic, service or official passports is a step forward towards establishing a full reciprocal exemption from the visa regime under regulation no 539/2001.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the implementation of the services directive, which entered into force in 2006. this directive aims to open the european union market to service providers, to remove protectionist restrictions on the provision of services by member states and to satisfy the principle of freedom of movement, which is the basis of the single market. in short, european service providers must have the right to do their work throughout the european union without bureaucratic obstacles. the directive covers a wide range of services, which generate 40% of the eu's gross domestic product (gdp). we hope that the implementation of this directive could potentially generate up to eur 140 billion in profits and increase the european union's gdp by 1.5%. however, in order to deliver the expected benefits, it is necessary to implement the directive properly. unfortunately, it has already been established that not all eu member states managed to fully transpose it into their national law by the end of 2009. i agree that the establishment of contact centres is a key element in the effective implementation of this directive. these centres are designed to provide the necessary information and to enable all procedures to be carried out electronically and not only in the national language. according to the european commission, 22 eu member states have established such centres, but only 17 of them have e-government portals, which still vary considerably from one country to another. it should be emphasised that without properly functioning single contact centres, users will not have all the information, which will impede the achievement of the objectives set out in the directive.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the aim of the services directive is to make it easier for service providers, in particular the self-employed and small and medium-sized enterprises, to carry on their activities, to develop new business areas and to recruit staff in other member states. the services sector, which accounts for 40% of the european union's gross domestic product, is of particular importance for economic growth and the fight against unemployment. this directive is an important step towards the creation of a single market for services, which should enable businesses, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, to provide better services in the internal market at more competitive prices and to exploit the significant economic and job-creation potential of the internal market for european services. in order to allow service providers to reap the benefits of the services directive, it is necessary to ensure that the provisions of this directive are fully and timely implemented in the member states. i believe that the commission must closely monitor the implementation of the directive in the member states and report on its implementation on a regular basis in order to remove the remaining barriers in the services sector and to exploit the economic potential of this sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the services directive aims to open up the european union market to service providers, to remove protectionist restrictions on the provision of services by member states and to satisfy the principle of freedom of movement, which is the basis of the single market. the scope of the services directive covers, in principle, all services of a commercial nature offered by a service provider established in a member state. services of general interest, financial services, communications services, employment agency services, health care services and social services in the field of care, childcare and housing construction are not included. services of general interest are not included in the scope of this directive and it is not in any way intended to weaken the provision of basic public services. in addition to a clear distinction between services falling within the scope of this directive and services of general economic interest, it is necessary to ensure that services of general economic interest are covered by the adoption of basic legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the implementation of the services directive, which entered into force in 2006. this directive aims to open the european union market to service providers, to remove protectionist restrictions on the provision of services in the member states and to satisfy the principle of freedom of movement, which is the basis of the common market. the meaning and purpose of the services directive is to shape access to the markets of the member states in such a way as to reduce deliberate barriers and/or to ensure that the rules in force in the member states are appropriate and non-discriminatory. the european parliament attached great importance to ensuring that this legislation did not affect either workers' rights or labour law. service providers in europe must have the right to operate throughout the european union without bureaucratic obstacles. the directive covers a wide range of services, which generate 40% of the eu's gross domestic product (gdp). i agree that the establishment of contact points is a key element in the effective implementation of this directive.
in writing. − the adoption of the services directive was aimed at facilitating the conditions for businesses wishing to cross national borders. the system created has significantly reduced the administrative burden. however, experience shows that in some eu member states, there are still a number of bureaucratic obstacles for small businesses to overcome. the one-stop shop principle is not yet working or not working properly in many countries, with businesses sometimes still having to obtain endless licenses and being audited by a multitude of regulatory authorities. these inconveniences are not limited to local businesses, but also to service providers wishing to provide services in other eu member states. i therefore support the text of the report and call on the eu member states to continue to make it easier for businesses to operate and to ensure the free movement of services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which sets out the ep's position on the protection of passenger rights. this refers to scheduled services for journeys within and between eu member states where the planned distance is no more than 250 km. we are talking about the rights of bus passengers in cases where a city or long-distance bus service is cancelled or delayed for more than 120 minutes. passengers must then be offered the choice immediately, whether they wish to continue their journey, whether they wish to travel to the intended destination by another route at no additional cost, or whether they wish to receive a refund of the ticket price. if the carrier does not provide this option, the passenger is entitled to additional compensation in addition to the compensation for the ticket. it is also important that passengers are provided with all the necessary information in the event of cancellation or delay. in addition, the aid must also be granted in the event of cancellation of a journey of more than three hours or a delay of more than 90 minutes. in this case, food or refreshments must be offered, as well as accommodation in a hotel for a maximum of two nights. unfortunately, the obligation to provide accommodation does not apply if the trip is cancelled or delayed due to severe weather conditions or a major natural disaster. i think that in view of the difficulties experienced by passengers this winter, when they were prevented from reaching their destination by the weather and had to spend even a few nights in the stations, their right to accommodation should be guaranteed.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. with the growth of the transport sector and the mobility of eu citizens, it is necessary to establish protection rights for passengers that apply across the eu and ensure a level playing field for carriers from different member states. air passengers have long enjoyed many rights, and two years ago the eu's rail and air passengers were unified in their rights and enjoyed a high level of protection. similar rights must be guaranteed to people travelling by bus and improved mobility for people with reduced mobility. i believe that after long and difficult negotiations, a really good and balanced agreement has been reached with the council, which fully protects passenger rights without imposing any burden on the carriers, most of which are small and medium-sized enterprises. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which sets out the european parliament's position on the protection of passenger rights. i believe that this will contribute to improving the conditions of passengers and provide them with more legal clarity in the event of an accident or other unforeseen circumstances, and that the implementation of the passenger rights enshrined in this document will not impose an additional burden on carriers, the majority of which are small and medium-sized enterprises. the most important thing is that the rights of passengers on bus routes will be similar to those of passengers using other modes of transport.
in writing. − today we voted in favour of a document which, while not ideal, is nevertheless a good compromise, having brought the council and the european parliament to an agreement. this regulation lays down rules on compensation for damage in the event of accidents or delays, on the handling of passenger complaints and on the rights of disabled persons, as regards passenger rights. it is of course not satisfactory that the regulation will apply to distances of 250 km or more. this would not be very fair in the case of small countries, but it is not just local routes that are at issue here, but international ones as well, and i believe that this document will be a guarantor of the rights of eu citizens travelling, with a particular focus on the rights of disabled people.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this draft resolution extending the rights of passengers in urban and long-distance bus transport. this document is the result of a long-standing compromise, which does not impose an additional burden on carriers in the exercise of their rights. i think it is important to ensure that passengers on bus routes enjoy rights similar to those enjoyed by other modes of transport throughout the european union, and that carriers are guaranteed a level playing field. in order to ensure that the compensation for damage suffered is adequate, i support the proposal to set compensation limits to be respected by the member states. it is particularly important to ensure fair and adequate compensation in the event of death, and i therefore consider that at national level the ceiling for such compensation cannot be lower than the minimum amount laid down in the regulation. in addition, adequate and operational assistance must be ensured in the event of an accident, by providing the passenger with the most essential services and supplies. i agree with the provisions of the regulation which provide passengers with appropriate guarantees and even provide for additional compensation in the event of cancellation or delay. it is to be welcomed that the regulation pays particular attention to disabled passengers and passengers with reduced mobility, providing them with the necessary assistance during their journey.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, we have a duty to ensure that service providers treat passengers fairly and that disabled people do not encounter obstacles when using transport services. it is important to ensure a level playing field between carriers from different member states and between different modes of transport. we need a well-balanced compromise that will guarantee passenger rights in all eu countries, which sometimes vary greatly in size, while not imposing a heavy burden on carriers, many of which are small and medium-sized enterprises. most importantly, any new rules will improve the quality and competitiveness of the eu transport sector. however, road safety is not to be overlooked. in lithuania we are highly dependent on road transport more than 90% of all travellers use cars. the use of buses for urban and long-distance transport accounts for about 8%. a very important issue which i think has not been sufficiently addressed is road safety. according to eu statistics, there are 110 road deaths per million inhabitants in lithuania. for comparison, for the same population, sweden has 39 deaths, the united kingdom 41. this lithuanian figure is intolerable and far above the eu average of 70. that has to change.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the ep endorses a new eu regulation introducing co2 limits as of 2014 for light commercial vehicles (lcvs). i believe that new requirements and co2 limits will help to fight global warming, lower running costs through savings on fuel and boost innovation and the competitiveness of european car manufacturers. with these rules, green technologies have to be built into the vehicles which need to stay affordable. starting in 2014, 70 percent of new commercial vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes must comply with an average emission limit of 175 grams co2 per kilometre. in 2020, the limit will decrease to 147 grams. it is an ambitious, but feasible, plan.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. at its meeting of 8 and 9 march 2007, the european council made a firm commitment to reduce overall greenhouse gas emissions in the community by at least 20% compared to 1990 levels by 2020, or by 30% if other developed countries commit to similar emission reductions and more economically advanced developing countries contribute appropriately to this target within their capabilities. in order to achieve the necessary emission reductions, policies and measures at member state and union level should be implemented across all sectors of the union economy, not just the industrial and energy sectors. road transport is the second largest greenhouse gas polluting sector in the union and its emissions, including those from light commercial vehicles, are continuously increasing. if road transport emissions continue to rise, this could undermine efforts by other sectors to curb climate change. until now, there has been no legislation in the eu on co2 emissions from light commercial vehicles, although the demand for this transport is increasing in the eu. i think we have managed to agree with the council on a balanced document that will reduce co2 emissions and encourage the automotive sector to invest in new and less polluting technologies.
in writing. −light commercial vehicles are mainly used by business entities, including small and medium-sized enterprises. at present, light commercial vehicles account for about 12% of the car fleet. it must also be recognised that these vehicles are usually purchased in large quantities to supplement the fleet and are therefore already selected with regard to their economy and running costs. the average reduction in co2 emissions from light commercial vehicles was 0.4 to 0.5% per year between 2002 and 2007, but this increase in fuel efficiency was rendered meaningless by the increase in transport demand and the production of larger vehicles. it is therefore necessary to adjust the community targets for new light commercial vehicles in order to avoid fragmentation of the internal market which may result from different measures adopted at member state level. in addition, in order to set co2 emission standards for new light commercial vehicles, it is necessary to avoid the risk of regulatory inadequacies that may arise due to the partial overlap between the registration of passenger cars and that of light commercial vehicles.
in writing. − i supported the provision that the light commercial vehicle sector should make the same effort to reduce co2 emissions as the passenger car sector. this would allow manufacturers to bring new vehicles with improved co2 emissions to the market. this would enable consumers to have access to more intelligent vehicles and to contribute more to reducing co2 emissions from vehicles. the objective of this proposed legislation is to reduce co2 emissions from light commercial vehicles. this is more difficult than in the case of passenger cars, as the body shape of light commercial vehicles cannot be changed quickly or cheaply to increase their efficiency. all modifications shall be made to the engines or to the mechanical parts. these investments are quite substantial. however, i doubt that this proposal will achieve the objective pursued, as there are serious concerns about whether the measures in question will achieve the original objective of preventing climate change, and whether the proposed targets and timetable are realistic, economically justified and do not reduce competitiveness in this sector. however, i believe that three aspects should be taken into account more: the economic downturn and its negative impact on car manufacturers and consumers, the need to support industry (manufacturers) rather than putting pressure on it through onerous measures (or even fines), the need to support business (consumers) rather than burdening it with additional costs through questionable policy measures.
in writing. − we need to reduce co2 emissions as much as possible, and it is therefore essential to set an appropriate emission limit for vehicles, taking into account the negative effects on the environment and human health. however, the proposal in the resolution to tighten the emission limit for new light commercial vehicles to the same level as that for passenger cars is to be considered in particular because of the measures envisaged to achieve this objective and their impact on van manufacturers. the proposal to install speed limiters in cars would have a negative impact on the position of business operators, reducing their competitiveness on the international market. furthermore, van manufacturers would have to increase their prices in line with the costs they incur. therefore, before such important decisions are taken, detailed scientific studies should be carried out demonstrating that the introduction of speed limiters would significantly reduce co2 emissions. a clear and adequate credit mechanism and incentive initiatives must also be established. i believe that more attention should be paid to incentive financing measures in order to increase the competitiveness of the european automotive industry.
in writing. − the creation of common patent protection in the european union is an integral part of the development of innovation and the promotion of competitiveness. i supported this resolution, which will help member states to cooperate more closely in the creation of common patent protection. the european union has a fragmented patent system, with high certification costs and complexity across member states. although more than nine eu member states have now declared their intention to start closer cooperation among themselves in the area of the creation of unitary patent protection, the commission and the participating member states should encourage the widest possible involvement of the member states. stronger cooperation would facilitate the proper functioning of the internal market, remove barriers to the free movement of services, increase the number of inventors and allow for the use of common patent protection throughout the eu.

in writing. − i support this resolution on the proposal for a council decision authorising enhanced cooperation in the area of the creation of unitary patent protection. given the current situation, where obtaining a european patent is very difficult and expensive, i support the proposal to introduce a closer cooperation procedure and to allow all interested eu countries to develop a common patent system. we must make every effort to resolve the issue of the language regime, which will reduce the costs incurred by eu companies seeking to obtain a european patent. moreover, an effective patent protection would simplify dispute resolution procedures and reduce administrative burden. it is good to see that many countries in the european union are contributing to the creation of a common patent initiative, and i am confident that the rest of the countries will also join the goal of creating a common patent in the short term in order to improve the conditions for economic liberalisation in the european union. only through enhanced cooperation will the proper functioning of the internal market be facilitated and possible obstacles to the free movement of goods be removed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on maximum permitted levels of radiation in food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radiation exposure. we all remember the chernobyl disaster of 26 april 1986, when high levels of radioactive material were released into the atmosphere, contaminating food (cereals, vegetables, berries and mushrooms) and animal feed in several european countries and posing a serious threat to human health. the soil was also contaminated by radioactive fallout, which increased the radioactivity of forest and agricultural food products from the affected areas. the eu has one of its objectives: to provide high-quality protection of human health. it is therefore urgently necessary to establish a system allowing the european union to set maximum permitted levels of radiation in the event of a nuclear accident or any other radiological accident resulting in the contamination of food and feed by radioactive elements, in order to ensure a high level of protection of public health. all eu citizens must be protected to the fullest extent possible in the event of a nuclear or radiation accident, and the european commission must be ready to respond quickly. maximum levels of contamination fixed in advance must be applied to food and feed.
in writing. −a high level of human health protection is one of the objectives which the union must pursue in defining its policies. the eu regulations setting emission levels in the event of a nuclear or radiation accident have remained unchanged since 1990 and it is therefore necessary to review and update these provisions. a comprehensive system should be established to allow the union to set maximum permitted levels of radiation pollution in the event of a nuclear or other radiological accident which may cause significant contamination of food and feed by radioactive elements, in order to ensure a high level of protection of public health. i agree that the permitted levels of radiation pollution should be reviewed regularly in order to take account of the latest international scientific developments and scientific advice and to eliminate existing differences in regulatory practice.

in writing. - i support the proposal for a council regulation laying down maximum permitted levels of radiation pollution in food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radiation accident. the protection of human health is one of the european union's priority objectives, and we must therefore develop a mechanism to ensure adequate and effective safety in the event of a nuclear or radiation accident. the levels of radiation contamination of foodstuffs and feedingstuffs following a nuclear accident must be regulated with particular strictness in view of the possible negative consequences for society. we must take all possible measures to reduce the contamination of food by radioactive particles in the air in the event of an accident and to reduce radiation exposure to a minimum. i support the proposal to apply the eu's core environmental protection principle 'the polluter pays' by ensuring an effective compensation mechanism in the event of a disaster, with particular attention to farmers who would suffer the most damage in this case.

member of the commission. − i am very happy to have received this question, because i have good news to report. since 1 january there have, for the first time, actually been more women than men working for the commission. we are very proud of this result, but we know that this is not the end of it. we still need to continue with our policy of also improving the figures for our female colleagues in managerial positions and non-managerial posts (ad) in the commission. we therefore adopted this strategy from 2010 to 2014, until the end of this commission’s mandate. we really would like to achieve a result where women would represent 25% of senior management positions, 30% of middle management and 43% of ad non-management posts. we have already achieved quite a lot over the last 15 years with the tremendous increase of women in managerial positions. we would, of course, like to continue with this same effort. the method we are going to use would be that retirements would be replaced with women, who would represent 30% of recruitment among senior management and 50% among middle managers and ads. so that means that when these managers retired, 30% or 50% of them should be replaced by women. in answer to your question, i checked the situation in other institutions and i must say that you are doing quite well in parliament. the figures are very impressive. it is not quite the same in the case of the council, though to be honest we have slightly different results. but i think that the best method to progress further would be if we continued with our policy of exchanging best practice, and in exchanging experience about the implementation of our policies. i know that our heads of administration, our secretaries-general, are discussing this issue on a regular basis also, and i believe that this exchange of good practice will lead to the appropriate results in all eu institutions.

first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur for raising a really timely, timely and very topical question. energy poverty remains a major problem and related challenges prevent people in the poorest regions of the world from improving their quality of life, earning a living and contributing to growth and productivity in general. this is one of the main factors hindering overall social and economic development and preventing these regions from breaking out of poverty. as the rapporteur mentioned, the statistics are grim: about one and a half billion people have no access to electricity, and more than two and a half billion people still use traditional biomass fuels. according to the world health organization, the use of this fuel causes two million premature deaths worldwide each year from respiratory diseases. the energy strategies of the world banks have so far produced no tangible results. in addition, support for fossil fuels remains higher than for renewable or clean energy sources. large investments are still being made in coal-fired plants, which continue to make these poor countries dependent on fossil fuels that are highly polluting. the agreement reached by g20 leaders to reduce support and funding for fossil fuel projects, which should not be funded at all after 2015, is positive and welcomes the momentum. the new strategy also requires a thorough assessment of the supervision and control of the financing provided, so that this support is used for energy projects that can provide long-term benefits and make a real contribution to the development of these regions and to the improvement of the quality of life of the people.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the ep expresses its position on the directive on the prevention of falsified medicinal products and their entry into the legal supply chain. it is necessary to take into account the concerns of eu citizens about the quality and safety of medicines they consume. however, experts are also seeing some worrying trends: a sudden increase in the number of counterfeit medicines seized by customs (up to 385% since 2005), the introduction of counterfeit medicines of vital importance, which can have devastating consequences, and the increasing detection of counterfeit medicines in legal drug supply chains. eu citizens need to be very careful when buying medicines online, as the chances of buying counterfeit medicines are up to 50%. it is important that patients are absolutely sure that the medicines they are taking are the medicines they think they are taking. the eu must therefore respond swiftly and constructively to these dangerous trends. this directive is the first step towards ensuring that only quality medicines are distributed in the eu. to this end, i believe it is essential to establish strict controls and accountability at all stages of the production, distribution and sale of medicinal products. this will ensure that eu citizens feel safe when using medicines of genuine quality.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. the report presented by the commission notes that counterfeit medicines are increasingly being seized, and that vital medicines for cancer and heart disease are being counterfeited. the number of counterfeit medicines entering authorised distribution networks is also increasing. this poses a serious threat to the health of eu citizens. the falsification of medicines should be considered a criminal offence, which prevents patients from receiving the treatment they need and thus harms their health, sometimes even causing their death. this directive should therefore aim to protect public health by ensuring high quality control of imports of medicinal products, which is one of the main ways for falsified medicinal products to enter the european market. it is also essential to establish a system of checks and an effective system for detecting counterfeit products. i believe that the online trade in medicines needs to be properly regulated and controlled, as it is one of the main routes for falsified medicines to enter the european market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to address the growing concern of european citizens about the quality and safety of the medicines they consume. there is evidence of a sharp increase in the number of counterfeit medicines seized by customs, with 2.7 million medicines seized at the eu border in 2006 and 2.5 million in 2007, representing a 384% increase compared to 2005. the counterfeiting of life-changing medicines has been seen to transition from the counterfeiting of life-saving medicines, including those for cancer and heart disease, psychiatric disorders and infections. treatment with such counterfeit medicines can have devastating effects. in addition, there is a tendency to penetrate the normal supply chain. in addition to the internet, there is an increasing effort to use authorised distribution networks. out of the 13 member states with data, 7 reported the spread of falsified medicines through the legitimate supply chain. patients should be absolutely sure that the medicines they are taking are the medicines they think they are taking. the use of counterfeit medicines can result in treatment failure and even death. i therefore believe that the protection of public health against falsified medicines should be the main focus of the directive. no additional objectives should interfere with the achievement of this objective.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to address the growing concern of european citizens about the quality and safety of the medicines they consume. it is estimated that 1% of medicinal products sold through legitimate channels in the eu are now counterfeit medicines. in some parts of the world, counterfeits account for nearly a third of the market. the worry is that innovative and life-sustaining medicines are being counterfeited. the internet is known to be one of the main routes for falsified medicines to the european market. more than 50 percent of the medicines purchased online from websites that hide their real physical addresses are counterfeit. people who search for cheaper medicines online often fall into the trap of fraudsters who sell counterfeit products with harmful ingredients. many counterfeit medicines are also 'legalized' during repackaging. dishonest repackagers and online scammers have long been unpunished, and more and more people are risking their health and even their lives by buying drugs online from unreliable sites. it is good that sanctions are being introduced for counterfeiters and that measures are being taken to ensure that checks are more stringent. in countries where online sales of medicines are allowed, registered pharmacies will have to obtain a special authorisation, their websites will be marked with a european logo and will be included in a european database. patients should be absolutely sure that the medicine they are taking is the medicine they need to take. the protection of public health against counterfeit medicinal products should be a priority.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the problem of counterfeiting medicines is widespread throughout the eu and there is an urgent need for strict measures to prevent counterfeit medicines from entering the market, which can have negative consequences for human health and even life. we need to ensure that only safe and effective medicines reach consumers and that criminal groups are prevented from profiting from the distribution of counterfeit medicines. we must do everything we can to ensure that the eu has a strict system of labelling prescription medicines, including safety labels to identify the manufacturer and the supplier. i believe that there should be stronger sanctions for falsifiers of medicines and that there should be an effective eu-wide control mechanism covering all market participants in the supply of medicines. particular attention and security measures must be given to the online trade of medicinal products by establishing strict authorisation, monitoring and control systems. each state must take all necessary measures to ensure the effective functioning of a system which informs the public of the dangers of counterfeit or substandard medicinal products and even allows the withdrawal of such products from the market.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the number of falsified medicines entering the eu is growing at an alarming rate. this is of particular concern to countries such as lithuania, which is the eu's eastern border. eastern europe is a major route for the multibillion-dollar trade in counterfeit medicines. this is a very serious problem: the commission estimates that 1.5 million packs of falsified medicines are sold in the legal supply chain every year. the increase of almost 20% is even more worrying. counterfeit drugs are not killers. the people who distribute them are dangerous criminals and should be treated as such. the penalties for falsifying medicines should be the same as those for smuggling drugs. this will require better coordination between the various national and international institutions. we need to strengthen the control of counterfeit medicines sold online, as the internet is one of the main ways for falsified medicines to enter the european market. according to the world health organization, one in two medicines sold online is counterfeit. i think one of our priorities should be to try to raise public awareness of the risks involved in buying medicines online.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the review of the european union's financial support for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the forthcoming programming period. the 23 million smes, which account for approximately 99% of all businesses in the eu and create more than 100 million jobs, play a key role in ensuring economic growth, social cohesion and job creation, and are a key source of innovation and vital for maintaining and increasing employment. however, smes have limited access to finance, which is a major obstacle to their creation and growth, especially in the context of the current financial and economic crisis. i therefore support the call in the resolution for a substantial increase in funding from the eu budget for innovative financial instruments to meet the financial needs of smes and in line with the europe 2020 strategy. however, it should be noted that the current eu financial rules on the use of european funds and programmes are unnecessarily complex and the time and costs of complying with these rules are not fully commensurate with the benefits to the final beneficiary. i therefore support the call on the commission to propose simplified and cost-effective rules and guidelines, in particular for programmes to support small-scale financing for smes.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) account for about 99% of all enterprises in the european union and create more than 100 million jobs. they play a key role in ensuring economic growth, social cohesion and job creation. the limited access to finance for smes is a major obstacle to their growth, and the ongoing financial and economic crisis has further limited access to finance. the banking sector is demanding more collateral and higher risk premia from smes. i believe that credit and loan guarantee schemes are crucial to ensure the viability, growth and job creation of this sector. the eib's lending to smes, which was still worth €15 billion in 2008, needs to be given special attention, but studies show that only a small proportion of this money has reached smes, as banks administering loans in the member states have tightened the requirements for issuing loans. i believe that the european commission must take the necessary measures and controls to ensure that the funding it provides reaches smes and ensures the viability and growth of this very important sector.
in writing. −it should be noted that many small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) will continue to be heavily dependent on credit and loans for external financing. it should be noted that the increasingly capital and risk-sensitive banking sector requires more safeguards and higher risk premia, and that both these requirements result in underfunding and lost business and employment opportunities in this very large sector of the economy. in this context, i believe that credit and loan guarantee schemes are of paramount importance in order to exploit the potential of smes to generate growth and create jobs. it is therefore necessary to apply the existing programmes effectively at both national and european union level. it is essential that the guarantee measures under the competition and innovation programme (cip), the risk sharing and financing programme and under the 7th framework programme and the structural funds (jeremie) continue to apply. the proper implementation of these measures is currently hampered by overly complex administrative procedures and the european commission should facilitate the use of structural funds resources allocated to sme financing instruments, in particular to finance renewable funds to ensure guarantee schemes, avoiding the creation of structures that duplicate existing schemes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), which account for approximately 99% of all enterprises in the eu and create more than 100 million jobs, play a key role in ensuring economic growth, social cohesion and job creation, and are a key source of innovation and vital for maintaining and increasing employment. the main obstacle to their development and growth is the limited access to finance for smes, a problem exacerbated by the current financial and economic crisis. the banking sector is demanding more safeguards and higher risk premia, both of which result in underfunding and lost business and employment opportunities in this very large sector of the economy. credit and loan guarantee schemes are crucial to unlocking the potential of smes for growth and job creation. i agree that every effort should be made to ensure that existing funding programmes are implemented effectively at both national and eu level by simplifying administrative procedures and facilitating access to structural funds.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because smes play a key role in ensuring economic growth, social cohesion, job creation and innovation. it is essential to identify effective financial support instruments, with particular attention to interim financial instruments in the future programming period, which would remove barriers to financing and stimulate the creation and growth of new innovative enterprises by providing greater access to european venture capital and bond markets, while removing obstacles to their expansion. i support the proposal to make access to equity capital easier for newly established and innovative companies. we must make every effort to ensure that existing funding programmes are implemented effectively at both national and eu level by simplifying administrative procedures and facilitating access to structural funds. it is essential that member states carry out substantial reforms in their taxation and support systems for smes. the eu budget must also increase funding for innovative financial instruments, together with increased funding for the competition and innovation programme. in addition, administrative barriers for smes must be reduced by simplifying the management of innovative financial instruments, harmonising sme funding programmes and establishing a one-stop shop.
in writing. − colleagues, small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the backbone of our society and the engine of our economy. both lithuanian and eu smes account for 99% of all enterprises. smes create more than 70% of jobs for lithuanians. smes play a key role in achieving the objectives of the lisbon strategy, which promote innovation, competitiveness, social cohesion and job creation. it is therefore important to create an environment in which this can develop. smes, as well as start-ups and innovative companies, must be given better access to eu financial instruments. credit and loan guarantee schemes are crucial to unlocking the potential of smes for growth and job creation. at present, most investment plans are at risk of being abandoned due to uncertainty and lack of funding. it is therefore important that banks restore liquidity provision and support investment in the real economy. it is also important to support equity markets for start-ups and innovative companies. we must do more to remove administrative obstacles. this will require smart management and cost-effectiveness in conjunction with innovative financial instruments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this very important resolution on the european pension system. europe is ageing, with a steady increase in the number of people of retirement age due to demographic deterioration and declining birth rates. the importance of social security and pension funds is therefore undoubtedly growing, especially in the light of the current economic crisis. people need to feel secure in their old age, and this can only be achieved through stable, well-functioning pension systems. there are currently almost 100 different pension schemes in the european union. the large differences between eu countries make eu citizens feel unequal. people who have worked hard all their lives, especially in the new eu member states, receive different pensions compared to citizens of the old eu member states. it makes them feel second-class. while the regulation of pension systems is undoubtedly a matter for the member states, it is clear that there is a need for greater coordination at european level in this area. the eu must look after those who need it most: the disabled, the unemployed, the elderly. the european union, in pursuit of the well-being of its citizens and with the help of the member states, must endeavour to level the pension systems as much as possible. this would undoubtedly contribute to improving people's living standards and to the eu's economic growth.
in writing. − the european union faces major challenges, the most important of which is the ageing of the population. due to changing demographic trends, longer life expectancy means that older people will remain healthy and active and able to participate in social life for longer. meanwhile, low birth rates will reduce the number of people of working age, and will therefore pose significant difficulties for member states' social protection systems. the financial crisis has led to increased unemployment, poverty and social exclusion, which have exposed the fragility of some pension fund systems. in many member states, budget deficits have increased and pensions have become more difficult to finance. some private pension funds have also been unable to meet their commitments and it is therefore essential that the activities and supervision of such funds be properly regulated in the future. i supported this report and believe that new impetus must be given to the creation of strong, sustainable and secure european pension systems at national and eu level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in view of the rapid ageing of the european population, it is essential to focus on retirement age, the security of pension funds, and the establishment of common minimum pension standards in order to ensure normal living conditions for all europe's elderly. while the determination of retirement age and the size of pensions is a responsibility of the member states, the european parliament and the commission are proposing measures to help overcome the threats to pension systems. in addition, some coordination of reforms of national pension systems is inevitable in the context of the completion of the internal market and the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. it is a pity that the commission's green paper pays little attention to equality between men and women. women are more likely than men to work under atypical contracts or in precarious employment, and therefore earn less on average. in addition, women are more likely to interrupt their careers to care for motherhood, children, elderly or disabled family members, and as a result lose their insurance coverage and ultimately receive lower pensions. it must be acknowledged that there is no perfect pension system. economic and financial capacities vary across member states, and therefore more attention needs to be paid to ways of improving pension systems, such as early entry into employment, 'flexible' retirement age, better reconciliation of work and family life, and common criteria for a minimum pension.
in writing. − the demographic trends, i.e. the inverted population pyramid we can expect in the future, and the longer life expectancy we can all enjoy when older people stay healthy, active and involved in society for longer, require a new strategy for cohesion and compatibility in pensions. there are large differences in pension systems in europe and the new member states and their citizens face additional problems because of the strong desire to create a heterogeneous (multi-tier) pension system to spread the risks. the financial and economic crisis has shown that no pension system is immune to such events, but it is clear that the high budget deficit, the high unemployment rate, the very low potential for tax increases have caused a great deal of damage to current pension funding models, with some member states, such as lithuania, even having to take drastic measures, namely pension cuts, which i consider to be intolerable and unacceptable. member states must make every effort to prevent reduction measures that have a severe impact on the poorest. i have reserved my position on this report because most of the solutions proposed are socially sensitive and the report did not adequately assess all the benefits and risks. this is particularly the case when it comes to raising the retirement age or reducing the influence of member states on pension policy.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased that the rapporteur acknowledges that there are major gaps in pension systems in europe and that citizens of some of the new member states, such as lithuanians, face additional problems. in my country, life as a pensioner is not easy. in recent years, it has even worsened: last year, the monthly pension of lithuanian pensioners was reduced by 5%. it's time to stop the double standards. in some european countries, such as lithuania, the government claims that the crisis is over and the economy is slowly recovering. and when it comes to practical measures, our leaders say they can't find the resources to bring pensions back to their previous levels. suddenly, they declare that the crisis is not over. financial sustainability is important in reforming our pension systems, as well as ensuring adequate income. it is impossible to achieve real sustainability without adequate pensions. an ageing society and financial pressures mean that our labour market is changing. this needs to be taken into account in the reform of the pension system. the balance of flexibility and security in the labour market supports the adaptability of the economy and thus contributes to sustainable, secure and fair pensions.

in writing. i would like to draw attention to two aspects of food prices. first, as my country's very recent experience has shown, it is very easy to manipulate public opinion a little bit to influence the rise in food prices. over the course of the day, the price of sugar in lithuania rose by more than 10% due to the resellers. therefore, food for daily consumption cannot be left to self-regulation. they can be considered as an investment which requires specific knowledge to manage, which is not available to the growers (farmers). although the free movement of goods is one of the fundamental principles of the eu's free market, stronger measures are needed at both national and eu level to limit food speculation and to protect the rights of the weaker side - consumers, small farmers and traders - in their dealings with large processors and trading centres. the second aspect is the close link between food and energy resources and their price relationship. on the one hand, we are promoting the use of biofuels to combat climate change (and have even set mandatory quotas for their use), and on the other hand, the growing of biofuel crops on agricultural land that could also be used for food production is increasing food prices. therefore, while tackling climate change is one of our priorities, we must find a way to do so without affecting food prices (for example, only land that will never be suitable for agricultural production will be used for biofuels).

their equal participation in society, it is important to involve them in the decision-making and policy-making that affects them. in its 2008 and 2010 resolutions, the council consistently called for the inclusion of persons with disabilities and their organisations in policy-making. it should be recalled that the council also adopted a directive prohibiting discrimination on grounds of disability in the field of employment and occupation. that directive also provides for membership of and participation in workers' and employers' organisations, a specific measure taken by the council to guarantee that persons with disabilities can effectively participate in decision-making. the commission also has a new disability strategy. we are very pleased that this autumn has been born and focuses primarily on the implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the hungarian presidency intends to submit draft conclusions to the council on this strategy with a view to adopting it at the end of the hungarian presidency in june. as regards the establishment of a special committee on disability, no proposal to this effect has yet been received by the council for consideration. in this context, we would like to remind you that the council can only act in its legislative capacity on the basis of a proposal submitted by the commission, but of course we always keep an eye on parliament, but that is the way legislation is done in the union.
in a meeting of the european disability forum in the european parliament in january this year, commission vice-president reding said that some eu member states were opposed to the council directive on equal treatment for all, regardless of religion, belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. the anti-discrimination directive is therefore one of the most important issues in the field of human rights, especially in the area of the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities. does hungary, as the current presidency of the council of the european union, intend to take any concrete action on the adoption and revision of this directive and what concrete measures will it take to move this directive from the deadlock?
mr president, i welcome the fact that we have finally adopted the resolution on this very important topic. i have been a close observer of political developments and the situation as regards the rule of law in russia for many years now. most recently, i had a chance to visit russia with an official delegation of the human rights subcommittee in september last year. during the visit i had a first-hand opportunity to observe how the rule of law is upheld in russia when attending the trial of the former yukos boss, mikhail khodorkovsky, and his business associate, platon lebedev. the trial of khodorkovsky and lebedev is only the most conspicuous of many examples of the selective application of the rule of law in russia, which means that there is no genuine rule of law. if russia wants to be a strategic partner of the eu it must follow a path of comprehensive modernisation. any modernisation plan will be a failure if the rule of law is not vigorously developed in russia.
in writing. − on 23 april 2007, the council authorised the european commission to open negotiations with the republic of korea for an eu-korea free trade agreement. the agreement includes a bilateral safeguard clause which provides for the possibility of re-establishing the mfn duty rate if, following the liberalisation of trade, imports are introduced on such a large scale and under such conditions as to cause or threaten to cause serious injury to an industry of the european union producing a like or directly competitive product. in order for the branch of the measure in question to be effective, the safeguard clause must be incorporated into european union law. in addition, the procedural aspects of the application of safeguard measures and the rights of interested parties should be described. this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council constitutes a legal instrument implementing the safeguard clause of the eu-korea free trade agreement. i would stress that the legislative function of this regulation must be limited to the implementation aspects, avoiding unilateral changes to essential elements which are already included in the agreement and avoiding adoption of measures which would be contrary to the spirit of the agreements with south korea. to give some examples, safeguard measures, their period of application or the period during which this safeguard clause can be invoked should not be changed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the free trade agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of korea, of the other part. in particular, in order to achieve more effective eu-korea cooperation, it is important to remove the existing trade barriers that have isolated the korean market until now. the entry into force of this agreement will create favourable conditions for economic growth and job creation. the eu will provide a favourable business environment for growing, competitive eu companies to enter south korea, which offers many new opportunities for eu goods and services, increasing the volume of trade between companies and reducing export costs. in view of the expected future expansion of trade between the eu and south korea, there will be significant savings in the revenue from customs duties, especially in the chemical, industrial and pharmaceutical sectors. in addition, fair competition will be ensured in the automotive, home electronics and textile sectors, where korea has a contingent advantage over the eu. the liberalisation of export tariffs will also bring significant benefits to the agricultural and service sectors. the agreement's strong focus on sustainable development is to be welcomed.
in writing. − i want to congratulate the two rapporteurs – mr sturdy and mr zalba bidegain – for guiding us through the complicated adoption procedure for the free trade agreement itself, as well as the important safeguard clause. the eu-south korea fta is the most comprehensive and ambitious agreement of its type that the eu has concluded so far. it covers many areas beneficial to eu producers and consumers, such as the elimination of tariffs on eu exports of industrial and agricultural goods, improved market access for eu services suppliers, the removal of non-tariff barriers in electronics, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, enhanced access to government procurement, protection of intellectual property rights, improved market access for eu car manufacturers and, very importantly and thanks to the safeguard clause, the protection of european car manufacturers against any imbalances that may occur in the sector in the future. i hope this agreement will be a model for many other ftas that are in prospect – with canada, singapore and mercosur, for example. at the same time, i congratulate parliament on the use of its new powers, this being the first fta to which we are giving our consent under the terms of the treaty of lisbon.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the europe 2020 strategy. the european parliament is convinced that the eu 2020 strategy should help europe recover from the crisis and strengthen its capacity to create jobs and to ensure smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, based on the five eu core objectives of promoting employment, improving conditions for innovation, research and technological development, tackling climate change and energy, improving education and promoting social inclusion, in particular by reducing poverty. i believe that the actions of the europe 2020 strategy are crucial for the future prospects of all european citizens, as they ensure sustainable jobs, long-term economic growth and social progress, but i agree with the concerns expressed in the resolution that the weak governance structure of the europe 2020 strategy will not meet expectations. it is important to note that the successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy requires closing the gap between the publicly announced objectives of the strategy, the resources available and the methods used, implementing reforms and ensuring high and rapid public and private sector investment in a wide range of projects. the european commission and the council have a major role to play in this. at the same time, member states should be encouraged to give the fight against unemployment the highest priority in their national reform programmes. only by joining forces between the eu and the member states can we hope to achieve the success of the europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. according to data published by the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) at the end of april 2010, 2 900 people died in europe from influenza a (h1n1) in 2009. this is well below the official estimate of mortality from seasonal influenza, which the commission estimates to be around 40 000 deaths per year on average and 220 000 in a particularly severe season. this figure is also below the most optimistic forecasts of the health services of the eu member states. the virus was declared a high-risk threat and some member states took very costly and disproportionate measures that did not reflect the real threat level of the virus (e.g. costs in the uk were as high as €1,300 million and in france 990 million, while costs related to seasonal influenza were up to €90 million). i agree that the world health organisation should revise the current definition of pandemic, not just to limit the spread of the virus, but to include the possible severity of the disease and a more appropriate response, in order to respond adequately and protect eu citizens from real risks. i believe that this requires better cooperation between the member states and the responsible institutions and organisations, and a more transparent allocation of responsibilities between the main actors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as the world health organisation should urgently revise the definition and include a definition of severity of disease in the definition of pandemic stages to ensure a more appropriate response. the response to pandemics requires better cooperation, a review of prevention plans, clarification and, where appropriate, a review of the roles and responsibilities of key actors, enhanced cooperation between eu member states to ensure consistent risk management in the response to pandemics in line with the international health regulations, and stronger coordination between member states and the european centre for disease prevention and control. a procedure should be introduced to allow member states to participate in group purchases on a voluntary basis. manufacturers are required to take full responsibility for the indications of their medicinal products and member states should apply this rule fully when procuring vaccines from the public. the plans for the prevention of future influenza pandemics in the eu and the member states need to be revised to be more effective, consistent and reasonably autonomous and to be adapted to the real risks in a flexible manner in each case within the shortest possible time, based on the latest available scientific data. i agree that for a vaccination strategy to work, three conditions must be met: the vaccine is effective, the benefits outweigh the risks, and it is given to people at risk.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is particularly difficult to predict the severity and course of a pandemic and because a large number of disproportionate decisions are often taken in the event of a pandemic, which requires a strong focus on cooperation, independence and transparency. in particular, the plans for the future prevention of influenza pandemics, both in the eu and in each country, need to be reviewed in a consistent manner in order to be flexible and adapted effectively to the threat of influenza pandemics on a case-by-case basis. in addition, cooperation and coordination of action at international and regional levels should be encouraged in order to ensure appropriate risk management and an operational response to the pandemic threat. i believe that more financial resources should be allocated to research and development, and to that end, we need to increase investment in predicting and assessing the impact of the influenza virus. it is essential to ensure that the procurement and allocation process for medicines and vaccines is transparent, thereby reducing corruption in this area. the influence of pharmaceutical companies must be limited not only in the prescribing but also in the testing of vaccines and antiviral drugs. scientific experts should publicly declare that they have no connection with the financial or other interests of the pharmaceutical industry.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the objectives of the common fisheries policy (cfp) are to ensure the sustainable and resilient use of living aquatic resources and to ensure a high level of protection of the ecosystem. the common fisheries policy for the mediterranean (cfp) was established by international agreement in 1949 and the european community is a member of the commission. the cfp has an important role to play in achieving the key objectives of fisheries policy, which are to promote the development, conservation and good management of living marine resources, to develop and present recommendations for conservation measures and to promote joint training projects. since the recommendations of the jha are binding on the contracting parties, of which the community is one, the provisions of the agreement should be transposed into community law, ensuring the consistency and compliance of this policy.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because the main tasks of the jrc (joint fisheries commission for the mediterranean) are to promote the development, conservation and sound management of living marine resources; to develop and make recommendations for conservation measures; and to promote joint training projects. the proposal for a regulation merely transposes into a single community act the recommendations adopted by the jha that are already applicable in the member states of the jha. this would greatly simplify the procedure, given that until now the european community has adopted regulations for the purpose of approximation of legislation only on an annual basis. the proposal sets out a number of rational solutions: the proposal for a regulation details the fishing gear (minimum mesh size for the mediterranean (article 15) and the black sea (article 16)) and prohibits fishing with trawls and seines at a depth of more than 1 000 metres (article 17), regulates aspects of vessels engaged in illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because fishing, especially in the mediterranean, is more than an economic activity, it is part of a culture and a way of life. all regions are created and extended in line with the fisheries. this requires special attention to be paid to fisheries in the region, since the mediterranean fisheries are more specific than elsewhere and require specific measures. in my view, it is appropriate to incorporate the recommendations adopted by the mediterranean common fisheries commission into a single community act, given that those recommendations are already applicable. it is also appropriate to lay down certain technical measures to establish fishing restrictions in the gulf of lion by strengthening the requirements for fishing gear, the process of issuing fishing authorisations. i am in favour of stricter regulation of vessels authorised to fish for large golden mackerel and a ban on fishing with trawls and seines at depths of more than 100 metres. it is also appropriate to regulate control measures more strictly, by providing for the possibility of inspecting third-country vessels both during unloading and loading and in cases where member states do not allow access to their ports. the proposal to cooperate actively and exchange information with the jrc is welcome.
in writing. − the global economic and financial crisis has exposed serious weaknesses in the regulatory and supervisory framework of the global financial system. it is now clear that new measures are needed to curb speculation and restore the financial sector to a leading role, ensuring fair and proportionate burden-sharing between the main financial players. it is essential to start talking about the taxation of the financial sector, which, unlike other sectors, is largely exempt from taxation and all the main financial activities are subject to the vat exemption system. i support the introduction of a financial transaction tax, which could help to address the growing and highly harmful trading patterns in financial markets, improve the efficiency of the market itself, reduce price volatility and provide incentives for the financial sector to undertake value-added investments.
in writing. − i supported this report because one of the main advantages of innovative financing instruments is their dual purpose, as they can contribute to important policy objectives such as financial stability and transparency and offer significant revenue potential, but should also take into account the impact of these instruments on the negative spill-over effects of the financial sector. i support the provision and the call for innovative financing instruments to generate more income from the sector and to contribute to reducing the tax burden on working people. this would provide opportunities to improve market efficiency, increase transparency and reduce speculation, offset excessive price volatility and create incentives for the financial sector to undertake long-term investments with added value to the real economy, as well as help finance universal public goods and reduce the government budget deficit. i also supported the idea of issuing common european project bonds to finance large european infrastructure needs and structural projects in the context of the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and other strategies such as the new strategy for the development of energy infrastructure, as well as other large-scale projects. in this way, eu project bonds would secure the necessary investments, attract the necessary support and become an important tool to increase the level of state support. these projects must also contribute to the environmentally sustainable transformation of our economy, preparing the ground for a zero-carbon economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on innovative finance at global and european level. europe, the world's largest financial market, is gradually recovering from a crisis whose effects will be felt for years to come. in this context, it is necessary to establish innovative financing instruments that ensure financial stability and transparency. at present, most financial services are not subject to vat, which means that the financial sector loses a lot of revenue, increasing the tax burden on working people. i believe that the financial transaction tax is an effective financing instrument that would contribute to reducing speculation and the public budget deficit. after having duly assessed its potential negative impact on the eu's global competitiveness, we must make every effort to ensure that it is applied at global level. in addition, in order to increase the gdp of each country, it is appropriate to impose a tax on bank assets that is proportionate to the systemic importance of the credit institution and the level of risk associated with its activities. i support the proposal for the issuing of joint european project bonds, which, as a common debt management tool, will help to attract more investment in european infrastructure projects. in addition, in order to maximise the benefits of the application of the carbon tax, it is necessary to set a threshold of minimum requirements for all member states, ensuring that the lowest income consumers are not the most burdened by the tax.
in writing. − in the european union, there are very large disparities in healthcare provision between countries and regions. the economic and financial crisis has led to austerity measures in some member states, which have led to a reduction in funding for public health, disease prevention and long-term care services in some member states. not all eu citizens have access to quality healthcare. this is particularly true in poorer regions of the eu where patients lack access to high quality healthcare and treatment services. there are also wide disparities in the treatment and reimbursement of individual complex diseases such as alzheimer's disease, which prevent patients in some member states from receiving the treatment and reimbursable medicines they need in their own country. i believe that the european commission must take measures to reduce the disparities and inequalities in the access of people in the eu to high quality healthcare and medicines and to establish mechanisms to monitor healthcare disparities. the commission should also present as soon as possible an initiative to encourage and support the development of integrated national or regional strategies by member states to reduce health disparities.
