in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, despite the progress made in healthcare, the gap in health achievement between those at the top and those at the bottom of the social ladder is still wide and in some places still widening. difficulties experienced early in life in accessing education, employment and healthcare, as well as gender and cultural differences, can affect people throughout their lives. the combination of poverty and other vulnerabilities such as childhood, old age or disability increases the risk to health and vice versa. poor health can mean poverty and/or social exclusion. the link between social factors and health disparities is increasingly recognised. this means that there is a growing recognition that social problems are linked to health problems and that an integrated response is therefore needed. the social consequences of the current economic and financial crisis have now become apparent. at the beginning of the crisis, almost 5 million people were unemployed. many families have lost their income, many are facing poverty, are deep in debt, and some have lost their homes. the crisis hit the short-term workers first. migrant workers and young or older workers, whose jobs are often precarious, have been particularly affected, but those who had relatively safe working conditions have also lost their jobs. addressing health inequalities requires an innovative approach to policy measures, especially for people from lower socioeconomic groups.
in writing. − developing countries face difficulties in setting up tax systems (establishment, collection and administration of taxes). one of the key challenges set out in the millennium development goals is to combat tax havens, which weaken the institutions and political systems of developing countries. tax havens and tax havens facilitate the illicit flow of $1 trillion a year in capital, about ten times the amount allocated to developing countries to reduce poverty and promote economic development. i support the proposals in the report that financial assistance should be provided by donors to support developing countries' efforts to improve tax management and ensure the transparent and responsible use of aid.
in writing. − i voted for this document because it highlights positive aspects such as a clear understanding of taxation, which is important in providing the basis for an accountable and responsible democratic system. another aspect is that the eu is committed to upholding the principle of developmental autonomy and recognises that developing countries have a primary responsibility to improve income systems in the light of economic and policy circumstances and opportunities. the commission is seeking to use eu instruments to provide increased support to developing countries in developing tax systems and implementing the principles of good tax governance, i.e. to focus more on ensuring that the principles of good tax governance are effectively integrated into the programming, implementation and monitoring of national and regional strategic plan documents. the commission supports the country-by-country financial reporting regime for multinational enterprises as a means of detecting tax fraud and tax evasion on an international scale. it is also important to emphasise that the csr communication will discuss how to develop a system for the mandatory publication of management-related information in the annual reporting documents. the commission aims to accelerate international dialogue and cooperation in the field of taxation, in particular by strengthening the participation of developing countries in important international fora. stresses the need to conclude and implement agreements on the exchange of information in tax matters, to use the multilateral mechanism and to refer to the example of the eu savings tax directive based on automatic exchange of information;
in writing. − given that developing countries currently lose a lot of revenue from trade taxes, it is therefore essential to ensure effective cooperation in both tax and development areas. it is essential for each member state to establish an effective and efficient tax system and the policies implementing it, as this is the basis for attracting public finance and investment. developing countries should therefore be left with a margin of discretion in this area. cooperation shall be based on mutual assistance without creating additional obstacles or burdens for either party. i agree with the proposal that we should help developing countries to achieve both quantitative and qualitative improvements in income. support to developing countries should be targeted and effective and should be limited to its essential need, rather than being left to the parties to decide on its necessity. i do not think it is appropriate to impose an additional burden on the eu to compensate developing countries for the reduced revenue from customs duties. in my view, a financial transaction tax should be introduced to limit speculation and make the market work more efficiently. in addition, every effort should be made to extend the application of this tax not only to the eu but also to the world.
in writing. − the european union's agricultural sector creates significant added value for the european economy and plays a strategic role in meeting economic, social and environmental challenges. therefore, external trade policies and agreements with foreign importers must not undermine the eu's ability to maintain a strong and viable sector. the commission must take a clear position in the world trade organisation and carry out specific impact assessments when negotiating with other parties on the import of certain products into the eu market. the principle that the production methods used in third countries for products exported to the eu should ensure the same minimum standards of health, food safety, animal welfare, sustainable development and social standards for eu consumers as those applied to eu producers should be respected. this is the only way to ensure that eu producers can compete on equal terms with third countries and to protect the interests of eu farmers.
in writing. − i voted for this document because as the eu considers the future of its common agricultural policy (cap), it is becoming increasingly important to ensure the coherence of agricultural and foreign trade policies. the cap and the eu's external trade policy must be coordinated to ensure that the european agricultural model is preserved and that eu producers are treated equally on the world market. our priority must be food safety, security and quality at affordable prices for eu citizens. the world is facing increasing demand for food in the face of higher production costs, high volatility in agricultural markets, and declining arable land, water and energy resources. a strong cap is crucial to preserve environmental sustainability and economic development in the eu's rural areas, where land is threatened by abandonment and rural depopulation. the european agricultural sector creates clear added value for the european economy and plays a strategic role in the europe 2020 strategy, which is designed to address the economic, social and environmental challenges facing the eu internationally and as a major global player. the eu's trade policy will play a crucial role in determining whether agriculture continues to make a full and positive contribution to these objectives. trade policy should not hold back the eu's agricultural sector. on the contrary, trade policy and agricultural policy can and must be reconciled.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on eu agriculture and international trade. the eu is one of the world's largest importers of agricultural products, but its share of the global export market is declining due to the growth of its main agricultural trading partners and the low world market prices and high production costs in the eu. as the eu imports the majority of agricultural products from developing countries worldwide, it is necessary to ensure that the interests of eu farmers are properly safeguarded by providing for a mechanism to compensate for the losses suffered as a result. eu farmers need to be protected from unfair competition, which means that products exported from third countries must be subject to the same standards as those applied in the eu agricultural sector. these conditions must be included in bilateral trade agreements. in addition, eu products must be granted full aid for access to third country markets. i believe that the commission's proposal to grant pakistan a three-year tariff quota at zero duty for exports of 100 000 ethanol per year to the eu will prevent direct and immediate aid and a negative impact on the eu renewable energy industry. given that ukraine's cereals production is highly competitive and subject to lower tariffs, the commission must be more cautious in applying concessions in its negotiations with ukraine.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report. over the last decade, the union's protein crop production and our market have become largely dependent on imports. this situation was the result of previous eu international trade agreements, under which the eu protected its cereal production in exchange for duty-free imports of oilseeds and protein crops into the eu. this has enabled the necessary production to be imported at low cost and has preserved the competitiveness of the agricultural sector, especially the livestock sector. however, within the eu itself, there has been a marked decline in interest from farmers and business in the processing sector. research has been reduced, research on resistant and productive plant varieties has been discontinued, and practical experience in protein crops has been lost across europe. the current situation in volatile price markets and the high price of protein feed may have a negative impact on the eu livestock sector, which is heavily dependent on imports. the commission should consider measures to promote the cultivation and production of protein crops in the eu, as well as support for farmers growing such crops, as a matter of urgency and this support should be reflected in the reform of the common agricultural policy. this would provide an opportunity to revitalise the sector, provide income for farmers and contribute to more sustainable farming in the eu.
in writing. − i voted for this document because the cap reform must include appropriate and credible new instruments and mechanisms to help farmers improve crop rotation systems, thus significantly reducing the current protein deficit and price volatility. the eu's protein deficit is rising steadily, and the eu grows 30% of its protein crops for feed. proteins account for only 3% of all arable land in the eu, which means that the eu has to import 70% of these forage crops. the wider use of protein crops for sowing could have significant agricultural and environmental benefits and mitigate climate change. in terms of climate change, leguminous species can contribute significantly to the reduction of greenhouse gases by absorbing and fixing nitrogen in the soil, thereby helping to reduce nitrogen fertilisers. the use of more protein crops in planting improves soil fertility and structure and nutrient reserves, and subsequently crops grown grow healthier. mixtures of perennial grasses and herbs and mixtures of cereals and protein crops for fodder provide better soil cover and thus help to reduce nutrient leakage to groundwater and rivers, and also provide better conditions for bees and other pollinating insects. the use of extensive planting reduces the need for plant protection and can help to preserve the diversity of species and varieties, both wild and cultivated.
in writing. − protein deficiency is a current and important problem in the eu. given the deep-rooted nature of the problem in the eu and the growing protein shortages, every effort should be made to address this problem as soon as possible and to increase the production of local protein crops. i think this resolution is an important step towards solving the problem. the production of protein crops not only mitigates the effects of climate change, but also has a positive impact on farmers' incomes. it is also an important factor in strengthening the eu livestock sector, with a view to reducing its dependence on protein crops imports and increasing its competitiveness. i believe that the commission must take immediate action to prevent at least a minimum amount of gmos from entering the eu market. we cannot allow the import into the eu of at least minimal quantities of gmo impurities with food and feed protein plants. i support the proposals to support eu research on the selection and supply of protein crops and to use improved decentralised feed production infrastructure under the rural development measures scheme. i believe that financial support measures for farmers in the eu should actively promote crop rotation, which would reduce the current protein deficit and price volatility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and i am pleased that the european parliament has paid particular attention to gender equality issues. we must recognise that there is still a lot of work to be done to improve the situation of women in terms of gender equality, in the labour market, in politics. women's rights issues must be integrated into all european union policies and initiatives must not remain on paper, but must be implemented in all member states of the european union. in the european parliament's report on equality between women and men in the european union, we therefore identified the need to close the gender pay gap, to stop violence against women and trafficking in women, to ensure maternity leave and to provide adequate access to day-care and childcare facilities, and to reduce poverty among women. as regards gender equality in business, it is worth noting that only 3% of company directors are women, as they face discrimination and barriers to advancing their careers and reaching leadership. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of quotas for the promotion of gender equality in the workplace. i hope that in the future we will find solutions and instruments that will consolidate gender equality and equal opportunities for women in the family and in society.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the financial, economic and social crisis we are currently experiencing has serious implications for unemployment, the living conditions of our people and society in general. women have been particularly affected by this crisis, in terms of their working conditions, their access to employment, their place in society in general and their equality with men in particular. women must be able to hold positions that are commensurate with their qualifications, whether on the boards of large listed companies or in the political sphere. indeed, women do not always have the opportunity to take up leadership positions, and this creates a gap between their education and their status. as 2010 is the european year against poverty, special attention should be paid to women who are more vulnerable. where they are vulnerable because of disability or their migrant status, specific measures should be taken to avoid their vulnerability and to facilitate their social inclusion. equality is also promoted in the fight against violence against women. it should be noted that any physical, psychological or sexual violence, no matter how severe, must be combated and condemned. on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of international women's day, i would like to congratulate all women on this occasion.
in writing. - i supported this report. poverty remains a major problem in the eu and the fight against poverty is one of the five evaluated objectives of the europe 2020 strategy proposed by the commission. the integrated guidelines of the europe 2020 strategy (promotion of social inclusion and combating poverty) aim to protect people at risk of poverty, in particular women and single-parent families, and older people who are at higher risk of poverty than the rest of the population. social protection and employment policies play a very important role in reducing people's poverty. member states, in conjunction with the commission, should agree on more effective measures to guarantee the rights of the most vulnerable groups in society to adequate education and to provide vocational training and university study opportunities that will allow them to better integrate into the active labour market and prevent the risk of poverty.
in writing. − i voted for this report because we need to overcome the exacerbation of poverty among women in the difficult years. although the economic and financial crisis has had a significant impact on unemployment rates for both sexes, women have been the most affected by the crisis. during the difficult year, wages in female-dominated sectors fell sharply or women lost their jobs altogether. in addition, lower wages mean that older women receive lower pensions and are therefore more likely to be poor. the high prevalence of maternal poverty, especially among single mothers, during the crisis has a direct impact on child poverty, with some 20 million children already living in poverty in europe. without concrete measures to reduce poverty among women, it will not be possible to reduce child poverty. i would like to emphasise that both european and national legislation must take gender into account. the member states of the european union should develop specific programmes for the integration and reintegration of women into the labour market. in addition, all mothers must be guaranteed maternity leave. sadly, motherhood is now totally undervalued, as is the work of caring for young children, the elderly, or the disabled. i hope that in the future member states will take appropriate measures to overcome women's poverty and to recognise the contribution of mothers to the development of the family, society and the economy.
in writing. − i voted for this report because we need to overcome the poverty of women, which has been exacerbated by the financial and economic crisis. almost 17% of european women are classified as poor; in terms of labour market and social protection indicators, women are disproportionately affected by the structural causes of poverty. during the difficult year, wages in female-dominated sectors fell sharply or women lost their jobs altogether. in addition, lower wages mean that older women receive lower pensions and are therefore more likely to be poor. the high prevalence of maternal poverty, especially among single mothers, during the crisis has a direct impact on child poverty, with some 20 million children already living in poverty in europe. as women's contribution to family, social and economic development is consistently undervalued and underrewarded, measures to reduce women's poverty are necessary and urgent.

in writing. the events of the past year regarding the displacement of roma from one country to another and the discrimination and exclusion of this ethnic group from society have prompted the european union to take concrete action. one such action is the european union roma inclusion strategy, initiated by the european parliament. the inclusion of this ethnic group is not only a human rights obligation but also an economic necessity, not only a moral obligation but also an important financial interest of all member states. furthermore, given the extent of the segregation, the overall inclusion of roma is a fundamental human rights issue. i would like to emphasise that the adoption by the european parliament of a europe-wide strategy on roma inclusion shows that the european union is not leaving the member states alone to solve the problems of roma integration. as recent events have shown, these problems can no longer be solved at national level alone and therefore require close cooperation between the european union and the member states. it is also essential that the european commission and the member states mobilise existing eu strategies and instruments and must coordinate and find a common dialogue to ensure the social and economic inclusion of roma. only when a common european approach to roma integration issues is found will the strategy be actively implemented. in addition, the roma community should be involved as much as possible in the process of developing eu roma policy.
in writing. the roma community in the european union, despite being the largest ethnic minority group, still suffers from discrimination and segregation. i agree with many of my colleagues who have said that it is very important to develop a roma inclusion strategy at european level. in each country, we have excellent examples of how to reduce roma segregation in a variety of areas: education, culture, employment, healthcare or even roma participation in political and civic life. however, the visibility of such initiatives is insufficient. the european union would therefore, in my view, be an appropriate platform to improve cooperation between member states, to collect and disseminate good practice and experience or to provide funding. while the eu level is very important, i believe that the most effective results can be achieved at local or regional level. only in specific areas or towns will we have the best understanding of the local problems, needs and social environment, so that the projects we implement are closer to those for whom they are intended.
member of the commission. − people have often said that societies should be judged by the way they treat their weakest members. clearly, if we fail to provide adequate support for persons in need, we are likely to exclude them even further, and so make it harder to integrate them into society and bring them onto the labour market. the commission believes that, in addition to acting as automatic stabilisers, minimum income schemes can play an important role in protecting the most vulnerable from the worst effects of the crisis by providing safety nets. the commission recommendation on the active inclusion of people excluded from the labour market and the epsco council conclusions of 17 december 2008 on common active inclusion principles to combat poverty more effectively both highlight the importance of access to adequate resources, alongside quality services and inclusive labour markets. the recommendation calls on the member states in particular to ‘recognise the individual’s basic right to resources and social assistance sufficient to lead a life that is compatible with human dignity as part of a comprehensive, consistent drive to combat social exclusion’. the approach outlined in the recommendation has proved to be a step in the right direction, especially during the economic crisis. but more needs to be done to fully implement active inclusion reforms. as the commission announced in its communication on the european platform against poverty and social exclusion, it will report in 2012 on the implementation of the common principles on active inclusion, focusing inter alia on the effectiveness of minimum income schemes. it will propose action based on that assessment, including ways in which eu financial instruments could support active inclusion.

in writing. - the european union needs turkey and vice versa. it is not just trade, economic relations and investment that are important. turkey, which turned its back on europe almost 100 years ago, can and must become the bridge that connects our continent with the muslim world. unfortunately, it has to be admitted that the negotiations on turkey's accession to the eu have slowed down. the eu expects progress, in particular in the areas of human rights, gender equality, freedom of expression, freedom of the press and freedom of religion. another important issue is the normalisation of relations with cyprus. this conflict must be resolved in favour of both turkey and cyprus. it is important to seek a peaceful solution to the conflict. the events in north africa demonstrate the important contribution turkey makes to promoting the values of stability and democracy. people in libya, egypt and other arab countries look to turkey and the eu as an example to follow. i voted for the report because it is well balanced. it reflects well the state of eu-turkey integration in 2010. i have always supported turkey's membership. but it would have to implement the ankara protocol, do more, especially in the areas of minorities, women, press freedoms, rule of law.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the european council has repeatedly reaffirmed that the future of the western balkans is linked to the european union and that growth and stability in the region are of paramount importance. progress in montenegro in various fields shows that the country is serious about preparing for european integration. the montenegrin government and the opposition parties have a common understanding of european integration and give priority to this issue. the report also shows that the preparatory measure for membership (pem) support is being well implemented in montenegro, with significant judicial and administrative reforms. montenegro is a successful regional cooperation and constructive regional partner and plays a stabilising role in the western balkans.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the montenegrin government and the opposition parties share a common commitment to european integration and give priority to this issue, which has led to significant progress in reform since the country's declaration of independence. i welcome the fact that montenegro has been granted the status of a candidate country for eu accession, as well as the possibility for montenegrin citizens to travel without visas (full visa liberalisation) to the eu schengen area. i am pleased that the process of developing the country's legal and constitutional framework is almost complete, that significant progress has been made in the adoption of important legislation in the fight against corruption, and that progress has been made in the reform of the judicial system. however, further reforms in the public administration sector, strengthening the human resources of local level administration, combating organised crime, and in particular money laundering and smuggling, and avoiding political interference in the media sector are still necessary to guarantee the independence of regulatory authorities.
in writing. − eu integration is a key driver of progress for montenegro. in the last 12 months, the country has achieved a lot: it has successfully implemented structural and economic reforms, effectively fought corruption, organised crime. montenegro is a country where ethnic minorities live together well and where good neighbourly relations are successfully promoted. the eu and montenegro therefore signed a stability and association agreement. i voted in favour of this resolution because it correctly indicates the next steps in the reform of montenegro. progress in the establishment of the rule of law, further administrative reforms, capacity building of civil servants, amendment of the electoral law, strengthening of civil society and independent media. it is important that the country maintains the momentum it has gained and continues the work it has started.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the eu roma inclusion strategy. roma are the largest ethnic minority in europe, but they are also the most isolated and therefore almost completely excluded from the economic life of the country. i agree with the rapporteur that roma integration is a necessary investment, because it is cheaper to integrate roma than to maintain the poor standard of living and economic conditions in which they live. the other important aspect that i would like to emphasise is that the overall inclusion of roma is fundamentally a human rights issue. the large number of roma in europe living in substandard conditions almost completely cut off from economic life and therefore unable to enjoy basic human rights, means that promoting their social inclusion cannot be seen as a mere matter of general policy adjustment, but must be addressed in order to close one of the biggest constitutional and human rights gaps in europe. the european parliament, by adopting this strategy, took the first step towards promoting the social and economic inclusion of the roma, and it is now up to the council and the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that this strategy is successfully implemented.
in writing. - the situation of roma in the eu is quite complex. a large proportion of europe's roma, estimated at between 10 and 12 million, suffer from persistent discrimination and experience high levels of social, cultural and economic exclusion, human rights violations. furthermore, the majority of roma communities live in regions that are among the least developed economically and socially in the union, which often leaves roma children without access to education and training systems that in the future discriminate against them in the labour market and prevent them from integrating into society. the european union has developed a number of useful instruments, mechanisms and funds to promote roma inclusion, but they are applied in a wide range of policy areas, which limits their impact and benefits. i agree that member states need to better implement the eu roma inclusion strategy and ensure full transposition and application of all relevant directives and other eu legislation, preventing segregation and discrimination against roma.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the roma in europe need the support of the european union (eu). the eu roma inclusion strategy proposes to establish mandatory minimum standards for education, employment, housing and healthcare. however, a large proportion of europe's roma live in substandard conditions and are almost completely excluded from economic life, thus deprived of basic human rights. in the proposed strategy, the european parliament thus gives priority to improving the employment, education, housing and social protection of roma. it is important to ensure that segregation of roma children in schools and classrooms is eliminated. it is also essential to promote the involvement of roma in all areas of public and political life, as well as to encourage their participation in the activities of non-governmental organisations. in order to implement the roma inclusion strategy, it is necessary to ensure that it is, in particular, an internal strategy of the european union and that the implementation of the priority areas and objectives is monitored by commission structures which provide an annual progress report on the implementation of the strategy and an evaluation of the results.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document, although i think that it should have been rejected. there is no need at this stage to strengthen the strategies targeted at one group only, but an effective and urgent strategy to tackle legal and illegal migration is needed, with a view to ensuring, in particular, economic stability, employment, security, public order and justice for all european citizens who are part of a member state in demographic, cultural, traditional, historical and economic terms.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is urgently necessary to remedy the situation where the majority of the 10 to 12 million roma living in europe continue to suffer discrimination, economic and social exclusion, even in the 21st century. the path to integration is a long and complex process, which is adapted to the conditions of individual countries and local regions. the european union strategy should provide clear objectives, funding methods for programmes. however, the national governments and municipalities, which are best placed to know the situation in the region, have the greatest responsibility. education, healthcare, housing policy and faster integration of roma into the labour market are key to solving the long-standing problem. failure to integrate roma eu citizens properly into the societies of the eu member states would send a bad signal to eu integration policy in general.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on industrial policy for the globalisation era. the global economic crisis has affected european industry and to overcome the effects of the crisis and address these challenges, the eu needs an industrial policy approach that combines competitiveness, sustainability and decent work, while boosting the economy, increasing employment, reducing environmental degradation and improving quality of life. i therefore supported the call in the resolution for the commission and the member states to develop an ambitious, environmentally friendly and green eu industrial strategy to restore production capacity throughout the eu and to create high-skilled and well-paid jobs in the eu. the european parliament stresses the importance of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) for industry, in particular in securing long-term jobs in the regions, as well as in maintaining economic and creative vitality and rapid economic growth. it is therefore necessary to ensure better access to finance for smes and, in particular, to develop effective alternatives to risk capital by creating a new financial market structure to strengthen the short- and long-term financing opportunities and the most acceptable sources of finance for smes; to open markets, to create the necessary conditions for fair competition and thus to allow more entrepreneurs and small enterprises to expand their activities and become companies operating across europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european union is the largest market in the world, but we are not exploiting its enormous potential. we have a very open market, but we face significant barriers to entry in foreign markets. the unfinished single market, in areas such as energy, forces us to submit to external conditions that directly affect our competitiveness. the viability of industry depends directly on the viability of our small and medium-sized sector, which, despite the measures adopted, is experiencing some very difficult times. i agree that innovation is at the heart of today's industry, but even in this area we cannot boast of our ability to respond in a timely manner to changing global market conditions. i believe that today we have a well-balanced and comprehensive vision of industry, and now the member states and the european commission will have to do their part to ensure that our ambitious ambitions allow us to create a modern and competitive industry.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because eu industry accounts for almost a third of the eu's gross value added, almost three quarters of european exports are industrial goods and almost a third of the workforce, or almost 57 million people, live off this. the recent economic crisis has had a severe impact on european industry. however, the crisis has highlighted the importance of industry to the eu economy and has shown that insufficient measures have been taken to fully address its needs in the current difficult situation. manufacturing industry growth is at its lowest level in two decades, and some european industries are experiencing a 'permanent crisis' due to unfair competition from third countries in the areas of labour relations, the environment and intellectual property protection. with the us, japan and china pursuing effective and active industrial policies that support modern products and services, european industry is at risk of falling behind. an integrated and sustainable eu industrial policy should be based on the following key aspects: the need to develop an innovation chain linking research and practical application, to use resources more efficiently and to increase the production of clean energy. the eu must be encouraged to adopt strategies for long-term change and to pursue education policies that respond to labour market needs. it is necessary to combat the distortive effects of the shadow economy and the spread of informal activities during the crisis, and it is also proposed to facilitate the participation of smes in public procurement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because eu industry has been hit hard by the current economic crisis. in the modern world, industrial competition is very high and industrial sectors need to remain competitive and innovative, based on innovative ideas and on quality and technical excellence. we need to strengthen the material base, introduce high-level technologies, and enable their easy transfer between companies. we must make every effort to exploit the resources (minerals) available within the european union, avoiding their export outside the eu and preventing the formation of oligopolistic structures in the trade sector. european support should not be used for starvation but for investments in the future, aimed at creating new jobs so that every citizen has a job in his or her own country. particular attention shall be paid to those regions identified as problematic, with a low level of industrial development and a high level of unemployment. in this context, the establishment of technology, industrial and scientific parks and business centres should be encouraged. these organisations are particularly important in actively developing and developing modern technologies, ensuring economic development and modernisation, while creating new jobs. small and medium-sized enterprises should be encouraged to invest in clusters. they must be given a favourable business environment and a reduced administrative burden. the entrenched bureaucracy hinders the development of industry and the competitiveness of the products produced.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i am pleased we also have the chance this afternoon to debate the work of the un human rights council and, in a sense, to look at how we can strengthen its overall impact. as honourable members may know, i addressed the council last week together with many foreign ministers from across the world. for obvious reasons on that occasion, the situation in libya was at the heart of our discussions. i am pleased that the international community sent a strong and united political signal regarding the ongoing human rights violations in libya. already before the high-level segment, the council had called for an inquiry and recommended the suspension of libya’s membership of the council – which, as you know, has since been confirmed by the general assembly in a unanimous decision. all that is proof that multilateral institutions can live up to their mandate and can act in what we call real time. as i stressed in my remarks there, the un human rights council has a responsibility to ensure that stated intentions are translated into real action and real progress. i think that ms pillay, the un high commissioner for human rights, whom i met in geneva, is giving exactly the right direction politically in order to make a difference on the ground. what matters in the end is not the number of resolutions that are passed, but results in the real world that make a difference to people who are in need. i also emphasised that human rights are universal. i pointed out that we in europe reject the accusation that somehow the eu is trying to ‘export’ so-called european values to other countries. the rights to free speech, freedom of assembly, justice and equality are not european rights: they are universal rights. we must never fall into the trap of believing that people in other parts of the world – whether it is africa, asia or latin america – should be any less passionate about their rights. that is why we speak out and we act against human rights violations wherever they occur. we also recognise that europe’s own path on human rights protection has not been a straight line and that constant efforts are also needed inside europe. at the human rights council we are ready to discuss our own challenges, share experiences and offer support to those working to improve respect for human rights around the world. we have several priorities for the 16th session of the human rights council and we have discussed these actively with our partners. the eu will present an initiative on freedom of religion or belief. faced in recent months with an increasing number of acts of religious discrimination and violence in different parts of the world, we need to send a strong, collective message against religious intolerance and in favour of the freedom of religion or belief for all people everywhere. we will also table resolutions on burma/myanmar and the democratic people’s republic of korea. we believe that in both cases the severity and number of human rights violations justify the extension of the mandates of the respective un special rapporteurs. the eu also supports the initiative to create a special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in iran, as proposed by several countries and regions. we are seriously concerned about the deteriorating human rights situation in iran. this was highlighted by the un high commissioner for human rights, ms navi pillay. a particular concern is the dramatically increasing number of death penalty cases – more than 100 so far this year, as we discussed in our previous debate – and the repression of those exercising their rights to freedom of expression and assembly.we feel the council should address the situation in egypt in an appropriate manner, taking into account the rapidly evolving situation in that country. the eu welcomes egypt’s invitation to ms pillay to send members of her office to the country. we hope this mission will be dispatched without delay. the eu also is engaging with the tunisian authorities to jointly present a draft resolution on the subject of boosting un technical assistance on human rights in the context of ongoing transition. other key situations that need to be addressed by this session of the human rights council are belarus, where we are deeply concerned at the number of political prisoners, the democratic republic of congo – where there are distressing reports of continuing human rights violations, in particular widespread sexual violence – as well as côte d'ivoire. let me conclude by stressing once again the importance of the human rights council for the eu: the debates, the resolutions and the rapporteurs. but in the end, these are only inputs. what truly matter are the outputs. the real test is whether we make a difference on the ground. for that reason, the eu will work hard to strengthen the human rights council and especially its ability to address urgent situations. this is a key objective of the ongoing review process. we will continue to push for an ambitious result.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i would like to take this opportunity to express my full support for the decision taken by the un general assembly on 1 march to suspend libya’s membership of the united nations human rights council. i think this sends a strong signal, not only to colonel gaddafi and his regime but also to those countries in the world where human rights violations are frequent and widespread. in my report on the un human rights council and the eu’s role in it – adopted by this house in february 2009 – i strongly advocated the introduction of membership criteria for this important un body. in the case of libya, the united nations general assembly acted in line with the european parliament resolution and took a correct and timely decision. speaking of the 16th session, i would like to draw special attention to the council’s review process. it is important that the eu member states and the european external action service actively engage in the 2011 review of the council to strengthen compliance with its mandate. the unhrc should become more an early-warning and preventive mechanism. there is also a need for a transparent and all-inclusive review process, including ngos, civil society and all relevant stakeholders. last but not least, i would like to welcome the establishment of the directorate for human rights and democracy in the eeas system. the establishment of the external action service also provides us with a unique opportunity to streamline our action on the protection of human rights in the united nations human rights council. i therefore want to encourage the high representative to make sure that european efforts in the human rights council are well coordinated and that eu member states belonging to this body are united and effective as never before.
in fact, in the context of an economic crisis, countries have financial problems in meeting their commitments and, of course, have different possibilities to overcome these consequences, and it is necessary to look for ways to balance the budget, to reduce the budget deficit. but, commissioner, is it really necessary to do this at the expense of the most deprived? is it morally right for the european commission to pressure national governments to reduce minimum wages, pensions or other social benefits? commissioner, you have expressed your views on the irish memorandum. but i want to remind you that you signed a similar memorandum with latvia, where you pressured the latvian government to reduce already low pensions. pensions in latvia were reduced, but the constitutional court of that country said that the country's basic law did not allow it, and those pensions were restored. so when you make these decisions, when you sign these memoranda, you have to be very careful about the legal and social implications.
for the efd group the fact that we are talking today again about the volcanic ash crisis shows that this topic is still relevant and that there are still unanswered questions. we understand that volcanoes are not subject to any rules and we cannot rule out the possibility of unforeseen circumstances. all of this is part of the life of the aviation industry, but aviation is not only disrupted by volcanoes but also by storms, snow and similar phenomena. of course, it is not possible to eliminate, block or foresee everything that can happen in the field of aviation. of course, the safety of aircraft, the lives of people and their mobility must be one of our top priorities. i am pleased that a large-scale programme is under way to modernise air traffic management in the context of the single sky. i agree with what my colleague said just now, that we need to work together to build a common infrastructure. but i would say that, in terms of this problem, we should be thinking and talking about the development of alternative transport today. further progress is needed and necessary in this area. the crisis particularly affected the eastern european union, which remained isolated from the western european part and, unlike the other european union countries, did not have sufficient alternative transport options. we now know that we urgently need to develop alternative secondary mobility systems, trans-european networks, rail networks, an alternative to air transport, as has been done wisely with electricity and telecommunications networks. the revision of the trans-european networks should therefore be subject to higher targets in the light of the financial perspective. land transport, and in particular rail, should be able to replace air transport more smoothly when it is interrupted. it is time to consider concrete alternatives and to implement them as soon as possible.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution as the hungarian media law should be suspended and reviewed accordingly in the light of the comments and proposals of the european commission, the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce) and the council of europe, in order to ensure that it is fully in line with european union (eu) law and european values and standards of media freedom, pluralism and independent media governance. the european parliament also recalls that all member states of the european union must respect the copenhagen criteria for eu membership, adopted at the 1993 copenhagen european council, on freedom of the press and freedom of expression, and apply them in accordance with the relevant provisions of eu law. the european parliament therefore calls on the hungarian authorities to restore the independence of the media authorities and to stop the state interference in freedom of expression and the balanced provision of information. it also considers that excessive regulation of the media is detrimental to the presence of effective pluralism in the public sphere. parliament also called on the commission to present a proposal for an eu law on media freedom, pluralism and independent governance by the end of the year, with a view to establishing minimum mandatory standards to ensure, protect and promote an appropriate level of media pluralism and independent governance in the eu member states.

on behalf of the s&d group this resolution is a clear signal to the belarusian authorities that the european union has not tolerated and will not tolerate restrictions on freedom of demonstration, political prisoners in the country and even more so torture in detention facilities. brussels is increasing its support for civil society, non-governmental organisations, independent media and students in belarus. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the visa regime is simplified and that the visa requirements are met. i think it would be very useful in this situation for a delegation of the european parliament to go to belarus, despite the obstacles to this, and if the whole delegation cannot go, then the members of the european parliament must go there individually to get to know the situation better and to influence it.
in writing. − today we voted in favour of amending article 136 of the lisbon treaty, which will allow the eu to establish a stability mechanism applicable only to euro area members. the european stability mechanism will aim to strengthen the budgetary discipline of the euro area member states, the coordination of their economic and financial policies and a common european response to challenges such as growth, the reduction of economic and social disparities and the improvement of competitiveness. i believe that this mechanism will help to ensure greater financial stability in the euro area and will accelerate the economic recovery of the euro area member states. however, the non-euro area countries that have been hit hardest by the crisis will be left behind and prevented from recovering their economies more quickly and sustainably. i believe that the eu must show more solidarity and provide full support to member states so that they can join the club of eurozone countries and become full eu member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the amendment to the treaty of lisbon which has been adopted will allow the creation of a permanent euro stability mechanism. the current situation shows that we are in a difficult economic and financial situation and that very concrete measures of economic coordination and surveillance must be taken. however, this mechanism and the guarantee fund are only available to euro area members, leaving non-euro area countries out of the loop, which in turn contributes to the eu's fragmentation. i believe that the eu should show more solidarity by helping not only the euro area member states but also the non-euro area member states to become full and equal eu member states as soon as possible, thus removing the temporary discrepancy in the eu treaty between the accession of member states and contributing to the creation of a more cohesive eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is important for the whole of the european union as it recovers from the severe financial crisis. in this context, it is essential to establish a mechanism to stabilise the euro area and ensure its efficient and effective functioning and development. the european stability mechanism is a permanent aid fund to help euro area countries affected by the crisis. however, the effective functioning of this mechanism requires its full integration into the institutional framework of the union. in particular, it is necessary to ensure that it is open from the outset to all member states, including those whose currency is not the euro. i think it is appropriate to provide for financial instruments which would allow the purchase of bonds from those member states which are facing particularly serious debt problems. this would open the way for them to access financial markets, thereby facilitating a faster economic recovery. i support the proposal to involve other eu institutions in the governance process of the mechanism, giving the commission more powers to effectively implement the union's enlarged functions in this area.
today we voted in favour of an amendment to the lisbon treaty which will allow the creation of a permanent euro stability mechanism. we have shown solidarity by agreeing to the amendment of the treaty and by understanding that we are in a difficult economic and financial situation and that we need to take very concrete measures of economic coordination and surveillance. this mechanism and the guarantee fund, which are only available to euro-area members, although non-euro-area countries are excluded, essentially threaten to fragment the european union and to abandon community methods. the european union must therefore also show greater solidarity by helping non-euro area members to join the club as soon as possible and to regain full decision-making rights in the european union, thus removing the temporary discrepancy in the treaty on european union that has arisen as a result of the accession of the member states.
the japanese nation has suffered the unimaginable effects of natural disasters and nuclear accidents. the people of lithuania are actively gathering support and are trying to help the victims of this country in every possible way. the chernobyl nuclear disaster has left a deep impression on our minds, and it will continue to do so for a long time. three decades later, the region is still reeling from the effects. the japanese disaster is forcing a fundamental rethink on nuclear safety. we cannot control natural disasters, so we must at least ensure that natural disasters do not trigger additional, but extremely painful, nuclear disasters. i am in favour of reviewing existing infrastructure and building new capacity, but we must also analyse in detail the events at the japanese nuclear power plant, especially since there is a precedent for chernobyl. we must draw conclusions and adopt measures which will make it possible to substantially increase nuclear safety throughout europe.
in writing. first of all, i would like to express my condolences to the people of japan for the earthquake and tsunami that devastated the country and claimed many lives. in the light of the tragic disaster at the fukushima nuclear power plant following the earthquake and tsunami, i would urge europe to consider the future of nuclear energy and to look for alternatives to energy production. in addition, we must rely on the information and knowledge of specialists and experts and look at new ways of generating electricity from a scientific perspective when assessing the consequences of the disaster. the events in japan should be of concern to all member states, whether or not they have nuclear power stations, because if similar disasters occur, radiation would threaten the whole of europe. at present, eastern european countries, especially the baltic states, are very concerned about the plans of russia and belarus to build nuclear power plants. the radiation effects of these planned nuclear power plants and the adherence of neighbouring countries to international safety standards are of even greater concern. i would like to point out that germany closed down all its reactors built before 1980 immediately after the japanese tragedy. the eu energy commissioner also argues that europe should strive for a future without nuclear power plants. the european parliament should therefore consider the risks of nuclear power stations on the external borders of the european union, after having assessed the potential radiation threat to europe.
in writing. – we should not only focus on nuclear safety within the eu, but also look at its immediate neighbourhood. two new projects for nuclear power plants with experimental reactors are being developed on the edges of the eu: one in kaliningrad and another located in belarus, 23 km from the eu’s external border and 50 km from lithuania’s capital city. both sites were selected on unknown criteria. the lack of transparency in the process, flawed consultations and failure to share information with the affected countries make both projects a cause for serious concern. work has already started, although the international environmental impact assessments of both plants are far from complete. moreover, immediately after the tragedy in japan, russia and belarus signed an agreement giving a green light to build the plant in belarus. data from the chernobyl and fukushima tragedies show that the area of immediate radioactive impact is 50-55 km. in the event of an accident, the capital of an eu member state would be immediately affected. the eu should demand that these third countries take their responsibilities seriously and carefully observe international obligations and standards for nuclear energy. i hope the upcoming european council will agree to take the appropriate decisions.
for the efd group the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, extended the conditions under which parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of an international agreement. at present, aviation agreements fall into this category as they fall within the scope of the ordinary legislative procedure. i believe that the implementation of these agreements would bring significant economic benefits and create jobs. moreover, greater harmonisation would promote fair competition. while the stage two agreement is an important step forward, it is important that it is not seen as the end of the process of creating a transatlantic aviation market. as far as canada is concerned, it is good that all european union companies will be able to operate direct flights to canada from any european country. the agreement removes all restrictions on routes, prices or the number of flights per week between canada and the eu. the broad ambition of this agreement should be particularly appreciated. it can be seen as a model for other negotiations currently under way. i therefore believe that parliament should give its consent to the eu-canada air transport agreement. the same applies to the air transport agreement between the european union and the government of the socialist republic of vietnam. all these air transport agreements are useful and necessary for the european union, our airlines and our citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this communication, which increases the tariff quotas for wine grapes for moldova. moldova is experiencing difficulties in wine exports, which threaten its economic recovery and agriculture, especially medium-sized and family farms. the agricultural sector accounts for about 40 percent of moldova's economy. the wine sector alone employs some 300 000 people, most of whom live in rural areas. moldova has so far fully used its quota and the increase in the duty-free tariff quotas will allow moldova to increase its sales of its production to the eu without harming the eu wine industry.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this document as it proposes to increase the tariff quota for wine beet from 100 000 hectolitres (hl) to 150 000 hl in 2011 from 120 000 hl to 180 000 hl in 2012 and from 2013 to 240 000 hl per year. such an increase is proposed on the basis of the systematic use of the existing quota by moldova to date and the potential of the moldovan wine sector to improve its niche markets in the european union, and such an increase will not destabilise the eu wine industry. the wine sector in moldova is expected to continue to improve the quality of wine. in view of the expiry of council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 on 31 december 2012 and the importance of ensuring legal certainty for producers, exporters and importers, it is proposed to extend the validity of council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 for a further three years, until 31 december 2015.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which proposes to increase the autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova in the wine sector, which is vital for this country. it should be noted that this would be an even greater incentive to strengthen the mutual relations between the european union and moldova, to develop the eu's good neighbour policy. given that moldova has so far fully used the wine quota established, i support the proposal to increase the tariff quota for wine without sparkling wine. it should be noted that such regulation will not have any negative consequences for the eu wine industry. moldova is one of the weakest countries in europe, facing major problems not only economically but also politically. the eu should facilitate moldova's choice of the right geopolitical direction to help resolve the country's difficulties. moreover, the provisions of this resolution will create favourable conditions for the moldovan wine sector to improve the quality of the product. i believe it is appropriate to extend the whole regulation for a further three years in order to provide legal clarity and certainty for wine producers, exporters and importers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report since the generalised system of preferences (gsp) is a highly important trade and development mechanism that the eu has at hand. however, i would like to urge the commission to come up with a more substantial review of the gsp scheme as soon as possible. i also think it is time for us to engage in a more substantial review of the gsp and gsp+ beneficiaries’ lists. the european parliament should be consulted on this issue from the earliest stage. i also expect that parliament will be involved in the process of monitoring whether the gsp+ beneficiaries uphold the 27 ilo and un conventions, something that must be scrutinised thoroughly in order to maintain the reliability of the gsp+ mechanism.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in 1968, the united nations conference on trade and development (unctad) recommended the creation of a common system of preferences (cps), under which industrialized countries would grant unilateral trade preferences to all developing countries, not just their former colonies. the european community was the first to implement the scheme in 1971, and it became one of the main instruments of trade and development policy, helping developing countries to reduce poverty by generating revenues from international trade. the eu gsp provides the least developed countries with the most favourable treatment for importing their products into the eu market without duties and quotas. the system also contributes to the promotion of sustainable development and good governance in developing countries that ratify and implement international conventions and protocols in the fields of human and labour rights, environmental protection, the fight against drugs and the fight against corruption.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, it is essential that the eu's 'general system of preferences' becomes more transparent. it is important that eu tariff preferences for imports from third countries are based on democracy and ethics, not just profit. tariff preferences should benefit society as a whole and not just a certain number of undertakings. the rapporteur rightly noted that the proposal to extend the current regulation is not ideal, but it would avoid a legal vacuum lasting more than six months. the existing regulation does not give the european parliament the right to express an opinion on the eligibility criteria or the list of beneficiary countries. this should change: it is time for parliament to use the powers granted to it by the lisbon treaty in the field of trade. the eu should pay more attention to developing cooperation with neighbouring countries in the field of trade policy. this would help to create stable and liberal business conditions and allow for the gradual expansion of the eu's single market. the eu should have an interest in signing a free trade agreement with ukraine and in entering into negotiations with the other eastern partnership countries that are members of the world trade organisation georgia, moldova and armenia.
in writing. − i have approved this protocol amending the eu-us air transport agreement. the protocol contains important provisions for the advancement of eu-us cooperation in air transport. it also avoids the risk that, in the absence of such an agreement, someone could invoke the suspension clause provided for in the first-stage agreement. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 20 march 2008 and that the agreement was signed on 1 march 2008. it should also be noted that this new agreement has created opportunities for new investment and market access opportunities and enhanced cooperation in regulatory areas such as safety, security and the environment. for the latter, the two parties agreed to draw up a separate joint statement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, has extended the conditions under which parliament's consent is required for the conclusion of an international agreement. aviation agreements fall into this category because they fall within the scope of the ordinary legislative procedure. the eu and us aviation markets account for about 60% of the world's air transport. the non-discriminatory opening of the market to eu and us airlines would provide a diversified and cost-efficient service to passengers and cargo operators, and would result in significant economic benefits and job creation. harmonised legislation would be a major contribution to promoting fair competition, in particular in the areas of state subsidies and social and environmental standards. while the stage two agreement is an important step forward, it is important that it is not seen as the end of the process of creating a transatlantic aviation market. i believe that the commission should plan negotiations on a next stage agreement covering, inter alia, the following issues: further liberalisation of rights of way; additional opportunities for foreign investment; the impact of environmental measures and infrastructure constraints on the exercise of rights of way; better organisation of passenger rights policy to ensure the best possible level of protection for passengers. harmonised standards of passenger rights, including those of persons with reduced mobility, are particularly important in order to avoid discrimination between passengers during journeys. all these air transport agreements are useful and necessary for the eu, our airlines and our citizens.
in writing. − the open skies agreement between the united states and the european union is a guarantee of progress for both regions, a reflection of their economic level. the full opening of the transatlantic market would be an important step towards improving the situation in the global air transport sector. both countries would benefit from millions of dollars in economic benefits, creating many new jobs, business development opportunities. we cannot afford to ignore safety requirements for economic gain. air safety and security standards are vital for passengers, crew and the aviation sector as a whole. in the field of safety, harmonisation of standards should be achieved in an incremental manner. eu and us authorities responsible for aviation safety must cooperate at all levels. eu safety standards shall comply with the requirements established by the international civil aviation organisation. we must do everything we can to ensure that the fate of ourselves, our children and all those we love and care for is not jeopardised. we cannot allow the european union to apply to flight crew members, their working hours and their rest periods, lower safety standards which would put human lives in mortal danger.
