in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the procedure for submitting single applications for residence and work permits for third-country nationals. this document establishes a single application procedure for third-country nationals seeking to enter the territory of a member state to work and ensures their legal status. this will undoubtedly simplify the often complex administrative procedure for the reception of economic migrants. i agree with the rapporteur that one of the best ways to combat illegal immigration and illegal work is to establish a balanced legal immigration policy that meets the needs of our labour markets. economic immigration is a reality we have to deal with, but it is also a necessity in view of the demographic and economic challenges that the european union will face in the near future. it should be noted that this document does not define the conditions for the admission of third-country nationals. member states remain responsible for determining the reception conditions and the number of migrants they wish to admit to their territory for work. it is time for the european union to draw up legislation on economic immigration to establish a common approach to be followed by the 27 member states. the amendments to the lisbon treaty have made this progress possible, and now we have to make it a reality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the directive on a single residence and work permit for third-country workers should be a general framework directive on the rights of third-country workers, as this is the only way for this european legislation to contribute to the european union's objective of establishing a common migration policy. unfortunately, the position adopted today by the european parliament on the single directive on residence and work permits has not improved the commission's proposal for this directive. it is not acceptable that legally arrived migrant workers from third countries, working in the same jobs as european union workers, should have the same rights and working conditions as local workers. it is necessary to recognise that legal migrant workers contribute to the economy of the european union both through their work and through their taxes and social contributions and that they must therefore be guaranteed the same minimum rights and equal treatment in the labour market. i would like to stress that there can be no two-tier labour market, either within the european union or outside it. we cannot allow the creation of a second class of workers in the european union labour market, discriminated against as a second gender, without any rights, without any guarantees, otherwise all the social standards that have been established so far will be forgotten.
in writing. − the hague programme recognised that legal immigration will be crucial for economic development. in this context, the commission was invited to present a policy plan to enable the labour market to respond quickly to the constantly changing demand for foreign labour. in accordance with the stockholm programme adopted by the european council on 10 and 11 december 2009, labour immigration can increase the competitiveness and vitality of an economy. in view of the major demographic challenges facing the eu in the future and the growing demand for labour, this multiannual programme encourages member states to pursue a flexible immigration policy in order to support the union's long-term economic growth and productivity. the advantage of the proposed provisions is that they provide better protection for workers from third countries than is currently possible under international conventions ratified by only some member states. i abstained from voting because it is not clear who, employer or employee, can make an application and from which country this application can be made, it was important to clarify this important issue. nor are the requirements of legal certainty and transparency in decision-making by national authorities emphasised. these decisions have important consequences for the lives of these people and for the member states and must therefore be taken in full transparency. decisions to reject an application shall be duly reasoned, transparent and objective.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on consumer rights, which aims to consolidate four existing community directives into a single legal act. i agree with the rapporteur that inconsistency in legislation is holding both consumers and businesses back from buying and selling in other countries. however, caution is needed as the nature of this area makes it rather difficult to fully harmonise consumer rights legislation and may reduce the level of consumer protection in some member states.
in writing. − i voted for this report, which will be returned to the ep's committees responsible for reconsideration. this directive aims to bring together eu legislation governing consumer rights and to ensure a high level of protection of consumer rights in all eu member states and to encourage businesses to provide services and sell goods in other member states. at present, obstacles to the smooth functioning of the market remain. businesses tend not to trade in other member states and consumers tend to conclude purchase contracts because of the different rules applicable to consumer contracts in the member states. the legislation in force until now has only set minimum requirements for the protection of consumers' rights, while member states have been able to apply more stringent measures, which has resulted in the maintenance of different legal regimes within the community. i think it is necessary to review this directive again and to strengthen its provisions. it is necessary to ensure that the same standards for the protection of consumers' rights are applied in all eu member states in order to avoid the current inconsistencies in the internal market, to strengthen consumer confidence in the internal market and to encourage businesses to trade in other member states.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the new rules, which are designed to update the current eu legislation on consumer rights, must cover all types of purchases: whether by telephone, online, in-store or on the doorstep. the amendments should encourage consumer confidence in buying from other countries and ensure a level playing field for businesses, thereby exploiting the full potential of the single market. on the other hand, the new rules must be balanced so as not to become an unbearable burden for smes. consumer protection is of paramount importance. only by taking a serious look at consumer protection levels could full harmonisation be achieved. it is also important that citizens know their rights. it's one of the problems in all of europe, but especially in my country. a eurobarometer survey commissioned by the ec shows that a large majority of lithuanians would like to know more about their rights as consumers. according to the survey, 2⁄3 of all lithuanians (66%) believe that the lithuanian legal system does not provide adequate protection against punishing companies that have cheated or defrauded them. the message is clear. we can't ignore that. the statistics also showed low trust in the government and the eu information offices less than 7% of all lithuanians trust these institutions to provide them with accurate information and advice on consumer rights. we can't leave it like this. the eu must act now.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which extends the mandate of the european network and information security agency (enisa) until the adoption of a new regulation on the updated operating rules and principles of the agency. enisa was established in 2004 for a period of five years to ensure a high and effective level of security of eu networks and information, thus contributing to the smooth functioning of the internal market. the cyber-attacks in the member states in recent years have led to a review and re-formulation of the agency's mandate, with a view to creating a more flexible response capacity and enhancing the efficiency of the agency's work. one of the key objectives of the eu digital agenda is to give all eu citizens access to digital technologies, while ensuring trust and security on the internet. the modernisation of the european network and information security agency will bring together the latest information from all european countries and encourage the sharing of good practices, thereby making the european union and the member states better equipped to prevent, detect and respond to network and information security problems.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the conclusions of the presidency of the eu member state of the tallinn ministerial conference on the protection of critical information infrastructure state that in order to address new and long-term challenges in the future, the mandate of the agency (enisa) needs to be thoroughly reviewed and re-structured to allow for a greater focus on eu priorities and needs, to build a more flexible response capacity, to build capacity and expertise at european level, to support the efficiency and overall impact of the agency. in this way, enisa could continue to be of benefit to each member state and to the european union as a whole. the commission proposes a regulation extending the agency's current mandate for 18 months to allow sufficient time for discussions on the revision of the new provisions of the agency. the commission shall be assisted by the committee established by article 15 of regulation (ec) no 460/2004. the european network and information security agency (enisa) was established in march 2004 for a period of five years, in particular to ensure a high and effective level of network and information security in the european union and to shape a culture of network and information security for the benefit of citizens, consumers, businesses and public sector organisations in the european union, while contributing to the smooth functioning of the internal market. regulation (ec) no 1007/20082 extended the mandate of enisa until march 2012 and extended the mandate of the agency until 31 december 2012.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. japan has been hit by a major natural disaster, coupled with a major nuclear accident, the scale of which is still beyond realistic estimation and which will have consequences for human health and the environment for decades to come. the european union immediately used its civil protection capabilities to coordinate humanitarian, technical and financial assistance in a timely manner. the accident should serve as a reference point for a comprehensive assessment and review of nuclear safety issues. nuclear energy is not only about operating the power plants themselves, but also about storing nuclear waste that lasts for centuries. the damage caused by the earthquake in japan to underground nuclear fuel storage facilities suggests that the prevailing view that landfilling is the safest way to dispose of waste is largely unfounded and that waste storage facilities could become a major source of danger to human health and the environment. i believe that it is necessary to start active discussions within the eu and at international level in order to ensure the highest level of nuclear power plants and waste storage already in operation and to seriously consider the benefits and assess the potential risks of nuclear power plants planned for construction.

in writing. - japan has suffered before our eyes a catastrophe unlike any other country in the world. an earthquake, a tsunami, a nuclear accident - each of these disasters would be a great test, and all together they have placed an immeasurable burden on the country, on its people. the shutdown of the still-burning fukushima nuclear power plant will raise a number of questions: could some of the disasters have been avoided, and what safety improvements should other nuclear power plants make to prevent natural disasters from causing nuclear accidents? all countries using nuclear energy should check the safety of their nuclear power plants. and those planning to build new power plants should do a better job of analyzing the risks they pose. but at this moment, the european union must show solidarity with the ordinary people of japan. the resolution on the situation in japan is therefore urgently needed. we must provide all the necessary humanitarian, technical and financial assistance to help people survive now and in the future to rebuild the devastated regions as soon as possible.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on migration flows caused by instability: the scope and role of eu foreign policy. the main drivers of migration are political, social and economic instability, insecurity, political persecution and authoritarian regimes, which leave affected communities without any viable options in their homeland and income, thus depriving them of the right to choose to emigrate or to remain, and placing individuals in constant danger of their lives and therefore their only remaining option to migrate. recent dramatic events in egypt and other countries in north africa and the middle east have clearly increased the flow of legal and illegal migration to europe. the european union must therefore be prepared to withstand waves of migration. it can only do so by having an effective and smart migration policy, similar to the policies that are in place in canada, australia or new zealand. i agree with the rapporteur that the commission should be urged to ensure that any readmission agreement signed between the eu and its member states fully respects the principle of human rights and non-refoulement and does not endanger persons in need of international protection. in this way, the eu will once again demonstrate that values and respect for human rights are paramount and undeniable, and that asylum seekers will feel safe and respected.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. recent developments in egypt and other countries in north africa and the middle east have increased legal and illegal migration flows to europe. the member states of the european union face forced migration of people as a result of economic failures, impoverishment, human rights violations, environmental degradation, the growing gap between rich and poor countries, civil wars and political persecution. managing migration flows is a major challenge for the european union, which must act to develop a common migration policy that can contribute to reducing illegal immigration. i agree that it is necessary to take preventive measures by including human rights clauses in all eu bilateral trade agreements and to consider the application of appropriate sanctions to countries that do not comply with such clauses.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because migration is a particularly pressing and recent issue, with events in north africa forcing the european union, as a neighbouring region, to accept massive flows of migrants. the report highlights the many factors that contribute to the flow of migration, such as political, social, economic instability and even climate change, which are still not taken into account in the analysis of the causes of mass migration. for all these reasons, it is stressed that the eu needs a more effective migration policy, which should be complemented by foreign policy instruments. these measures would help to address the causes of instability in countries of origin, which force people to emigrate en masse to more stable neighbouring regions. the communication also calls on the commission to develop proposals for legal migration that would be easier to manage and could promote economic and social progress in both host, transit and origin countries. it is claimed that the most serious human rights violations, as well as criminal activities that often turn into a business for those who organise them, are linked to illegal migration. finally, the need to assess the demographic situation of the eu itself is emphasised in order to estimate how many people europe can take in.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because migration flows caused by instability are a challenge for the eu. prisons, armed conflicts, tensions between ethnic groups, persistent human rights violations such as religious persecution, natural disasters, and the lack of economic and democratic structures are the main causes of this type of migration. this phenomenon is of particular concern because it may create or increase tensions not only between the countries of origin and destination but also between the countries of origin and transit. to address this challenge effectively, the eu must adopt a policy of prevention, using the most appropriate foreign policy instruments to address directly the causes of instability, so that emigration becomes an opportunity rather than a necessity. it is therefore necessary to initiate a debate in order to better understand all aspects of migration phenomena and their structural causes. this would encourage the eu to establish a clear and effective policy on migration flows from countries of origin and transit and to decide how and how much to invest in these countries in order to compensate for their internal demographic and social tensions and thus contribute to the creation of conditions for stability.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, following the unrest in the arab countries, which has seen a particularly high level of migration flows, it is essential that a common migration policy is in place across the eu. given that migration cannot be stopped, foreign policy has a special role to play in this area. the countries on the eu's external borders are most affected by the increased migration flows. we therefore need to make every effort to develop a common eu migration policy at eu level in order to optimally manage and control migration flows. only by working together will the economies of the countries receiving the largest flows of migrants be protected from the negative effects of the crisis, as will the sustainability of labour markets and the prospects for development. this will be an effective tool to prevent illegal migration, organised crime and trafficking in human beings. the eu must make every effort to promote legal migration and effectively combat illegal migration. it is essential that the legal migration system is designed to meet the needs of the european labour market, taking into account the capacity of each member state to receive and integrate migrants. legal migrants in the european union must have the same rights and obligations as other workers. it is also essential to reduce the outflow of knowledge and skilled professionals in each country. this requires support for return programmes, encouraging exchange migration, regulating recruitment practices, and supporting skills development.

in writing. - i voted for this important document. with their accession to the european union, lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria have made politically and economically complex commitments to close down their operating nuclear power plants, and the european union has committed to providing the necessary financial support for closure, construction and storage of nuclear waste and the development of energy projects. i believe that such a european union solidarity concept can be effective in mitigating the negative economic consequences of early closure in the energy sector, but there are still a number of important issues that remain unresolved. the question of the allocation of funding is not entirely clear, as it is already known that the funding currently allocated will not be sufficient to carry out the decommissioning works in a timely and proper manner. there is a risk that the decommissioning of nuclear power plants will be delayed due to lack of financial resources and may pose a threat to the environment and human health. detailed plans for decommissioning programmes have not yet been finalised, and therefore there is a lack of data on calendar schedules, the cost of specific projects and their sources of funding. i agree that the european commission needs to play a greater coordinating role with these three countries in order to agree on the level of funding for the submission of detailed plans, the timely completion of the work. the commission should also explore possible ways to harmonise the decommissioning financing arrangements in the eu, taking into account the strategies applied by the member states, their national administrative structures and simplify the actual procedures for administering the funds in a way that does not compromise the safety and security of decommissioning.
in writing. − as is known, old soviet nuclear reactors were operating in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria, which the international community has determined cannot be upgraded to meet minimum safety standards at economically acceptable costs. recognising the enormous financial burden of early shutdowns, and acting in solidarity, the eu has in turn committed to provide the appropriate additional financial support to bring these reactors to a standstill by the end of 2013. however, there is concern that major waste management infrastructure projects (spent fuel storage and waste repository project) are being implemented with significant delays. the possibility of inactivity is almost exhausted and delays may start to interfere with the entire decommissioning plan and increase costs accordingly. the commission should communicate the results of the reassessment of the project timetable. a large part of the funds has been allocated to energy projects, but there is still a large need for decommissioning and insufficient national funding: the funds accumulated so far in the state ignalina nuclear decommissioning fund are insufficient. the cost of technical decommissioning could range from eur 987 million to eur 1 300 million. member states shall take appropriate measures in this regard. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of radioactive waste in the transport of dangerous goods. this could be a new challenge for the eu, posing a real threat to our human health and the environment in the future.
in writing. − i support this resolution on the efficiency and effectiveness of the use of eu funds for the decommissioning of nuclear power plants in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria. in particular, efforts should be made to ensure that all decommissioning operations are carried out in a timely manner with the proper implementation of all necessary safety measures and with the avoidance of any minimal risk to human health and the environment. if we are to decommission ignalina and other nuclear power plants, all the financial resources allocated to this process must be used for their intended purpose in accordance with the principles of transparency and efficiency. the national management authorities shall complete the detailed decommissioning plans as soon as possible. i believe that the results of the audit carried out by the european court of auditors will show the objectives of the use of funds and their effectiveness. we must make every effort to ensure that the dismantling and decommissioning of waste starts before 2013. i think it is appropriate to impose an obligation on the commission to submit a detailed financing plan to the european parliament and to establish the responsibility for the use of european union aid. given the lack of sufficient planned amounts in the national decommissioning funds, it is appropriate to include new lines of action in the strategies and plans developed and to provide for additional eu funds accordingly.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on dual-use items and technologies, i.e. goods which can be used for both civilian and military purposes. export controls on dual-use items are essential to prevent the proliferation of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. it is therefore essential to make the eu's export regime for dual-use goods more democratic and transparent, while at the same time being sufficiently rigorous. currently, the requirements for the export of dual-use items and technologies vary in severity across the eu member states. i believe that the eu should aim to apply the strictest export regime applicable to all member states to each object. the commission should establish an effective system in this area to help collect reliable data on the end-use of dual-use items exported from the union.
in writing. − export controls on dual-use goods (civil and military) are crucial to preventing the proliferation of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction. for 15 years, the eu has been strengthening export controls on dual-use goods, based on preventive measures, export licensing requirements and customs registration procedures. however, in the light of continuous technological developments and new threats, it is necessary to keep the lists of controlled dual-use items up to date, in line with the similar lists used under the main international export control regimes. the main task of these international export control regimes is to keep up to date the lists of goods whose exports need to be controlled. until now, these lists have been transposed into eu law almost automatically, without the involvement of the european parliament, but since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the ep's consent is also required. i supported this report and the european parliament's proposals to ensure a more democratic and transparent eu export regime for dual-use goods and a stronger role for the commission in assessing the implementation of this regulation in the member states.
in writing. − chemical and radioactive materials, nuclear centrifuges, hardware and software and their components are used for both civilian and military purposes. in the wrong hands, these items could become tools of torture or weapons of mass destruction. i voted in favour of this document because it proposes to improve the export control regime for dual-use items and technology, i.e. to strengthen the control of exports of dual-use goods. this document also extends the list of goods for which an authorisation is required and the movement of exports of those goods is to be notified.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on officially supported export credits. export credits are an important tool to support eu businesses. i agree that the promotion of medium and long-term export credits is a powerful instrument which has not yet been fully exploited by all member states and should therefore be encouraged. export credits can be used to finance projects of a non-commercial nature that would otherwise have limited access to capital, and to help create jobs. however, it should be noted that there is currently insufficient transparency to identify what export credit agencies are financing or have financed in the past. the lack of transparency results in high costs and delays and creates the conditions for bribery and corruption. therefore, i support the rapporteur's proposal to require member states to provide the commission with annual reports on the activities of their export credit agencies in relation to risk assessment and publication of off-balance-sheet measures and to provide for an obligation to report on social and environmental risk assessments.
in writing. − many industrialised countries, including all eu member states, have at least one officially supported export credit agency, which together constitute the world's largest source of official financial support for private sector projects. the amount of export credit guarantees granted by the eu member states' export credit agencies alone in 2004-2009 amounts to eur 468 billion. export credit agencies facilitate legitimate trade where the private capital market is weak and their capacity to adapt to risk is much higher than that of private entities, as they do not have to pay taxes and make profits and have a much greater margin of manoeuvre than private banks to avoid incurring losses on the credits granted. however, for the same reason, export credit agencies can cause significant distortions of trade if their financial operations are not regulated by common rules. while export credit agencies are an important tool to support the activities and investments of european companies, it is necessary to ensure that companies carry out sound financial activities and do not require taxpayer assistance to refinance their operations. i supported this report and the requirement to report annually to the european commission and the european parliament because there is currently very little data on what such agencies finance or have financed in the past, and some national export credit agencies do not even report regularly on the overall state of their annual operations, which is contrary to the principle of transparency.
in writing. − as you know, it is impossible to understand what export credit agencies are financing or have financed in the past. some national export credit agencies did not even report regularly on the overall state of their annual operations. many other agencies do not provide non-aggregated data on lending by sector or geographical distribution. this is contrary to the transparency requirements of the 2005 oecd agreement, to which all eu member states are parties and which will now be transposed into eu law. the oecd agreement does not contain any requirements to ensure the fair determination of premiums, as it does not provide for any transparency requirements or minimum standards for the assessment of social and environmental risks. it is proposed to introduce a procedure for transparency requirements relating to risk assessment and publication of off-balance-sheet items and to provide for an obligation to report on social and environmental risk assessments, and to require member states to provide the commission with annual reports on the activities of their export credit agencies relating to the items specified. i therefore voted in favour of this document because it will set more standards for transparency and for assessing social and environmental risks.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is essential to put an end to violence against women as soon as possible. i would like to point out that one in ten women in europe has experienced violence, and this is one of the most common causes of death among women. although the issue of violence against women has been discussed for decades, it is painful to see that we are still failing to protect women from violence. it is therefore essential that the european commission develops a common directive on combating and combating all forms of violence against women, whether physical, sexual or psychological. gender-based violence includes sexual exploitation, trafficking in human beings, forced marriage, genital mutilation and other violations. such violent crimes have a significant impact and irreversible damage to the physical and mental health of women and member states should therefore ensure better healthcare for victims of violence. i would also like to urge commissioner cecilia malmström, responsible for home affairs, not to reduce financial support to non-governmental organisations (ngos) fighting violence against women. the economic and financial crisis has led to an increase in violence and there is no reason to reduce funding in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because we must put an end to all violations of women's rights and all violence against women. and i believe that, in line with the action plan for the implementation of the stockholm programme adopted last year, the commission should draw up a strategy to combat violence against women as soon as possible. in the meantime, member states must ensure that healthcare, social workers, the police, the courts and other institutions are better able to respond in a timely and professional manner to all cases of violence against women.

member of the commission. − firstly, on the effectiveness of humanitarian assistance from the beginning, from the outset of the crisis, the most dramatic humanitarian impact so far can be split into three parts. first, the outflow of migrant workers into tunisia, egypt, algeria and niger – there the commission and the member states have been very effective. we have mobilised both air and sea deployment of member states assets so we can take people home, and a humanitarian injection into the international organisation for migration and the un organisation for refugees so that they can help with a huge amount of people – 420 000 people – fleeing libya. second, in the eastern part of libya to which we have access, we have provided support for medical treatment as well as for the prepositioning of food supplies. this is not yet a food crisis, but this is a country that imports 90% of its food, so we must be ready. there we also are helping sub-saharan africans, in particular chadians, who found themselves in a very difficult position because of the risk to their safety, being perceived to be mercenaries, being perceived to be fighters, when of course many of them are not. helping them to get to safety, mostly in egypt, has also been a priority. third, we know that in gaddafi-controlled areas there are humanitarian needs but we are restricted in getting there. we have set aside eur 9 million even when conditions allow for us to be mobilised. we actually gave instructions to the world food programme as well as to other humanitarian organisations, to be ready to help. on the second part of your question, access to markets, this is at the heart of the southern mediterranean initiative which i outlined. it is about making sure that we can offer a prospect of a better future for jobs and prosperity to these countries. there we are putting a very strong emphasis indeed on trade, trade with europe, but also trade among the countries of the mediterranean.

member of the commission. − let me first say that the evacuation of european citizens has been very successful. we managed to achieve coordination between our member states and deployed the monitoring and information centre to provide a platform for this coordination. as a result, we got the vast majority of our citizens out of libya in the fastest and safest manner. by the time this massive evacuation was completed, there were only around 200 people left who wanted to be evacuated. right now — as we speak — some of them have been safely evacuated by a russian aircraft. on the question of medical services, as we evacuated european citizens the law of unintended consequences kicked in, because some of these european citizens had been providing medical services as part of the libyan health service. many nurses were evacuated, though not so many doctors. we are now making every possible effort to enable humanitarian organisations that specialise in medical care to provide access to such care for libyans and third-country nationals in libya. once again, the critical importance of gaddafi allowing humanitarian organisations to operate in the western part of libya cannot be over-emphasised. unfortunately this has not yet happened. we have a team of our own experts in the eastern part of the country. they have returned from an assessment mission and reported that, although there are increasing numbers of wounded people in need of medical care, the medical supplies and support — including personnel — that the intentional community is providing are broadly sufficient in the eastern part of libya. that is not the case, however, in cities like misrata and other areas controlled by gaddafi. as you probably know, attempts are now being made to send in medical ships by sea as a means of increasing the availability of medical treatment.

the importance of the role of european political parties is also enshrined in the treaty of lisbon, which aims to create an effective european political area. our politicians' job is to engage their citizens in the european union, to make it more understandable and accessible, and to involve them in decision-making. however, this requires appropriate, clear and uniform regulation of the activities of european political parties and european political foundations and the democratic functioning of such parties. as a source of democracy, these political parties should enjoy a uniform legal and fiscal status, which would allow for a better understanding of parties and better representation of european citizens. it is of particular importance that the formation of the internal management bodies of such political parties be based on transparent principles, which allow for the democratic election of all party bodies and the democratic decision-making processes.
in writing. the debate on how to strengthen the role of european political parties in developing democracy in europe and shaping public opinion is timely. although parliament is gaining more and more power, its democratic deficit is not being reduced by the declining participation of citizens in the european elections. political parties at european level are the main instruments of parliamentary democracy, helping to shape european political awareness, to stimulate interest in eu issues and to express the will of the citizens of the union. i therefore fully support and agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to consolidate the position of political parties at european level and to provide them with a clear and uniform legal status and funding model. such parties should not remain strangers. at present, the role of european political parties in the public sphere is rather limited. they are only organisations that link national parties, not organisations that directly contact voters. the new legal status of such parties in the european union would help to ensure organisational unity and enable them to play their role more effectively. i would like to stress that we must continue to work towards a secure and transparent environment for party financing. the financing of political parties should not be based solely on a grant scheme, but should also encourage own-funding, which is a sign of the viability of political parties.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp) often involves bilateral fisheries agreements between the ec and third countries, known as fisheries partnership agreements (fpas) since 2004, and is an important external aspect of this policy. the agreements with the african and pacific countries provide for a substantial part of the eu's financial contribution to be devoted to supporting this particular area of national fisheries policy, which is based on the principle of sustainability and the sound management of fisheries resources. partnership agreements therefore commit to promoting responsible and sustainable fishing wherever eu vessels fish, and are based on a thorough assessment of existing stocks, and aim to ensure that fishing opportunities are based on sound scientific advice and that any threat of depletion of local stocks is eliminated. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty gave parliament increased powers in relation to fisheries partnership agreements: article 218 (6) (a) of the eu treaty now requires parliament's prior consent before an agreement can be concluded, instead of the previously existing simple consultation procedure. i believe that this proposed new protocol on the fisheries partnership agreement with the union of the comoros is of fundamental benefit to both parties.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the minimum requirements for the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection in the member states. the establishment of a common european asylum system began as soon as the treaty of amsterdam entered into force in may 1999, but despite all the efforts made over the last decade to harmonise asylum provisions, there are still significant differences between national provisions and their application. i agree that, regardless of the member state in which asylum seekers lodge their application, they must be guaranteed a high-level procedure, uniform throughout the european union. it is therefore essential not only to harmonise the requirements of the legislation in this area but also to encourage practical cooperation between member states. it is clear that these objectives require urgent reforms to ensure that persons seeking asylum in an eu member state are effectively protected. by voting in favour of this resolution, we, the members of the european parliament, are contributing to the development of a fair and effective european asylum policy.
in writing. − the european union's main objective in the field of asylum is to establish by 2012 a common area of protection and solidarity based on a uniform asylum procedure. despite all the efforts made over the last decade to harmonise asylum provisions, there are still significant differences between national provisions and their application. regardless of the member state in which they lodge their application, asylum seekers must be guaranteed the same treatment, taking into account common standards established throughout the european union. the establishment of a strong european legal framework is necessary if the european union is to implement the common european asylum system properly and effectively. it is therefore only through improved and harmonised procedures and the associated guarantees that a common asylum system can be established. furthermore, a review of the asylum procedures directive is necessary in order to create an accessible, fair and efficient procedure that will benefit both asylum seekers and the member states themselves. i would like to stress that the commission's new revised proposal for this directive can indeed help to ensure greater coherence, to improve international protection standards and to improve the quality and efficiency of asylum procedures.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because we must make every effort to achieve an even greater effectiveness of the european asylum system, which has a direct impact on individuals. asylum policy is of paramount importance as it has a major impact on the eu's overall ability to develop and create a common area of freedom, security and justice. first, there is a need to ensure greater consistency in asylum measures. the procedures must be harmonised in order to be applied fairly and effectively. in addition, the minimum procedural safeguards need to be improved. the right of asylum seekers to information, to be heard and to legal aid must be guaranteed and unrestricted. all procedural measures must be non-discriminatory, applied in the same way and with due regard to the guarantees and principles of personal rights. special attention shall be paid to the vulnerable group of asylum seekers. the best interests of the children must be duly safeguarded and represented in the necessary procedures. i support the proposal that provides for the immediate expulsion of a person who may pose a threat to the national security of the state or who has been forcibly expelled from the country under national law because of a threat to public security. such an option is very important and necessary as it will enable member states to prevent the operation of terrorist networks and to take appropriate preventive measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. tourism is an important economic activity in the eu, which can make a major contribution to job creation and higher economic growth, as well as playing an important role in the social and economic integration of rural and less developed areas. the european tourism industry comprises some 1,8 million businesses, mainly smes, employing about 5,2% of the total workforce (about 9,7 million jobs). i support the commission's efforts to redefine european tourism policy, as the eu has gained more competence in this area with the lisbon treaty. the tourism sector faces major challenges such as global competition, demographic change, climate change and environmental constraints, the seasonal distribution of tourist flows and the increasing use of new information and communication technologies. i believe that the tourism sector needs to be strengthened at eu level by coordinating actions that complement the initiatives of the member states. this regulation, which aims to establish a common system for the production of systematic european tourism statistics for the collection, production, processing and transmission of harmonised european statistics on tourism supply and demand, is of particular importance as its proper implementation will allow the real situation of tourism in the member states to be known and to be better adapted to the changing needs of tourists.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the need to improve european tourism policy, especially in view of the recent difficult economic situation of the european tourism sector. the european union has gained more competence in the tourism sector since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, following a change in the legal framework, and the european commission has put forward a proposal for a new tourism policy. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to update and improve the legal basis for european tourism statistics, but there is concern that the new proposed regulation does not provide for satellite accounts for tourism. these accounts are particularly important for the progressive development of integrated tourism statistical systems and for a better understanding of the real value of tourism and its impact on job creation and economic growth. in addition, in order to improve the knowledge base for the development and growth of tourism, the commission should develop pilot studies in the field of tourism. these studies are proposed to be carried out on a voluntary basis in the member states with a view to developing a system for collecting data on the environmental impact of tourism.
in writing. − i voted for this document because it is necessary to improve and redefine european tourism policy. tourism is an important economic activity in the eu, which can make a major contribution to job creation and higher economic growth, as well as playing an important role in the social and economic integration of rural, peripheral and less developed areas, such as those with a strong industrial heritage. in addition to being used to monitor tourism policy, statistics in this area also have an impact on regional policy and sustainable development. the main challenges facing the sector, such as global competition, demographic change, climate change and environmental constraints, the seasonal distribution of tourist flows and the increasing use of new information and communication technologies, need to be addressed. it is necessary to strengthen the tourism sector at eu level by coordinating actions that complement member states' initiatives. to successfully implement the new policy, legislators at all levels need to make informed decisions based on reliable, comparable statistical data. tourism is an important economic activity with a positive impact on economic growth and employment in europe and it is therefore necessary to update and improve the legal basis for european tourism statistics, thereby strengthening the tourism sector at eu level. the measures will thus increase the competitiveness of european tourism and promote its sustainable growth.
in writing. − today, parliament adopted an important document on the legal basis for european tourism statistics. member states are required to provide regularly updated data on the availability and employment of accommodation facilities and on tourism needs. with the changing travel habits of europeans (e.g. increasing short-term travel) and the shift of the tourism sector towards certain innovations (e.g. online booking of travel), it is necessary to update the legal framework governing the collection of statistical data in the field of tourism. however, in my view, the most important provision supported by the ep relates to the collection of data relating to persons with reduced mobility and their impact on the access of such persons to full tourism services. in the constant talk about improving the quality of life of disabled people, we must also include tourism in this area. only in this way will we be able to ensure that tourism policy is effectively implemented and that consumer rights are protected.
in writing. − i voted for this document because there is a growing recognition that fisheries management must be based on the most up-to-date and accurate knowledge of the state of fish stocks. this is a prerequisite for the sustainable development of fisheries. for this reason, i believe that the co-financing rates for the collection, processing and use of key data should be allowed to be increased, with a maximum proposed rate of 75%. given that aquaculture is considered to be a sector of increasing importance (as reflected in the recently prepared, discussed and adopted report 'new impetus for the implementation of the european strategy for the sustainable development of aquaculture') and given the real growth prospects for it, the relevant provisions for the collection, management and use of data should also cover environmental and socio-economic data. environmental and health monitoring and surveillance should be carried out accordingly. this would help to make the sector more sustainable. the sustainability of the fisheries sector is of particular importance at this time. member states and their control authorities have and should continue to have a key role in monitoring and implementing control measures in their waters, as a key means of achieving compliance and resource consideration. in order to do this effectively, member states should acquire new technologies or be able to develop and modernise existing technologies. the management of investment control systems could be made more efficient and could be operated more cheaply.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in the absence of an agreement on a draft regulation simplifying and clarifying the legislation on the conservation of fishery resources, a regulation was adopted in 2008 laying down transitional measures initially intended to apply for the period 1 january 2010 to 30 june 2011. the purpose of this legislative proposal is to extend this transitional arrangement for an additional 18 months, until 1 january 2013, in order to define a new set of technical measures to implement the reform of the common fisheries policy currently under way. one proposal is to be submitted by the commission in 2011. the commission should therefore use the new extension of the current regulation to assess, together with other entities, the impact of the existing measures on the vessels applying them and on the relevant ecosystems. the commission should therefore take into account the results of this evaluation and prepare a new proposal for a regulation to apply after 1 january 2013 and which, in accordance with the treaty of lisbon, should be adopted by the co-decision procedure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i agree that the european parliament and the other eu institutions need to respond appropriately and effectively to the current financial, economic and social situation in the eu and apply strict management procedures in order to save money. the overall level of expenditure in the european parliament's 2012 draft estimate is expected to increase by 2,3% compared to the 2011 budget, and this does not exceed the current inflation rate of 2,8%. in the future, parliament must make even more effective use of its budgetary resources and strengthen its management and control procedures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the institutions must respond appropriately and effectively to the current financial, economic and social situation in the eu and apply strict management procedures to save money. it is clear that it is necessary to ensure that the institutions have sufficient resources, but in the current economic circumstances, resources should be used prudently and efficiently. i also believe that parliament must be even more efficient in saving money and in tightening management and control procedures. we need to further modernise and streamline administration, reducing dependence on external services through effective human resource management. all institutions should make every effort to reduce the cost of preparing their estimates of expenditure for the 2012 draft budget, as this would undoubtedly help and save taxpayers' money.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document on the authorisation and refusal of authorisation of certain health claims made on foods in relation to children's development and health, as products in the common market must be safe, comply with standards and be legal, and health claims made on foods must be justified and scientifically proven, especially when it comes to children and their health. it is necessary to ensure that the nutritional or physiological benefits of the substances for which a claim is made are demonstrated. claims should be scientifically justified, taking into account the totality of the available scientific data and giving weight to the evidence. the use of health claims should be subject to the highest possible scientific evaluation and should not be misleading as regards nutrition and health claims.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty gives the eu exclusive competence in the field of foreign direct investment (fdi). this innovation has a major impact on two factors: the management of the bilateral investment treaties (bits) already concluded by more than 1 200 member states and the definition of the future investment policy of the european union, which meets the expectations of investors and the countries in which they intend to invest, while taking into account the objectives of the eu's external action. the aim of dis agreements between developed and developing countries is to provide legal and financial security for investors in developed countries. i agree that in shaping the future eu investment policy, investor protection must remain the main priority of investment agreements. future eu policy should also promote sustainable and environmentally friendly investments (especially in the extractive industries) and quality working conditions in the companies invested in, and the eu should therefore support the current reform of the osce guidelines to promote responsible behaviour by multinational companies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the need to develop an integrated and coherent investment policy that promotes quality investment and has a positive impact on global economic progress and sustainable development. i believe that the common investment policy can meet the expectations of both investors and the countries concerned and can help to increase the competitiveness of the eu and its businesses and to increase employment. investment risks are generally higher in developing countries and lower in developed countries. strong, effective investor protection in investment agreements is essential to protect european investors, which can improve governance and ensure stability. in order to continue to benefit these countries, investment agreements must also be based on the commitment of investors to respect human rights and anti-corruption standards, as part of a broader partnership between the eu and developing countries to reduce poverty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on international investment policy. as foreign direct investment is an exclusive competence of the eu, every effort should be made to develop a coherent and integrated investment policy, respecting human rights, the rule of law. the common investment policy will promote quality investment, sustainable economic, social and environmental development and will have a positive impact on global economic progress. i believe that such an investment policy will help europe to remain a major player in foreign direct investment, which will help to boost economic growth, increase the competitiveness of businesses and stimulate job creation. i believe that the commission must develop an eu investment strategy as a matter of urgency, as both foreign investment in the eu and eu investment abroad have a positive impact on growth and employment in the eu and in other countries, including developing countries. every effort must be made to ensure a high level of investor protection, which is a guarantee of stability, good governance. in addition, small and medium-sized enterprises must be guaranteed legal certainty to facilitate their investment in foreign markets. investment agreements shall be concluded in strict compliance with anti-corruption standards and with a commitment to respect human rights.
in writing. − i have supported this report, which calls for action and resources to be allocated to ensure that eu funds are not used in corruption cases and that full transparency is ensured in the recipients of eu financial support. eu taxpayers' money must be used properly and efficiently. member states must have effective control mechanisms and adequate fraud detection capabilities. all funds paid out in the course of the infringements must be recovered from the eu budget.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because member states must ensure that the fight against fraud is primarily aimed at protecting taxpayers' money. the reporting methodology and fraud detection capacity in the member states need to be strengthened. the commission's 2009 report on the protection of financial interests does not provide information on the possible level of irregularities and fraud in individual member states, and therefore it is not possible to assess the overall level of irregularities and fraud in the member states and to identify and sanction the member states with the highest levels of irregularities and fraud. the commission report does not cover fraud in detail and the infringements are very broad. it is regrettable that a large part of eu funds continues to be misused and the commission must take appropriate action to ensure that these funds are recovered swiftly. there must be no tolerance for error and the commission must, together with the member states, draw up an appropriate report, in accordance with the treaty, and give parliament the appropriate assurance that this objective has been achieved and that the anti-fraud measures are being properly implemented.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the application of the regulations governing european political parties and the rules on their funding. it is an important document contributing to the development of european political parties in order to stimulate public interest in eu affairs. a common and transparent system of funding for european political parties is necessary to ensure that eu citizens support and trust these parties. by adopting this resolution, the european parliament is making a clear case for transparent funding, which is a key element of democratic values and good governance. it is essential that european political parties promoting democracy in the union have a common and equal legal status. the parties need more than ever to have european statutes based on eu law to help harmonise the tax aspects of eu political parties in order to achieve their objectives. i agree with the rapporteur that this document contributes to a more efficient eu political party system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report. the treaty of lisbon provides for the important role of political parties in the creation of a single european citizens' area, and it is therefore essential to ensure their equal legal status and their funding in a way that is as transparent and accountable as possible to society. the current relatively closed nature of many political parties in europe, with little change of leadership, weakens the role of these political organisations in ensuring the involvement of citizens in political decision-making. by reforming the rules governing the activities of political parties, the european union could seize the opportunity to encourage the renewal of european political parties. i believe that the new unified rules for the activities and financing of political parties should include criteria for the democratic nature of the formation of internal party structures, a kind of safeguard for democracy, failing which political organisations would lose part of their opportunities, for example, they would not be able to apply for public funding.
in writing. − i have supported this report because the creation of a safe and transparent environment for the operation and funding of european political parties is a goal of a strong democracy. we must create a space, a european space, in which parties can act to unite the citizens of the union and help them in their daily lives. the adoption of specific rules which will make it possible to achieve this objective has two consequences. on the one hand, up-to-date and public information on the formation of european political parties and their position in europe will be provided rapidly. citizens will know that their participation in the activities of a european political party is governed by european union law and that political parties have rights and obligations. on the other hand, the statutes of european political parties provide the opportunity to establish a cross-border party system. this system is the first and necessary step towards more participation, more democracy and more europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because political parties at european level are an important factor in the integration of the union with a view to creating a european pole, a political space and democracy. european political parties need to work closely with their members, existing national and regional parties, and therefore need to be given favourable conditions for their activities and funding. it is necessary to ensure maximum transparency and financial control of european political parties financed from the general budget of the european union. in particular, the financial regulation should be supplemented by provisions designed to regulate the financing of european parties and foundations only. it is also appropriate to provide for an exception whereby those lots would be allowed to receive 100% of the funding at the beginning of the financial year instead of 80% and the proportion of independent resources to be demonstrated would be reduced to 10%. in order to ensure that the funding allocated is used in a transparent and appropriate manner, the regulation should provide for penalties for breaches of the funding arrangements. given the political role played by european political parties at eu level, i support the proposal to give them the right to participate in the campaigns for referendums directly related to eu issues and to use the funds allocated to them to finance these campaigns. only strong and effective european political parties can help to bring the eu institutions and citizens closer together, and the commission should therefore propose a draft statute for european political parties as a matter of urgency.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the fragmentation of the internal market reduces the confidence of eu citizens in it, since they cannot fully enjoy the freedoms that belong to them. the commission's communication sets out a package of measures that should help achieve an integrated and smooth-functioning single market, which could boost the recovery of the european economy and its competitiveness. i would like to stress a very important aspect: the importance of the creation of a single energy market. the common energy market is of particular importance for the eu's competitiveness, both internally and externally. the creation of such a market would help to reduce external dependence and make energy prices accessible, fair and competitive for our citizens and businesses. legislative and other initiatives in the field of energy should aim at ensuring energy supply through a variety of energy networks and sources, new renewable energy infrastructures and coordinated research and development of new energy sources. these initiatives must be implemented by the european commission with consistent coordination and supervision of the member states and the industries concerned. the real development of the single market for the benefit of citizens, business and european competitiveness must be fostered by the creation of infrastructure projects with added value for europe as a whole, financed and managed at eu level, in order to ensure our energy independence and security.

in writing. − a smoothly functioning single market based on free and fair competition is a key objective of eu economic reform. the internal market currently remains fragmented and the remaining administrative and regulatory barriers have a negative impact on all businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, which are not able to take full advantage of the single market. the eu has no clear rules on licensing of ownership. this has a direct impact on counterfeiting and piracy, thereby reducing business confidence in electronic commerce and encouraging fragmentation linked to intellectual property protection rules, which in turn hinders innovation in the single market. the issue of public procurement, which accounts for about 17% of eu gdp, is particularly important to address properly. so far, cross-border procurement accounts for a small share of the total procurement market, as access to the procurement market for smes is still limited. the common market in services, which is a crucial sector for growth and employment, is still underdeveloped, in particular because of the gaps and difficulties encountered by member states in implementing the services directive. i agree with the proposals in the commission's communication 'towards a single market act', but i believe that to ensure the effective functioning of the single market, member states need to better implement the eu initiatives already adopted, such as the small business act, which would solve many of the administrative and regulatory problems facing eu businesses today.

mr president, i would like to make a short comment regarding nuclear plants in third countries that are very close to eu borders. two particular cases have already been mentioned today, two simultaneous nuclear projects: one in the kaliningrad district of the russian federation, which is completely surrounded by lithuania, poland and the baltic sea, and the second in belarus, where a nuclear power station is planned to be built just 20 kms away from the lithuanian border. when the whole world was watching the dramatic developments in fukushima, on 15 march the belarus government and the russian state-owned energy company rosatom signed a contract under which rosatom will have to finish the nuclear plant in belarus by 2018. russia is also preparing a usd 6 billion envelope to belarus to finance this project. so the belarus authorities have been defiant about the need to properly inform belarus’s neighbours about the planned project, and the project as it stands clearly violates the espoo convention on environmental impact assessment.
mr president, we should not turn a blind eye to blatant human rights violations taking place in the three countries. the situation in syria is very serious and its stakes the highest. in syria, teachers, opposition activists, journalists and bloggers are being targeted. there are many people killed; many detained; foreign journalists have been kicked out of the country; an information blockade is in place; no independent press at all. so we should consider sanctions against syria. we should also consider policy actions in yemen and bahrain. as for yemen we have a standing agreement on arms exports; we should consider suspending this agreement. as we debate the situation in those three countries: firstly, let us call for accountability; secondly let us have special sessions in the united nations human rights council in geneva… (the president cut off the speaker)
madam president, at this time it is important to consider carefully, and strike the right balance between, both the european neighbourhood policy factors. the enp should become more flexible, proactive and optimised. if we want to create an area of stability, shared values and progress surrounding in europe we should, firstly, no longer limit ourselves with predefined quotas. financial assistance should be balanced according to political involvement and the will to move closer to eu values, freedoms and standards. it should be result-oriented and tied to objective and clear criteria on democratisation and the progress achieved in reforms. secondly, we should consider creating a rapid reaction tool within the enp for prompt and flexible response to political changes in partner countries, as has happened recently in the southern neighbourhood. thirdly, the attractiveness of eu assistance is also important. the simplification of eu fund allocation procedures and active sharing of expertise by the member states at the early stages of programming would be an additional incentive.
the review of the european neighbourhood policy is one of the most important tasks. the events in egypt, tunisia, libya, yemen, bahrain and elsewhere are ruthlessly shattering many of the stereotypes of european thinking: that most people in the middle east or north africa do not care about human rights, that they are accustomed to living under dictatorships. the revolutions in the arab world have shown the fallacy of such thinking. i was in egypt a few weeks ago, on the day of the referendum on constitutional amendments. everyone we met talked about freedom, justice, democracy, and so on. most stressed that the european union's support must be different, that it must support the strengthening of civil society, the creation of political parties, the protection of human rights, so that the forthcoming parliamentary and presidential elections are democratic, free and fair. the democratic processes that are taking place there are very fragile, vulnerable, and they need our help in time.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because bluetongue affects ruminants (e.g. cattle, sheep and goats). since the beginning of the 21st century, a number of outbreaks have occurred in many member states, including those in central and northern europe, resulting in significant losses in animal morbidity, mortality and disruption of trade in live animals. until now, the requirements for the control and eradication of bluetongue have been based on the practice of administering live attenuated vaccines, as these were the only vaccines available. possible adverse reaction to the use of these vaccines the virus contained in these vaccines may spread to unvaccinated animals. new inactivated vaccines have been developed over the last few years. unlike the ' live attenuated vaccines', these inactivated vaccines do not pose an undesirable risk of spreading the virus they contain and can therefore be used successfully in areas where animal movements are not restricted. the adoption of this proposal would remove some restrictions which, in the light of recent developments, have become unnecessary. the new rules would allow member states to apply vaccination more effectively and to control outbreaks of bluetongue, as well as to reduce the burden of the disease on agriculture.
in writing. − i voted against the resolution on the lessons to be learned from the nuclear accident in japan on nuclear safety in europe. i voted against the resolution as a whole because, in voting on paragraph 5 of the resolution, the ep majority supported the second part of the resolution, which calls for a moratorium on the development of nuclear energy and the construction of new nuclear power plants in the european union. this provision was adopted despite the fact that my group european people's party (christian democrats) voted against it. having lost the vote on this most important issue, i could not vote for the entire resolution, so i voted against. otherwise, i would have voted against my country's energy strategy, which is aimed at energy independence. lithuania has been preparing for the construction of a new nuclear power plant for several years, and preparatory work has been underway for several years.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, although not all the s&d amendments were adopted in the vote. the text of the resolution contained provisions of particular importance concerning the planned construction of nuclear power plants in the kaliningrad region and in belarus. the resolution notes that there are significant problems in the field of nuclear safety standards and compliance with relevant obligations under international conventions. these problems are relevant not only to lithuania, which directly borders belarus and the kaliningrad region, but also to europe as a whole. the document also contains important proposals to ensure that the highest nuclear safety standards are met and to carry out comprehensive testing of existing nuclear power plants in the eu in order to assess the real safety situation of such plants.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the nuclear accident in japan has left thousands dead and missing, caused extensive material damage, and will have long-term consequences for human health. we are still feeling the effects of chernobyl, and today we need to re-evaluate our approach to nuclear safety in the eu and in the world. the completion of nuclear projects in belarus and kaliningrad presents major problems with respect to nuclear safety standards, compliance with relevant commitments under international conventions, as these problems are relevant not only to the member states directly bordering these regions, but also to europe as a whole. the eu and the relevant ec entities must necessarily act together in accordance with the principle of solidarity. the resolution on the eu's baltic sea strategy and the role of macro-regions in the future cohesion policy states that, in view of the planned development of nuclear energy in the baltic sea region, eu countries must adhere to the highest safety and environmental standards and the ec must monitor and control the observance of the same approach and international conventions in neighbouring countries close to the eu's external borders. nuclear power plants built at the eu's external borders must comply with international nuclear safety and environmental standards. the importance of energy efficiency and energy saving, renewable and sustainable energy, and the deployment of european-wide electricity grids has increased in particular today. it is also important to have a smart grid that can operate by drawing energy from decentralised energy production facilities.
