i am pleased to be here today to talk about the mid-term review of the seventh framework programme. many of the highlights listed in the document are very true, especially in view of the more active participation of young researchers and industry in the projects of the framework programme. the document expresses concern at the rather low participation of some member states. i would point out that there are objective reasons for this. the funding schemes in force today are in some ways more favourable to the old european union. the figures illustrate this. for newly acceded countries, the amount of funding per project participant from that country is twice as low as for former eu countries. this situation is creating a gap in the community and a segregation of new members, which i am convinced should not be the case. i therefore believe that it is necessary to review funding schemes and to ensure that no unequal or discriminatory conditions are left in place during the eighth programme in order to effectively address the challenges identified in the europe 2020 strategy.
i am very pleased with the document adopted today on impact assessment and its independence. impact assessment is the backbone of the legislative process. i believe that effective impact assessment independence must become a general principle applicable to all types of impact assessment, and this is particularly true of environmental impact assessment. the implementation of this principle should also be ensured in the environmental impact assessment directive, which is likely to be revised in the near future. i am glad that the proposals in the environment committee, the amendments to which i have tabled, reflect precisely the independent assessment of environmental impact, which is really extremely important. the european commission must also play a more active role in defending the interests of the european union and its member states in cases where projects by third countries may affect the european union, one or more of its members. i believe this document is a step forward in the direction of our common security.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the application of the schengen acquis in bulgaria and romania. i agree with the rapporteur that, although there are some outstanding issues that will need to be regularly reported and that will need to be followed up at some point in the future, they do not constitute an obstacle to these two member states becoming full schengen members. the integration of bulgaria and romania into the schengen area is of great importance both for these countries, for their economic growth and investment, and for the european union as a whole, in the interests of greater integration and solidarity between member states.
in writing. − cooperation on schengen matters was launched with the conclusion of the schengen agreement on 14 june 1985, which abolished the systematic internal border controls of the signatory countries and created the conditions for the creation of a common area in which the free movement of persons is ensured. the free movement is currently ensured in an area with 42 673 km of external sea and 7 721 km of external land border, covering 25 countries and 400 million citizens. bulgaria, romania and cyprus currently only partially apply the schengen acquis and therefore checks are still carried out at the border with these three member states. romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis in 2007 when they joined the eu. the european parliament and the council , having regard to the results of the evaluations and the re-visits of the expert groups, have concluded that, although there are some outstanding issues which will need to be regularly reported and on which further action will be required, they do not constitute an obstacle to these two member states becoming full schengen members. i supported the proposal that bulgaria and romania inform the european parliament and the council in writing within a period of six months of the further action it intends to take on the recommendations contained in the evaluation reports and those referred to in subsequent reports which have yet to be implemented.
in writing. − romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis in 2007 upon accession to the eu. the verification, by means of evaluation procedures, of the fulfilment by the new member states of the necessary conditions for the application of all parts of the schengen acquis (data protection, the schengen information system, the airspace border, the land border, the sea border, police cooperation and visas) is a precondition for the council to be able to adopt a decision on the abolition of internal border controls with these member states, in accordance with the act of accession. i did not approve this document as, in the light of the results of the evaluations and the re-visits of the expert groups, the committee responsible concluded that there are outstanding issues that will need to be reported on regularly and that further action will be needed in the future. it should be noted that the area comprising bulgaria, turkey and greece is the most sensitive point of the eu's external borders in terms of illegal migration. it is therefore necessary for bulgaria to take additional measures, in particular a specific plan setting out the actions to be implemented upon accession to the schengen area and a common approach (greece, turkey and bulgaria) to ensure the ability to respond to potential increased migration flows. i consider that the member states concerned should be required to inform the european parliament and the council in writing of the implementation of the additional measures and of any deficiencies within a period of six months from the date of entry into force of this decision.
in writing. − the abolition of internal border controls is of particular importance for the european union as a whole and for each member state individually. in order to ensure the effective functioning of the schengen area and the achievement of its objectives, it is necessary to ensure that the abolition of border controls does not have negative consequences, in particular in relation to illegal migration. each country must fulfil all the conditions of the schengen acquis without exception in relation to data protection, the information system, air, land and sea borders, police cooperation and visas in order to join the schengen area. it is also essential to ensure that each member state carries out strict and effective external border controls. i think that when romania and bulgaria will be able to become full members in the near future, they will be able to apply all the provisions of the schengen acquis properly. bulgaria should now be given special attention, as it is situated along the eu's external borders with turkey and greece. it is the most sensitive and vulnerable area in the union. in this context, it is essential that bulgaria and romania, upon becoming full members of the schengen area, are adequately prepared to manage the increased migratory flows, to be able to implement adequately and effectively the measures to combat illegal migration and to ensure the effective functioning of the external border control mechanism.
in writing. - i voted for romania and bulgaria to be admitted to the schengen area. after a thorough examination, the eu's responsible commission has recognised that these countries fulfil all the criteria for membership of the schengen area: they ensure the protection of national borders by land, sea and air sufficiently well, have an effective mastery of the schengen information system for the exchange of data and ensure data protection in a reliable manner. my group considers the introduction of new membership criteria to be wrong at this stage, as it would imply a double standard for these countries. the problems still facing romania and bulgaria - organised crime and corruption - are clearly a serious handicap for the governments of these countries, which should be able to combat these phenomena more effectively. however, i am of the opinion that the closure of the schengen gate for romania and bulgaria should not be a punishment for honest citizens, who would suffer the most if they were to lose the opportunity to travel freely in europe now.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution not only because of the importance of the upcoming 66th session of the un general assembly but also because it is vitally important that the eu finally steps up cooperation and coordination in this and all other un bodies. article 34 of the treaty on european union clearly stipulates that member states shall coordinate their action in international organisations and that member states, which are also members of the un security council, will concert and in the execution of their functions, defend the positions and the interests of the union. so far, cooperation was not exemplary in the un general assembly. neither was it in the un security council. we all know well that member states that belong to the un security council (france, the united kingdom and germany) failed to act in concert and come up with a single position vis-à-vis military intervention in libya, in particular with regard to the vote on the un security council resolution 1973. i would therefore urge eu member states to strive for a common position on issues vital to international peace and security, especially in areas where there is already a broad international consensus.
in writing. − the international order is undergoing a fundamental change and the european union needs to engage more actively with the world's current and emerging powers, as well as with bilateral and multilateral partners, to promote effective decision-making on issues of concern to eu citizens and the world. under article 21 of the treaty on european union, the eu is formally committed to an effective multilateral partnership, with a strong united nations at its core, as it is essential to tackle global challenges such as climate change and environmental degradation, the universality and indivisibility of human rights, poverty reduction and development for all, the consequences of demographic change and migration, and transnational organised crime. i agree that the eu should play an active role in creating a united nations that can effectively contribute to global solutions, peace, security, democracy and the rule of law in an international order.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it seeks to facilitate effective multilateral partnerships as a key strategic priority for the union and to increase the coherence and visibility of the eu as a global actor at the un, including through better coordination of eu internal consultations on un issues and the promotion of increased influence. cooperate also with the eu's strategic partners in the un system; and give the strategic partnerships a multilateral dimension, i.e. including global issues on the agenda of eu bilateral and multilateral summits, helping to increase the un's effectiveness and transparency and improving the management of un financial resources. in addition, it touches on the crucial aspects of strengthening the role of the international criminal court and the international criminal justice system, promoting accountability and ending impunity, strengthening crisis prevention units and increasing their effectiveness in the implementation of the united nations development programme, in order to make the united nations a global leader in crisis prevention and recovery, the eu and the un need to cooperate closely in the field of civil and military crisis management, in particular in humanitarian aid operations, the fundamental transformation of the international atomic energy agency (iaea) by eliminating its dual functions of monitoring and promoting the use of nuclear energy, and the limitation of the iaea's responsibilities for controlling the nuclear industry and monitoring compliance with the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons, as well as other important aspects that i support and support in principle.
in writing. − i voted for this proposal because it gives an extensive review of the current global issues in the eu and un, pointing out the challenges and the opportunities that the eu is facing. it has also addressed solid and far-reaching suggestions for the eu in various areas on the international level, such as engaging with the eu’s strategic partners within the un system, ensuring the important role of the eeas, enhancing peace, security and justice, and combating climate change. i believe that these are the issues that are critical on the global stage right now, and the eu has to involve itself and play a vital role in all these aspects. therefore i support this proposal and recommend to the council that it should give careful consideration to this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the mid-term review of the european union's seventh framework programme for research, technological development and demonstration. by adopting this resolution, the european parliament sends a clear signal to the european commission on the future implementation of the research programme. one of the most important proposals, which i also support, is the simplification of the administrative requirements for projects implemented under this programme. indeed, one of the difficulties identified is the complex and cumbersome administrative procedures which make it easier for researchers to access national funding rather than eu funding and make europe unpopular in research. it is also essential that research and development policy is implemented on a territorial basis in order to ensure a balanced distribution of research to all universities. the quality often achieved in cities could be ensured by strengthening intangible links, for example through regular videoconferencing and by cleverly linking territorial research centres with centres of excellence.
in writing. − the lisbon european council of 23 and 24 march 2000 set an ambitious strategic objective for the european union (eu): to become the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world by 2010. this strategy recognises the essential role of research. the seventh framework programme, with a budget of 54 billion for 2007-13, is one of the most important research support programmes in the world and is the main instrument of eu research policy. its aim is to enable the european union to respond to the major societal challenges that concern all member states and that cannot be tackled by a single member state (ageing populations and health, energy and water supply or food security, sustainable development, combating climate change, etc.) and to increase knowledge by enabling businesses to innovate more and increase their competitiveness. in this report, the european parliament carries out a mid-term evaluation to ensure that the seventh framework programme meets eu policy needs. i agree that in order to maximise the effectiveness of this programme, it is necessary to simplify as quickly as possible the complex and cumbersome administrative procedures in order to achieve the creation of a european research area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a proper mid-term evaluation of the eu's seventh research, technological development and demonstration programme is crucial to determine whether the programme is delivering on its objectives. it is one of the most important research support programmes in the world and is the main instrument of eu research policy. in addition, in many of the recent documents setting out its development objectives and guidelines for the next decade, the european union has stressed the importance of research and innovation in strengthening the eu economy and keeping it among the most competitive in the world. in addition to the generally positive assessment, the communication draws the commission's attention to a number of aspects of the implementation of the programme and makes specific proposals for improving them. for example, it is proposed to increase the funding of the programme, but at the same time it is proposed to identify which general research areas offer the greatest promise for specific application and where they can be most widely acted upon from an ethical point of view in order to achieve tangible results in the implementation of this programme.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution as it calls for the implementation of the seventh framework programme to take into account the different impact of the economic crisis in the final years of the programme (2011 to 2013) in each member state, as there is still a large amount (eur 28.8 billion over three years) to be planned, to be used to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and to be ready to implement the european research area and the innovation union initiative, and in particular calls for alignment of the objectives of the seventh framework programme with the eu's strategies on resource efficiency, raw materials and the digital agenda. the remaining amounts should not be deducted from the research area and used to cover expenditure on other programmes or measures not related to the research and innovation sector and to the objectives of the seventh framework programme. it is necessary to strengthen, promote and secure funding for the development of research in the european union by significantly increasing the related costs from 2013 onwards, as such increased funding, ideally through budgetary increases, should foster sustainable growth and competition through excellence. the approach needs to be combined with a more results-oriented, efficiency-oriented approach and radical simplification of funding procedures. i believe that there is a need to support further cooperation between eu research, technological development and innovation programmes and i believe that the continuity of the future programme once established is important for all stakeholders.
in writing. − dear colleagues, research and innovation are important for ensuring sustainable and inclusive growth in lithuania. according to a world bank study, lithuania has a high potential to become a dynamic, knowledge-based economy. however, the study also states that my country faces management, structural and regulatory problems in the research and development (r&d) sector. these obstacles must be overcome if we are to make real progress. this also poses problems for europe. r & d spending in europe is low compared to other global powers due to a lack of private investment and a favourable environment for innovation. i agree with the rapporteur that there is an urgent need for better coordination and co-financing of research projects within the union. in addition, research facilities and infrastructure in central and eastern europe need to be modernised and expanded. this will boost european competitiveness and help to overcome the infrastructure gaps between the old and new member states. i also believe that research and technological development must be made more accessible to ordinary europeans. according to a survey by the european commission, only 10% of europeans think they are well informed about science, while 65% think governments need to do more to get young people interested in science. we should do the same.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on eu-canada trade relations. canada is one of the eu's oldest and closest partners and was the first industrialised country with which the eu signed a trade and economic cooperation framework agreement in 1976. however, the potential of the eu-canada economic relationship is not yet fully exploited and i believe that an eu-canada free trade agreement can make a significant contribution to the development and implementation of this potential by improving trade and investment flows and removing maximum tariffs and unjustified non-tariff barriers and promoting closer cooperation, in particular in the areas of regulation, labour mobility and recognition of professional qualifications. i welcome an agreement with canada that goes beyond wto commitments and complements multilateral rules, provided that negotiations reach a harmonised, ambitious and high-quality agreement that goes beyond tariff reductions and includes other measures such as the application of the principle of reciprocity in conjunction with existing legal instruments in trade disputes, improves the protection of intellectual property rights, including the protection of trademarks, patents and geographical indications.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. canada is one of the eu's oldest and closest partners and was the first industrialised country with which the eu signed a trade and economic cooperation framework agreement in 1976. over a long period, a number of bilateral agreements have been signed to facilitate closer trade relations, and the eu is now canada's second largest trading partner and the second largest source of foreign direct investment in canada. i agree that the potential of the eu-canada economic relationship is not yet fully exploited . the proposed free trade agreement could make a significant contribution to the development of the economic partnership and would be a clear growth-enhancing signal to investors and businesses in the eu and canada.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the eu and canada have close trade and foreign direct investment relations. the negotiations on a comprehensive economic and trade agreement aim at a very advanced agreement, going beyond any trade and economic agreement between the eu and canada that has been concluded so far, and further accelerating the already vibrant bilateral trade and investment relationship. i supported the view that an agreement with canada that goes beyond wto commitments and adds multilateral rules provided that a negotiated agreement is reached that is coherent, ambitious and of high quality. it is considered that the agricultural chapters will be an important issue for both sides in these negotiations. the potential for significant concessions in the areas of genetically modified products, milk and labelling of origin is a matter of concern. therefore, the interests and priorities in the field of agriculture should be fully taken into account, the agreement should benefit eu and canadian consumers as well as the agricultural sector of both countries, and, by achieving a coordinated overall outcome, ensure greater but fair competition in the supply of agricultural products from eu and canadian suppliers. i welcome the initial commitment by both parties not to maintain, introduce or reintroduce export subsidies on traded agricultural products as a positive step in the ambitious and fair negotiations and the agreement to cooperate in the wto negotiations on agriculture.
in writing. − the agreement will stimulate and accelerate active bilateral trade and investment links. the liberalisation of trade relations will bring mutual benefits to business entities and create more favourable investment conditions. in order to achieve a comprehensive and high-quality agreement that goes beyond wto commitments, both parties should not impose requirements that run counter to their internal policies or institutional arrangements. in addition, the principle of reciprocity should be applied in cases of trade disputes, the protection of intellectual property rights should be improved and mutual access to the market for services and public procurement should be granted. particular attention should be paid to the agricultural sector and consumers. we must maintain a firm stance on genetically modified products and milk and on labelling of origin. fair and increased competition between suppliers of agricultural products must be ensured. i believe that the commission should only start investment negotiations with canada after parliament has expressed its position on the future common eu investment policy. the most vulnerable sectors of both countries must be protected from falling within the scope of the investment agreements. the commission must maintain a firm position on the ban on seal products and canada should withdraw its request to the wto to establish a formal dispute settlement group on this issue. such a requirement is not in line with the principles of a positive commercial relationship.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on credit rating agencies: the future. the ratings issued by credit rating agencies serve a number of useful functions: they provide information on the creditworthiness of issuers in a global environment. ratings allow issuers to assess the situation in global and local markets, reduce information costs and broaden the circle of potential investors, thereby providing liquidity to markets and helping to set prices. the recent financial crisis has highlighted three problems in the sector: a lack of competition, an over-reliance on external ratings in the regulatory process and the lack of legal responsibility of credit rating agencies for ratings. i agree with the rapporteur that credit ratings are not just opinions and that credit rating agencies should be responsible for their ratings. therefore, in order to anticipate a tangible threat, the civil liability of credit rating agencies should be increased.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. rating agencies not only rate private equity firms and their products, but also countries. the rating of a country depends on the conditions under which it can expect to borrow on international markets. in the face of negative ratings and financial difficulties, the country is entering a debt spiral, as a falling rating makes borrowing more expensive and thus further complicates the state's financial situation. all market participants and market surveillance authorities should be aware of the criteria for determining the ratings and should be able to verify them themselves. the commission is invited to work with the g20 countries to develop a new global valuation methodology that would reduce the likelihood of errors, regulate the activities of rating companies and reduce the risks associated with financial valuation. i agree with the proposal that europe needs to establish its own credit rating agency as soon as possible, with objective and independent assessments. i support the call in the communication for the creation of its own independent rating agency, which is proposed to be called the european credit rating fund in the first stage. the success of the reform of financial valuation will depend not only on the ability of all eu member states to borrow on fair terms on international markets, but also on the stability of the global financial system as a whole and on the effectiveness of crisis prevention.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the credit rating sector faces a number of problems, the most important of which are competition, lack of accountability and transparency and oligopolistic structures. the problem of the dominant rating agencies in particular is the payment model, and the main problem of the regulatory system is the over-reliance on external credit ratings. as you know, credit rating agencies evaluate three different sectors: public sector, corporate and structured finance. therefore, an unavoidable conflict of interest arises if market participants carry out an internal credit risk assessment relating to their own regulatory capital requirements. i believe that the responsibilities, capacity, powers and resources of supervisory authorities, the monitoring, evaluation and oversight of the adequacy of internal models, and the establishment of risk mitigation measures need to be increased. i believe that credit ratings should facilitate the objective of informing the market in such a way that investors receive a comprehensive assessment of credit risk across all sectors and countries, that it is important to allow consumers to have better oversight of credit rating agencies and that the key role of greater transparency in their activities should be emphasised in this regard. i am convinced that the creation of new credit rating agencies should be supported and that the possibility of distortion of competition should be avoided.
in writing. - i support this resolution on the future prospects of credit rating agencies. the credit rating sector is frequently confronted with problems of competition, lack of accountability and transparency, and oligopolistic structures. in this context, the commission should consider the possibility of establishing a completely new independent european credit rating fund, which would have the right to participate in decisions on sovereign debt ratings and credit rating agencies. the management, staff and governance structure of this fund would be fully independent and autonomous. i support the proposal to establish eu-wide civil liability for credit rating agencies in cases of gross negligence or misconduct. in addition, the capacity of supervisory authorities, their responsibilities, powers and resources to monitor, assess and monitor the adequacy of internal models and to establish risk mitigation measures and to carry out investigations and inspections must be strengthened. a level playing field for credit rating agencies is essential to promote competition, transparency and the openness and stability of markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the external dimension of social policy promoting labour and social standards and on european corporate social responsibility. it should be noted that the external dimension of social policy covers eu activities and initiatives aimed at promoting labour and social standards in third countries. this includes the access of men and women to decent and productive work in conditions of freedom, equality, security and dignity. international labour standards should, in particular, help to ensure the development of the individual as a human being. people are not commodities to be negotiated. work is part of our daily lives and is essential to personal dignity, well-being and development. the eu has a good reputation in the field of international social dialogue. in this respect, it is considered a sensitive and reliable partner. this must be used to achieve the more ambitious objectives set by the eu. one of them is to develop a coherent, integrated and professional eu approach to the external dimension of social policy. the main activities are coordinated by the european parliament, but also in conjunction with the european commission and the newly established external action service.
in writing. − the external dimension of social policy covers eu activities and initiatives aimed at promoting labour and social standards in third countries. the eu has set itself the goal not only of becoming a model for corporate social responsibility (csr), but also of promoting csr in its external policy. non-compliance with key international social standards is a form of social and environmental dumping that is damaging to european businesses and workers. i agree with the need to strengthen the role of the relevant international institutions, such as the international labour organisation (ilo), the world trade organisation (wto), the organisation for european cooperation and development (oecd) and the united nations, and to encourage their cooperation in the development, implementation and enforcement of key international social standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because there are still cases of inadequate or partial implementation of the conventions and agreements of the international labour organisation and of breaches of the principles of corporate social responsibility. international labour standards should, in particular, help to ensure the rights of workers, as work is part of our daily lives and is essential for the dignity, well-being and development of the individual. alongside social standards, corporate social responsibility should contribute to sustainable growth, but companies should not avoid dialogue with workers and should respect and promote decent employment relations, encourage workers' participation through consultation and information, collective bargaining, the development of their professional skills and lifelong learning, adhere to safety standards at work, promote equality between men and women, create an enabling environment for the social partners to anticipate and manage labour market developments, including restructuring, improve the quality of work, integrate and protect vulnerable groups of workers such as young people, older people, disabled people and migrants. the european union should therefore continue to apply sanctions and incentives in bilateral and regional agreements in order to ensure the implementation of the social provisions of eu agreements. it is also essential that governments themselves do not abdicate their responsibility for preserving the european social model, otherwise there is a risk of privatisation of labour law and social security systems and services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because, at the beginning of the new century, the eu changed its strategy on the external dimension of social policy and adopted a softer approach, focusing on international cooperation and dialogue rather than social standards linked to trade agreements. the eu uses a variety of instruments to implement its social policy in third countries. these are legally binding, legally non-binding and financial instruments. the use of these instruments is evidence that the eu expects a certain behaviour in its relations with its trading partners. however, the implementation and application of these measures in the partner countries is a major obstacle. it is therefore necessary that the eu makes greater efforts to apply and implement them, in particular the ilo conventions and the principles of corporate social responsibility. the legal framework of the country often impedes this, but weak political will and internal economic pressures also play a role. another important factor is that workers are not aware of their rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on european cooperation in vocational training in support of the europe 2020 strategy. the opportunity and ability to learn and work in an international environment is an important prerequisite for a successful professional life in a globalised economy. there is an increasing need for workers who are mobile, flexible and experienced in an international environment. this is why urgent action is needed, especially in the context of young people. the increasing rate of youth unemployment is one of the most urgent problems in europe. member states are required to implement a targeted policy strategy in the fight against poverty, taking into account national characteristics and needs. i agree with the resolution that the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy to reduce early school leaving to below 10% and to increase university graduation to 40% need to be achieved through concrete, creative and effective means. with demographic change increasing the demand for continuing training and the need for lifelong learning, it is necessary to provide workers with a tool to enable them to define and plan their own needs for continuing training. in addition, access to finance for people in different life situations and specific groups of people in the field of vocational training and education must be made broad, simplified and more accessible, through all lifelong learning programmes and the erasmus for young entrepreneurs project. we must ensure that europe's workers are able to adapt to the demands of the economy.
in writing. − the opportunity and ability to learn and work in an international environment is an important prerequisite for a successful professional life in a globalised economy. there is an increasing need for workers who are mobile, flexible and experienced in an international environment. the key issues listed in the europe 2020 strategy for smart growth (promoting knowledge, innovation, education and the digital society), sustainable growth (production with better resource efficiency and thus increased competitiveness) and inclusive growth (increasing employment, improving skills and fighting poverty) also need to be addressed through specific measures in the field of vocational training and education at european union level and in the member states. action is urgently needed, especially in view of the increasing rate of youth unemployment. not only are young workers more likely to be unemployed than older workers, but their employment relationships are more temporary, their wages are lower, and their social security coverage is lower. i agree that the eu institutions should take a more pragmatic, comprehensive and ambitious initiative, endorsed by all member states, aimed at integrating vocational education and training, vocational skills, lifelong learning, traineeships and the labour market, in order to fully implement the flagship initiative 'agenda for new skills and jobs' under the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i agree that, in the face of demographic change and increasing life expectancy, the need for as diverse a range of work experience as possible and the need for lifelong retraining and development is already a necessity. for these reasons, the report highlights the need to modernise both initial and continuing vocational education and training, proposes an assessment of the propensity for certain professions at the end of basic education and stresses the importance of initial teacher training. it also stresses the need to promote more effective cooperation between institutions, agencies, research centres and enterprises at local and regional levels in order to change the closed nature of education systems and to eliminate the gap between knowledge and skills and labour market needs. i agree that in order to create a more modern training and education, the link between potential employers and training institutions needs to be strengthened, and that involving the social partners in the design of training programmes would be another step towards greater employment in europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because europe needs to act with urgency, especially with regard to young people. not only are young workers more likely to be unemployed than older workers, but they are also more likely to have precarious and temporary employment relationships, lower wages and poorer social security coverage. member states are required to implement a targeted policy strategy in the fight against poverty, taking into account national characteristics and needs. the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy to reduce early school leaving to below 10% and to increase the number of graduates at university level to 40% need to be achieved through concrete, creative and effective means. vocational training and training must be a long-term common political priority and its implementation requires the involvement and commitment of all stakeholders: not only the eu institutions and the member states, but also local and regional stakeholders should contribute to the achievement of these objectives. we must ensure that europe's workers are able to adapt to the demands of the economy. policy makers need to enable people to develop and acquire more skills. skills development should not be seen as a mere means of getting a better job, but should enable people to shape the jobs of the future and thus actively contribute to the development of an innovative economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because cooperation at european union level in the field of vocational training is a crucial factor in achieving the europe 2020 goals and reducing youth unemployment. i support the proposal that each member state should pay particular attention to low-skilled people, migrants, ethnic minorities, disabled people and other socially vulnerable groups in the design of its vocational training and education system. learning programmes should be geared to their needs and level of ability. in addition, there is a need to promote closer cooperation between the different education systems in the member states in order to ensure the integration of young people, to promote lifelong learning and formal and non-formal learning. in order to ensure that vocational training meets the needs of the labour market, i believe it is appropriate to include data on labour market developments in national education strategies and programmes. the commission has a major role to play in this area, providing information on the skills and training needs of individual regions and on developments in the eu labour market. it is also essential to create a favourable business environment for companies that cooperate in the development and implementation of vocational training programmes.
in writing. − colleagues, one of the main reasons why lithuania has such a shockingly high youth unemployment rate (34%) is the disproportion between the skills of young people and the needs of the labour market. in 2010, 52% of all unemployed young people (50 000) who registered on the lithuanian labour exchange had no vocational training. the inability of young people in my country to find suitable work is causing a large wave of youth emigration - every second lithuanian who has emigrated in the last few years has been between 20 and 34 years old. the need for a mobile and flexible workforce is growing, and we need to help european workers adapt to the needs of the economy by giving them the opportunity to upgrade their skills and knowledge. it is important that vocational training is accessible to all. i am glad that the rapporteur understands this. esf funding could be invaluable in helping to provide training to the marginalised sections of lithuanian society. it is also time for the eu to use effective and creative means to achieve the europe 2020 goals of reducing the number of out-of-school children to 10% and ensuring that 40% of young people have access to higher education.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on ensuring independent impact assessments. i agree with the rapporteurs that impact assessment is a key legislative tool that european legislators should make more use of in the future. the impact assessment shows the legislator the possible consequences of its options and helps to take a decision. impact assessment can therefore make a significant contribution to better regulation. however, it does not in any way replace the political discourse and the decision-making process of a democratic and legitimate legislator. it should be noted that impact assessment only contributes to the specific content of a policy decision. it is important that the impact assessment is carried out in full independence and transparency and that the consequences for small and medium-sized enterprises are taken into account. the european parliament can already use its impact assessment and scrutinise the commission's impact assessment. however, this procedure has so far been used very rarely. i agree with the position expressed in the resolution that the european parliament must make more active use of the rights it has been granted in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. impact assessment (ia) is a key tool in the development of legislation, which shows the legislator the possible consequences of its options and helps to make a decision, and which european legislators should make more use of in the future. the eu can make a significant contribution to better regulation. i agree that it is necessary to involve external experts and stakeholders from all affected policy areas in the impact assessment process in order to ensure the independence and objectivity of the study being carried out.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i agree that it is very important to continuously improve the quality of eu legislation, and it is this report that sets out concrete proposals for improving the legislative process both in the european parliament and in the commission. the commission has been carrying out impact assessments for some time before submitting proposals for draft legislation to the european parliament and the council, but the report states that these impact assessment procedures still need to be significantly improved. for example, the independence of the impact assessment board, which is currently subordinate to the president of the commission, should be strengthened. the report also calls for the european parliament and its committees to carry out more frequent impact assessments of draft legislation and to examine more closely the impact assessments carried out by the commission, which it says still often serve more to justify a legislative proposal than to consider facts objectively. this prior impact assessment of proposed eu legislation was further strengthened by the lisbon treaty, which included provisions on the social and environmental impact of any proposed legislation.
in writing. − i supported this report because impact assessment (ia) is a key legislative tool that european legislators should make more use of in the future. the benefits of the ip are clear. the ip shall demonstrate to the legislator the possible consequences of its operational possibilities and assist in decision-making. the eu can therefore make a major contribution to better regulation. however, the goc does not in any way alter the political discourse and the decision-making process of a democratic and legitimate legislator. the ip only contributes to the elaboration of the specific content of the political decision. the draft report is divided into four parts. in particular, common requirements are established for the ce at european level. the second part of the report discusses the impact assessment of the european commission and shows the possibilities for improving the situation. the third part is devoted to the ip carried out by the european parliament. the fourth and final part calls for the establishment of an autonomous mechanism for the ep's pa in the european parliament, which should be used by all parliament's committees to further improve legislation and build links.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the green paper from the commission on policy options for progress towards a european contract law for consumers and business. contract law determines and organises transactions within the internal market, its potential for both hindering and facilitating those transactions is therefore obvious. choosing the right way forward in the area of contract law can make a significant contribution to improving the functioning of the internal market and opening up its full potential for businesses, in particular smes, and consumers. the potential benefits of european contract law to the internal market have been discussed for a many years. the ep pronounced itself for the first time on the issue in 1989 and with this resolution which the ep adopted today, it intends to respond to the recent commission green paper on european contract law, and to set out the parliament's priorities in this area. i support the view of the rapporteur that the option of setting up an optional instrument (oi) for european contract law by virtue of a regulation is to be favoured. it could be complemented by a "toolbox" for commission and legislator which should be implemented by an interinstitutional agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in the wake of the global financial crisis, it is essential to unlock the full potential of the internal market and thus contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. today, the single market remains fragmented for a number of reasons, including the failure to implement the existing single market legislation. consumers lack confidence in crossborder trade and businesses face significant administrative and legal difficulties when expanding their activities in other eu member states. differences in national contract law lead to additional transaction costs, legal uncertainty for businesses and insufficient consumer confidence in the internal market. partly for these reasons, consumers and businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) with limited resources, avoid international transactions, which prevent the creation of a competitive internal market. i support the call in the report for action and for proposals to harmonise contract law practices at eu level to ensure a level playing field and a fair playing field for market participants.
in writing. − if you have i abstained in voting in favour of this report because, although, according to the rapporteur, one of the most obvious obstacles faced by consumers and smes in the single market is the complexity of contractual relationships. it is therefore proposed to create a common european contract law which would benefit consumers and help to ensure more active cross-border trade in the internal market. according to the rapporteur, all parties to contracts, whether in business-to-business transactions or in consumer-to-business transactions, should be free to choose whether to apply the bcp as an alternative to national or international law (optional application). more attention should be paid to the objective of ensuring that the application of the ttber protects consumers and small enterprises, taking into account their position as the weaker partner in commercial relations, and to preventing any confusion in the choice of the applicable law. i abstained because the eu recently adopted a regulatory instrument in this area, rome i, which protects consumer rights well, and this proposal is based on the uk situation only, which would only cause confusion and increase bureaucracy.
in writing. − a uniform contract law regime must apply in the european union. in particular, to remove barriers related to the complexity of contractual relationships that consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises often face. moreover, the common european contract law ensures more active cross-border trade in the internal market. the current roma i regulation is a sufficient regulatory instrument, providing a high degree of protection for the weaker party to the contract. the provisions of this regulation provide protection for consumers wishing to have recourse to their remedies against an undertaking of another member state with which they have concluded a contract. given that the european union already has a legal regulatory mechanism in place and working effectively in this area, i do not support this resolution on the political options for the creation of a european contract law for consumers and businesses, which proposes the adoption of a new regulation establishing a new optional measure applicable to business-to-business transactions and to consumer-to-business transactions. it is to be noted that the new regulation would create a lot of confusion and uncertainty in this area. in addition, additional funds and a more bureaucratic mechanism should be allocated for its implementation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on gdp and other indicators to measure progress in a changing world. gdp is an indicator of economic market activity, which is used as a standard criterion by policymakers worldwide. it should be noted that gdp is measured in terms of production and does not reflect ecological sustainability, resource efficiency, social inclusion or social progress in general. moreover, gdp can be misleading because, following certain incidents, such as accidents and natural disasters, the remedial measures applied are treated as benefits rather than costs. i therefore support the resolution's view that additional indicators for the assessment of medium and long-term economic and social progress should be developed and that clear and measurable indicators should be established to provide information on climate change, biodiversity, resource efficiency and social inclusion. it is also necessary to develop indicators that better reflect the level of households: income, consumption and welfare. it is therefore important to develop a tool that complements gdp it should be designed in a way that is practical and uses clearly defined indicators and is based on high quality data.

madam president, threats to eu nuclear power plants, if they are real, are a question of life and death for thousands of people. even small nations must be prepared for the most severe circumstances, including terrorist attacks and airplane crashes. how would the citizens of major eu countries feel if a non-democratic country built an insufficiently tested nuclear power plant close to brussels, berlin, paris or london, without consulting its public or sharing reliable information with its neighbouring countries? lithuania is currently facing such a situation. in close proximity to vilnius, belarus – with a total absence of transparency – is beginning to construct a nuclear plant. it is vitally important that the eu, with the support of international organisations, extends the practice of nuclear plant stress testing around the world, and especially to its external borders.
nuclear safety is a matter for all states, whether they have nuclear power plants or not. of course, it is possible to be angry about what happened in the past, but today it is clear that we must move forward. it is very good, mr commissioner, that you have indeed responded promptly to the fukushima accident and initiated the issue of inspections of nuclear power stations, and it is also good that the member states have agreed to carry them out. however, there is no system at all for the construction of new nuclear power plants near the european union's border, as has been mentioned several times in connection with the construction of nuclear power plants in kaliningrad and belarus. i therefore believe that we must initiate and adopt the appropriate legislation as soon as possible to ensure that the question of the construction and operation of nuclear power stations is systematic, binding and based on clear principles throughout europe. in this way, we would have objective information about the potential threat and could hope to avoid it.
in writing. there is no doubt that the consequences of a nuclear power plant disaster are long-term, both for the environment and for people, and do not stop at national borders. three months have passed since the tragedy in japan, and the solution to all the problems is still not clear. the european commission responded swiftly and appropriately to the disaster: it proposed stress tests for all nuclear power plants, it sought tougher nuclear safety standards, and regular audits would strengthen nuclear safety and public confidence in nuclear energy. however, we are already seeing that stress tests will be difficult to implement even within the eu, despite the general recognition of the importance and necessity of such tests. we cannot think only of european nuclear security. if the kaliningrad and astravyansk nuclear power projects currently on the eu's borders are carried out without the highest international safety standards, not only will the neighbouring baltic states be threatened, but also the whole of europe, not so far away. the european commission has repeatedly stated that some of the neighbouring countries - ukraine, russia, sweden, turkey - are ready to join the european testing, but it is still unclear what concrete steps the commission intends to take to make the cooperation happen and what the situation will be with belarus.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the european parliament has received more than four hundred petitions concerning widespread misleading business practices by business directory publishers, which have a particularly significant financial impact on thousands of eu businesses, mostly small ones. this practice is usually accompanied by tempting offers to businesses, professionals and non-profit organisations to be included in business directories free of charge, although the subscribers only subsequently learn that they are contractually obliged to pay the corresponding fee. since business directory publishers are often established in one eu member state and have their business in other eu member states, it is difficult for them to seek protection or compensation from national authorities. while the european commission cannot require individuals or companies to comply with the provisions of the directive on misleading and comparative advertising, it is its duty as guardian of contracts to ensure that the directive is properly implemented in the member states. i agree with the call for the commission to take action to monitor the transposition of the provisions of the directive into national law and their proper implementation by the member states and to take corrective action, if necessary, to prevent misleading behaviour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as parliament has received more than 400 petitions concerning widespread misleading business practices by business directory publishers which affect thousands of businesses in the european union, mostly small businesses, with a particularly significant financial impact, and parliament continues to receive petitions and complaints about business directory publishers. this misleading practice usually consists of tempting offers to businesses, as well as to professionals and non-profit organisations, to be included in the business directory free of charge, since the subscribers subsequently find out that they have signed a contract for which a fee is payable. publishers of business directories are often established in one member state and have their objects in another, which makes it difficult for the latter to seek protection and/or compensation from the national authorities. the commission is invited to accelerate the work on the review and improvement of directive 2006/114/ec and other relevant legislation with a view to bringing an immediate end to misleading practices by business directory publishers, in particular by establishing a blacklist of misleading practices in business directories.
in writing. − i support this resolution because we must promote honest business practices and prevent the spread of misleading business practices. effective legal aid measures should be provided for that purpose. the commission has also found that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are in line with the market economy operator principle. the companies are given false business offers and are fraudulently forced to enter into unwanted contracts for advertising in business directories. in this case, the national authorities cannot provide adequate protection or compensation, as often the publishers of business directories and the affected business entities are established in different countries. this provides a clear opportunity for business directory publishers to exploit the situation. in order to put an end to such unfair practices as quickly as possible, the commission should establish a blacklist of misleading practices in business directories and adopt the relevant legislation, paying particular attention to the implementation of the provisions of the directive on misleading and comparative advertising. i believe that the national authorities of the member states must be given the appropriate conditions for cooperation to enable them to apply administrative or legal measures at cross-border level. only if these measures are implemented will the internal market of the european union be able to function properly, consumers be protected and businesses be able to engage in fair business practices.
in writing. − i voted for this motion for a resolution because it has clearly pointed out the current situation of misleading business practices, which are already against eu law, and that the international dimension of the fraud makes it difficult for the victims to pursue and fight against the fraudsters. i believe that vulnerable small businesses and professionals need to be protected from the misleading business directories, and thus the ep and the eu as a whole must show that european law is there for everyone to follow and respect. therefore, i fully support this resolution that calls on the commission to proactively verify member states’ transposition, implementation and national enforcement of directive 2006/114/ec and take corrective action where needed. the commission should also speed up revising and improving the directive and other relevant legislation to end the misleading practices of business directory companies as soon as possible.

today we are discussing one of the most important issues in european union policy, which is about ensuring the well-being of our citizens and the competitiveness and growth of the union as a whole. the past cohesion policy has been a driving force in ensuring greater integration and growth in the poorer regions of the european union and in significantly reducing economic and social disparities. today we have the europe 2020 strategy, which envisages an even greater role for structural cohesion policy in order to overcome the crisis and contribute to the well-being of our citizens. we will, of course, have to overcome many challenges related to globalisation, demographic change and conservation of resources. but to do so, we will have to tap the potential of all the regions of the european union without exception. i believe that the regional policy of the future should be linked to the main european objectives, i.e. innovation, research, environmental and energy challenges, and help to create european added value. but only with maximum transparency, efficiency and highly efficient control.
in writing. in preparation for the new funding period after 2013, we need to make concrete proposals for the financial perspective of the european union (2014-2020) on a common strategic programme to ensure the implementation of the eu's cohesion policy objectives and the effectiveness of the structural funds. in this difficult period, we have a good opportunity to use the time available for the forthcoming negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework to achieve more effective management and implementation of the eu's structural funds and programmes in order to overcome the effects of the financial and economic crisis. the european commission should increase its technical assistance to member states' and regional and local authorities and organise more training for them, in order to increase their capacity and knowledge of the rules applicable to the handling of implementation problems. in addition, member states should themselves prioritise investments in institutional capacity, simplify administrative provisions in order to reduce administrative burdens. i support the european parliament's call for the commission to develop a european multi-level governance guide and encourage member states to follow it, taking into account specific local and regional objectives, and to extend the application of cohesion policy governance tools (i.e. programming, financing and implementation based on national, regional and local partnerships) and to apply them to funds that will be included in the planned overall strategic programme, in order to ensure greater efficiency in public spending.
i am pleased that today we are talking about simplifying and making cohesion policy more effective. i have repeatedly said that the development and improvement of the quality of life of the member states supported by the european union would be more effective if the planning method were more effective and if the horizontal objectives were pursued using funds from different funds. however, the revision of the rules governing the funds themselves is equally important. often, a problem is not solved because of a lack of funds. although another programme pursuing similar objectives, financed by another fund, is not fully implemented. unfortunately, in this case, redistribution of funds between funds is not possible due to different rules. in this context, while supporting the need to introduce a coordinating mechanism with even greater impact, as set out in the resolution, i also call for the rules for the reallocation of funds to be amended to make them as flexible as possible.
the management of spent fuel and nuclear waste is of paramount importance for the safety of the environment and of both man and society. i therefore urge the council to take account of the opinion of the european parliament, which is playing an increasingly important role in environmental matters, when adopting the directive. it is regrettable, however, that in playing political games we sometimes want to include in documents various provisions which can have opposite results. some member states, when they came into being, brought with them to the european union the burden of nuclear power plants that were built against their will. one of the conditions for lithuania's accession to the eu was the closure of the ignalina nuclear power plant. the european union, for its part, has contractually committed itself to financing this closure. this eu commitment arises in particular from the fact that it is impossible for a state such as lithuania to finance all the work on the closure of the power plant alone. closure work includes the disposal of spent fuel and nuclear waste. therefore, calls to place this burden on the shoulders of the member states would have the opposite effect. without adequate funding, lithuania would not be able to provide security effectively on its own. on the contrary, the closure of the ignalina nuclear power plant must remain a concern for lithuania and the european union as a whole in the coming financial perspective.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the bilateral eu-canada civil aviation security agreement that is being negotiated will benefit the people of europe by facilitating trade relations between the two countries. the aim of this agreement is to reduce the number of double-checks, tests and inspections and to achieve mutual confidence in the eu and canada's aviation product certification systems. by harmonising the requirements and regulatory processes of both countries, the importing authority will be able to issue the certificate for the aviation product, part or appliance itself and will not have to repeat all the checks carried out by the exporting authority. the shorter, simpler and therefore cheaper product approval procedures will save both companies millions of euros per year, benefit airlines and make the canadian and european aviation markets even safer.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the main objectives set out in the negotiating directives were to reduce the number of double assessments, tests and controls (unless there are significant regulatory differences) and to achieve that both the eu and canada can rely on each other's certification systems. this could be achieved by gradually harmonising the two systems of requirements and regulatory processes, by continuing to consult both parties and by ensuring that the regulatory bodies involved in the implementation of the agreement remain adequately prepared and capable, and by establishing a joint committee to propose solutions to problems arising from the implementation of the agreement. to maintain trust in each other's systems, the agreement provides for joint inspections, investigations, exchange of safety data (aircraft inspection and accident information), increased regulatory cooperation at the technical level and consultation to resolve problems before they become 'disputes'. it is envisaged to establish a joint committee and sub-committees on issues such as airworthiness and maintenance. it also provides for strict safeguards which would ultimately allow either party to suspend acceptance of the conclusion of the other competent authority or to terminate the agreement in whole or in part. however, the whole system of consultations, committees and subcommittees is designed to ensure that all objections are properly resolved and not prejudged.
in writing. − the benefits of the ec-canada agreement on civil aviation safety are clear to both parties. it is noted that the eu and canada are home to the most important aviation technology producers. the trade and export volume of both countries in this area is huge. it is essential to ensure that certification schemes meet the requirements of both countries for effective cooperation in the field of aviation security. it is encouraging that an agreement was reached during the negotiations on the reduction of double assessments, tests and controls. i consider it appropriate to allow the importing authority to issue its own certificate for the aviation product, thus avoiding the duplication of the checks carried out by the exporting authority. the mutual recognition of maintenance and airworthiness and maintenance licensing only demonstrates the confidence of both parties in each other's systems. such an agreement will facilitate better cooperation between the regulatory authorities of both countries in all areas of certification, inspection and enforcement, consultation. the joint inspections, investigations and exchange of safety data will ensure the highest level of safety for passenger and cargo flights. it should be noted that the entry into force of this agreement will make product approval and licensing procedures more flexible, shorter and cheaper. all these conditions are lower than the costs of the companies in this sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because cohesion policy remains relevant, since it makes a major contribution to improving the social and economic environment. cohesion policy also aims to reduce disparities in the development of europe's regions, to help achieve modern and sustainable growth, and to demonstrate european solidarity. it has proven to be of crucial importance for the progress of european integration and for the interaction of european policies. it is clear that europe's regions have a number of economic, social and environmental differences. some of the differences arose from the last two developments, while others were exacerbated by the direct consequences of the global financial and economic crisis. member states have welcomed the new requirements and are making progress towards the objectives of cohesion policy, as evidenced by the facts and figures presented in the national reports, but there are still natural differences between countries and regions. taking into account that the european social fund is the main instrument for combating poverty, social exclusion and unemployment, gender inequality, social discrimination (for people with disabilities, migrants, the elderly, etc.) by ensuring people's access to employment, parliament calls on the commission to increase the potential and financial independence of the fund. in addition, project management should be simplified, procedures and controls harmonised and improved, and the monitoring of ongoing projects more effective.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the main objective of the improved european urban agenda should be to help develop and upgrade the infrastructure and services of european cities. future measures must be closely linked to the overall priorities of the european union in order to justify support from the eu budget. cities are the centres of economic activity, innovation and employment in europe, but they are also the source of many problems. complex problems such as the trend towards suburbanization, the concentration of poverty and unemployment in the suburbs or the increasing congestion of transport need to be addressed through complex transport, housing, training and employment programmes tailored to local needs. these problems should be addressed in the context of european regional and cohesion policy. in addition, the european commission should seek to harmonise as far as possible the rules applicable to individual european union funds and programmes implementing urban and local development projects, in order to minimise bureaucratic burdens and possible implementation errors. the commission should prepare a study comparing the latest integrated strategic planning experience of individual member states and, on the basis of its findings, develop specific guidelines for integrated urban planning in the european union, which promote effective and legally regulated partnerships, including cross-border urban partnerships.
in writing. − i have supported this document as it recommends that the urban dimension of cohesion policy focuses on three objectives: firstly, to help urban areas develop their core physical infrastructure, which is of particular importance for growth, in order to take full advantage of their potential contribution to european economic growth, economic diversification and energy and environmental sustainability, in particular to maintain and improve air quality in urban centres without damaging rivers. secondly, to help urban areas modernise their economic, social and environmental dimensions through smart investment in infrastructure and services, based on technological progress and closely linked to the specific needs of the regions; thirdly, to restore urban areas through the reuse of industrial sites and contaminated land, and to take account of the need to ensure urban-rural links in order to promote inclusive development in line with the europe 2020 strategy. urban areas are not isolated regional elements and their development must be closely linked to the surrounding functional, suburban or rural areas. i agree that the european commission should seek to harmonise as much as possible the rules applicable to individual eu funds and the programmes under which urban and local development projects are eligible for co-financing, in order to minimise bureaucratic burdens and possible implementation errors.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to strengthen territorial cooperation, which aims to encourage territories and regions to work together to tackle common challenges, to remove physical, cultural, administrative and regulatory barriers to this cooperation and to mitigate the impact of borders. cross-border cooperation programmes are also important for achieving efficiency and results in the implementation of strategies relating to poverty reduction and the integration of the most vulnerable groups into european society as a whole. in addition, the historical legacy of close cultural and linguistic links between border regions in different member states should be exploited to promote cross-border cooperation. better coordination between the management authorities and existing cross-border institutions, such as the euroregions, should also be pursued in the implementation of cross-border programmes, in order to ensure the quality, transparency and proximity of projects to citizens.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because territorial cooperation is included in the 2007-13 financial framework as one of the three pillars of the european union's cohesion policy, replacing the community initiative interreg. subsequently, territorial cohesion, like economic and social cohesion, was included in article 174 of the treaty as one of the three components of cohesion policy. territorial cohesion is now firmly established as one of the european union's top priorities. territorial cooperation should aim to remove physical, administrative and regulatory barriers between territories and regions and to mitigate the impact of borders between territories and regions, so that they can jointly address common territorial (services, infrastructure, urbanisation and spatial planning), common (globalisation, climate change), economic or social challenges. territorial cooperation and its role, which is crucial in strengthening the internal market and promoting greater eu integration in several sectoral policy areas, is beneficial for the european union, and i support the view that territorial cooperation should continue to be one of the pillars of cohesion policy.
in writing. − funding for territorial cooperation should be increased in line with its impact on cohesion policy. however, the budget increase for this programming period must clearly indicate the budget lines for the general cohesion policy for which funding will be reduced, without prejudice to the achievement of the objectives pursued by the cohesion policy. territorial cooperation removes administrative and regulatory barriers between territories and regions and helps to address issues related to territorial, economic and social cohesion. in addition, cooperation between border regions must remain a priority compared to cooperation in other areas. in view of this, the funding for its implementation should be increased. i think that the geographical limit of 150 km should be more flexible for coastal and maritime regions. the development and implementation of large-scale strategies must take account of the different regional cooperation programmes. in addition, the commission should assess the results of the first macro-regional strategies implemented. territorial cooperation is closely linked to europe's external borders, which requires better interaction between the erdf and other cooperation instruments, facilitating financing opportunities and implementing the new neighbourhood policy. it should be noted that the implementation of territorial cooperation programmes is currently complicated by the fact that many different institutions are involved in their implementation. it is also necessary to simplify the rules on auditing and control.
