in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the more rational use of expenditure requires more effective and efficient policies at the european union, national, regional and local levels. in addition, in the interinstitutional negotiations on the new financial perspective of the european union (2014-2020), the european parliament should make concrete proposals for a common strategic programme to ensure the implementation of the eu's cohesion policy objectives and the effectiveness of the structural funds. it should be noted that the economic and financial crisis has further increased the urgency of the application of the measures to the sectors supported by the european social fund, with a particular focus on employment, vocational training, social inclusion and poverty reduction. i would also like to emphasise that the european social fund, as a support instrument for lifelong learning, skills acquisition and career change, should be seen as a crucial (but still under-utilized) resource for promoting inclusive and effective growth and knowledge-based competitiveness in europe. it is necessary to aim at a more rational use of cohesion policy expenditure by reducing the fragmentation of funding instruments and promoting a greater complementarity between different funding instruments. in addition, the commission's proposal to achieve a better allocation of european union and national resources by priority and a better concentration by theme in order to ensure a more efficient coordination of eu funds should be taken into account.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this amendment because i believe that, following the financial and economic crisis in europe and worldwide, it is essential to review the issues of european macroeconomic development and fiscal discipline. it is a difficult but also a good time to complete and correct the existing model, taking into account past and present experience, and the european parliament is involved for the first time in these important decision-making processes. the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances is a new disciplinary measure for euro area member states that would introduce sanctions for fraud and failure to act on agreed recommendations without an acceptable explanation, but not for failure to achieve the proposed objectives. this disciplinary measure will take into account the entire burden of the fines imposed on the state and will set a ceiling on the total amount of the fines. the fines paid will become the revenue of the central fund of the permanent crisis management mechanism.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because this procedure should create an alert mechanism to detect emerging macroeconomic imbalances at an early stage. it should be based on the use of a benchmark and a transparent scoreboard with reference thresholds and an economic assessment. this assessment should take into account, inter alia, nominal and real convergence within and outside the euro area. in the event of a significant macroeconomic imbalance, including one that threatens the proper functioning of economic and monetary union, an excessive imbalance procedure should be initiated, which could include the provision of recommendations to the member state and the imposition of stricter supervisory and monitoring requirements, and the possibility of enforcement (sanctions) in the event of a repeated failure to take corrective action by member states whose currency is the euro. i think it is a good instrument to avoid macroeconomic imbalances.
in writing. − it is essential to establish an effectively functioning and fully-fledged mechanism for the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances, which would alert and respond to the threat of macroeconomic imbalances. it is essential that this mechanism is based on an indicative and transparent scoreboard. the commission, together with the council and the ep, is to prepare the abovementioned summary and the macroeconomic and macro-financial indicators for the member states. i believe that both euro-zone and non-euro-zone countries should, in the event of exceptional economic circumstances, be provided with symmetrical aggregates and thresholds for different indicators. in addition, the council should keep the council informed of the measures taken to suspend the excessive imbalance procedure in a member state. i support the proposal to empower the commission to carry out enhanced surveillance visits, during which contacts should be maintained with the ecb, the social partners and other national stakeholders. the risk of imbalances must be assessed on a continuous basis in order to prevent them from escalating, and recommendations must be made to the member states in a timely manner in order to eliminate possible disruptions to the functioning of economic and monetary union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this particular report on macroeconomic imbalances because it addresses the details about the current debt issue in some member states, and more importantly, it offers a progressive method to solve such a serious problem concerning not only short-term but also long-term consequences. i believe that europe needs progressive investment to help with economic growth and job creation, and therefore just cutting budgets could only undermine the entire economic and political system in the long term. as a social democrat who emphasises the fundamental social rights of the people and the long-term well-being of society, i support this proposal for its depth and comprehensiveness in addressing these issues.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because it contains provisions designed to speed up and clarify the excessive deficit procedure. the objective of the excessive deficit procedure is to prevent the occurrence of an excessive general government deficit and, if it does occur, to help bring it to an end as quickly as possible by monitoring compliance with the budgetary discipline criteria for general government deficit and general government debt. the rules on budgetary discipline should be strengthened, in particular with a significantly greater focus on the level and evolution of debt and overall sustainability. compliance with those rules and enforcement systems should be strengthened. economic governance should be carried out more actively and in a timely manner, involving the european parliament and national parliaments.
in writing. − the excessive deficit procedure needs to be made more rapid and operational in order to prevent excessive government deficits. i believe that the rules on budgetary discipline should be tightened up, with particular attention to the level of debt. in order to achieve the objectives set, the commission should be given a specific role in the areas of evaluation, monitoring and the development of recommendations. the commission and the council should also take into account the pension reforms implemented by the member state concerned in their assessments. i do not support the proposal to reduce the amount of the fine for member states that have not taken or have taken inadequate action or measures to control the deficit. i do not think it is appropriate to reduce the total annual amount of fines either, as the fines collected must be used to implement the stability mechanisms.
in writing. - colleagues, one of the things that the greek crisis can show us is the great need for fiscal responsibility. otherwise, all eu countries, not just greece, face serious problems, as two thirds of the eu countries have an excessive deficit. i am glad that the rapporteur has emphasised this. the communication contains more, but its main proposals are to tackle the excessive deficit and to shape the way forward. the report also touches on another important aspect: we must tackle the budget deficit without undermining growth, especially in the emerging economy. it is important that the system for managing public and private debt supports long-term growth. this would include improving investment conditions and the development of the internal market, while taking into account the specific priorities and needs of the member states. and above all, we need transparency, accountability and independent oversight. this is an integral part of the strengthening of the economy's governance. national budgetary frameworks should include the establishment and strengthening of independent fiscal authorities and ensure the publication of transparent fiscal statistics.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the economic governance package aims to meet the need for greater coordination and closer monitoring of economic policies in the economic and monetary union. it also sets requirements for the budgetary systems of the member states to promote fiscal responsibility by setting minimum requirements for national fiscal systems and ensuring that they comply with the obligations laid down in the treaty. the commission also proposed strengthening enforcement measures for euro area member states to support the preventive and corrective components of the stability and growth pact. i support in principle the proposal put forward to ensure the improvement of national fiscal systems and to encourage member states to take better fiscal decisions in the future. in particular, there is a need to provide proposals for improved reporting of fiscal data statistics in order to avoid a repetition of recent experience in some member states. proposals for independent budgetary services, national fiscal rules and the establishment of mandatory multiannual budgets should also contribute to greater fiscal stability.
in writing. − economic and monetary union must provide for effective and efficient coordination and surveillance of economic policies. to this end, fiscal responsibility of the member states should be promoted. it is necessary to set at least minimum requirements for national systems as soon as possible and to ensure the effectiveness of the excessive deficit procedure. member states must pursue prudent and targeted fiscal policies in upswing periods and build up reserves that may be needed in downturns. i support the proposal that the numerical fiscal rules of the member states with a derogation should specify the information related to the definitions of the target indicators, the scope of the rules, the monitoring and the consequences of non-compliance. i think it is appropriate to provide in the medium-term budgetary systems for procedures to give an opinion on the impact of the proposed measures on the long-term sustainability of public finances. it is also appropriate to provide for limitation of liability clauses to identify cases where the right to temporary derogation is granted.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because, under the preventive arm of the stability and growth pact, adjustment to and compliance with the medium-term budgetary objective should be ensured by imposing an obligation on a member state whose currency is the euro and whose progress in budgetary consolidation is insufficient to pay a temporary interest contribution to it. this obligation should apply in the event that a member state significantly deviates from the medium-term budgetary objective or the corresponding adjustment plan for achieving that objective and fails to correct that deviation, even if its deficit is below the 3% of gdp reference value. the required interest contribution should be reimbursed to the state concerned together with the accrued interest as soon as the council is satisfied that the situation giving rise to the obligation to make that contribution has been remedied. the non-interest-bearing deposits should be repaid when the excessive deficit is corrected and the interest and penalties collected on such deposits should be allocated to the stability mechanisms of the member states whose currency is the euro, which are established to provide financial assistance to ensure the stability of the euro area as a whole.
in writing. − i believe that member states which do not comply with the requirements of the union's fiscal system should be subject to appropriate financial sanctions. the penalties applied under the preventive and corrective arm of the stability and growth pact should be gradually differentiated. the proposed system of penalties will ensure gradualness and a level playing field between member states, as both the interest deposit and the non-interest deposit and the fine will be fixed at a level of 0,2% of gdp. in addition, the commission will be empowered to recommend a reduction in the level of the penalty or its lifting, taking into account exceptional economic circumstances. in order to implement an effective budgetary surveillance system, it is essential that the commission submits a report to the european parliament and the council on the feasibility of the introduction of euro securities. i do not support the proposal that the revenue from unused payment appropriations in the union budget be transferred to the union budget for the following year and be used for programmes implemented in accordance with the union priorities. i believe that the tax system must remain a national matter for each member state and that it is therefore not appropriate to oblige the commission to submit a package of legislative proposals for a comprehensive common european tax system.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because the economic and financial crisis has highlighted the need to reconsider the framework for economic and monetary union (emu) in order to strengthen the instruments available and to extend the procedures for coordination and multilateral surveillance. as the commission stresses in its explanatory memorandum, the system needs to be strengthened 'in order to consolidate macroeconomic stability and the sustainability of public finances, which are a prerequisite for long-term output and employment growth'. the economic governance package consists of six proposals to improve the coordination and surveillance of economic policies in the economic and monetary union (emu) in the context of the europe 2020 strategy and the european semester, a new cycle of surveillance combining the process with the provisions of the stability and growth pact and the broad economic policy guidelines. i think it is crucial to ensure that the strengthening of economic governance goes hand in hand with the strengthening of the democratic legitimacy of european governance. in this context, the role of the european parliament throughout the surveillance process should be strengthened. in addition, regular consultation of the social partners and the involvement of national parliaments are necessary conditions for a sound and transparent supervisory system.
in writing. − strengthening economic governance would be accompanied by strengthening the democratic legitimacy of european governance. we must make every effort to achieve macroeconomic stability and public finance sustainability. in order to ensure better coordination of the economic policies and activities of the member states, it is necessary to extend the procedures for coordination and multilateral surveillance. multilateral surveillance is required by the council and the commission to identify possible deviations of the budgetary position from the medium-term budgetary objective or from the adjustment plan envisaged to achieve that objective. the implementation of the convergence programmes and the economic policies of non-participating member states in accordance with the objectives of the convergence programmes shall be monitored on a regular basis. i consider that the five-month period for the member state to correct the deviation from the adjustment plan for the medium-term budgetary objective is sufficient. in addition, the actions taken by the member state to correct the deviation must be strictly monitored.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document as enforcement of the regulation on macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area should be supported by the setting of interest-rate deposits in case a member state does not comply with the recommendations and does not take the corrective action recommended by the council, which is replaced by an annual fine if it repeatedly fails to comply with the recommendations to reduce excessive macroeconomic imbalances. these enforcement measures are imposed on member states whose currency is the euro. in order to ensure a level playing field between member states, the interest rate and the penalty should be the same for all member states whose currency is the euro and equal to 0,1% of the gross domestic product (gdp) of the member state concerned in the preceding year. i believe that the commission should be given the possibility to propose a reduction in the amount of the fine or its abolition in exceptional economic circumstances, and that the power to take individual decisions on the imposition of the sanction provided for in this regulation should be conferred on the council.
in writing. − a better economic governance system must be based on a commitment by member states to respect established rules and policies and a stronger system of supervision of national economic policies at european level. a wide-ranging reform of the governance system is needed. in order to ensure that the provisions of the regulation on microeconomic imbalances in the euro area are properly implemented and achieve the objectives pursued, a differentiated system of sanctions should be established. as a result, interest-bearing deposits must be applied to a member state if it does not comply with the recommendations and does not implement the corrective action proposed by the council. when a member state repeatedly fails to comply with the recommendations, the interest deposits will be replaced by an annual penalty. i support the proposal that member states whose currency is the euro should be subject to the same interest deposits and penalties in order to ensure that all member states are treated equally. only a strong and independent commission can properly supervise and direct the new deeper and broader framework for economic policy surveillance. in view of this, the commission should be empowered to propose a reduction in the amount of the fine or its abolition in exceptional economic circumstances. the power to adopt individual decisions to impose a sanction should be conferred on the council.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it has done a great deal to simplify eu consumer protection legislation and to extend the rights of consumers shopping online. in addition to strengthening consumer protection, this proposal for a directive aims to remove unnecessary legal obstacles to businesses wishing to market their goods and services throughout the european union. some of the newly established consumer rights in online shopping are the possibility of beautifying the goods within 14 days of delivery, the right to withdraw from the purchase if it has not been delivered within 30 days of the order, the buyer will have to be informed of the final price of the goods. in contrast, the protection of traders and service providers is provided by consumer obligations such as the payment of the shipping costs for the return of the goods to the seller, while in the case of the provision of services the recipient will have to pay for the part of the service already provided.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the aim of the directive is to achieve a high level of consumer protection and thus to contribute to the proper functioning of the internal market by harmonising certain aspects of the laws and regulations of the member states relating to consumer and trader contracts. the most important aspects of the amendment of the directive concern distance contracts and contracts concluded outside commercial premises. the legislation will give consumers more control over their purchases, protect them from unfair practices, increase consumer choice and increase competition between businesses. it may also contribute to the increase of cross-border trade flows and the intensification of long-distance trade. this directive shall not apply to contracts for social services, for healthcare services, for financial services, for rights in immovable property, for the construction of new buildings, or to contracts concluded by means of vending machines or automated trading venues, or concluded with telecommunications operators for the use of public pay telephones, or for the use of a telephone, internet or fax connection for a single use by the consumer. member states may decide not to apply this directive to contracts concluded outside the trading venue where the amount payable by the consumer does not exceed eur 50. this directive does not prevent traders from offering consumers contractual terms that provide for a higher level of consumer protection than that provided for in this directive. it should be noted that the european consumer organisation supports this proposal.
in writing. − we must make every effort to achieve a high level of consumer protection throughout the european union. only by achieving this objective will the internal market be able to function effectively. in particular, it is necessary to harmonise the requirements of the laws of the member states relating to distance contracts and contracts concluded outside the premises of a trading venue. it is therefore necessary to lay down specific information requirements for those types of contracts in order to ensure adequate consumer protection. the implementation of these measures will give consumers greater control over their purchases. moreover, they will be protected from dishonest practices. consumer choice will be increased, business competition will increase, cross-border trade flows and distance trade will increase. it should be noted that member states are allowed to exempt contracts concluded outside the trading venue from the provisions of this directive where the contract value does not exceed eur 50 in order to avoid creating additional legal obstacles.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i believe that the new rules set out in the report provide clarity and set acceptable criteria for both consumers and businesses to transact online. i hope they will improve consumer protection and the functioning of the internal market while promoting crossborder trade within the eu. these changes are late the original directive provided for a digital revolution and consumers shopping online today are not well protected. the new rules are good news for lithuania, which has one of the highest internet penetration rates in europe. according to lithuanian media reports (verslo vikėė), the number of consumers shopping online in lithuania has increased by 73% over the past two years. the shopping list is very broad from tickets (32%), clothing, shoes, accessories (also 32%) to electrical appliances (23%). however, the improvement of consumer rights should not be limited to the internet. we need to reduce red tape and promote transparency in all areas of consumer rights. efforts should also be made to improve consumer rights awareness. eu surveys show that 7 out of 10 lithuanians still want to know more about their rights when buying airline tickets online, shopping online or facing additional credit charges.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it relates to emissions from agricultural tractors and only makes quantitative amendments to directive 2000/25/ec without changing the environmental objectives of the directive, the methodology or the period of validity. this is an urgent directive as it relates to a period which has already started on 1 january 2011, which is very important as it is expected to have a positive impact on the industry concerned. directive 2000/25/ec on emissions from agricultural tractors lays down maximum levels of carbon monoxide (co), hydrocarbons (hc), nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm) which may be emitted in combination with the exhaust gases of diesel engines of tractors. the directive sets maximum emissions for each type of tractor, taking account of engine power, and aims to ensure a gradual reduction in emissions in stages. it is important to support the adequate economic development of the industry concerned and at the same time to contribute to environmental protection.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution tabled. in order to achieve the environmental objectives related to emissions, i believe that the emissions of tractors should be determined in relation to the power of the tractor engine. this will ensure the effective implementation of the phased emission reduction. the inclusion of a flexibility scheme in the directive is welcome to facilitate the transition from one stage to the next. this scheme will be applied in the light of the uneven development of technology and the negative effects of the economic crisis. the interests of both eu producers and farmers will thus be duly taken into account. producers will not be burdened with additional workloads and will have sufficient time to adapt their production to the requirements of each stage, while farmers will be able to replace older tractors with new ones with less polluting engines. in view of this, i consider it appropriate to increase the current 20% annual turnover percentage to 50%. such regulation will create favourable conditions for the economic development of the industry, while preserving the current environmental protection programme.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the responsible management and disposal of waste harmful to the environment and to humans is of vital importance. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. in this report, the european parliament gave its general approval to the commission's proposal for a directive establishing an eu legal framework for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. the legal framework proposed by the commission aims to oblige member states to establish national programmes for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. the european parliament's report proposes the following improvements to the text of the future directive: it establishes the so-called principle of reversibility, which would allow access even to waste buried by deep geological burial, for example if recycling methods for such waste were developed in the future. the communication also proposes to impose stricter financial obligations on member states, obliging them to allocate the costs of possible waste management, as well as to finance reserves, and proposes a system for managing regional waste management projects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it sets out the eu legal framework for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste. the proposal sets out specific requirements to ensure that member states establish a national regulatory and organisational framework and develop appropriate national programmes for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste, from generation to disposal. the management of spent fuel and nuclear waste is of paramount importance for both environmental and public safety. but we cannot guarantee security without adequate funding, and i believe that the closure of nuclear power stations such as ignalina should be a matter of concern not only for one member state, in this case lithuania, but for all of europe.
in writing. − every effort should be made to adopt the safest solutions for nuclear fuel and radioactive waste management. the fukushima nuclear accident has shown that the disposal of radioactive waste remains a complex, risky process with potentially devastating negative consequences. nuclear safety assessments, tests and controls must therefore be carried out on a continuous basis. we need to exchange best practice on this subject on a regular basis across the eu. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected. it is essential that member states establish a national regulatory and organisational framework and draw up programmes for the management of spent fuel and radioactive waste from generation to disposal. in the interests of safety and economy, i believe that member states may share spent fuel and radioactive waste facilities, but only if both parties agree. this will allow member states to benefit from the favourable geological and technical advantages of the specific site and to share the financial burden of the joint project. it should be noted that spent fuel pools present high risks and hazards and all unused fuel must be transferred to dry storage as soon as possible.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree that demographic change, climate change and the objectives of territorial cohesion policy require a review and modernisation of the eu's common agricultural policy. the resolution adopted calls for the eu budget to maintain its current level of agricultural expenditure, but calls for the elimination of disparities in the allocation of these funds to the member states. the resolution proposes to introduce a system of incentives for farmers to develop organic and sustainable agriculture through the efficient management of limited resources and the reduction of the use of means of production. it is also proposed to differentiate payments between different agricultural sectors and farmers and to strengthen the bargaining power of farmers in the food supply chain. the paper also focuses on the impact of agricultural policy on reducing the differences in the level of territorial and economic development between the different regions of the eu, on rural development and on promoting young farmers.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because a sustainable, productive and competitive agricultural sector in europe can make an important contribution to achieving the objectives of the cap and the europe 2020 strategy as laid down in the treaties, and can also help to address new policy challenges such as food, energy and raw material security, the fight against climate change, the protection of the environment and biodiversity, health and demographic change in the eu. i welcome very much the commission's communication on the cap towards 2020. the future challenges of food security, natural resources and territorial balance are to be addressed. i believe that further cap reform is needed to respond to the changing nature of the agricultural industry in the eu27 and to the new international circumstances of globalisation. it is necessary to maintain a strong and sustainable cap in the future by providing budgetary allocations to achieve ambitious objectives while facing new challenges. the most important objective, i am convinced, is to ensure that aid is distributed fairly between the member states and the different categories of farmers. at present, new member states such as lithuania receive less financial support than the old european member states. i am convinced that the harmonisation of direct payments is one of the essential conditions for the creation of a single eu agricultural market. last spring, i joined a group of other meps in calling on the european commission, the council and parliament to harmonise direct payments to farmers in all member states.
in writing. − a sustainable, productive and competitive agricultural sector is the key to food security, natural resources and territorial balance. as the world's population continues to grow, the world's agricultural production will have to grow in proportion. we must therefore aim to create a strong and sustainable cap that responds to the changing nature of the agricultural industry in all member states. we need to take the best decisions to combat rural decline and to counter possible pressure on the agricultural economy from third countries. more attention should be paid to smes. the disparities between the granting of aid and the support to farmers must be eliminated. direct payments are a legitimate source of income for european farmers. the single payment scheme must therefore ensure that direct payments are distributed fairly and that a level playing field is created throughout the eu. each member state shall receive the lowest percentage of the average direct payments. to achieve this, it is necessary to set ceilings. it is essential that market regulation measures and intervention mechanisms are put in place to ensure fair prices for production and to provide farmers with a sufficient level of income to ensure continuity of production and a regular supply of food.
in writing. − dear colleagues, lithuanian farmers work hard and make a significant contribution to our society. however, there are limits to what they can achieve if local infrastructure and funding are insufficient. if the future cap is to win the approval of eu taxpayers, it must guarantee food security and jobs. the eu's agricultural budget should therefore remain unchanged. lithuania cannot afford to look to the agricultural sector. last year, my country's agricultural exports amounted to eur 2.6 billion, and farmers in lithuania account for 7.1% of the total workforce, compared to the eu average of 4.8%. the cap must help us achieve a competitive, sustainable farming and an active rural economy. according to eu statistics published last month, lithuania is still trying to catch up with the eu-27 with a rural development rate of 51.5% in the cap and 23.3% in the eu-27. we must continue to support our farmers in their efforts to modernise their farms. i support the rapporteur's call for a fair distribution of aid between member states and between different categories of farmers. the new member states, such as lithuania, now receive less financial support than the old member states.
on behalf of the s&d group. – mr president, after dealing with nuclear energy we are now broaching another sensitive subject: gmos. it is immensely tricky to find a perfect balance between those who would like to show a red light to gmos – seeing them only as a danger – and those who want to give them a green light, seeing them as cause for hope. the rapporteur, corinne lepage, has managed this delicate task very skilfully and prepared a balanced report, which received broad support during the committee on the environment, public health and food safety vote. at the moment, the member states and the council cannot find common ground on which approve or reject gmos. governments feel the scepticism of public opinion and try to transfer responsibility to the commission. at the same time, there is no consensus behind the removal of any safeguard clauses if member states decide to introduce them. the eu is, therefore, in a hypocritical situation where the council does not approve gmos, but some member states cultivate them. gmos approved for eu-wide use should be cleared for cultivation in the union, but they are banned in some member states. this report will bring more legal certainty for member states and could help to break the existing deadlock. usually our group is a proponent of a community approach, but in this particular case we should not have a one-size-fits-all policy. the inclusion of complementary environmental reasons – as well as a list of social and economic grounds for the restriction or prohibition of gmos by member states – will make this report more legally solid. this report should not in any way prevent member states from cultivating eu-approved gmos if they so wish, nor should it hamper research. but each country has to solve the problem of co-existence and take all necessary steps to avoid the unintended presence of gmos in their territory and in their neighbouring countries.
in writing. it is clear from the comments made by colleagues today that the european parliament has a strong and clear position on the cultivation of genetically modified crops in the eu member states. european citizens are also strongly opposed to the release of gmos into the environment . over a million signatures have been collected in favor of the cultivation of genetically modified crops. i think that the ep's position today is a good reflection of the mood in society. indeed, we still lack reliable, objective and unbiased data on the long-term environmental and human health impacts of genetically modified crops, and we must therefore respect the will of our citizens and allow member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the issue of labelling of gmo products is also of great importance in this context. these products and derived products are already on the market and it is therefore necessary to ensure the very clear and comprehensible labelling of such products, which has not been done properly so far.
we voted today on a rather controversial issue about the cultivation of genetically modified organisms. 61% of europeans are concerned about the consumption of gm foods, and an equal number of europeans are opposed to incentives to develop the production of gm foods. however, it must be acknowledged that a significant proportion, 21%, of the european population has a positive view of gmos and expresses the belief that they should not cause harm to future generations. neither the arguments for the negative effects nor the arguments for the positive effects, nor the arguments for the solution of food shortages by gmos, are fully scientifically based. this means that it is impossible to find a solution that is uniform for all countries. the view of the member states also differs, and the proposal to allow the member states to restrict the cultivation of gmos on their territory is therefore very correct. that is why i voted in favour of the corinne lepage report.
while we talk about the greater added value of cohesion policy for the european union and wonder whether some projects could not be implemented at national or regional level, we must also see the big picture. the reality is that many eu countries are still below the eu average. as a lithuanian, who has been supported to close these differences since joining the union, i see my country changing. the majority of new projects that improve the quality of people, whether in the environment, transport or social sphere, are implemented in lithuania with eu funds. nevertheless, we still have a long way to go before we reach the eu average. but it is not possible to do so on our own. this is why, even after 2013, the new member states of the european union must be guaranteed an adequate level of funding. this is the only way to ensure the balanced development of the european union by acting in solidarity.
i welcome the report by my colleague, sosa wagner, which is well balanced and comprehensive, and which also reflects important aspects such as the unconditional nature of the environmental impact assessment of new projects. the call for third countries to respect international environmental and other commitments in the development of new energy projects is also not forgotten. propose ways to move towards an efficient, co2-reducing and flexible european supernet. however, i would stress that in order to achieve an integrated and competitive european internal energy market by 2014 at the latest, it is not enough to implement legislation and ensure regulation properly. the full and efficient functioning of the eu internal market is not possible without the full integration of the energy islands into the eu energy system through new infrastructure connections. it is therefore necessary to carry out a rapid and consistent inventory of existing and missing infrastructure and to develop financial instruments to enable the objective of a physically integrated internal market to be fully achieved by 2014. infrastructure shortfalls should be one of the important criteria for determining the hierarchy of projects of european interest.

in writing. − national authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection legislation need to cooperate actively with each other, making better use of the possibilities of the consumer rights cooperation network. in particular, there is a need to provide the authorities with more means to effectively detect, investigate and bring to an end or prohibit infringements adversely affecting the common interests of consumers in cases of a cross-border nature and to prevent fraudulent traders. it is also essential that the eu-wide enforcement authorities establish common priorities and draw up multiannual plans. member states should make effective use of the consumer rights cooperation network to facilitate the exchange of information and the handling of requests for mutual assistance. only by implementing these measures will the objectives set be achieved and the public authorities responsible for enforcing consumer protection legislation be able to function properly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories. as meps, we are calling for transparency and stability, in particular with regard to those derivatives which are traded on stock exchanges and can cause massive disruption to financial markets. we are also calling for standard procedures, reporting requirements and the use of clearing devices via organised trade platforms. i support the rapporteur’s view that the volume of all transactions has to be transparent in order to ensure maximum financial market stability and enable supervisory authorities to do their work properly. it is important to stress that national supervisory authorities and the european securities and markets agency (esma) will be in charge of supervision.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because the financial crisis has raised the issue of the robustness and transparency of the otc derivatives market. the g20 agreed that, from the end of 2012 at the latest, all standardised otc derivative contracts should be traded on exchanges or, where appropriate, via electronic trading platforms, using ccp clearing. otc derivative contracts should be reported to trade repositories. this regulation lays down the conditions for the authorisation of ccps, the criteria for the verification of the proper clearing of ccps, the reporting of otc derivatives to trade repositories where the information collected may be used, inter alia, for systemic risk analysis. however, it should be borne in mind that any regulation should be applied with restraint. when regulation is insufficient, the market is threatened. when regulation is too strict, costs increase and, in some cases, prices for end-users increase. in some food and energy products, such effects would not be desirable.
in writing. − the otc derivatives market must remain robust, transparent and competitive. this is why it is essential to establish a balanced regulatory approach, since under-regulation threatens the market and over-regulation increases costs and even prices for end-users. ccp clearing can pose systemic risks, which is why it is essential that ccps have robust risk and default management strategies that do not pass on the risk to the taxpayer. i believe that pension funds with a low risk profile should be required to report and implement risk mitigation measures for otc derivative contracts that are not cleared by a ccp. the clearing obligation should apply as long as the net position and exposures in non-financial derivative contracts exceed the clearing threshold. it should be noted that in all cases we must ensure that disproportionate costs to pensioners are avoided. in addition, the european supervisory authorities should be given more powers, giving them the power to impose fines for infringements of this regulation.
in writing. - i voted for the report. directive 2002/87/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 16 december 2002 (the financial conglomerates directive) proposed supplementary and consolidated supervision of financial groups. the purpose of this supplementary supervision is to control the potential risks associated with dual use (i.e. re-use of capital) and the so-called group risks, i.e. risks of proliferation, management complexity, concentration and conflict of interest, which may arise when a single entity holds several authorisations to provide various financial services. all eu directives relating to banking and insurance activities aim to ensure the protection of customers and insured persons and to calculate adequate capital buffers for this purpose, while the financial conglomerates directive (fcd) regulates additional group risk supervision. i support the revision of this directive, which will help ensure appropriate supplementary supervision and close the gaps in supplementary supervision, as only european union legislation can ensure that financial conglomerates operating in several member states are subject to the same requirements and the same supervision.
in writing. −it is necessary to provide for additional supervision of financial entities forming a financial conglomerate in order to close the existing gaps. i believe that the powers of supervisory authorities should be extended at european level, giving them the power to supervise mixed financial holding companies in a similar way to the banking or insurance sectors. to this end, those supervisory authorities should develop common guidelines for the supervision of financial conglomerates. this will increase the transparency of the supervision of financial conglomerates. in order to ensure that citizens' interests are properly represented in this area, to ensure the smooth running of the legislative process, to ensure legal transparency and to allow for the swift verification of the compliance of national rules with eu provisions, member states are required to draw up and submit to the commission compliance tables showing the links between the transposition measures they have adopted and the eu directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it gives more powers to the new european securities supervisory authority. i believe that increased supervision is necessary in the sale of debt securities and certain credit obligations in order to avoid economic crises in the future. member states have adopted different measures as the union does not have a specific legal framework to address the problems of sales of securities lent. therefore, in order to ensure the functioning of the internal market, to improve the conditions under which it operates, in particular financial markets, and to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection, a common framework of requirements and powers should be established for the sale of debt securities and credit default swaps, and better coordination and consistency should be ensured between member states when measures are required in exceptional circumstances. it is necessary to harmonise the system for the sale of debt securities and certain aspects of credit default swaps in order to avoid the creation of barriers to the internal market, as it is likely that member states will continue to take different measures.
in writing. − i think that a common framework is very necessary in this area of financial markets. we must make every effort to reduce the risks arising from the sale of debt securities and credit default swaps in a consistent manner. it is essential that the sale of debt securities and the swap of credit default swaps are properly managed by the escb. to achieve this, the authority needs to be given more powers. it should be noted that credit default swaps in sovereign debt securities are a highly effective and efficient way to reduce the risk of various financial instruments. in this context, it is necessary to define objective criteria for market instability. there must be strict control and monitoring of the sale of securities to borrowers without agreement and a discipline in settlement, and no restrictions or requirements should be imposed on market makers in exceptional situations. only if all these measures are implemented will the financial markets function smoothly and achieve optimal results.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. directive 97/9/ec on investor-compensation schemes (icsp) was adopted in 1997 to complement the investment services directive, which was subsequently replaced by the markets in financial instruments directive (mfid). ten years after the entry into force of the iczm and following the financial crisis, the operation of the iczm was reviewed as the commission received numerous complaints from investors concerning the application of this directive, which sometimes resulted in very high losses for investors. the review of this directive should also take into account the objectives set at g20 level to close all regulatory and supervisory loopholes and to restore investor confidence in the financial system. the objectives of the proposal cannot be fully achieved by member states alone, as the current eu system provides only for a few minimum harmonisation principles, leaving member states free to develop it further. however, the problems encountered in some member states show that additional and much wider harmonisation at eu level is necessary to ensure that the eu achieves the objectives of the directive. the amendments to this directive will improve the proper functioning of the single market for investment services, enhance investor protection and investor confidence in the european union and establish common rules aimed at ensuring the harmonisation of system financing and day-to-day practice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document as the new eu legislation should increase the coherence and integration of the european single market, strengthen consumer protection, increase consumer and depository confidence and enhance financial stability. main objectives: to increase consumer protection through a higher level of compensation. better consumer protection and stricter common rules, in particular as regards the financing of systems at national level, need to be ensured. investors with investments in foreign countries should enjoy the same level of protection in all member states. consumer rights should be strengthened by faster and better payments and by ensuring greater protection. where an investment firm holds financial instruments on behalf of a consumer (customer), a system of investor compensation should be in place accordingly. it also aims to improve the single european market for financial services and to ensure the coherence of eu investor compensation schemes. this will enhance investor protection and contribute to a level playing field. there is a need for more and better harmonisation of eu legislation. establish strict financial principles for long-term investor compensation schemes. the contributions of schemes should be defined as general insurance arrangements and should not be so high as to constitute a tax or a payment of a fiscal nature. the systems should consistently apply a risk-based approach and the contributions should be calculated on the basis of the potential compensation risk incurred by the undertaking.
in writing. − the european single market must function harmoniously, its integration must be constantly promoted, consumer protection must be strengthened. consumers and depositaries need to be confident that they are operating in a stable financial environment. an effective compensation system is needed, and more stringent common rules on financing at national level. it is essential that investors with investments in foreign countries enjoy the same level of protection in all member states. i agree with the proposal that the level of compensation should be increased to eur 100 000. in addition, in cases where an investment firm or a third party becomes insolvent, it is essential to facilitate the return of financial instruments held by investors. in order to strengthen investor protection by creating a level playing field for investors, it is necessary, in particular, to improve the european single market for financial services, to harmonise eu legislation. it is necessary to establish strict financial principles for long-term investor compensation schemes, to reduce the contributions of schemes so that they are considered as general insurance arrangements rather than as taxes or payments of a fiscal nature.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because it is a proposal for a european society that is strongly opposed to the release of gmos into the environment and their use in agriculture. according to the latest eurobarometer survey, 61% of europeans think that the consumption of gm foods is a concern, and a similar proportion (61%) are against encouraging the expansion of gm food production. only 21 percent agree (and 58 percent disagree) that gm foods are safe for future generations. in no country does a majority of respondents agree that gmo cultivation is beneficial to their country's economy. moreover, there is not yet enough information and reliable scientific evidence to say that gm products and the food produced from them are completely safe for the environment and human health.
in writing. − it is essential that we work together to fight the release of gmos into the environment and their use in agriculture. we must give member states the right to decide for themselves whether to ban or restrict the cultivation of gmos on their territory. therefore, when adopting measures restricting or prohibiting the cultivation of all or of specific gmos, they should take into account factors related to the protection of flora and fauna, land use or town and country planning. in all cases, all factors shall be duly justified and the measures applied shall be scientifically justified or supported by arguments relating to risk management or other justified factors arising from the release of the gmo into the environment. in order for insurance to function effectively, member states should establish a common mandatory system of financial reporting and financial guarantees. i believe that studies should be carried out as soon as possible to determine the long-term environmental impact of gm crops and their possible effects on non-target organisms. in addition, the commission should make every effort to ensure that new gmo risk assessment guidelines are adopted in the near future, identifying the direct or indirect long-term effects and scientific concerns.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the drafting of the hungarian constitution lacked transparency and the new constitution was drafted and adopted in a very short time, leaving insufficient time for a comprehensive and substantive public debate on the draft constitution. in addition, the constitution has been widely criticised by national, european and international ngos and other organisations, the venice commission and the governments of the member states, as no political and social consensus has been reached on this crucial document. it is of concern that the new constitution does not explicitly enshrine some of the principles that hungary is obliged to respect and promote as a result of its legally binding international obligations, such as the prohibition of the death penalty and life imprisonment without the possibility of early release of prisoners on certain conditions, the prohibition of discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and the suspension or limitation of the exercise of fundamental rights by special decrees. i therefore support the european parliament's position that the new constitution and constitutional laws to be adopted in the future need to be thoroughly reviewed and analysed in order to verify their conformity with community law, in particular the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and the text and principles of the treaties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the constitution-making process lacked transparency and the new constitution was drafted and adopted in a very short time, leaving insufficient time for a comprehensive and substantive public debate on the draft constitution, and because a successful and legitimate constitution should be based on the widest possible consensus. the hungarian authorities are invited to address the problems and concerns raised by the venice commission and to implement the recommendations by amending the new constitution or by adopting future constitutional and simple laws. in the meantime, the commission is invited to thoroughly review and analyse the new constitution and constitutional laws to be adopted in the future, in order to verify whether they are in conformity with community law, in particular the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and the text and principles of the treaties. the drafting and adoption of a new constitution is a matter for the member states, and the existing and prospective member states and the eu must ensure that the content and procedure of the constitution are in line with the eu values, the charter of fundamental rights and the echr, and that the content and principles of the constitutions adopted are not incompatible with those values and legislation. it should be noted that hungary is a signatory to the echr, the international covenant on civil and political rights and other international instruments which oblige it to respect and apply the principles of separation of powers, balance of powers and promotion of democracy and human rights.
in writing. - the constitution the supreme law. it is a complex process. a constitution cannot be written in a day. this legislative process must be based on the broadest possible consensus in order to ensure transparency and to create the conditions for genuine political and social inclusion and a broad public debate. i believe that the hungarian authorities should take the recommendations of the venice commission into account and implement them properly in their own country's constitution. the basic law of the country must take due account of the social and political life of the country, and the rule of law must be implemented. it should be noted that tax and pension systems, family policy, cultural, religious, social and economic issues must be clearly regulated at constitutional level. it is essential that the constitution guarantees the protection of the political and civil rights of every citizen, guarantees the independence of the judiciary and prohibits the death penalty. as a democratic state, hungary must respect the territorial integrity of other countries by supporting hungarians living abroad. it is important to note that the new constitution of hungary must be in line with the values of the european union, human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the absence of a global agreement to ensure a level playing field for measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, some european industries will continue to face unfair competition unless specific measures are maintained for sectors facing carbon leakage. progress at the global level is the only way to tackle climate change, and the european union must continue to encourage its partners to deliver on their commitments. the european commission, for its part, should reorganise the eu's climate diplomacy, working with the newly established european external action service and the high representative of the union to develop a clearer eu climate policy, giving a new impetus to international climate negotiations and incentives to partners around the world by setting binding greenhouse gas reduction targets. i agree with the european parliament's call for the commission to come forward as soon as possible with a proposal to increase europe's climate change target to 30% of greenhouse gas emissions by 2020.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the 5th cohesion report and the strategy for the post-2013 cohesion policy. today, we members of the european parliament demanded stronger rules and more transparency for eu structural funds in the next financing period – 2013 to 2020. although the rules for using eu structural funds are already tough, it is important to find a balanced approach which helps avoid the misuse of eu funds and combats fraud. the european parliament is of the opinion that eu structural funds should provide greater support for border regions. i support the rapporteur in saying that more cross-border motorway connections, railway lines and shipping routes could provide a strong impetus for economic growth.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the importance of the european community as a whole will decline, as shown by the overall growth and population projections. today, the eu of 27 member states still accounts for 8% of the world's population, but will only account for 5% in 2050. its economic importance will decrease from the current 20% to 12% due to growth, especially in china and other important emerging economies. in order to survive in economic and political competition and to avoid a decline in prosperity due to the loss of importance, the european community of states must address the important issues of future security in a more concentrated way, and cohesion and structural policies will therefore have a key role to play in future competitiveness. future policy must be geared to growth and innovation, but it will be sustainable if regional policy objectives are linked to common european objectives relating to innovation, research and environmental challenges, and if the practical experience of richer regions is taken into account. it is also necessary to reduce regional and social disparities which prevent the eu from realising its full potential, since, despite the trend towards reducing regional disparities, large imbalances still persist, and in some member states, or even increase in comparison with others. i agree that cohesion policy must continue to focus on reducing regional disparities and on the harmonious and sustainable development of all regions of the union, regardless of the member state in which they are located.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because cohesion policy after 2013 has to take account of many important challenges, including social disparities in urban areas, demographic change and social exclusion. moreover, the economic and social imbalances of the regions, the geographical disadvantages of certain regions and the specific structural problems or the need to adapt to new challenges will continue to require a broad-based well-funded eu cohesion policy across all european regions. moreover, transparency of cohesion policy and its programming cycle, cost allocation and access to information for potential beneficiaries of structural funds is a key prerequisite for achieving the overall objectives of cohesion policy and should therefore become a key principle in the cross-sectoral cohesion programming and decision-making process for the next funding period. the open method of coordination should also be strengthened, and better cooperation and exchange of information between national, regional and local authorities on cohesion policy issues should be established.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the eu's cohesion policy has made a major contribution to productivity gains in all eu regions over the past and current support periods. the ex post evaluation shows a clear reduction in economic, social and regional disparities. these trends have a positive impact on social protection and investment in the environment. cohesion policy was conceived as a response to the single market and was intended to promote the development of an innovative and secure europe based on solidarity, taking into account the challenges of globalisation, demographic change and the conservation of resources, while the internal potential of all regions should be exploited to achieve higher growth and regional and social cohesion. cohesion policy is important to citizens because it brings europe closer to people's daily lives. the flexibility of cohesion and structural policies has been demonstrated in crisis situations and these policies have made a significant contribution to the various national economic promotion and upskilling programmes. european structural policy is a major contribution to the fight against the economic and financial crisis, and is generally aimed at innovation and the removal of obstacles, at encouraging european regions to improve their infrastructure, at increasing the regional innovation potential, and at promoting environmentally sustainable development. the economic and social imbalances in the regions, the geographical disadvantages of certain regions (especially the outermost regions) and the specific structural problems or the need to adapt to new challenges continue to require a broad-based well-funded eu cohesion policy across all european regions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as eu budget support is only granted to countries that meet the following three eligibility criteria: (a) a well-designed national development policy and strategy, (b) a stability-oriented macroeconomic system and (c) a sound and appropriate programme to improve public financial management. the aim of the document is to continue to support budgets in developing countries and to encourage the commission to assess the relevant indicators before granting aid. the aim of better coordination should be to optimise the allocation of resources, to increase the exchange of good practices and to increase the effectiveness of budget support. the union should recognise the additional benefits of having a high degree of political influence and the potential importance of its actions and use them to ensure that its political influence is proportionate to the financial support provided.
in writing. − it is essential to continue to provide adequate support to the budgets of developing countries, but the commission must carry out a detailed analysis of the relevant indicators in each individual case before granting support. in addition, in addition to financial support, there should be advisory assistance on technocratic public financial management to help promote internal development in partner countries. however, to achieve this objective, it is necessary, in particular, to clarify the criteria for the budget support in order to avoid possible discrepancies or misuse of support. attention is drawn to the fact that budget support must become the main form of assistance from the commission, and therefore a general objective for eu budget support must be set the assistance must ensure democratic accountability and prevent depoliticization, and the development policy measures applied must be in line with the principles of the rule of law and democracy. every effort should be made to ensure that countries with oil and mineral wealth have a transparent tax system to combat poverty and finance their development.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. under the lisbon treaty, the main objective of eu development policy is to reduce and eradicate poverty. the european consensus on development reaffirms the eu's commitment to eradicating poverty and achieving the millennium development goals, and to adhering to principles such as responsibility and partnership, aid effectiveness and policy coherence for development, which remain of paramount importance and must be guided by the objective of maximising the impact of eu development aid. i agree that european country strategies should be developed to better coordinate the actions of the commission and the member states. the implementation of eu development policy should thus aim at removing obstacles to development, such as dumping of agricultural products, the illicit debt burden, capital flight and unfair trade, and at creating an international environment conducive to the fight against poverty, the guarantee of adequate income and livelihoods, and the enjoyment of fundamental human rights, including social and economic rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the recent period of increasing poverty and social exclusion around the world, it is high time to examine the european union's development policy. indeed, eu development policy should aim to remove obstacles to development such as agricultural dumping, the illicit debt burden, capital flight and unfair trade, and to create an international environment conducive to the fight against poverty, the guarantee of adequate income and livelihoods, and the enjoyment of fundamental human rights, including social and economic rights. it is also necessary to combat inequalities, including gender inequalities, as gender equality, the political and economic empowerment of women and the enjoyment of women's human rights play a major role in reducing poverty and ensuring sustainable development. it is equally important to raise public awareness and to work towards improving transparency of aid expenditure, strengthening the independent dissemination of evaluation research results and applying stricter sanctions to participants if they are found to have misappropriated development aid funds. it should also be stressed that any policy to promote economic growth cannot be pursued without a policy to promote social and environmental standards and to implement social protection measures.

in writing. − it is essential that the european union's development policy instruments are implemented promptly and properly. in the light of the recent financial crisis and its negative consequences in the european union and worldwide, it is essential to maintain the same eu funding, but with new instruments and methods of financing. we must also define our specific objectives, vision, ambitions and the appropriate measures, especially where inclusive and sustainable development is concerned. i think that the developed world needs to take a leadership role in creating a low-carbon global economy. only by implementing these policies will we be in a position to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves. it is essential that member states take appropriate action to reduce emissions. in order to better coordinate the actions of the commission and the member states in this area, european country strategy papers and an effective implementation of the aid effectiveness agenda should be developed and the right of democratic oversight of the european parliament should be ensured.

in writing. the main principle to be implemented by changing the current procedure for providing food information to consumers the right of the consumer to receive information about the food and to be able to make a decision on the purchase or consumption of the food on the basis of that information. the adoption of a food information decision should also reduce consumer complaints about misleading food labels. it is true that the provision of information to the consumer does not eliminate the risk of going to the other extreme - too much information. on the one hand, too much information would make it difficult for the consumer to become a nutritionist, on the other hand, providing a lot of information (and in a readable font) would require a lot of space, which would mean an increase in packaging and containers (consumers often complain that they have to buy a product in large packages they do not need), and therefore an increase in packaging waste, and the costs of packaging would inevitably be passed on to the consumer. since the nutritional value of the product and the content of the constituents (carbohydrates, fats, proteins, salt, sugar) will be indicated, what allergens could be the risk of the use of one or another selected product. strict information requirements would be a significant burden, in particular for small traders who sell unpackaged, self-cooked or self-manufactured products. on the other hand, it is good that these traders are exempted and that unpackaged food sold will not be required to be labelled.

recognising that the financial crisis has led to an economic and social crisis, which can lead to a very serious political crisis, we should take much more decisive action to tackle unemployment and reduce social exclusion in the member states. i support the provision proposed in the resolution to call on the commission to carry out a rigorous financial audit of all member states in order to establish their actual financial situation and this should be done as soon as possible rather than in a year or two, as the situation is changing much faster than eurostat is able to summarise it. if we really want to build public confidence and trust in the potential of the europe 2020 programme, we should not only create highly favourable incentives and mechanisms, but also significantly reduce bureaucracy by simplifying many procedures. and another thing: i think that the commission should draw up a package of legislation as soon as possible to limit the ability of monopolies to raise unjustifiably the prices of raw materials, foodstuffs and services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the purpose of this decision of the european parliament and of the council is to ensure the legal specificity of the list of travel documents. this decision should also have added value, namely that it should ensure the security of border guards authorised to check travel documents at the external borders. otherwise, the purpose of the draft proposal would be meaningless and the list of travel documents should therefore be legally binding. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposed wording would not only respect the competence of the member states to recognise travel documents, but also ensure legal certainty after the expiry of the period of time, which could indeed be longer than the commission proposes. i also agree that, in the long term, an online database should be created to store all the specimens of travel documents, in order to make it easier for border control services and consular staff to check a specific travel document. it is important to note that the purpose of the travel document list is twofold. this means that the list can be used by border control authorities to determine whether a particular travel document is considered to be suitable for crossing the external border or by consular staff to check whether a particular travel document is recognised by the member states and whether it can be affixed with a visa.
in writing. - i have approved the document because, as provided for in the 1985 convention implementing the schengen agreement, a guide to travel documents entitling the holder to cross external borders and to which a visa may be affixed has been drawn up. however, these decisions are outdated and need to be adapted to the current eu institutional and legal framework. the purpose of the travel document list is twofold. on the one hand, it is possible for border control authorities to determine on the basis of that list whether a particular travel document is considered to be suitable for crossing the external border. on the other hand, it allows consular staff to check whether a specific travel document is recognised by the member states and whether it is capable of being stamped with a visa. this decision establishes a list of travel documents entitling the holder to cross the external borders and on which a visa may be affixed, and the mechanism for drawing up such a list. this decision applies to travel documents such as national passports (ordinary, diplomatic or service and official or special passports), temporary travel documents, travel documents for refugees and stateless persons, travel documents issued by international organisations or laissez-passer. this decision does not affect the competence of the member states to recognise travel documents.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which establishes a list of travel documents entitling the holder to cross the external borders and on which a visa may be affixed, and the mechanism for drawing up this list. in order to allow border control services and consulates to carry out their functions properly, the travel document guide needs to be updated and aligned with the current eu institutional and legal framework. it is essential that the recognition of travel documents remains a matter for each member state and is not affected by this decision. i believe that the three-month time limit within which states must communicate their position on the recognition of travel documents is appropriate and sufficient. in order to combat the use of false identity documents more effectively, the commission should draw up a list of known false and masked passports.
