in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on a comprehensive approach to the protection of personal data in the european union. this is an important document in which the european parliament advocates the strengthening of the existing rules on the protection of personal data, the introduction of new principles and measures and the maintenance of a consistent and high standard of data protection, in compliance with the binding charter of fundamental rights, in particular article 8 thereof. it is important that every person should at all times know who, what, when, for what purpose and for how long they are storing data and how they are processed, and should have the possibility to delete, rectify or block data in a non-bureaucratic way and be informed of any unlawful use of data or breach of data security. i agree with the rapporteur that children and minors need to be particularly protected, inter alia, in view of the increased use of the internet and digital content by children. media literacy should be an important part of formal education in order to teach children and minors to behave responsibly in an online environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because breaches of data protection provisions can seriously threaten the fundamental rights of individuals and the values of the member states, and the european union and the member states must take effective measures to combat such breaches. in addition, such breaches create a lack of trust among the public, which reduces the ability to properly apply new technologies, and misuse and abuse of personal data should be punishable by appropriate, strict and dissuasive sanctions, including criminal sanctions. the european commission should establish a mandatory personal data breach notification system and extend it to sectors other than telecommunications, and ensure that it does not become a routine system for warning of various breaches, but for warning of breaches that may adversely affect an individual. it is also necessary to ensure that all breaches are, without exception, recorded and made available to data protection authorities or other relevant authorities for investigation and evaluation, thus ensuring a level playing field and protection for all persons. it is essential to recognise the need to protect vulnerable persons, in particular children, in particular by imposing a mandatory requirement for a high level of data protection and by implementing appropriate specific measures for the protection of data of such persons.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the ep very much welcomes and supports the commission communication 'a comprehensive approach to the protection of personal data in the european union' and the fact that it focuses on strengthening the existing regime, proposing new principles and measures and ensuring consistent and high standards of data protection under the new system proposed to be applied after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. the principles and standards set out in directive 95/46/ec are a good starting point and should be further developed, extended and implemented. the ep recognises that technological developments have, on the one hand, created new threats to the protection of personal data and, on the other hand, have led to a significant increase in the use of information technology for everyday and generally harmless purposes, and that these developments require a thorough assessment of the existing data protection rules in order to ensure that: the rules continue to ensure a high level of protection; the rules strike an appropriate balance between the right to the protection of personal data and the right to freedom of expression and information; and the application of these rules does not unnecessarily create obstacles to the everyday processing of personal data, which is generally harmless.
in writing. − protection of personal data one of the human rights to privacy enshrined in the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. attention should be drawn to the fact that technological developments pose new threats to the protection of personal data. we must make every effort to ensure the highest level of data protection and the proper implementation of the right to the protection of personal data. in addition, the revised data regime should reduce the bureaucratic and financial burden. the obligations of controllers in relation to the provisions on information on data subjects need to be increased in order to ensure proper compliance with the requirements of data protection legislation. it is also necessary to regulate the processing of non-public data more strictly and to strengthen the guarantees attached to it.
in writing. − colleagues, privacy and security are of paramount importance to all people. citizens cannot be forced to choose between freedom and security. i agree with the rapporteur that we need to modernise data protection laws to meet the privacy challenges posed by new technologies. but the problem is much bigger than the report. in some eu countries, including lithuania, the problem is not only obsolete legislation but also enforcement. article 22 of the republic of lithuania prohibits interference with a person's personal correspondence or life. according to a report published in the american magazine a few months ago, in 2010, the lithuanian state data protection inspectorate investigated 270 allegations of arbitrary intrusion into privacy by government officials or companies. in most complaints, individuals claimed that their personal data, such as their personal identification code, had been collected or used by government agencies without any legal basis or explanation. trust has to be restored. it is important that citizens know what is happening with their data. european leaders must take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure protection against data loss or unauthorised access. it's a matter of honor and dignity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on consumer information on foodstuffs. the free movement of safe food is a fundamental element of the internal market, important for the health and well-being of the population and for its social and economic interests. with this resolution, we, the members of the european parliament, seek to take account of the interests of the internal market, the reduction of bureaucratic burdens and the interests of citizens by requiring food labelling to be clear, understandable and legible. people need to know what they are eating, where it is made and what it is made of. the labelling of foodstuffs must be easily recognisable, understandable and legible to the consumer. i think it is appropriate and right to ensure that consumers have access to an impartial information provider in the member states to find out about individual nutritional issues. member states should therefore set up appropriate telephone helplines.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document as it aims to further regulate the information to be provided to consumers on food labels. for the purposes of this regulation, the indication on the label of the name of the food business operator, the name of the establishment or the address shall not be considered as an indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of the food. food labels should be clear and understandable to help consumers who want to make informed food and nutrition choices. studies have shown that good legibility is important to increase the likelihood that labelling information will have an impact on the persons reading it and that illegible product information is one of the main reasons for consumer dissatisfaction with food labels. a comprehensive approach should therefore be adopted to take into account all aspects related to legibility, including font, colour and contrast.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation as there is a need to strengthen the requirements for food labelling. in particular, the functioning of the internal market will be improved and the free movement of goods will be facilitated. in addition, clear, understandable and readable information will be provided to consumers. it is very important that the food label contains the information that is necessary to know in order to make informed purchasing decisions. it should be noted that the strict labelling requirements should be exempted for micro-enterprises, in particular those producing handicrafts. i think it is appropriate to provide for a transitional period for the new labelling requirements to take effect. this will ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and reduce packaging waste.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the cross-border exchange of information on road-safety-related traffic offences. the resolution is aimed at helping to ensure more safety on european roads and so reduce the number of casualties. the basis of cross-border law enforcement is a smooth data exchange among member states. dangerous traffic offences covered under these provisions include speeding, not wearing a seat belt, not stopping at a red light and drink-driving. the list of offences has been expanded to cover crimes such as driving under the influence of drugs and using mobile phones at the wheel. i strongly believe that this resolution will make a significant contribution to ensuring road safety in the member states and urge the council to follow the european parliament’s ambitious recommendations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the main objective of the union's transport policy is to improve road safety. the union shall implement a policy to improve road safety aimed at reducing the number of fatalities, injuries and material damage. an important aspect of this policy is the enforcement of the penalties for continuous infringements of the road traffic rules, when committed within the union and posing a serious risk to road safety. the enforcement of sanctions fines for certain road traffic offences is often not guaranteed if those offences are committed in a vehicle registered in a member state other than the member state of the offence, or in another member state. this directive aims to ensure that in such cases the effectiveness of the investigation of road safety infringements is ensured. this directive also aims to ensure a high level of protection for all road users in the union by facilitating the exchange of information at cross-border level on road safety related traffic offences and thus ensuring the application of sanctions for offences committed in a member state other than the member state of the offence in which the vehicle is registered.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this legal recommendation, which facilitates the exchange of information at cross-border level on road safety violations, as it will help to improve road safety, harmonise road safety policies, enforcement procedures at eu level. i think that there should be more consistency in the way controls and technical equipment are harmonised between member states. the implementation of the provisions of this directive will improve consumer information on the consequences of non-compliance with the road traffic rules when travelling in another member state and will enable the member state authorities to carry out their functions more quickly and efficiently. it should be noted that in all cases, the exchange of data between member states must ensure the protection of fundamental rights of the individual and the protection of personal data.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that road traffic offences should not go unpunished, whether they are committed in one's own country or in another eu country. drivers who have moved to another country often have less respect for speed limits and other traffic rules. although the number of road deaths has decreased over the last decade, accidents, especially in the baltic states, are still too many. the feeling of impunity when driving abroad does not make things any better. i regret that denmark, ireland and the united kingdom have not yet shown their willingness to join this agreement. eu countries are obliged to ensure the protection of personal data in the exchange of information. however, concerns that this information may be misused should not delay the introduction of a data exchange system.
in writing. − i abstained in this vote because the ep does not support the draft council regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework 2007-13. the council shall adopt the regulation on the multiannual financial framework after obtaining the consent of the european parliament. the tfeu requires that all three institutions work together to find a solution through the procedures for adopting the financial programme. however, as the existing legal instrument establishing the needs of the multiannual financial framework needs to be amended following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the commission presented the so-called lisbon package, which includes a proposal for a council regulation establishing a multiannual financial framework for 2007-13, a draft interinstitutional agreement on cooperation in budgetary matters and a proposal to amend the financial regulation. the council adopted the commission proposal and asked the european parliament to give its consent to the proposal without entering into any negotiations with the european parliament with a view to agreeing on a common position.
in writing. − it is essential that the european parliament and the council agree, by means of mutual negotiations, on a common position on the draft regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework 2007-13. the council may not ignore or disregard parliament's position on the matter under consideration. the proposal to parliament provides for a certain degree of flexibility, but in general the proposal for a multiannual financial framework is not sufficient to cover the needs of the member states. in view of the increased demand and the reduced margin, as well as the increased use of the flexibility instruments provided for under the interinstitutional agreement, it is necessary to provide for greater flexibility. it should be noted that the proposal provides for much less flexibility than is allowed under the current interinstitutional agreement.
in writing. − the european parliament has repeatedly called on the commission and the council to provide greater flexibility for the eu's multiannual financial framework, which was one of the main obstacles to overcoming the consequences of the economic crisis in europe, especially with regard to emergency aid. the eu must face up to increasing competition in the world and new challenges such as energy security. the eu's global competitiveness will be enhanced by ensuring fair competition between member states. cohesion policy must therefore be refined to address the economic and social disparities existing between member states. the agricultural policy must be established and direct payments to farmers must be balanced. it is unacceptable that, for example, greek farmers continue to receive three to four times more aid than latvians. i would also like to see more money in the eu budget to support business. the draft regulation submitted does not provide the necessary flexibility in the eu budget, nor does it provide for additional funding for the implementation of common political and economic priorities. this resolution rejects the draft financial framework submitted, which is why i have supported it.
in writing. − the european commission has a key role to play in shaping the future of the eu and its future work programme. the europe strategy sets out a number of ambitious objectives in key eu policy areas which will need to be properly reflected in the future financial perspective. an open and constructive dialogue and cooperation on the objectives, scope and direction of the union's multiannual financial framework (mff) and the reform of its revenue system, including a conference on own resources involving members of the european parliament and national parliaments, should be initiated at eu level. in the light of the commitments made in the field of energy and the objective of achieving a single energy market by 2014, i support the call for the commission to monitor the implementation of eu legislation in the fields of energy and energy efficiency and to adopt without delay the appropriate implementing measures and to submit any new proposals needed to achieve these objectives. another major challenge - the future cap - is to be closely aligned with the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. we expect the commission's forthcoming proposals for cap reform to be guided by the principle of sustainability, in order to ensure the long-term viability of european food production, while improving farmers' competitiveness, fairly distributing direct payments and promoting rural development, preserving the diversity of farming methods and production and avoiding red tape.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as the european commission should continue its work and collaborate with the european parliament and the council in improving the quality of legislation. i agree with parliament that it is essential to submit as soon as possible a proposal for a european social fund a key instrument to combat unemployment and social inequalities and to reduce poverty by improving education and vocational training. more attention should also be paid to the youth unemployment problem, which is of great concern, and to the problem of early school leavers. it is regrettable that the commission has still not put forward a legislative proposal to combat violence against women under a framework comprising a comprehensive strategy and an appropriate harmonisation of sanctions. there is also a lack of proposals and initiatives in the area of public health. in addition, new multiannual programmes in the fields of education, culture, sport and citizenship should be considered as important, as they are crucial for the successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and for preserving the eu's multicultural and multilingual diversity. it is essential to take actions and measures based on an appropriate and effective budgetary framework to ensure that these effective programmes continue to meet the needs of european society beyond 2013.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the european commission has a key role to play in shaping the future of the eu and should use its future work programme to promote the union's objectives and values, to strengthen its responsibility for the eu project, to bring the eu out of the crisis and to ensure its representation and honourable positions in the world. it is important for us to restore growth today to create jobs. continue to implement the citizens' agenda: freedom, security and justice. and also to increase our influence on the world stage.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document because in 1997-98 bse reached epidemic levels in the european union as a result of the feeding of bse-infected processed animal protein (pgb) to cattle. in response to the bse epidemic in the eu, regulation (ec) no 999/2001 of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2001 laying down rules for the prevention, control and eradication of certain transmissible spongiform encephalopathies established for the first time a common legal framework for the control and prevention of tse and bse. the regulation consolidates all previous eu legislation governing the tse. since the date of adoption, the regulation has been amended several times, modified or introduced several additional measures to further eradicate, control or monitor tse. other measures contribute to ensuring full security and the tse monitoring regime. communication from the commission to the european parliament and the council of 16 july 2010 second action plan to combat tse. the ep welcomes the commission's proposal to amend the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the ep stresses, however, the importance of ensuring that the significant reduction in bse cases in the eu does not lead to a softening of the tse measures or a weakening of the eu's strict control and monitoring mechanisms; notes that the past and current tse legislation have contributed to the elimination of tse in the eu.
in writing. − infectious spongiform encephalopathies (ises) are caused by the transfer of the causative agent prion, which is a pathological form of protein. this disease is very dangerous to humans and animals. although the number of cases of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (bse) has decreased in the european union in recent years, it is essential to maintain the same level of control and strict monitoring mechanisms for transmissible spongiform encephalopathies and related food and feed. we must be constantly prepared to prevent an outbreak of this disease throughout the eu. i think that the commission should encourage the silos which are being set up to create urgent diagnostic tests for bse. it is also essential that the commission reassesses the lower limit values for dioxin in fishmeal. it should be noted that the currently allowed limit is too high because of the risks to human and animal health. in this context, i support the resolution on the implementation and prospects of eu legislation on transmissible spongiform encephalopathies and related controls on food and feed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on aviation security, with a special focus on security scanners. the resolution lays down the conditions for the use of body scanners at airport check-ins and calls for a definitive end to the ban on carrying liquids in 2013. it is very important to stress that the new generation of scanners fulfil parliament’s demands for the protection of human rights, as, rather than showing a human body, they display a standard image that simply indicates if the passenger is carrying anything dangerous or not. the european parliament rejected the use of body scanners in 2008 because there were no guarantees on the respect of passenger privacy. developments in the technology of the scanners have overcome doubts regarding fundamental rights or risks for human health due to frequent exposure to x-ray technologies. i support the rapporteur on the issue of liquids, aerosols and gels in passengers’ hand luggage. the european commission must quickly clarify the current ambiguous situation and, in any case, transform the ban on carrying liquids into an obligation to screen them from 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i agree with the rapporteur that an integrated approach to aviation security is needed, applying the principle of a single security check, so that passengers, baggage and cargo arriving at one eu airport from other eu airports do not have to be re-checked. in the communication, the european parliament calls on the commission to propose the inclusion of body scanners, which should help speed up screening at airports and reduce inconvenience to passengers, in the list of permitted screening methods. i agree that appropriate rules for the use of body scanners and common minimum standards should be included. i also consider that an impact assessment is necessary before the inclusion of body scanners in the list, which would confirm that the devices do not pose a risk to the health, personal data, dignity and privacy of passengers. the use of body scanners should be governed by common eu rules, procedures and standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because while ensuring the security of air transport in the fight against terrorist attacks is undoubtedly essential, we must also examine the impact of the measures designed to ensure such security on our health, fundamental rights and freedoms, privacy and dignity. the european parliament's task is therefore to examine fully the measures adopted and, if necessary, to propose others to prevent risks. in addition, international coordination of aviation security measures is necessary to ensure a high level of protection and to avoid the restrictions and additional costs of multiple screening of passengers. it is important to note that the introduction of new technical measures aimed at achieving a high level of security at airports is also essential to establish the boundaries between human rights and security itself, since those measures concern not only the protection of citizens but also their impact on their rights and freedoms. it is also necessary to ensure that those technical security measures are genuinely safe, effective and reasonable. in order to protect the identity of passengers and to ensure that they cannot be identified by any body image, all body scanners should use identifiable body images. therefore, once member states have installed body scanners, they must comply with the minimum standards and requirements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document as it deals with the issue of body scanners, the decisions taken on liquids, aerosols and gels and the security measures applied to cargo and mail. eu aviation security legislation provides for a list of screening methods and technologies from which member states and/or airports have to choose, and existing legislation will need to be amended to include body scanners in this list (without prejudice to the possibility of installing body scanners during a trial period or as a more stringent security measure). supports the implementation of harmonised rules across the european union governing the conditions of use of body scanners and common quality standards for detection.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as we need to ensure civil aviation safety at eu level, based on an integrated approach to aviation safety and applying the principle of a single safety check. i believe that body scanners can only be included in the list of acceptable methods of testing after a thorough scientifically based impact assessment has been carried out by an independent body. this assessment shall take into account the direct and delayed effects and the long-term cumulative effects on human health, risks to personal data, personal dignity and privacy. in addition, common eu rules for the use of scanners, common minimum standards and procedures should be developed. only by implementing these measures will the health of passengers, crew, seamen and security staff be adequately protected and their fundamental rights and interests protected. it is also essential to ensure that the random selection of passengers for body scanners is not based on discriminatory criteria. it should be noted that i do not agree with the claim that the quality of detection of objects, especially non-metallic and liquid, by body scanners is superior to that of metal detectors, until this has been scientifically proven.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on women and business leadership aimed at increasing access to top jobs for competent women. we, the members of the european parliament, have required companies to take daring measures to increase women’s participation on boards of directors. the new legislation ought to include quotas in order to increase female representation in corporate management bodies: 30% by 2015 and 40% by 2020, while taking account of the member states’ responsibilities and of their economic, structural (i.e. company size), legal and regional specificities. it is important to further raise awareness among social partners, companies, governments and public opinion on the necessity of enhanced representation of women on boards, and to inform them of the specific targets that need to be reached. i welcome the commission’s strong support for this process and its stated aim of proposing binding measures on companies if voluntary measures fail to increase women’s representation.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it is vital to help competent and qualified women to take up positions that are currently difficult for them to access. as regards gender equality in business, it is worth noting that only 3% of company directors are women, as they face discrimination and barriers to advancing their careers and reaching leadership. the proposed quota system is designed to ensure that companies do not take any action or make any changes to improve gender equality in their business, and therefore the quota system is intended to be enshrined in legislation. in addition, the european commission has already announced that it will present legislation to ensure that companies take effective measures to ensure equal representation of women and men on boards if this is not achieved through self-regulation in the next 12 months. the commission plans to propose european legislation in 2012 if companies do not voluntarily increase the number of women on company boards to 30% by 2015 and to 40% by 2020. the european parliament calls on the commission to present an action plan setting out specific, measurable and achievable objectives to ensure a balance of representation in all sizes of enterprises and calls on the commission to draw up specific guidelines for small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. − i agree with the view that in politics, both in the eu and in the member states, as well as in business, there is a need to remove barriers to women's entry into the labour market, especially in management positions, and to give women equal opportunities to take up responsible positions, in order to ensure the effective use of all available resources, to optimise the uptake of women's skills and good qualities and to make the best use of the human potential of the european union and to defend the eu's core values, taking into account that equality is a fundamental principle. i abstained, as the report stresses that if the measures taken by companies and member states prove insufficient, legislative measures, including quotas, should be proposed by 2012 to help increase the number of women in management positions to 30% by 2015 and to 40% by 2020, taking into account the competences of the member states and the specificities of the economy, structure (size of companies), law and regions. i do not think it is logical to set quotas in the business sector.
in writing. − first, when appointing people to management positions, companies must first take into account and assess their competence, knowledge and experience. i believe that requiring companies to increase the number of women on management boards to a certain number will not be effective and efficient, and that business entities may suffer certain losses as a result of such an imperative requirement, especially in terms of staff competence. furthermore, i do not consider that good economic performance and competitiveness depend on the gender of the head of the company. we must do everything possible to ensure that women are not discriminated against. all obstacles to their integration into the labour market, in particular in management positions, must be removed. women must be guaranteed equal pay. in addition, member states should develop initiatives at national level to ensure fair sharing of family responsibilities and to reduce the gender pay gap.
in writing. − the report notes with concern that only 3% of the eu's largest companies are headed by women, and that women make up 10% of the board. i agree that we need to help qualified and competent women to pursue careers and to reach high positions. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for change, and sets out the way forward, by stimulating debate at both national and eu level. companies need a practical model to promote women's participation in the board, with objectives and a defined timeframe for their implementation. i agree with the commission that women should make up 30% of board seats by 2015 and 40% five years later. the proportionate representation of men and women on boards should be a priority for companies and the eu could set an example for the world in this regard.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, women's rights are human rights, whether on the website or in the offices of the chairmen of the boards. it is impossible to imagine a fully democratic society without the participation of women. democracy cannot exist if some members of society are not equally respected and protected from abuse - this applies to women as well as to other discriminated groups. this report focuses on the representation of women on the boards of medium-sized and large companies. but the issue is much broader, especially in lithuania. according to eurostat, more than 91% of lithuanian women have completed secondary and higher education - the highest rate in the eu. at the same time, less than 17% of lithuanians hold the position of chairperson of the board of directors, and only 18% of them are elected to parliament, and there are almost no women university rectors at all. it's not enough to have a woman president. a rapid response is needed to prevent talent and skills from leaking into the eu workforce. the gender pay gap needs to be reduced in lithuania and across the eu. in lithuania, women often earn 20% less than men for the same job. the eu must demonstrate that fundamental rights apply to all citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the report entitled ‘financial, economic and social crisis: measures and initiatives to be taken’. we, the members of the european parliament, call for ‘more europe’: a ‘smarter’ more efficient and more united eu with clearly defined and commonly agreed goals, to which all member states should clearly commit and which should be supported by ambitious financial means. it is true that existing vulnerabilities in the eu’s capacity to respond to the crisis derive from the lack of adequate european instruments or their inappropriate use. the main prerequisites for europe’s recovery are competitiveness and sound finances in member states. innovation, the internal market and the further opening-up of economies and markets are the main domains of european action. i agree with the rapporteur in that, if europe is to succeed in delivering the necessary answers to the crisis, concrete strategic action needs to be taken at european level to bring additional benefits for citizens, member states and the union. the eu needs to be able to achieve more with less, and the prioritisation of eu spending should help bring about competitive, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. - i voted for this. the financial and economic crisis has led to the loss of 23 million jobs among the economically active population (9.6% of the total), a 21% rise in youth unemployment and 17% of eu citizens at risk of poverty. the crisis has clearly demonstrated the need for a transition to a genuine economic governance of the european union, consisting of systematic policies to ensure sustainable growth, stable and quality employment, fiscal discipline, the correction of excessive macroeconomic imbalances, the competitiveness and efficiency of the european economy and stronger regulation and monitoring of financial markets, as well as an appropriate response to the financial crisis. i agree with the observation in the report that credit rating agencies have significantly contributed to the worsening of the financial crisis by giving structured finance instruments incorrect ratings that should have been downgraded. i believe that the dependence on external credit ratings must be reduced and that the eu must set up its own credit rating agency as soon as possible, which will allow the member states' economies to be assessed objectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it seeks a transparent audit of public debt in order to identify the origin of the debt and to find out who are the main holders of debt securities and what their amounts are. the sovereign debt crisis has exposed the dangers of imbalances within europe. i believe that there is a need for the european union to act as one, to develop much closer coordination of fiscal policies and, where appropriate, a common policy with a sufficient eu budget partly financed by its own resources, and to implement appropriate provisions for crisis management and economic convergence.
in writing. − we must act as one for the benefit of the european union as a whole and each of its member states. each state must ensure that the country has good business conditions and that the public is well-behaved. the member states must strive and act to reduce as rapidly as possible the material well-being gap with the european average. we need to increase employment, reduce social exclusion. the european union's financial, knowledge, intellectual and capacity resources must be fully mobilised to tackle unemployment and emigration. decisions on job creation and the promotion of employers who create them can no longer be delayed. we must support not only foreign firms investing in the eu, but also local employers creating new jobs. high labour costs are one of the most serious obstacles to new business creation and employment growth. lower taxation of labour would stimulate investment. it is also essential to increase investment in research and experimental development. another problem requiring urgent action is the volatility of agricultural and food prices. we need to reduce the tax and administrative burden on small and medium-sized enterprises. pensions must meet people's needs and enable people in work to start saving for their future pension today.
mr president, it looks as if parliament has recently begun a thought process on the frozen war between armenia and azerbaijan. for too long we have buried our heads in the sand, washing our hands of the affair by means of the minsk group, and repeating happily that fruitless dialogue lasting 20 years is better than war. the reality is that military force continues to be used. the cancer of the world is there and this illness continues to spread when the lands are occupied by foreign forces and when an enemy is not stopped from carrying out sniper killings. we should therefore at least stop kidding ourselves here; ‘to act or not to act’, that is our question. all of our resolutions will be fruitless if they do not concern the realities of the occupied territories of azerbaijan, all expelled people, and all the problems of communication with nagorno-karabakh and the nakhichevan region. we must fully understand what is at stake and have a serious talk with russia about its role there as actor and stage manager.
the first task for all of us is to get the citizens of the european union interested in european issues. over the years, a number of significant steps have been taken to improve the various electoral systems, and the additional list for elections to the european parliament will hopefully help to involve our citizens more actively in the electoral process. however, the european parliament itself has not yet fully fulfilled its obligations under the treaties of paris and rome, such as the unification of the electoral procedure in the member states and the right of individual candidates to stand as candidates, and other problematic issues. i think we should also take account of the shortcomings of the current system, as expressed by the osce, which do not allow the european parliament to fully implement the principles of democracy and do not encourage our citizens to participate actively in elections, simply because they are disappointed with the long-running reform.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to take measures to adapt the working environment to the needs of older people, to ensure health care for all older people and to provide them with the necessary social support. sadly, many older ones experience isolation in their old age. moreover, if older people are to remain in the labour market for longer, for example because of the extension of the retirement age, it is necessary to take concrete measures to provide them with better employment opportunities, as this is the only way to eliminate the causes of poverty in this age group. unfortunately, there are still many concerns that older people may become too much of a burden for younger people of working age, and this may lead to tensions between generations. it is vital, therefore, to overcome such a viewpoint and to remember the great benefit that older ones bring to the world today and can bring to the world in the future. active ageing is also an effective way of combating poverty among older people. it must be clear to society and the economy that older people are not a burden but an asset because of their experience, work and knowledge gained during their lifetime. the european year 2012 should therefore be the guiding light for these changes in europe, as the proportion of older people in europe is increasing and promoting healthy ageing is more important than ever.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it aims to designate 2012 as the european year of active ageing and to allocate money from the eu budget to this end. eurostat demographic projections show a decrease of around 6,8% in the working age population in 2030. thus, only two persons of working age (15-64 years) will have to support one retired person (over 65 years), compared to the current ratio of four persons to one. the eu will thus experience a large relative increase in the number of older people compared to a large decline in the number of people under 50 years of age, and this may increase pressure on national budgets and pension systems, social and care services. in addition, old age is still often associated with illness and dependency on others, and older people may feel unnecessary in the labour market, in family life and in community life. the proposed active ageing year should encourage and support the efforts of member states, their regional and local authorities, social partners and civil society to promote active ageing and to focus more on the generational potential of people approaching 60 years of age and older people. the european year would thus provide a framework for informing the public, identifying and disseminating good practice and, in particular, encouraging legislators and stakeholders at all levels to promote active ageing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because ageing is a problem facing the whole of european society and all its generations. the european year for active ageing 2012 will build a sustainable culture of active ageing in europe, based on a multi-age society and generational solidarity. the efforts of member states, their regional and local authorities, social partners and civil society to promote active ageing will thus be encouraged and supported. it will also facilitate active ageing and ageing with the preservation of the vitality and dignity of all persons. it should be noted that the objectives to be achieved should be at least minimal budgetary resources, with a separate budget line.
in writing. − in 2030, the number of people of working age in the european union will decline by 6.8%. only 2 people of working age will have to support one pensioner. the ageing of european society poses economic threats, and it is important to ensure that people remain in the labour market for as long as possible, that older workers are active in society, that they are healthy, active and independent. i voted in favour of the report on active ageing in 2012 because it calls for helping older people to maintain not only their social, but also their physical and spiritual well-being. i agree that solidarity and cooperation between generations is essential to achieve these goals. i welcome the proposal to declare 2012 the european year of active ageing. this would promote solidarity between generations, and highlight the importance of the contribution of older people to society.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the promotion of democracy in the world is one of the european union's most important tasks. the eu does indeed have a wide range of instruments to support democracy and human rights in the world, but these instruments are not currently being used effectively enough. the resolution adopted by parliament therefore calls on the eu institutions to allocate aid more consistently and efficiently, in a way that is harmonised and based on standard methods, but adapted to each country receiving aid. however, as another weakness of existing eu support for democracy in third countries, the resolution points to the inconsistent application of eu sanctions and criminal measures to countries that commit serious violations of human rights and democratic principles in defiance of their international obligations. the european parliament therefore proposes to strengthen the support provided by means of sanctions, chosen in a fair, proportionate and reasonable manner, which would allow for an appropriate and effective response to the continued failure of third countries to fulfil their international commitments to democracy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document, as it is necessary to continue to respect democratic instruments in cooperation with foreign countries, especially third countries, and to involve all the social partners, including the media. i believe that only democratic countries, in accordance with the rule of law, can provide the basis for a balanced and legitimate partnership between the eu and third countries, in which the eu takes account of both countries' needs and interests. partnership based on dialogue and consultation strengthens accountability for democracy-building processes and elements of democratic governance. all eu institutions must therefore make greater efforts to use these various dialogues in a clearer, more coherent and more coordinated way. i also believe that the eu's role as a 'non-aligned power' in the international system can only be consolidated if its policy towards third countries genuinely prioritises the protection of human rights. the document also stresses the need for a paradigm shift, which should be based on genuine democratic consolidation, based on endogenous, sustainable, inclusive and population-friendly development, respecting the rule of law and fundamental human rights and freedoms. the eu must help create an environment conducive to the development of democratic societies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the eu's external policy in support of the establishment of democracy, as social justice and the fight against inequality must be the main objectives of the eu's external policy. cooperation with foreign countries, in particular third countries, must be conducted in accordance with democratic procedures. it shall involve all social partners, including the media. it is worth noting that the experience of the transition to democracy should be shared with the emerging democratic forces in north africa and elsewhere in the middle east. i support the proposal to set up a european democracy fund to support political actors seeking democracy in non-democratic and transition countries, particularly in the eu's eastern and southern neighbourhoods. the eu must also be more active in building a coalition with the united states, focusing joint eu-us efforts to better coordinate their development policies. it is also essential to develop a more open and dynamic policy to support the driving forces of society and the actors promoting citizen participation. the need to promote close cooperation between the public and private sectors, to strengthen the capacity of civil society and to enable it to participate in policy processes
in writing. − this european parliament resolution is a strong statement for the promotion of democratic values outside europe and recognition that a ‘one size fits all’ policy on external democratisation may not be possible. the resolution affirms european values based on civil, political, cultural, and economic rights and highlights europe’s obligation to ensure that these rights are practised in europe and around the world. in cases where states are perpetrating human rights abuses, this resolution outlines several methods for dealing with foreign governments, such as imposing appropriate sanctions on individuals or using effective conditionality agreements with these countries. i voted for this resolution, because it declares that any true promotion of democracy in foreign countries cannot happen with the support of and consultation with local actors. i believe that the resolution effectively outlines the european parliament’s strong but pragmatic support for democratisation in the world.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the preparations for the russian state duma elections in december. we members of the european parliament strongly deplore the decision by the russian authorities to reject the registration of the people’s freedom party (parnas) for the forthcoming duma elections in december 2011. it is not acceptable that russia, which is one of the european union’s most important partners in building strategic cooperation, does not guarantee free and fair elections – which are the basis of a democratic society and one of the eu’s main values. i would like to stress once again that the state duma elections should be based on the implementation of the election standards set by the council of europe and the osce, and that the russian authorities must allow the osce/council of europe to carry out a long-term election observation mission and must cooperate fully with it from its earliest stage. those steps would send a signal to the eu and to the world that the russian authorities are ready for the modernisation and democratisation of the country.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it reaffirms my conviction that russia remains one of the european union's most important partners in the development of strategic cooperation, with which it shares not only economic and trade interests but also the objective of working closely together in the common neighbourhood and at global level. it is regrettable that the russian authorities have decided to reject the application to register the people's freedom party (parnas) for participation in the forthcoming duma elections in december 2011. i believe it is necessary to call on the russian authorities to ensure free and fair elections and to repeal all decisions and rules that are inconsistent with this principle. concern is also expressed about the difficulties faced by political parties wishing to register for elections, which in fact restrict political competition in russia, reduce the choice available to voters and demonstrate that there are still real obstacles to political pluralism in the country.
in writing. − russia is one of the european union's most important partners and this makes it necessary to constantly expand political dialogue in many areas. in particular, closer cooperation on economic and trade interests must be developed. there is also a need to strengthen the strategic partnership with russia and to seek solutions to common challenges in the common neighbourhood and globally. in this context, it is essential that all processes in russia take place in a manner that respects the principles of democracy and the rule of law, and ensures respect for human rights and freedoms. it is also essential that free and fair elections be held, free from violence and without any restrictions on any social group, and that decisions and rules which are inconsistent with this principle be abolished.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which expresses concern at the decision of the russian ministry of justice not to register the people's freedom party on the eve of the duma elections. the reasons for non-registration still need to be examined, but the eu has a strong interest in the forthcoming elections in russia as a stepping stone towards a stronger democracy. refusal to register the party in russia may reduce the freedom of choice, citizens' trust in their state. russia is and will remain one of the eu's most important partners. we should be bound not only by economic and trade interdependence but also by common goals of sustainable cooperation in the neighbourhood and around the world.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is another important step taken by the european parliament towards safeguarding the schengen area of free movement. indeed, the free movement area has recently been threatened for various reasons, and this has led to a great deal of public debate about how the schengen area should be managed and supervised in the future. i am convinced that we need not to reform the existing system but simply to strengthen it, because the schengen rules, as defined in the schengen borders code, already provide for the conditions and procedures for the temporary reintroduction of internal border control. on the other hand, this system has some shortcomings and could be improved. first, it is unilateral and therefore cannot be used to prioritise the collective interest of the eu. the strengthening of the schengen system should change this in the future. secondly, the mechanism now in place for assessing the compliance of member states with the provisions of schengen law, where such assessment is carried out by an intergovernmental working group, is clearly inadequate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document, which, given that a common european asylum system is to be established by 2012, proposes that no exceptions to the schengen code be made in any way. in particular, last year saw a massive upsurge in people leaving some north african countries and the system has recently been under pressure due to a sudden influx of migrants in some member states, leading to the possibility of reintroducing checks at national borders. i think that any new additional exceptions to the current rules, such as a new framework for the reintroduction of internal border controls in exceptional cases, would not strengthen the schengen system. it should be noted that the influx of migrants and asylum seekers at the external borders cannot in itself be considered as an additional reason for the reintroduction of border controls.
in writing. − it is worth noting that in recent years there has been an increase in the influx of people from some north african countries, and that some member states are considering the possibility of reintroducing checks at national borders in response to the sudden influx of migrants. since a common european asylum system is to be established by 2012, exceptions in the code of schengen systems would clearly not contribute to the achievement of this objective, the strengthening of freedom of movement and the eu's governance in the schengen area. however, in exceptional cases where an emergency situation arises and a member state is at risk, derogations from the strict schengen rules should be allowed, but only after a thorough investigation. we must continue to make every effort to strengthen the governance and evaluation mechanism of the schengen system. the member state needs to be provided with effective assistance and support to enable it to effectively control the part of the eu external border that it owns and to manage the largest flows of migrants.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document as article 19 of protocol no 1 states that the european parliament and the national parliaments are to determine jointly how to organise and promote any form of effective and permanent interparliamentary cooperation. the european parliament shall decide, together with the council, on the budget of the eu's external action, including the budget of civilian missions under the cfsp and the csdp and the administrative costs of the eu's military coordination. the european parliament is the source of democratic legitimacy for its politically controlled csdp and cfsp. i share the view that stronger interparliamentary cooperation in the field of cfsp and csdp would enhance the influence of parliaments on the political choices of the eu and its member states, taking into account the european parliament's responsibility for the general policies of the union, including the cfsp and the csdp, and the prerogatives of each national parliament in the decision-making of national security and defence policy. the ep's own involvement in any new form of interparliamentary cooperation should be such as to reflect the breadth and importance of the ep's role in the oversight of the cfsp and the gsp, to recognise the common european nature of these policies and to meet the need to reflect the political and geographical diversity of the parliament as a whole. in order to limit additional benefits and costs, the secretariat and premises of the european parliament can in principle be used to support the organisation of interparliamentary meetings.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because stronger interparliamentary cooperation in the field of cfsp and csdp would enhance the influence of parliaments on the political choices of the eu and its member states. firstly, because the european parliament is the source of democratic legitimacy for the csdp and the cfsp, which it controls politically. it shall decide, together with the council, on the budget of the eu's external action, including the budget of civilian missions under the cfsp and the csdp and the administrative costs of the eu's military coordination. in this context, effective interparliamentary cooperation in the field of the cfsp and the csdp is essential. i think it is appropriate to support the efforts of the polish presidency to reach an agreement between the european parliament and the national parliaments on new forms of interparliamentary cooperation in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the programme for the distribution of food to the most deprived persons in the union. the commission estimates that 80 million eu citizens are at risk of poverty and that the economic and financial crisis could lead to an increase in the number of people living in poverty. however, even in this difficult situation, it is planned to reduce food aid funding sharply from eur 500 million in 2011 to eur 113 million in 2012. i support the provisions in the resolution calling on the commission and the council to prepare a transitional solution to avoid a sudden and significant reduction in food aid during the remaining funding period (2012 and 2013) following a reduction in funding from 500 million to 113 million, and to ensure that people who are dependent on food aid do not suffer from food shortages. it is important to underline that the right to food is a fundamental human right and is guaranteed when all people have the physical and economic possibility to have access at all times to adequate, safe and nutritious food to meet their daily nutritional needs and to lead an active and healthy life. it is the duty of all of us to work to ensure that this right is guaranteed to every eu citizen.
in writing. − the commission estimates that 80 million people in the eu are at risk of poverty, and that the economic and financial crisis and rising food prices are putting more and more people at risk of food shortages. the programme for the distribution of food to the poorest people in the union was set up in 1987 under the common agricultural policy (cap) and currently provides food aid to 13 million people living in poverty in 19 member states, with some 240 food banks and charities involved in the distribution chain. the eu's common agricultural policy programme has increased its dependence on products purchased on the market, and this has led to a reduction in intervention stocks, which are the traditional source of supply for that programme. in 2012, there is a sudden reduction in funding from eur 500 million in 2011 to eur 113 million in 2012, which will have a huge impact on the most vulnerable eu citizens. i support the call for a transitional solution to avoid a sudden and significant reduction in food aid over the remaining funding period (2012 and 2013) following a reduction in funding from 500 million to 113 million and to ensure that people who are dependent on food aid do not suffer from food shortages.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i fully agree that the abrupt termination of the food distribution programmes which have been in operation until now, three years before the start of the new approved schemes for the financing of food distribution, and also in the midst of a crisis, is unjustified. according to the commission, 43 million people in the eu are currently food insecure, and another 80 million are at risk of falling below the poverty line as a result of the economic and financial crisis and rising food prices. the response to the growing poverty of the eu population cannot therefore be to cut off funding without any transitional measures. this is why the european parliament, in its resolution, calls on the commission and the council to prepare a transitional solution to avoid a sudden and significant reduction in food aid during the remaining funding period (2012 and 2013) following a reduction in funding from 500 million to 113 million, and to ensure that people who are dependent on food aid do not suffer from food shortages.
in writing. − i abstained because the programmes for the poor must be implemented in the light of the judicial processes before the court of first instance. this is rightly noted by the commission in its 2012 budgetary estimates. in its judgment of 13 april 2011, t576/08, the court stated that the scheme financed only food from intervention stocks and did not cover the costs incurred in buying food on the market. i consider that, on the basis of that judgment, article 2 of regulation no 983/2008 cannot be regarded as the legal basis for the distribution of food to people in need. the commission should propose amendments to the regulation on the programme for the most deprived persons in order to find a way out of the current impasse at council level. the legal basis should be established before the start of the next financial programming period. agrees that the right to food is a fundamental human right and is guaranteed when all people have the physical and economic possibility to have access at all times to adequate, safe and nutritious food to meet their daily nutritional needs and to lead an active and healthy life; stresses that poor nutrition has a negative impact on health. high-quality food and healthy nutrition are particularly important for children as they contribute to meeting their developmental and educational needs. meanwhile, farmers must be guaranteed adequate and fair income and remuneration for their work. the commission should address rural poverty and the breakdown of rural communities.
in writing. − the right to food is a fundamental human right. however, millions of people in the eu are at risk of food insecurity, making the benefits of the food distribution programme for the poorest people undeniable. in this context, it is essential that all interested parties carry out a long-term, in-depth assessment of the suitability of the food distribution programme, in particular as part of the cap, in the light of the new funding period. in addition, the commission and the council should take the necessary decisions as soon as possible to avoid a sudden and significant reduction in food aid following a reduction in funding. if decisions are not taken in time, people who depend on food aid will suffer from food shortages. i believe that the commission should initiate draft legislation on the relevant minimum income schemes and the contribution compensatory income scheme with a financial contribution equivalent to at least 60% of the average national income.

when we consider the eu's raw materials strategy, and if we want to solve the raw materials problem in europe, we must start first with ourselves. it is generally accepted that the most readily available source of raw materials is waste. unfortunately, although the average rate of waste recycling in the european union is constantly increasing, there are still a number of member states where a significant proportion of waste ends up in landfills. this could therefore be seen as a major opportunity by countries that have long lived in a planned economy and whose economies are still largely based on production, processing or recycling rather than innovation. more attention to recycling and recovering waste would not only help to solve the eu's raw materials problems, but would also have significant benefits for national economies. i therefore call on both the commission and the member states to take a more active approach to the recovery of raw materials from waste.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex) is a very important element of the eu's migration management mechanism and i believe that its full potential has not yet been exploited. the importance of frontex has been particularly highlighted in recent months, as refugees from north africa have flooded europe. i therefore consider that the adoption of this amended regulation would be very timely, even though the amendments it envisages were drawn up on the basis of the commission's report already submitted in 2008 and the recommendations of the governing council. the objectives of the present proposal are to strengthen the agency's capacity to design, coordinate and implement activities, with particular emphasis on sharing tasks with the eu member states in terms of the allocation of human resources and technical equipment, as well as the extension of internal and external mandates and assignments.

in writing. - i voted for this document. dual-use goods licences are valid in the european union (dual-use goods are defined as goods, including software and technology, which can be used for both civilian and military purposes, as well as any goods that can be connected in any way to the production of nuclear weapons or other nuclear explosive devices). the regulation establishes a list of dual-use items and it is constantly updated to reflect the international commitments of the member states and rapid technological developments. this update of the list, which we voted on, will ensure full implementation of the commitments throughout the eu and will provide legal clarity for eu exporters on which goods require export licences.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to oblige the commission and the member states to establish a regime for the control of the safe transit of dual-use items by establishing a reliable system for reporting, collection, transmission and storage. it is essential to strengthen the export of chemical and biological weapons and to strengthen and strengthen international arms export licensing to ensure the safety of people. the dual-use authorisation is decided under international export control regimes in countries that fall into four main groups: the australia group, which seeks to prevent the spread of chemical and biological weapons; the nuclear suppliers group, which seeks to stop the spread of unmanned nuclear weapon delivery systems; the missile technology control group, which seeks to reduce the spread of nuclear weapons and control exports; and the wassenar agreement, which focuses on the transparency of export control regimes. all these export regime countries are committed to good relations, cooperation and security.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the international tropical timber agreement. the current state of the rain forests is tragic. the area of primary forest lost each year is the size of greece. this increases the risk of irreversible loss of biodiversity and global warming. although the first international tropical timber agreement was concluded more than 20 years ago, over-exploitation and illegal logging continue to be rampant. almost half of all logging activity in regions such as the amazon and congo river basins, southeast asia, and russia is illegal. so i support this international agreement on tropical timber, which i believe addresses the most important issues in the timber industry. the international tropical timber organisation will continue to address deforestation and illegal logging, but more can be done to strengthen enforcement of forestry legislation, for example, the eu should adopt strong sanctions such as fines proportionate to the environmental damage, the value of the timber or timber products involved, as well as the tax losses and economic damage caused by the infringement; confiscation of the timber and timber products involved; and the emergency suspension of the marketing authorisation.
