in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-switzerland agreement. switzerland is the european union's fourth largest trading partner. the volume of exports and imports of agricultural products from the eu and switzerland is particularly significant. in 2010, the eu exported eur 6,3 billion of agricultural products to switzerland, making it the third largest eu export market for agricultural products. the agreement aims to ensure mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and geographical indications in order to maintain conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products and to improve the quality of the food supply chain. the entry into force of the agreement will provide for better protection of origin and appropriate geographical indications for exporters of certain eu agricultural products such as meat and dairy products in one of the closest and largest export markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on the protection of designations of origin and geographical indications for agricultural products and foodstuffs. this agreement is of major importance for the european union switzerland is the eu's third largest export market for agricultural products. the conditions and arrangements for bilateral trade relations must therefore be continuously improved and updated. the agreement on trade in agricultural products was concluded in 1999 and entered into force in 2002. it did not create a completely free trade in agricultural products, but only partially liberalised certain agricultural sectors. by signing this new annex, the two parties to the agreement aim to ensure mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and geographical indications in order to maintain conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products and also to improve the quality of the food supply chain. this agreement is very important and long awaited, since until now only the protection of designations of origin for wines and spirits has been provided for in a bilateral agreement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as both parties agreed on a harmonised procedure to identify and effectively protect registered designations of origin and geographical indications. on the basis of this common understanding and the convergence of their national legislation, both parties have mutually recognised the list of registered protected agricultural products. the new annex 12 lists some 800 geographical indications registered in the eu and 22 geographical indications registered in switzerland. this is a serious and long-awaited improvement on the previously existing trading conditions, since until now only the protection of designations of origin for wines and spirits was provided for in the bilateral agreement with the swiss confederation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the entry into force of this agreement will significantly enhance the free trade relationship between the european union and the swiss confederation. in particular, the main barriers to trade will be removed and thus more opportunities will be created for access to the agricultural products market of the other country. it is welcome that after lengthy discussions, a harmonised procedure for the identification and effective protection of registered designations of origin and geographical indications has finally been agreed. it is gratifying that both parties have recognised the list of registered protected agricultural products.
in writing. − i have given my consent to the conclusion of this agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway, which will review the conditions for trade in agricultural products. norway is a member of the european economic area (eea) and enjoys the benefits of the internal market, but the 1992 eea agreement provides that agricultural and fishery products will not be subject to the free movement provisions. the agreement provides for the gradual liberalisation of agricultural production, with a review of the provisions of the agreement every two years. the latter agreement provides for full liberalisation, covering around 20% of eu exports to norway and amounting to some eur 250 million. in total, about 60% (in terms of market value) of agricultural trade between the kingdom of norway and the european union will be completely free.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway gradually liberalising trade in agricultural products between the two parties to the agreement. trade in agricultural products is an exclusive area of eu-norway relations, outside the scope of the european economic area agreement, which provides for the free movement of other products between the two countries. this agreement is part of the liberalisation process provided for in the eu-norway agreement, whereby the parties have committed themselves to reviewing the conditions for trade in agricultural products every two years, each time deciding what further action to take to remove all types of trade barriers in the agricultural sector. this time it is agreed that norway will apply tariff quotas or lower tariffs to some other important products such as meat, dairy products, fruit, vegetables and ornamental plants, while the eu will fully liberalise trade in those products for which norway already has a fully free trade regime (cheese, fresh oats, potato chips and petfood).
in writing. − i have supported this proposal because it provides for additional full liberalisation, which will cover around 20% of eu exports to norway and amount to around eur 250 million. in total, about 60% (in terms of market value) of agricultural trade between the kingdom of norway and the european union will be completely free. norway will apply tariff quotas or reduced rates to certain other important products such as meat, dairy products, fruit, vegetables and ornamental plants. the concessions granted by the european union to norway also include full liberalisation of those products for which norway applies full liberalisation and additional quotas for cheese, fresh lamb, potato chips and petfood. the agreement takes into account the situation of opium as a product of particular importance for agricultural production in both the eu and norway and provides for the relevant rules on tariff quotas or reduced customs duties; these duties will also be relevant in the medium and long term for agricultural production, taking into account the conditions provided for under the cap reforms after 2013. while norway's overall trade balance with the eu is positive, the agricultural trade balance is more favourable to the eu. between 2000 and 2007, eu exports of agricultural products doubled to €1.6 billion. however, the agreement will have budgetary implications. it is estimated that approximately eur 4,96 million in customs revenue will be lost (net of collection costs).
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the agreement will be mutually beneficial for both the european union and the kingdom of norway if it enters into force. this will be another major step towards the gradual liberalisation of agricultural trade between the two countries. it should be noted that only this agreement will allow for a fully free agricultural trade between norway and the eu, as it provides for additional full liberalisation of exports. in addition, tariff quotas and tariffs for certain other important products will be reduced. efficient measures will therefore continue to be taken to remove all types of barriers to trade in the agricultural sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this agreement. the eu's trade relations with liechtenstein are closely linked to the eu's trade relations with the swiss confederation, the european union's fourth largest trading partner. the eu and switzerland have defined their relations through bilateral agreements in various fields. following switzerland's rejection of the european economic area agreement in 1992, negotiations were launched on trade agreements in seven sectors, including the agricultural products sector, in order to mitigate the negative consequences. the so-called agricultural agreement was concluded in 1999 and entered into force on 1 june 2002. the agricultural agreement between the european community and switzerland was subsequently applied to the principality of liechtenstein. under the additional agreement, liechtenstein products are considered as products originating in switzerland. with this renewed agreement, the eu and switzerland aim to ensure mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and geographical indications in order to maintain conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the conclusion of another agreement between the european union and liechtenstein, which is very closely linked to the eu-switzerland agreement on the protection of designations of origin and geographical indications for agricultural products and foodstuffs. the scope of the eu-switzerland agreements on trade in agricultural products has been extended to the principality of liechtenstein since 2007, and it is this agreement that makes liechtenstein products products considered as products originating in switzerland. in the meantime, two food names included in the swiss geographical indications will also be applied in the territory of liechtenstein. by this annex to the agricultural agreement, which is extended to liechtenstein, the eu and switzerland seek to ensure the mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications in order to maintain the conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products while promoting quality in the food chain.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal, as this time a new annex (annex 12) is added to the agriculture agreement, the eu and switzerland seek to ensure mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications in order to maintain the conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products and at the same time to promote the quality of the food chain. it is by virtue of the additional agreement that liechtenstein products are considered as products originating in switzerland. the additional agreement between the european community, the swiss confederation and the principality of liechtenstein should therefore also be amended to extend the protection of geographical indications to liechtenstein. two names included in the swiss geographical indications will also be applied in the territory of liechtenstein.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the amendment of the additional agreement is a positive and necessary step towards improving bilateral agricultural trade between the ec and switzerland. it is noted that the entry into force of the amendment to the agreement will preserve the conditions for bilateral trade in agricultural products and foodstuffs, promote the quality of the food chain and the development of a system of designations of origin and geographical indications in a coherent manner. in addition, the eu and switzerland will be given a favourable opportunity to ensure the mutual recognition of protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications. it should be noted that the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation on trade in agricultural products will also apply to the principality of liechtenstein. the protection of geographical indications will therefore extend to liechtenstein and its products will be considered as products originating in switzerland.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this agreement. until now, the south pacific fisheries have been the responsibility of two regional fisheries management organisations (rfmo) in the south pacific: the iattc and the wcpfc. the objective of both organisations was to manage long-distance migratory fish stocks, and therefore stocks of other species were not regulated in this large area, except for the exclusive economic zones (eez) of coastal states, which applied their own rules. in order to fill this gap and in view of the fact that both iez and high seas are fished, the australian, chilean and new zealand governments decided in 2006 to open international consultations with a view to establishing a regional fisheries management organisation for the south pacific (rfmvo) with the objective of working together to fill the gap in the conservation and management of highly migratory fish stocks and the protection of the biodiversity of the high seas of the south pacific, without prejudice to international law and in line with good practice. the eu has been involved in the negotiation process from the outset and has made good progress, so it is now necessary to allow the eu to ratify the convention and to be active in international and bilateral fora, and to encourage countries with fishing fleets in the convention's region to sign, ratify and apply the convention in order to accelerate its entry into force.
in writing. − i supported this legislation because, as both organisations were aiming to manage highly migratory fish, stocks of other species in this large area were not regulated, except in the exclusive economic zones (eez) of coastal states which applied their own rules. in order to fill this gap and in view of the fact that both iez and high seas are fished, the australian, chilean and new zealand governments decided in 2006 to open international consultations with a view to establishing a regional fisheries management organisation for the south pacific (rfmvo) with the objective of working together to fill the gap in the conservation and management of highly migratory fish stocks and the protection of the biodiversity of the high seas of the south pacific, without prejudice to international law and in line with good practice. the parties now have to ratify the convention, and the purpose of this draft council decision is to enable the eu to ratify the convention.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it is appropriate and absolutely necessary for the eu to ratify the convention on the conservation and management of high seas fishery resources in the south pacific, as it has fisheries-related interests in the south pacific. in addition, under the terms of the un convention on the law of the sea, the eu is obliged to cooperate with other stakeholders in the management and conservation of the region's resources. it is important to stress that every effort should be made to ensure that the majority of coastal states in this part of the world recognise, as soon as possible, the management measures applicable in their waters in accordance with international law and do not oppose their implementation. it is to be welcomed that after lengthy discussions it has been agreed that the convention will ensure access for a contracting party to ports of other states parties. under this provision, community pelagic vessels will be granted access to at least chilean ports.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this agreement. the commission will first negotiate an agreement on mutual recognition of the conclusions of the certification of aviation products, parts and appliances. brazil is the tenth largest economy in the world and the eu's tenth largest trading partner. the agreement will therefore be of great benefit to eu and brazilian companies, as it provides for shorter, simpler and therefore less costly product approval procedures and mutual recognition of certification findings.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives the european parliament its support for the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an agreement with brazil in the field of civil aviation security. the aim of this agreement is to increase mutual trust in the trade of aeronautical products by harmonising product certification systems, while minimising the duplication of assessment, testing and inspection. the unification of these systems would allow the importing authority to issue its own certificate for the aeronautical product, part or appliance without having to repeat all the assessments carried out by the exporting authority. the european union's aeronautical product certification scheme has been fully taken into account in the draft text of the eu-brazil agreement, which clearly separates the tasks of certification of aeronautical goods and parts from those of organisations involved in the design and manufacture of these products and parts thereof. the text of the agreement is also designed to allow the parties to respond flexibly and promptly to safety concerns, or to establish an appropriate higher level of protection for their safety, as appropriate.
in writing. − i have endorsed the document because this agreement will be of great benefit to eu and brazilian companies, as it provides for shorter, simpler and therefore less expensive product approval procedures and mutual recognition of certification findings. the agreement will also bring a net benefit to the european union by establishing a procedure for all member states to mutually recognise the findings of certification in all areas of airworthiness. the main objectives of this agreement are to facilitate trade in goods and services covered by the agreement, to minimise duplication of assessment, testing and control (essential regulatory differences to be identified) and to rely on the certification system of either country to determine compliance with the requirements of the other.
in writing. − i support this resolution as it is another major step towards the gradual opening of markets and ensuring a high level of regulatory cooperation. it should be noted that the entry into force of the agreement will lead to more favourable conditions for trade. in addition, mutual recognition of certification findings in all areas of airworthiness and maintenance will be ensured for all eu member states. the agreement provides for shorter, simpler and cheaper product approval procedures, which will facilitate relations between eu and brazilian companies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement, which aims to improve the procedure for surrender for the purpose of prosecution or punishment between the member states and norway and iceland. the agreement only extends the provisions already in force in the eu member states and the contracting parties will ensure that the extradition system is based on surrender on the basis of an arrest warrant.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives the european parliament its consent to the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway and the republic of iceland on a mutual legal assistance agreement and a transfer agreement. this agreement aims to improve the surrender procedure for the prosecution or punishment of a criminal offence between the member states and norway and iceland. the contracting parties shall ensure that the system of extradition is based on surrender pursuant to an arrest warrant, in accordance with the provisions of this agreement. an arrest warrant may be issued for an offence punishable by a custodial sentence or a term of imprisonment of at least 12 months under the law of the issuing state and, where a sentence has already been imposed or a decision on imprisonment has been adopted, for a period of at least four months. the procedure for the conclusion of this agreement was launched as early as 2001, but for various reasons, including the many changes that have taken place in the relevant policy areas and in the structure of the european union itself during that period, it is only now, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, that the procedure for the conclusion of the agreement can be completed.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the situation of women approaching retirement age, as older women face at least two types of discrimination in the labour market, based on gender and age. it is important to note that women represent at least 50% of the population of any eu country and therefore form an important part of the labour force. europe also has the highest percentage of older women in the world. i therefore support the call in the resolution for the commission and the member states to take appropriate and effective action to combat discrimination, including the change of gender and age stereotypes, and to promote solidarity between generations. i believe that member states should strive to integrate the gender dimension as effectively as possible in the design and implementation of pension reform, promote a more equal calculation of contributions for male and female pensions, promote actions to reduce the risk of poverty, take measures to address the poverty that older people are currently experiencing, improve the quality, accessibility and affordability of health care and end the practice of mandatory retirement, and address discrimination by enabling older women to participate in the labour market. i also support the other important call in the resolution for the commission and the member states to implement appropriate policies to reconcile work, family and private life.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the gender gap in terms of social and economic status is most deeply rooted in the traditional division of roles between the sexes, where men are considered responsible for the maintenance of the family and women for unpaid housework and care of family and relatives, which has a major impact on women's opportunities, compared to men, to obtain social guarantees, such as the right to a pension, and therefore on their situation in old age, especially in the event of divorce, separation or orphanhood. in addition, women's careers are more likely to be slower, shorter and/or interrupted by maternity leave or caring for elderly, disabled family members, and they earn less on average than men, as there is still a pay gap for the same work, and as a result women receive lower pensions and are at increased risk of poverty in old age. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission and the member states to adopt without delay a comprehensive and multi-faceted approach to employment and social policy, including gender equality and age, in order to ensure the employment and social inclusion of women. calls on the commission and the member states to also make a thorough assessment of the situation of the older generation of women currently in poverty and to take appropriate and effective measures to end poverty among these women as soon as possible;

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, in order to mitigate the impact of the current economic and financial crisis, credit systems must operate in a transparent manner and it is necessary to limit market distortions and ensure a level playing field for all market participants. efforts should also be made to implement an effective control mechanism to ensure that firms are financially sound and thus to facilitate public support by export credit agencies. it should be noted that the role of the credit agency is of great importance for the development of world trade. in addition, these export credit agencies have become the largest source of official financial assistance to developing countries. they provide businesses with greater access to private sector-backed credit services, complement private sector-backed funds and insurance, and create more job opportunities by supporting exports and investment. given the importance of these agencies, it is therefore necessary to ensure that they operate in a transparent manner and that bribery and corruption are prevented.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. fair access to raw materials and stable and predictable prices are essential for the development of european industry, its competitiveness, innovation and survival. resource policy and resource diplomacy are of crucial importance to the eu not only in terms of industrial policy and international trade, but also in general terms of the various areas of domestic and foreign and security policy. i agree that action is needed to decouple economic growth from increased resource use, which would help reduce dependence on imports. it is necessary to invest in research, technological development and innovation and to exploit the potential of public procurement to promote the use of resource-efficient products.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the raw materials supply industry in europe is increasingly at a disadvantage. the countries of the european union do not have many of the raw materials they need, so they are forced to import them from other countries. it is essential that the european union establishes partnerships with countries in eastern europe, latin america or asia that have valuable raw materials or minerals. the partnership with china is also expected to grow in the future, as it controls 97% of the world's rare earth production and severely restricts its exports to other countries. these resources are crucial for the transition to a low-carbon economy and for mitigating future climate change. to do this, the european union needs to develop a strategy that identifies actions on key and essential raw materials and improves relations with resource-rich countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it sets out a range of measures to reduce consumption, increase organic processing and increase exports, in order to maintain competition and reduce the price of raw materials. the eu needs a strong industrial base, which, as it becomes greener, is highly dependent on the supply of the right raw materials to make the transition to a low-carbon economy and to remain competitive. the complexity of administrative procedures and the lack of coordination between the management authorities sometimes lead to mineral permits being issued with a delay of several years; as this delay is unreasonably long, it increases the cost of capital invested and puts small and medium-sized enterprises out of the market. the eu is heavily dependent on imports of many raw materials, especially key raw materials. the scarcity of resources may worsen the international political situation and lead to a resource war and a widening gap between high- and low-resource countries. no one would benefit from that scenario. it is therefore necessary to develop a new approach to non-energy and non-agricultural raw materials, in particular those identified as being of primary importance, in order to address the issue in an innovative and innovation-driven way, in order to ultimately avoid a game in which there can only be winners and losers. alongside its industrial innovation strategy, which aims to reduce consumption and increase recycling in addition to the sustainable local potential of the eu, the eu will of course continue to rely on external suppliers of its raw materials. this is why diplomacy on raw materials is of particular importance.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the european union needs a coherent and effective raw materials strategy to help boost growth and create jobs. the eu needs to strengthen its supply of raw materials, improve their efficiency and meet the needs of industry and the raw materials sector, especially now that global demand for raw materials is increasing. i support the proposal to the commission to establish a mechanism for the accumulation of rare earth elements, which would ensure that european companies, especially smes, have access to strategic materials and be protected from monopoly pressure and price increases. it is important to note that fair access to raw materials and stable prices will ensure the competitiveness of eu industry, environmental efficiency and innovation. in this context, the commission must constantly monitor the elimination of export and import restrictions and trade-distorting measures.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, mineral products and other raw materials account for up to 30% of lithuania's imports and exports, and so the shortage of raw materials is a very serious problem for my country. unfavourable raw material prices are holding back lithuania's export growth. according to a swedbank study published last month, rising commodity prices are also having a significant impact on high inflation in lithuania. the strong growth in raw material prices also means that the construction sector in lithuania will face difficulties in 2011. construction companies go bankrupt every month. it is time for the eu to develop an industrial innovation strategy to promote sustainability and security of energy supply. i agree with the rapporteur that the green paper is a positive first step. eu industry must use raw materials more efficiently by working with international suppliers. we should also promote mineral exploration and exploitation, particularly through eu programmes in the dg for research and innovation. the future of eu industry depends heavily on non-energy, non-agricultural raw materials. this is our chance to turn a challenge into an opportunity for european industry and for our own countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the main objective of this report is to lay the foundations for the medium and long-term development of the black sea fisheries. the black sea region is of major economic, social and political importance. following the example of the baltic sea organisation, a black sea regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) should be established to monitor the state of fish stocks throughout the black sea and, on the basis of scientific advice, to establish quotas for all countries in the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the ecological balance and fish stocks in the black sea have been severely reduced. this has resulted in illegal, unregulated and undeclared fishing in the black sea. restoring the ecosystem and increasing fish stocks is only possible through active cooperation between the eu and the black sea states. the black sea borders six countries, only two of which are members of the european union. it is therefore essential that the remaining countries strengthen their cooperation with each other and start to respect the principles of the common fisheries policy of the european union in order to improve the protection of the black sea basin and to address the problems effectively. in order to preserve the fisheries in the black sea, it is planned to establish a regional fisheries management organisation comprising all the black sea states and the european union. it is also necessary to take into account that it may be difficult to persuade non-eu countries to negotiate and to enter into political agreements. the future of the black sea depends on this and mutual cooperation is essential to achieve positive results.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because of the need to create a strong, stable and sustainable fisheries sector at european level, and in particular for the black sea, to provide for a specific policy to protect fish stocks, improve their status and ensure that the black sea fisheries sector is adapted to the specificities of the black sea region. the fisheries sector must be managed in a manner that ensures ecosystem suitability and sustainability, the development of legal fisheries and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential to develop an effective policy, adapted to the specificities of the black sea region, which will help to conserve fisheries resources and ecosystems. it should be noted that the black sea is an important fishing region, but the state of most fish stocks is poor. regional action is needed to help them recover. in particular, the commission must maintain a permanent dialogue with the non-eu black sea littoral states. sustainable development must also be promoted through fisheries management, cutting-edge research and technology, data collection and the assessment of fisheries resources in the black sea region. i believe that new ways and opportunities should be explored to ensure the sustainable and responsible use of fisheries resources and to promote sustainable, competitive and diverse aquaculture in this region. only by working together can we ensure that the european fisheries sector is strong, stable and sustainable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. more than 90% of oil and 60% of gas in the european union is extracted from the high seas. the oil-drilling accidents of recent years have prompted all operators involved in offshore oil and gas exploration and production to reassess the safety of their industry. i agree with the need to develop a strong safety culture by involving workers on the high seas in health and safety initiatives, to provide rigorous training in disaster management scenarios, to develop site-specific emergency plans and to ensure through appropriate regulation that operators have sufficient financial resources to compensate for the damage caused.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the growing importance of offshore oil and gas exploration and production, where accidents could cause serious damage to the member states of the european union. more than 90% of oil and about 60% of gas in the european union is extracted from the high seas, with the north sea being the largest source of oil and gas. the tragedy of the 2010 oil spill in the gulf of mexico was the largest in the world, with catastrophic consequences for people and the environment. one reason for the accident was that the company responsible for the oil exploitation did not have adequate insulation equipment. in order to ensure safety in the european union, it is necessary to designate an authority which should approve the safety evidence documents before any action relating to the extraction of gas or oil resources is taken. strict safety control requirements should be applied to the oil extraction industry worldwide to avoid future harmful effects and to ensure environmental protection.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the department of home affairs should develop a method based on the risk assessment of active operations, applicable to specific installations, operations and environments, similar to the 'safety proof' method used in the north sea. 'safety evidence' is a risk-based, site-specific approach whereby operators must demonstrate to the relevant national health, safety and environmental authorities that all hazards have been addressed and the necessary control measures have been put in place. before any operation is started, the safety evidence documents and any subsequent amendments thereto should be approved by the relevant authority. pre-drilling checks ensure that activities are not carried out automatically and that operations are not started without risk assessment and mitigation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which seeks to address a number of pressing issues concerning the safety of offshore oil and gas exploration and production. first of all, it is essential to ensure the effective functioning of the polluter pays principle. it is therefore appropriate to require undertakings wishing to engage in activities related to oil and gas exploration and production to demonstrate that they have sufficient financial resources to implement that principle. i agree with the proposal that stopping new deepwater oil drilling in all eu waters would be an illogical, hasty, disproportionate step towards ensuring high safety standards throughout the eu. decision-making and regulation in offshore oil exploration and production activities should take into account existing best practices and implement principles to control coastal hazards. i believe that a transparent, consistent and effective set of rules should be in place at eu level for all workers in the offshore sector. in view of the nature and the risks of the work of workers in this sector and in order to avoid human error as much as possible, workers should be covered by insurance which is proportionate to the risks they face.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on women entrepreneurship in small and medium-sized enterprises. in the business world, people who own their own businesses are often more dedicated to their work than employees, and they sacrifice their personal lives to stay competitive. women entrepreneurs face an even greater risk because they have to overcome discrimination in a traditionally male environment. many of these women have to juggle their business successes with family responsibilities. women are now an important part of the workforce in the member states. i agree with the rapporteur that we should get positive momentum through the sharing of best practice. this could be done through a women's business development agency, which would coordinate the women's representatives from each member state. the agency would work with national governments to promote, support and sustain projects for women. the approach of banks to women entrepreneurs is also very important. some banks already have systems in place to help women start businesses, and indeed recognize the unique approach of women to work. i agree with the rapporteurs that all financial institutions should adopt this best practice.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i agree that member states must have policies to help women achieve a good work-life balance. it is essential to establish an appropriate childcare infrastructure to allow women to enter the labour market more quickly and flexibly. the establishment of adequate childcare facilities is necessary as their lack of affordability, accessibility and quality creates additional obstacles for women who want to work or start a business.
in writing. − i voted for this report because men and women have unequal opportunities to manage and develop businesses and because empowering women entrepreneurs is a long-term process that requires time to change societal structures and attitudes. while women have always been entrepreneurs, certain rules and traditional roles have not always allowed them to choose the entrepreneurial path, and therefore it is necessary to encourage member states to carry out national campaigns, including various events and seminars, to better inform women about the use of the european microfinance facility progress and to inform them about all the funding opportunities offered under this facility. the european parliament calls on the commission and the member states to promote the participation of women in the mainstream business community, i.e. local chambers of commerce, lobby groups and industrial organisations, as this would enable them to develop and strengthen their competitive business skills. calls on the chambers of commerce to actively encourage women entrepreneurs to participate in their activities and to promote the establishment of dedicated services and representative groups for women entrepreneurs, which would empower them and help promote an entrepreneurial culture; in addition, the commission should organise a campaign to support women's professional activity by encouraging them to take up entrepreneurship, while informing them of the available measures to facilitate the taking up of economic activities.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this document because equality between women and men is one of the fundamental principles of the eu, enshrined in the treaty on european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and because inequality between women and men in entrepreneurship and decision-making still persists. i believe that member states should have policies to help women achieve a good work-life balance and to create appropriate childcare facilities, as the lack of affordability, accessibility and quality of these facilities creates additional obstacles for women who want to start a business.
in writing. − the free market system gives all citizens, regardless of their gender, the opportunity to achieve economic independence. it is therefore essential to establish effective mechanisms to ensure the implementation of effective gender equality policies. it is worth noting that smes are emerging as a tool for women to achieve economic independence. in this context, member states should provide more funding opportunities for business entities, in particular for women-owned small and medium-sized enterprises, in a fair and equitable manner. the public needs to be better informed about the european microfinance facility progress, its implementation possibilities and its benefits. in order to increase women's entrepreneurial opportunities, member states should develop specific national education programmes, implement cross-border cooperation programmes, and encourage women's participation in the main business communities. women must be encouraged to participate actively in the labour market, thereby creating favourable conditions for reconciling work and private life.
for the efd group it is indeed a good thing that the european union institutions have turned their attention to one of the most important problems facing consumers in recent times. of course, i am talking about electricity and gas prices. in the context of the economic crisis, the price of electricity becomes an important incentive for all consumers to survive and overcome further economic difficulties. the higher and more recently speculative prices of energy commodities are causing frustration in both the business community and household consumers. for these reasons, and in order to put energy suppliers in a position where they cannot abuse their dominant position, i support the provisions in the regulation that penalties for infringements should take account not only of the seriousness of the infringements and the profits made, but also of the damage caused to consumers. i think that this should include the various possible disruptions in energy supply which could arise from political differences between individual countries. some european countries have experienced this and lithuania is one of them. therefore, safeguards are necessary in the regulation to prevent such cases from recurring.
in writing. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the principle of transparency enshrined in the treaty has become a legally binding fundamental right of citizens. this means that eu decisions must be taken as openly as possible and as intelligibly as possible for citizens, especially since the perception and access of our citizens to the activities of the european union and the documents it adopts are linked to the evaluation of the eu's overall activities and to their confidence in its work. transparency and openness to the public are particularly necessary in order to strengthen democratic principles and respect for fundamental rights. it is also the best way to prevent corruption, fraud, conflicts of interest and mismanagement. i would like to emphasise that such decisions to deny citizens access to documents of the eu institutions must be based on clearly and rigorously defined exceptions, duly explained and justified, so that citizens understand the negative response and make effective use of the remedies available to them. the european parliament has already done a lot of work in this area, but all eu institutions need to work together to develop more transparent freedom of information rules that take due account of the proposals in this report, the latest case law of the court of justice and the new treaties. in order to fully ensure an open and continuous dialogue with citizens and their representative associations and to improve the practice of the institutions towards greater transparency, the council and the commission should negotiate with parliament with a view to adopting a new regulation on the right of access to documents.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the lisbon treaty introduced a new constitutional framework for eu institutional transparency to ensure an open, efficient and independent european administration by establishing a strict fundamental right of access to documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. transparency is a general principle and, with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it has become a legally binding fundamental right of citizens. therefore, any decision to refuse access to documents must be based on clearly and explicitly defined exceptions. the right balance needs to be struck between transparency and data protection. data protection should not be 'abused', in particular for the purpose of resolving conflicts of interest. documents relating to international agreements, including those adopted by any body responsible for enforcing the application of such agreements, should be disclosed to the public, as the possibility of their being made public cannot be categorically excluded. access to them should be refused only in the event of a genuine threat to international relations. the parliament, which is elected by eu citizens under the treaties, plays an institutional role in representing the public interest. it is necessary to ensure that the new prerogatives conferred on parliament in the field of international agreements are fully respected and that no bilateral agreements concluded with third countries may prohibit this.
in writing. europe is facing a very difficult period today, one in which it is necessary to manage the current situation and find the political momentum to invest in the growth of today's and tomorrow's economies. europe is also facing a deep crisis of political confidence, which will require a much greater concentration of wisdom and political will than before. this is what our citizens expect from the eu institutions and from their national governments. the difficult situation in some euro area countries should not be used as a pretext for a two-speed europe and prevent economic growth in a united, coherent and cohesive way in the member states and the eu as a whole. we must realise that only more effective and rigorous governance of the economies of the 27 member states can ensure deeper integration, greater social guarantees for our citizens and greater confidence in the european union itself.
the energy market integrity and transparency regulation is of particular importance to the european union in the context of the process of liberalising the gas and electricity markets. in this context, one aspect is important to note. in order to ensure the functioning of a single and transparent energy market in the european union, we need to ensure that the rules we adopt apply equally and without exception to all actors in the eu energy market, regardless of their true origin. market surveillance authorities should ensure that the final entity behind a transaction is identified and subject to eu law. unfortunately, there are still situations where third-country entities, in particular gazprom, have a real dominant or even monopoly position in one or another member state, but as they do so not only directly but also through controlled undertakings, the rules ensuring market transparency do not apply to them. i therefore welcome this report and call on the commission to further improve the rules governing the energy market in the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of granting financial aid to austria. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. in austria, workers were laid off due to globalisation and major structural changes in the production of mobile phones and devices, which was relocated to asia. austria indicates that the production of printed circuit boards decreased by almost 11% in 2008, compared to a decrease of 5,4% in china and 4,8% in the rest of the world. as a result, in november 2008, at&s decided to move all of its printing plate production from leoben to shanghai, resulting in 603 redundancies in leoben between november 2008 and december 2009, and the closure of the at&s plant in fondorf, some 50 km from leoben, resulting in the loss of 200 jobs that required support.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation and to assist them with their reintegration into the labour market. the scope of the egf has been extended from 1 may 2009, it is possible to grant aid to workers made redundant as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis. the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 provides for the possibility to mobilise the egf within the annual ceiling of eur 500 million. on 11 march 2010, austria submitted an application to mobilise the egf, following redundancies in at&s, a company active in the leoben area in the region of eastern upper styria, specialising in the production of printed circuit boards. this application complies with the requirements for financial support as laid down in article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006. i therefore supported the commission's proposal to allocate an amount of eur 1 221 128.
in writing. - i voted in favour of granting financial aid to austria. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 9 march 2010, austria submitted an application to mobilise the egf in respect of redundancies in 54 enterprises active in the production of base metals. this application qualifies for financial assistance and i therefore approve the allocation of eur 8 284 908.

in writing. − the european union has put in place appropriate legislative and budgetary measures to provide additional support to workers who have suffered damage as a result of major structural changes in the world trade system and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. each year, technical assistance may be granted at the initiative of the commission at a rate of 0,35% of the annual amount of the egf to finance the monitoring, information, administrative and technical support, audit, control and evaluation activities necessary for the implementation of the egf regulation, including the provision of information and consultation on the use of the egf, monitoring and evaluation to the member states and the provision of information on the use of the egf to the european and national social partners. i agree with the commission's request to mobilise eur 610 000 in 2011.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the commission's proposal to improve the collection, compilation and dissemination of information on the european globalisation adjustment fund and its support by creating a new database. in making this proposal, the commission hopes that mobilising the egf in this way will improve the efficiency of the management of the egf, which in turn will improve the functioning of the market. it should be noted that this is not the first time that the commission has submitted such a proposal to the budgetary authority this year, and that under the interinstitutional agreement which entered into force on 17 may 2006, it was decided that a maximum of eur 500 million could be allocated to this purpose. the main funding would be for monitoring, information, administrative and technical assistance, database creation, exchange of best practices between member states and evaluation.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 provides that each year 0.35% of the annual ceiling may be allocated to technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. i therefore supported the commission's proposal for an amount of eur 610 000. following the commission's proposal, this amount should be used to finance the following activities: monitoring activities commission will collect data on applications received and accepted, as well as on measures proposed and implemented, and will update and publish a publication on egf statistics; information activities egf website will be regularly updated and expanded, as well as translated into all official eu languages. a press release will be issued and the annual report of the egf will be prepared, translated, published and disseminated. the general awareness of the egf and its visibility will be increased; the commission will establish standardised procedures for the egf applications and their processing for the establishment of a database. this will allow for simplification of applications, faster processing and easy reporting for different purposes; two meetings of the expert group on egf persons relations, one from each member state, making a total of 27 members, will be organised for administrative and technical assistance; exchange of best practices between member states; evaluation the mid-term evaluation activities of the egf, as set out in article 17 (1) (a) of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006, have been allocated from the 2010 budget. the final evaluation of the egf will not start until 2012.

in writing. - i voted for this important document. the commission proposal for a regulation (remit energy market integrity and transparency regulation) is an eu legal framework to prevent market abuse and manipulation in the energy sector (gas and electricity). unfair practices in the wholesale energy market affect the price level. such practices may result in significant price volatility, increase energy prices for end-users (citizens and businesses) and reduce the confidence of potential investors in energy infrastructure projects. transparency of energy markets is a necessary condition for further integration of the eu energy market, which should bring great benefits to consumers. the regulation prohibits market abuse consisting of trading on the basis of inside information and market manipulation in the wholesale energy products (electricity and gas). i agree that the penalties for market manipulation should be uniform across the eu to prevent companies that violate remit from establishing themselves in the member states with the least severe sanctions. i support the call that the commission should present proposals for further harmonisation of sanctions and for minimum requirements for sanctions at eu level by the end of 2012.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to prevent the concealment of energy production capacity and to prevent market abuse and manipulation in the energy sector. preventing abuse is also crucial to enhance long-term confidence in the gas and electricity market. the abuse of the gas and electricity market in one of the member states of the european union has an impact not only on wholesale prices in other countries but also on retail prices for consumers and micro-enterprises. it is therefore essential that this issue be dealt with by a joint decision of the eu as a whole, rather than by individual member states. otherwise, there could be significant price fluctuations, higher energy costs for end-users and reduced investment in energy infrastructure. in some energy markets, conduct that undermines the integrity of the market is not currently prohibited in full and therefore requires strict action.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it aims to prevent market abuse and manipulation in the energy sector (gas and electricity). the regulation prohibits market abuse, which consists of trading on the basis of information which has not been made public (articles 1 (1) and 3) and market manipulation (articles 2 (2) and 4) in the wholesale energy products (electricity and gas). it requires market participants to disclose information which has not been made public (article 4 (4)). the main body for monitoring the transactions market is the recently established agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer). article 7 of the regulation requires market participants to provide the agency with data on their transactions in wholesale energy products. the agency shall monitor these data and report annually to the european commission (article 6). the agency shall share the information it receives with other authorities, in particular with national regulatory authorities and with the financial and competition authorities of the member states (article 8). the eu-wide penalties for market manipulation should be uniform in order to prevent undertakings that infringe remit from establishing themselves in the member states with the least severe sanctions. the commission should therefore submit proposals for further harmonisation of sanctions and for minimum requirements for sanctions at eu level by the end of 2012.
in writing. − energy is a highly relevant topic in the eu and especially for its energy island, of which lithuania is a part. this document calls for the creation of a single eu electricity and gas network, managed by brussels. increased eu involvement in the management of energy networks should protect eu citizens from sudden price spikes and ensure greater stability in the supply of energy resources to consumers. the document also calls for the identification of the energy laws of the countries concerned, thereby facilitating trade in this sector. the implementation of these proposals would bring lithuania and all the baltic states into the eu's single energy grid and reduce their vulnerability to energy blackmail. all this would also encourage internal competition between energy suppliers, which should have a positive impact on the price of electricity and gas on the market.
in writing. − the treaty of lisbon entered into force on 1 december 2009, introducing a number of new legal frameworks aimed at simplifying the implementation, application and enforcement of eu legislation. article 17 of the treaty on european union confers on the commission the primary role of guardian of the treaties. in this context, the commission has the power and duty to initiate infringement procedures against a member state which is not complying with its obligations under the treaties, including its obligations regarding fundamental human rights. this 27th annual report on the monitoring of the application of european union law showed that, despite the decline in the number of infringement cases opened by the commission, 2 900 complaints and infringement cases had been examined by the end of 2009 and that in more than 50% of cases member states continued to delay the transposition of the provisions of the directives into national law. i believe that this is not a satisfactory situation and that the commission should be more transparent in the conduct of the infringement procedures initiated and inform eu citizens as soon as possible, by appropriate means, of the steps taken to meet their requests. i agree that the commission should set a deadline for the member states to comply with the judgments of the court of justice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's assessment of the commission's role as guardian of the eu treaties. this is the 27th annual report by the european parliament on the commission's supervisory role in the member states. the first stage of this infringement procedure is one of the areas of direct interaction between europe and eu citizens, where citizens turn to the commission and parliament for help in exercising their european rights. it is therefore essential that complainants are treated in accordance with the principle of good administration. the report thus points out that, although the number of infringement procedures decreased in 2009, the situation remains unsatisfactory, and that this is mainly the fault of the member states, which are slow to transpose eu law into their national law. the european parliament also calls on the commission to ensure greater transparency in the process of dealing with citizens' complaints and asks the commission to propose a deadline within which member states should comply with the court of justice's judgments.
in writing. − this report assesses the commission's monitoring of the implementation of eu law in 2009. it focuses on the important role of the commission as guardian of the treaty and on the commission's powers and duty to initiate infringement proceedings against a member state which has failed to fulfil its obligations under the treaty. it reiterates that the infringement procedure consists of two stages: the administrative (investigative) stage and the judicial stage before the court of justice. the role of citizens (complainants) is crucial at the administrative stage, rather than ensuring compliance with union law. bringing europe closer to its citizens and good governance are closely linked. one of the areas of direct interaction between europe and eu citizens is the administrative phase, linked to article 258 tfeu, when citizens turn to the commission and parliament for help in exercising their european rights. it is therefore essential that complainants are treated in accordance with the principle of good administration. the rapporteur therefore calls on the commission to present a proposal in the form of a regulation on procedural law on the basis of the new legal basis provided for in article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union in order to better ensure citizens' rights and transparency. the procedural law would in no way restrict the commission's freedom of action, but would only ensure that the commission, in the exercise of its powers, respects the principle of an open, efficient and independent european administration, as set out in article 298 tfeu and article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the public's right of access to documents for 2009/2010. citizens are now demanding more democracy, transparency, openness of institutions and political actors and a stronger fight against corruption, so access to documents and information is one way to ensure citizens' participation in the democratic process, the prevention of corruption and the fight against it. it is important to note that, in order to ensure the accountability and legitimacy of a democratic political system, citizens have the right to know how their representatives, elected or appointed to public institutions, or persons representing member states at european or international level, operate, how the decision-making process takes place (reviewing documents, amendments, schedules, actors involved, votes cast, etc.), how taxpayers' money is distributed and allocated, and what the results of its use are. i therefore support this resolution and believe that the eu should be the first to show the member states and third countries the example of transparency of institutions and modern democracy.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the treaty of lisbon established a new constitutional framework for the transparency of the eu institutions, with the aim of making the european administration open, efficient and independent, by establishing a strong fundamental right of access to documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. this right is granted by the treaty not only to eu citizens but also to any natural or legal person established in an eu member state and should be exercised in accordance with the general principles and limits (protection of certain public or private interests) laid down in the regulations of the european parliament and of the council. transparency is a legally binding fundamental right of citizens and therefore all decisions to refuse access to documents must be based on clear and strictly defined exceptions, duly explained and supported by logical arguments, so that citizens understand the negative answer and make effective use of the remedies available to them.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because access to documents and information is one of the ways of ensuring citizens' participation in the democratic process and the prevention and fight against corruption. the treaty of lisbon establishes a new constitutional framework for the transparency of the institutions of the european union, with the aim of making the european administration open, efficient and independent, by establishing a strong fundamental right of access to documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. the european parliament thus stresses that the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies currently lack coherent administrative law, e.g. there are no rules on administrative decisions subject to appeal, and therefore calls on the eu institutions to define a common eu administrative law as a matter of urgency. the european union should also be the first to show the member states and third countries the example of transparency of institutions and modern democracy. since the principle of transparency has already become a legally binding fundamental right of citizens, transparency at the level of the european union should be reflected in the actions of the member states when transposing eu legislation into national law. the european parliament therefore considers that the amendment of the regulation on public access to documents should strengthen the right of access to documents without in any way reducing the existing standards of protection of this right and should take account of the case law of the court of justice. in addition, the revised regulation should be simple and accessible to citizens in order to enable them to exercise their right more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because i believe that it is necessary to allow citizens access to documents as much as possible, and that if they are truly confidential, this must be justified by clearly and strictly defined exceptions. the decisions of the european union must be taken in a transparent and open manner and must be as understandable as possible to the citizens of the european union. this will strengthen democratic principles and respect for fundamental human rights. it is also the best way to prevent corruption, fraud, conflicts of interest and mismanagement.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur that transparency is essential to ensure the accountability and legitimacy of a democratic political system. citizens have the right to know how and why political decisions are taken. lithuania is experiencing a crisis of public distrust due to a lack of transparency in its institutions. the courts in lithuania and europe have demonstrated their vulnerability to political manipulation. public confidence in the courts and local government remains low. according to a vilmorus survey, only 19% of lithuanian citizens trust the courts, compared to 35% a few years ago. according to the 'bertelsmann transformation index', the transparency of municipal decision-making is also not very high in lithuania. the city council acts are rarely found online, and decisions are usually only known after they have been adopted. it is important that our legislative and judicial processes are more transparent, accountable and accessible to the public. this report recalls that the treaty of lisbon has created a new constitutional framework for the transparency of the eu institutions, with the aim of making decision-making more open and efficient. all that's missing is the political will.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document as it draws attention to the commission's recently revised code of conduct for members of the commission and in particular its provisions on the financial declarations of members of the commission. it is decided to monitor the application of the new code of conduct for members of the commission on a regular basis in order to ensure that the european union achieves the highest standards of governance.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as aiming to create new trade opportunities, strengthen multilateral trade rules, address the problems associated with the current imbalances in the trading system and use trade for sustainable development, while underlining the importance of economic integration of developing countries, especially the least developed countries, in the belief that a multilateral system based on fairer rules will facilitate fair and free trade for the development of all continents.
in writing. − i support the provisions of this resolution on the state of play of the negotiations on the doha development agenda. i believe that comprehensive and balanced results will only be achieved if the negotiations on all the areas currently under discussion are concluded. given the particular importance of the wto as part of global economic governance to the world, we must make every effort to ensure that any wto reform agenda is considered, analysed and discussed with the principles of transparency and sufficient time for consultation to involve all members and other stakeholders. it is important to note that in order to ensure economic growth and poverty reduction worldwide, it is essential that all wto members continue to contribute to the comprehensive, balanced development of the wto. it is therefore essential to ascertain whether the changed economic circumstances since the start of the doha round are not an obstacle to the achievement of the initial objectives of the doha round. i support the proposal to encourage the developed and advanced countries to support the participation of the least developed countries in this negotiating process. i think market access is not the only solution for many of the poorer countries, because they don't have the real opportunity to take advantage of that access. it is also essential that the eu continue to favour the multilateral trading system created by the wto, as bilateral and regional agreements are not the best option.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that the objective of better regulation in the eu is a continuous one and must be pursued on an ongoing basis. this objective is multi-faceted: reducing the administrative burden on individuals and businesses, thereby encouraging markets to work for people, a clear focus on public consultation, impact assessments, simplification of existing legislation. in addition to all these aspects, the report also assesses how better regulation is implementing the two core principles of the european union's functioning - subsidiarity and proportionality - which national parliaments have become actively involved in overseeing since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. however, meps believe that the time limits within which national parliaments must carry out their work are often too short and that the ways in which documents submitted by national parliaments are incorporated into parliament's work still need to be improved.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the current deadlines within which national parliaments have to carry out their work are often too short, especially when it comes to assessing whether the principle of subsidiarity is being respected. similarly, the replies of national parliaments shall be in a form which does not constitute reasoned opinions or objections to the principle of subsidiarity. it also draws attention to the fact that they are often presented to the european parliament only in the language used by the national parliament for the production of documents. it is therefore proposed that the secretary-general of parliament should examine how to improve the way in which documents submitted by national parliaments are incorporated into parliament's work.
in writing. − one of the reasons why we are failing to achieve our goal of making the eu more attractive and closer to citizens is the complexity of the legislative framework. at the moment, eu citizens do not feel that they have an impact on eu legislation: they cannot really implement the law, the relationship between the institutions is too complex, the time between the legislative initiative and the entry into force of the law is too long. i congratulate the rapporteur on addressing many of these aspects in his report. unfortunately, if we want the citizens of the member states to feel that they are also citizens of the eu, we must not only put these proposals into words, but also implement them.
in writing. − i support this resolution on better regulation, the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality and smart regulation, as the european union's legislative process must be continuously improved and perfected, the decision-making process must be brought as close as possible to the citizens. all european institutions must pay greater attention to the implementation of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality when drafting legislation. it is also essential to ensure that all eu citizens are given the right conditions to make the most of their rights, so that they can have a greater say in eu policy in defence of their interests. it is therefore essential that the public is properly informed about the implementation of the european citizens' initiative. the proper implementation of this initiative will help the european union to get closer to its citizens and to properly implement the principles of direct democracy. the importance of national parliaments to the eu legislative process should be emphasised. national parliaments need to become more effective actors in the political process at both national and european levels. we must make every effort to tackle the democratic deficit and reduce the administrative burden by developing cooperation between national parliaments and the european parliament. it is very important to stress that only through the control of the subsidiarity principle can national parliaments have a real influence on the european parliament. in this context, i believe that longer time limits should be set to allow national parliaments to provide a more detailed analysis of compliance with the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which seeks to establish a comprehensive approach to anthropogenic pollutants that affect the climate. it should be noted that pollutants of anthropogenic origin are considered to be among the most dangerous for humans and animals. the commission and the member states must therefore take immediate action and develop as soon as possible a comprehensive european climate change policy and strategies to respond to climate change problems in an operational manner. in view of the dangers of these pollutants, technologies that can radically reduce emissions of soot and gases must be used in the eu and the use of the 'kirsk and burner' method must be banned.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is necessary to reduce the number of deaths from noncommunicable diseases in europe. the world health organization (who) session announced that noncommunicable diseases - mainly cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, cancer and diabetes - are responsible for the deaths of up to 86% of the world's population each year. the most important risk factors for noncommunicable diseases are those known to man: tobacco use, an unbalanced diet that can lead to overweight, high blood pressure, exposure to environmental pollutants, excessive alcohol consumption and physical inactivity. if no action is taken, such as promoting healthier diets, reducing alcohol abuse and promoting physical activity in the community by 2030, the epidemic could kill up to 52 million people in europe. in order to avoid or at least reduce these indicators, member states, researchers and health professionals are encouraged to seek the efficiency of uniform health systems and to strengthen the accessibility of health services.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it calls for the eu and its member states to support the five key commitments and include them in the political statement to be drawn up at the un high level meeting on noncommunicable diseases in september 2011, namely to reduce mortality from noncommunicable diseases by 25% by 2025, as proposed by the who, to take interventions to achieve cost-effectiveness and cost-saving measures, including faster implementation of the who framework convention on tobacco control, to improve access to healthy food and promote healthy diets, including reducing the consumption of salt, sugar, saturated fats and fatty acid transisomers in society, to take effective measures to combat alcohol abuse and to promote more active physical activity throughout society, to consider the overall impact of environmental pollution, to monitor the reduction of morbidity and mortality from noncommunicable diseases by 2025, to develop a mechanism to monitor the overall trends in noncommunicable diseases, to promote a high level of accountability and to develop a high level of accountability of all stakeholders at the level of the organisation, to ensure that the main trends of noncommunicable diseases are taken into account at the 2014 meeting.
in writing. − a major global problem noncommunicable diseases: including cardiovascular, respiratory, cancer and diabetes. the adoption of this resolution underlines the urgency of the problem and the need to prevent diseases. currently, 97% of healthcare spending is spent on treatment, compared with only 3% on prevention. prevention and public information on tobacco, alcohol consumption, overeating, physical inactivity and environmental pollution must be given priority. treatment and prevention of non-communicable diseases also have an economic effect. without action, society will be doomed to extinction as humanity grows morbid and deadly. the estimated global economic loss from noncommunicable diseases to the global economy between 2005 and 2030 is estimated at around eur 25 trillion. it is important to encourage people from an early age to take an interest in and care for their health and the environment. one option is to provide statistical data showing a direct link between the disease and its cause. the state can and must provide information on risk factors and their effects. on the one hand, individual risk factors remain individual, but environmental pollution is a common concern for all of us. it is therefore important to think not only about yourself but also about other residents. finally, i would like to mention that the eu does not yet have a common strategy on noncommunicable diseases, but the adoption of this resolution is a step forward.
