member of the commission. - madam president, madam rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, this is indeed an agreement which will not solve the problems in the region on its own, but which undoubtedly opens up important prospects which must be exploited. this new agreement, which the european union signed with the palestinian authority on 13 april, gives the palestinian authority free access to the european market for all agricultural, agri-food and fishery products originating in the west bank and the gaza strip, with the exception, as the rapporteur has said, of the fruit and vegetable sector, for which the european union has retained the system of protecting entry prices. this means that partial protection applies to certain periods which are important for producers in the european union; otherwise, the rest of the time, palestinian products can be exported to the european union. this unilateral concession by the european union is granted on a temporary basis for a period of 10 years, with the possibility of extending the agreement in the light of the future economic development of palestine. the agreement also contains a review clause, which will allow the terms of the agreement to be reviewed five years after implementation and possibly extended if necessary. the agreement also contains a temporary withdrawal clause, known as the 'anti-fraud clause', which ensures that only palestinian products benefit from the preferential agreement. i know that some of you, during the discussion in the committee on international trade, raised the concern that others are benefiting from the agreement. i think that the application of this clause will help to solve this situation. this agreement is one of the most generous agreements the european union has ever signed in the agricultural field. its adoption is justified by the political and economic situation and the specific conditions of palestinian agriculture. the palestinian authority is the european union's smallest trading partner in the euro-mediterranean region. eu exports to palestine amounted to eur 57,5 million in 2009 and eur 89,3 million in 2010 while eu imports from palestine amounted to only eur 6,5 million in 2009 and eur 9,3 million in 2010. the opening of the market to this region should support the economic development of the occupied palestinian territory and give a significant boost to the development of the palestinian agricultural sector and the activities of its farmers. the european union will complement the granting of additional trade preferences with a programme of technical assistance in the commercial field. this assistance has already begun in the field of sanitary and phytosanitary matters; it will continue according to the future needs and demands of the palestinians.

in writing. - i voted for this document. international air links between member states and third countries have traditionally been established by bilateral air services agreements. in 2002, the court of justice of the eu ruled that traditional bilateral air services agreements between member states infringe eu law as they allow a third party to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or licence of an air carrier designated by a member state but whose majority shareholding is not owned by that member state or its national entity and which is not effectively controlled by them. this is contrary to article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees that nationals of member states enjoying freedom of establishment may enjoy the same rights as nationals of that member state. mexico is an important market for eu carriers, with a turnover of around 2,5 million passengers and 90 000 tonnes of freight in 2009. given the size and importance of the eu-mexico aviation market, this new agreement aims to ensure that all eu air carriers can benefit from air routes between eu member states and mexico without discrimination.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because certain provisions on air services need to be amended in order to improve and strengthen the aviation relations between the european union and the united mexican states. mexico is a very important market for european union carriers and more agreements related to air transport are needed to bring more benefits to consumers in mexico and the european union countries. the new agreements and amendments are intended to provide better market access and to help strengthen trade links with mexico. the european commission has currently identified thirteen agreements between the united mexican states and the european union relating to communications services that are still in force. several key clauses of the agreement strictly prohibit anti-competitive activities and all consumers wishing to travel from the european union and mexico should not be discriminated against. but as i said, mexico is an important market for european union carriers, and more air transport agreements are needed to further improve cooperation between these countries.
in writing. − i have supported this document because i believe that there are important aspects of this agreement, such as the need to avoid discrimination against eu air carriers, the traditional articles on designations referring to air carriers from eu member states that have signed a bilateral agreement are replaced by an eu article on designation referring to all eu air carriers. the aim is to ensure that all eu air carriers can benefit from air routes between eu member states and mexico without discrimination. the safety provisions of bilateral agreements would apply in cases where the regulatory control of an air carrier is exercised by a member state other than the one that has designated that air carrier. anti-competitive activities are also prohibited.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this agreement. the european commission, acting under the authority of the council, has negotiated with the republic of cape verde the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of cape verde of 19 december 2006. the protocol aims to establish cooperation between the european union and the republic of cape verde with a view to establishing a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the fishing zone of the republic of cape verde, taking into account the interests of both parties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because a new protocol is needed to improve and strengthen the non-declared and unregulated fisheries in cape verde. cape verde is a small island nation of 465 000 inhabitants in the atlantic ocean, some 500 km west of the tip of west africa in senegal. cape verde is considered one of the best performing african countries in terms of political, economic and social development. the new protocol will have a significant impact on the political and financial stability of cape verde, as the annual financial compensation is eur 435 000, of which eur 110 000 will be allocated to support the cape verdean fisheries sector (eur 50 000 more than under the old protocol). in order to maintain the viability of european businesses, the new protocol must preserve the european union's ability to fish in the west african fishing areas and improve partnerships between them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document as it will allow fishing for 28 tonnes of fishing lines, 35 drift-nets and 11 re-screening vessels, with an indicative annual quota of 5 000 tonnes. these fishing opportunities may be reviewed and increased or reduced, taking into account the annual assessments of the state of the stocks, and the level of the financial contribution will be reviewed accordingly. the annual financial compensation shall be eur 435 000 (total for the whole period of eur 1 305 000), consisting of: (a) an annual fee for fishing rights in the exclusive economic zone (eez) of cape verde of eur 325 000; (b) an annual special amount of eur 110 000 to support the development of the fisheries policy of the republic of cape verde. these fishing opportunities will be allocated to the member states concerned following the submission of a proposal for a specific council regulation.

in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it defines the terms and conditions for bilateral cooperation between the eu and the us to promote and develop civil aviation research and development. this important instrument, developed on the basis of a legally binding framework and subject to the harmonised principles of reciprocity, will enable the contracting parties to work together towards the common objective of making air transport systems greener and more efficient. the draft memorandum will allow both contracting parties to undertake joint research and development activities in any field of civil aviation. the memorandum of cooperation with the usa provides a solid and legally binding basis for joint research and development activities and for the appropriate handling of sensitive issues such as liability, intellectual property rights and reciprocity. the memorandum may also establish international aviation standards that ensure global interoperability, meet the expectations of aviation stakeholders and ensure wider market opportunities for european companies.

in writing. − the euro banknotes and coins, introduced in 2002, are a pan-european means of payment that allows european citizens to pay in euro throughout the euro area, which currently comprises 17 member states. the very principle of the single currency means that euro banknotes and coins should move as freely as possible and be transported from one member state to another. however, the lack of harmonisation of national legislation makes it very difficult for professional cash carriers to move euro cash from one euro area member state to another in many cases, and the scale of cross-border transport by land is therefore very small. many things are regulated differently: the possession and carrying of firearms by cash workers, the types of transport allowed, the armor and equipment of cash vehicles, the staff in the cash vehicle. the current regulatory obstacles indicate the fragmentation of the common market in this sector. these restrictions on the professional carrying of euro cash have an impact on cash circulation and the price of cash for businesses and citizens. i supported the need to take action to remove existing regulatory barriers to the crossborder transport of euro cash by road and thus facilitate the free movement of the euro.
in writing. − although euro banknotes and coins were introduced in 2002, the market for the transport of euro cash remains highly fragmented. the large differences in national rules in this area make it very difficult for professional cash carriers to provide cross-border services. i therefore voted in favour of this regulation as it aims to simplify these regulatory constraints in order to facilitate the movement of euro banknotes and coins between member states that have adopted the euro.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to reduce the number of road accidents in the european union, which is currently on the rise, in the coming years. in 2009, more than 35 000 000 people were killed and about 1.5 million seriously injured on european union roads, many of them disabled. the number of people killed on the roads of the european union is enormous, with social and economic costs of €130 billion. the european commission has therefore presented a communication with the aim of doubling the number of people killed on european roads by 2020 compared to 2010. the commission has prepared seven key strategic actions to reduce road accidents by 2020. the strategic plans set out how to ensure safer road infrastructure, ensure compliance with road traffic rules and develop smart vehicles. in order to implement these strategies and reduce the number of casualties, it is necessary to ensure the highest level of coordination at both european union and national level.
in writing. − the commission's main objective is to halve the total number of people killed on european roads by 2020 (compared to 2010). to achieve these objectives, the commission has set out seven strategic objectives: improving the education of road users and the quality of the licensing and training system; strengthening the enforcement of road traffic rules; ensuring a safer road infrastructure; improving safety measures for lorries and light vehicles; developing advanced vehicles; improving emergency medical and first aid services; and ensuring the protection of vulnerable road users, especially motorcyclists. these are good, practical and necessary measures to reduce the number of people dying on eu roads. however, i abstained from voting in favour of this document because, in addition to the repeated calls from the european parliament, the rapporteur proposed additional measures to improve road safety in the eu, the implementation of which, in my view, would not produce the expected results. the measures taken must be adequate, logical and justified in the light of the facts. the road safety policy must be effective, consistent, and implemented and enforced with confidence.
in writing. − although road deaths in lithuania fell by half last year, road wars continue in lithuania and across the eu. in 2009, 35,000 people were killed in europe, 1,500,000 were injured and property damage was estimated at over €130 billion. i voted for this report because it aims to halve the number of deaths by 2020. the document calls on eu governments to focus more on road infrastructure and to ensure better cooperation between eu countries. it is unfair that a duplicate driving licence which has been withdrawn in one eu country can still be obtained in another eu country if you live or work there. it is therefore necessary to establish as soon as possible an eu system for the exchange of information on documents. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. it is rightly proposed to tighten the penalties by introducing a zero-alcohol rule for drivers with less than two years' driving experience. many accidents could be avoided by simple precautions, such as better road signs, better lighting, and alert police officers.
in writing. - i voted for this document. over the past century, it has become clear that despite the billions of dollars spent on flood control, no other natural disaster has caused more damage to property or killed more people. the second half of the 20th century has seen an increase in major floods, and in the coming decades, regular flooding will be a particularly serious problem. to ensure a reliable water supply during droughts and to contain excess water during floods, storage methods need to be improved. the challenge of re-evaluating freshwater management in the context of climate change is without doubt a major global challenge. i agree with the urgent need to adopt a comprehensive flood prevention strategy in those regions where there is a high risk of flooding and to make balanced investments in water demand management measures, land management, better water collection and storage.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the need to improve water storage methods and reduce the construction of the world's largest dams. during the period of construction of the great dams, an estimated 40 to 80 million people had to be evacuated. dams change the use of rivers and natural resources, have a major impact on biodiversity and river ecosystems, and most importantly, threaten human communities. in every continent, dams pose a threat to people or to biological ecosystems. one of the real envy, brazil is currently in the process of getting permission to build the third largest dam in the world, but its construction will cause and do immeasurable damage to the amazon ecosystem and to all of its biodiversity. in addition, some 50,000,000 people will be forced to leave their homes. reducing dam construction is necessary because current estimates put the world at high risk of flooding by 2050, with an estimated 2 billion people at risk. in addition, dam reservoirs pose a serious threat to the environment by emitting greenhouse gases.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because if areas with high agricultural production are not protected from the effects of flooding, emerging economies could face sudden development shifts and a rapidly increasing food supply problem. the melting of the himalayan glaciers is expected to increase the flow of all rivers for two to three decades in particular, and to weaken the flow considerably in the long term, making it particularly important to develop mitigation and adaptation strategies to combat future droughts. action is needed to reduce carbon monoxide and methane emissions, in particular by promoting research and investing in technologies to reduce emissions, i.e. urgent action to stop the melting of glaciers and snow. the short-term persistence of carbon monoxide and methane in the atmosphere requires a concerted effort to reduce emissions and urgent action to reduce the risk of tropical lake flooding effectively and rapidly.
in writing. − i welcome the european parliament’s initiative in addressing this important issue. improving dam infrastructure in developing countries is necessary to address climate change consequences and to achieve development goals. it not only helps in managing flood risks and in providing better access to fresh-water resources, but also may provide for hydropower generation capacity. i believe a good impact can be achieved through micro-projects for hydropower dams, requiring small investment and rather basic technologies. micro-investment may have a big positive effect for most vulnerable communities in remote areas. as regards the large-scale projects, the eu assistance should be provided only for those which underwent thorough impact assessment taking into account all environmental and societal consequences. the eu should work with the relevant organisations and partner countries so the dam infrastructure is developed in an environmentally sound way. having said all that, it is important to ensure the visibility of the eu assistance provided to the relevant projects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the eu's policy programme of aid to developing countries to address food security problems. it is clear that food shortages are hampering the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs), particularly in sub-saharan africa and the least developed countries. new challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and water quality, have affected the state of the world's food supply. i agree with the rapporteurs that, despite the strong commitment to the human rights to food, water, energy, etc., the institutions of the european union and the member states still do not consider the eradication of poverty, hunger and malnutrition as a key strategic objective. to achieve the mdgs by 2015, it is therefore necessary to review and, if necessary, change eu strategies such as 'europe 2020', 'global europe', energy policy, sustainable development strategy and, in general, future eu development cooperation. the eu and its member states must also stand firm in their commitment to combating poverty and hunger globally in international organisations such as the world bank, the imf and the wto. i agree with the rapporteurs that the eu's trade strategy is a concern, focusing on competition and the market share of eu products, but lacking a development-oriented approach. the reduction of tariffs on agricultural products imported from developing countries should be further encouraged in order to promote the growth of the economies of those countries.
in writing. − the food crisis, especially in developing countries, poses a major threat to peace and security in the world. since august 2010, food prices have risen monthly (the trend over the last 10 years) and have now reached a level higher than the highest food price increase recorded in 2008. such price fluctuations have a significant impact on low-income countries and on the poorest, most vulnerable and most socially excluded people in developing countries. i agree that the european union and the member states must urgently promote new investment in agriculture and rural development, and take targeted measures to build up sufficient global stocks of basic foodstuffs, remove trade barriers and reduce the debt of the most affected countries. there is a global need for more sustainable, energy-efficient and efficient production, especially in view of the growing world population and the increasing demand for natural resources. i agree with the call for the commission and the member states to take concrete action to tackle effectively the problem of financial speculation in cereals and food.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is unacceptable that so many people are suffering from hunger today. the european parliament calls for urgent action to fulfil binding international commitments to make the right to adequate and nutritious food a reality, despite the many joint international efforts that have been made. parliament welcomed the commission communication on the european union's policy programme for food aid to developing countries, but considered that the global food crisis was not only an unprecedented humanitarian disaster but also a serious threat to peace and security in the world. while recognising the commission's commitment to finding solutions to help a billion people escape extreme poverty, the european union and the member states must urgently promote new investment in agriculture and rural development, in particular in the context of the new common agricultural policy, and implement targeted measures to build up sufficient global stocks of essential food products, remove self-imposed barriers to trade and reduce the debt of the most vulnerable countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it calls on the eu to support the un's minimum social security initiative, which would help meet the basic food needs of the poor. i think it is necessary to look at the structural causes of price fluctuations. speculation in derivatives of major food commodities has greatly increased food price volatility. it is therefore necessary to take concrete action to effectively tackle the problem of financial speculation in cereals and foodstuffs in a substantial way, so as not to distort trade.
in writing. − we must do everything we can to ensure that the eu can respond as quickly as possible in the event of a major famine. a weak response in the face of hundreds of thousands of deaths does little to improve the image of the eu, the world's largest donor, on the international stage. hunger and food shortages are not caused by natural disasters alone; their origins are programmed in one way or another in international trade. it is important to align eu trade and other sectoral policies in such a way that they contribute as little as possible to food shortages in developing countries. increasingly, the causes lie in the domestic politics, inefficient governance, and armed conflicts of the countries involved. i therefore believe that aid measures aimed at long-term development have a real impact. at the same time, african countries need to be encouraged to take a more active role in building shared prosperity on the continent and to establish a mechanism for collective assistance to citizens of african countries suffering from hunger and food shortages.
in writing. - hunger is one of the world's greatest scourges. in 2010, nearly a billion people were hungry, a quarter of the world's children under five years old were undernourished, and about a third of them die from hunger. i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls for urgent and far-reaching action to combat hunger. we call for an end to speculation in food prices, which distorts the market, raises prices. hungry people, especially in african countries, cannot afford the higher prices. the resolution also calls for an assessment of developments in the common agricultural policy and for enhanced cooperation between the eu and non-governmental organisations fighting hunger. the document encourages countries and regions where famine is common to store some of the food so that people do not go without food because of sudden changes in weather, political or other crises. since food is more important than energy, we propose that biofuels be stopped as long as there are hungry people in the world. it occupies vast areas of land that could be used for food production.
in writing. − this report was initiated at the request of the conference of committee chairs to the committee on constitutional affairs in order to clarify parliament's position on the meaning and legal status of unilateral statements in the minutes of council meetings. the most commonly contested declarations are made by one or more member states, as they are responsible for transposing legislation. an attempt to interpret those acts differently from the interpretation reached by the general agreement between the two legislators could indeed undermine the necessary consistency in the application of union law. the case-law of the court of justice confirms that such unilateral statements cannot be relied upon for the interpretation of union law. they may be used only where the reference relates to the content of the wording of the relevant act. i agree that unilateral statements by member states should not be published in the official journal of the european union.
in writing. − i have endorsed the document because i consider that it is not to be incorporated into a legal text, but statements relating to it, whether issued by one or more member states, have no legal force and may undermine the coherence and clarity of the interpretation of union law. i am in favour of effective and transparent implementation of legislation throughout the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on a new european trade policy under the europe 2020 strategy. we must recognise that the eu's prosperity and growth depend on a functioning international trading system. the commission should therefore present a forward-looking trade and investment strategy, but we, the members of the european parliament, miss this important aspect in the commission's communication of 9 november 2010 entitled 'trade, growth and the international arena: the future trade strategy of the european union'. i agree with the rapporteur that the policy guidelines proposed in the communication on trade, growth and the international arena are for the coming months, not a comprehensive trade strategy for the european union, which is particularly needed now, faced with the challenges of a rapidly changing world economy and dramatic shifts in the balance of economic forces. i therefore support the call in the resolution for the commission to carry out a forward-looking study which takes account of the current situation in the world economy in general and the current situation in the european union and the likely future developments. on this basis, the commission could develop a long-term strategy that takes full account of the needs of the european union and its citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report. in 2000, when the lisbon strategy was launched, the union's gdp was 25% of world gdp. the union's contribution to global gdp is now projected to be only 18% in 2020. i agree that the union needs a coherent long-term strategy to take account of the challenges ahead and in particular the major emerging economies. such a strategy should be based on a thorough analysis of current trends in world trade and of developments within and outside the union, as well as of the diversity of european enterprises, practical experience and technological progress. i believe that the commission needs to review in depth bilateral trade relations with key trading partners to ensure that eu companies can compete on equal terms in third country markets.
in writing. − in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, the commission published on 9 november 2010 a communication on 'trade, growth and the international arena' for the future trade strategy of the european union. while welcoming this communication, the european parliament calls on the commission to present as soon as possible a forward-looking and innovative strategy for the future of trade and investment in the light of the new challenges facing the european union. the eu needs a coherent long-term strategy to address the challenges ahead, especially for the major emerging economies. such a strategy should be based on a thorough analysis of current trends in world trade and of developments within and outside the union, as well as of the diversity of european enterprises, practical experience and technological progress. the european parliament also calls on the commission to systematically assess the impact of eu internal policies and regulations on global competitiveness and to give priority to those proposals which have the least negative impact on the competitiveness of eu enterprises in europe and beyond. it is therefore essential that the commission carries out a comprehensive study which takes into account the current situation in the world economy and the current situation in the european union and the likely future developments. on this basis, the commission could develop a long-term strategy that takes full account of the needs of the european union and its citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it calls on the commission to present as soon as possible a forward-looking and innovative future strategy on trade and investment in the light of the new challenges facing the eu, and to provide projections of what the so-called world of trade could look like in 15 or 20 years' time in policy planning and to use them as a basis for the preparation of a revised medium- and long-term strategy by summer 2013. the eu also has to take account of the fact that population growth is falling sharply within the eu, while developing countries are increasing even more. this will affect the economic situation of the countries. when we realise that 18% of jobs within the eu today, or 36 million jobs, depend on external trade, and that by 2015 90% of global economic growth is likely to be generated outside the european union, we understand the importance of developing and implementing a long-term external trade strategy that takes account of the eu's changing role in the global economy. in the light of these developments, i therefore supported the rapporteur's call for the commission to carry out a forward-looking study that takes into account the current situation in the world economy and the current situation in the eu and expected future developments. on this basis, the commission could develop a long-term strategy that takes full account of the needs of the eu and its citizens.

in writing. your statement, mr president of the commission, that the european union needs to be renewed is undeniable. the ongoing and deepening crisis makes it abundantly clear that the current eu governance model is unable to respond to complex situations and to mobilise the political will to take possibly radical but unavoidable decisions. the only way for us to survive as a union in solidarity and unity is to fundamentally revise the whole eu governance model. the commission must become the body that sets the general guidelines for economic governance and has full powers to supervise the economies of the member states. without a clear economic governance structure, the proposed economic governance and coordination measures will not create the conditions for greater economic integration and coordination of member states' economies and financial market surveillance.

in writing. - i voted for financial aid to denmark. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. denmark applied for aid in relation to 813 redundancies in 6 enterprises active in the machinery and equipment manufacturing sector. this application qualifies for financial assistance and i therefore approve the allocation of eur 3 944 606.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 11 may 2010, denmark submitted an application to mobilise the egf in respect of redundancies (813 workers) in six enterprises active in the machinery and equipment sector in the region of central jutland. one of the commission's assessment criteria is the link between the redundancies and major structural changes in world trade or financial crises. in this particular case, the structural changes brought about by globalisation have had a serious impact on the wind turbine industry in the eu. furthermore, according to the danish authorities, the rapid expansion of the global wind energy sector did not allow for the reduction of employment in central jutland. the harmonised package of tailor-made services to be financed, including its compatibility with actions financed by the structural funds, includes explanatory and reorientation measures (to clarify the objectives and plans of the workers), additional support for further education and training, an innovation laboratory (with a particular focus on the development of the skills of the workers to prepare them for work in enterprises already operating on the basis of green technologies), a guidance programme, consultancy on qualifications, job-search allowances and mobility allowances.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 9 february 2011, germany submitted an application to mobilise the egf in respect of redundancies (778) in five enterprises active in the motor vehicle, trailer and semi-trailer sectors in the regions of arnsberg and düsseldorf. one of the commission's assessment criteria is the link between the redundancies and major structural changes in world trade or financial crises. in this particular case, it is the decrease in demand for new motor vehicles in the eu following the global financial and economic crisis. according to the german authorities, the 778 redundancies mentioned in this application will further increase the high unemployment rate in the regions of arnsberg and düsseldorf, which have already been severely affected by the closure of the nokia plant in bochum and the general motors plant. the following measures are included in the harmonised package of personalised services to be financed, including its compatibility with actions financed by the structural funds: short-term job-search allowances, training courses, comprehensive guidance for starting up a business, workshops for workers with practical and similar qualifications, guidance, promotion of activism, employment surveys, etc.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 17 august 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of portugal in order to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. one of the commission's assessment criteria is the link between the redundancies and major structural changes in world trade or financial crises. in this particular case, portugal points out that the clothing and footwear sectors have been particularly badly affected by the crisis. these sectors have been strongly affected by external factors such as the decrease in the purchasing power of consumers. the economic downturn had a negative impact on the labour market, with an increase in unemployment, which affected consumer confidence. the following measures are included in the harmonised package of personalised services to be financed, including the compatibility with actions financed by the structural funds, in order to reintegrate workers into the labour market: information and guidance, recognition, validation and certification of skills, vocational training, training grants for self-employed persons, support for self-employment, business support, support for setting up a new enterprise, integration plans, etc.
written. − on the draft council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the argentine republic pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the course of their accession to the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document as it aims to conclude an agreement with argentina, with the inclusion of bulgaria and romania. these agreements address two issues in order to implement wto requirements. first, the compensation for the higher duty rates to be compensated. the most common method is to open a country's tariff quota or to increase existing quotas. secondly, the pre-accession erga omnes tariff quota for bulgaria and romania (not allocated to a specific country but open to the whole world) has to be added to the existing eu erga omnes tariff quotas. the agreement covers boneless beef (argentina), boneless buffalo (argentina) and the increase of the erga omnes tariff quota for common wheat, barley, malted barley and maize. argentina is entitled to claim the restoration of its trade rights, which have been somewhat adversely affected by the enlargement of the eu customs union following the accession of romania and bulgaria. the objective of a customs union or a free trade area should be to facilitate trade within the territories forming the union and not to create obstacles to trade with other countries which have concluded agreements with those territories. this agreement demonstrates once again the eu's commitment to respecting multilateral trade rules. i believe that the commission has chosen correctly the method of increasing the tariff quota for the products concerned for argentina, as it is the most appropriate measure to compensate the country which deserves compensation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council's decision. the accession of bulgaria and romania to the eu has enlarged its customs union. the eu is therefore obliged under wto rules to enter into negotiations with wto members with a negotiating power over any acceding country's list of commitments with a view to agreeing on a countervailing adjustment. such adjustment is mandatory if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime results in an increase in the customs duties in relation to the duties for which the acceding country has committed itself to the wto. this contract refers to a sheep and a goat. australia has the right to demand that its trading rights, which have been somewhat adversely affected by the enlargement of the eu customs union following the accession of romania and bulgaria, be restored. the commission proposed the method of increasing the tariff quota for the products concerned as the most appropriate compensatory measure.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the economic and financial crisis has highlighted the need to reconsider the framework of economic and monetary union in order to strengthen the instruments available and to extend the procedures for coordination and multilateral surveillance. the economic governance package consists of six proposals to improve the coordination and surveillance of economic policies in the economic and monetary union (emu) in the context of the europe 2020 strategy and the european semester, a new cycle of surveillance combining the process with the provisions of the stability and growth pact and the broad economic policy guidelines. the two proposals under examination relate to the excessive deficit procedure. the other four proposals concern the multilateral surveillance system. this proposal for a regulation lays down provisions to ensure the prudent conduct of fiscal policies and the sustainability of public finances in the member states. despite these precise guidelines, the current economic situation indicates that progress towards the medium-term objectives has been broadly insufficient. moreover, it has become clear in practice that the structural balance sheet is not a suitable measure to assess the country's underlying fiscal position. the proposed regulation therefore provides for specific rules to ensure coordination of economic policies and activities in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the proposal for a regulation on enforcement measures to address excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the euro area extends the process of economic surveillance, which is partly laid down in the stability and growth pact. budgetary and fiscal surveillance thus complement the mechanism that can help to identify, avoid and correct macroeconomic imbalances. the eu needs greater economic surveillance, which should cover all relevant sectors of the economy. macroeconomic imbalances should therefore be considered in conjunction with fiscal policies and structural reforms to stimulate economic growth. the mechanism for preventing and correcting macroeconomic imbalances consists of two sets of draft proposals. the first set of measures is summarised in the proposal for a regulation on the excessive imbalance procedure, which aims to establish a framework for identifying and resolving macroeconomic imbalances. the second draft proposal focuses on ensuring the implementation of measures to address excessive macroeconomic imbalances. it is only applicable to member states that have adopted the euro and provides an incentive for member states to address macroeconomic imbalances as early as possible and to ensure that appropriate corrective measures are taken where necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the proposal for the prevention and correction of macroeconomic imbalances complements the multilateral surveillance regime provided for under the europe 2020 strategy by introducing a completely new element, namely the excessive imbalance procedure. this proposal establishes a framework for the identification and resolution of macroeconomic imbalance problems. this proposal should be examined together with the regulation on enforcement measures to address excessive macroeconomic imbalances. both these acts constitute a fully-fledged mechanism for preventing and correcting macroeconomic imbalances. the eu needs greater economic surveillance, which should cover all relevant sectors of the economy. macroeconomic imbalances should therefore be considered in conjunction with fiscal policies and structural reforms to stimulate economic growth. a trend can be identified which is characterised by the extension of economic policy surveillance beyond budgetary surveillance to avoid excessive macroeconomic imbalances, but also by the strengthening of fiscal surveillance. this procedure should provide for an alert mechanism to detect emerging macroeconomic imbalances at an early stage. it should be based on the use of a benchmark and a transparent scoreboard with reference thresholds and an economic assessment. this assessment should take into account, inter alia, nominal and real convergence within and outside the euro area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the purpose of the regulation is to avoid major budgetary policy errors that could put the sustainability of public finances at risk. this is achieved by obliging member states to avoid excessive government deficits, which are determined on the basis of two main criteria: deficit and debt. the excessive deficit procedure (edp), which implements the prohibition on running an excessive deficit, provides for a sequence of actions to be taken. this system is based on an enforcement mechanism which provides for financial penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of this regulation. the corrective arm of the stability and growth pact needs to be reformed to address the weaknesses that have emerged in the wake of the economic and financial crisis. the proposal therefore focuses on the following measures: the introduction of the pdp debt criterion. this measure responds to the fact that the debt criterion has hitherto played a secondary role, whereas both criteria (deficit and debt) should be equivalent; imposes new financial penalties on euro area member states to prevent and, if they do, to correct excessive general deficits as soon as possible; and provides for a clearer and more flexible framework for the commission to make possible recommendations. the main objective of this proposal is therefore to prevent and correct the excessive deficit, to avoid major budgetary policy errors and to lay down the detailed rules to be followed in the context of the excessive deficit procedure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as the main objective of this proposal is to promote fiscal responsibility by setting minimum requirements for national systems and to ensure the effectiveness of the excessive deficit procedure. the aim is to lay down detailed rules to be followed in the context of the excessive deficit procedure.

in writing. - i voted for this document. international air links between member states and third countries have traditionally been established by bilateral air services agreements. in 2002, the court of justice of the eu ruled that traditional bilateral air services agreements between member states infringe eu law as they allow a third party to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or licence of an air carrier designated by a member state but whose majority shareholding is not owned by that member state or its national entity and which is not effectively controlled by them. this is contrary to article 49 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which guarantees that nationals of member states enjoying freedom of establishment may enjoy the same rights as nationals of that member state.

in writing. − i have voted in favour of this report which depicts how the eu can use insurance guarantee schemes (igs), in order to ensure that the risks facing policyholders in the event of the failure of an insurance entity are reduced. this report aims at strengthening support for consumer protection in four main areas: ensuring customer protection in the event of the bankruptcy of an insurer; ensuring equal consumer protection regardless of the ‘home’ state of the insurer; ensuring consumer protection in the event of fraud or mis-selling; and ensuring taxpayer protection in the event of igs failure. i support the rapporteur’s view that these policy goals can be adequately met by a minimum harmonisation directive that ensures the same level of consumer protection regardless of the location of the insurer writing the policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report. the purpose of insurance guarantee schemes (igs) is to provide protection for consumers in cases where insurance undertakings are no longer able to meet their contractual obligations. these schemes will protect people from the risk of claims not being met and their insurance company becoming insolvent. the protection provided by the dgs often varies, which makes the protection of insurers different in different member states. the conditions for the provision of sme loans remain uncoordinated at eu level, which hinders the effective and uniform protection of consumers and disrupts the functioning of the internal insurance market. this leads to a loss of consumer confidence, threatens market stability and distorts cross-border competition. i agree that, in the light of the experience gained during the last crisis, it is necessary to develop harmonised insurance guarantee systems in order to overcome existing shortcomings and restore consumer confidence. national and european supervisory authorities, in particular the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa), must apply robust risk mitigation rules and effective supervision consistently to ensure a high level of consumer protection and the proper functioning of the insurance market.
in writing. − insurance guarantee schemes (igs) can be a valuable tool in reducing the risk that insurers would face if an insurance company went bankrupt. the current wide variety of insurance guarantee schemes in the member states, offering different levels of consumer protection across different products and financing systems, has resulted in inefficient and uneven protection of insurers and has slowed down the functioning of the insurance market in the face of cross-border competition, due to the lack of harmonisation of the gmps at european level and the different regimes in the member states. consumer confidence in financial services in the internal market can only be ensured by a consistent level of consumer protection, irrespective of the origin of the service provider, in particular by the consistent application of sound risk mitigation rules and effective supervision by the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and, where applicable, by the national competent authorities. the commission is invited to submit proposals for a cross-border standardisation directive establishing a coherent and harmonised cross-border insurance guarantee system in all member states. we must put the protection of consumers against the bankruptcy of loss insurance companies at the top of our agenda, and for this reason, and for the reasons mentioned above, i have voted in favour of this document.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because a coherent and harmonised system of insurance guarantee rules must function at european union level and the different regimes in the member states must be abolished. it should be noted that the insurance guarantee scheme is an effective instrument that reduces the risks of insurers, ensures different levels of consumer protection and effective cross-border competition. it is therefore essential to ensure that european rules provide a high and appropriate level of protection. given that many consumers lose some or all of their assets and are left in poverty as a result of the bankruptcy of insurance companies, i believe it is appropriate to establish in the resolution the principle of the home member state, under which the liability for the burden of bankruptcy would be assumed by the insurance guarantee scheme of the home member state. only then will people be protected from the risk of claims not being satisfied if their insurance company goes bankrupt. it should be noted that this principle, as a measure of last resort for the protection of consumers, should be applied only in exceptional cases where insurance undertakings are unable to meet contractual obligations due to insolvency and where other regulatory instruments have been exhausted.
in writing. - colleagues, only a few member states have insurance guarantee schemes. the rapporteur recalls that the lack of harmonisation in this area at community level hinders the effective and uniform protection of consumers. this may lead to consumer distrust and ultimately to a risk to market stability. consumer protection is a very important issue for lithuania. a recent world bank report states that consumer protection legislation in the financial services sector is not being implemented uniformly in my country. the eurobarometer survey on consumer protection in europe showed that lithuanian consumers need a better consumer protection programme. in addition, additional funding is needed to ensure more effective activities of lithuanian consumer associations. lithuania has over 20 consumer associations, but only a few in the financial services sector. some consumer associations receive limited funding from the government, but this is not enough. government funding should be complemented by funding from european agencies or bilateral agreements with established european consumer associations. measures to improve consumer protection and financial literacy must be pragmatic and effective and empower consumers. they should include improving consumer information on financial services and promoting market transparency. in the case of lithuania, this also means strengthening the functions of the state consumer protection service in implementing legislation related to consumer protection in the financial services sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. more than 40 years after the introduction of value added tax in the then european economic community, it is time to take a critical look at the vat system in order to increase the compatibility of that system with the common market and the capacity of the vat system as a source of revenue, while increasing its economic efficiency and stability. the eu currently has a fragmented vat system with different rates and a wide range of exemptions, which distorts competition in the internal market and creates opportunities for fraud. governments suffer huge losses each year, which can reach up to eur 100 billion, as a result of vat fraud. i believe that eu-wide vat reform is a necessary condition for strengthening the more efficient functioning of the internal market, increasing the competitiveness of the eu and protecting the community's interests against possible fraud in the future and ensuring higher revenues for the member states and the eu budgets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it aims to thoroughly examine and reform the current vat system. i believe that the vat system should reduce the operating costs of users and the costs of administrative authorities, and should also combat fraud, which is a major burden on public finances and consumers. member states should better implement the measures proposed by the commission in 2009 to reduce the administrative burden of eu vat legislation, namely to reduce the frequency of periodic vat returns, to simplify the evidence required for exemption from vat on exports, to abolish the establishment of zero intra-eu sales lists, to increase the use of e-government decisions in line with the provisions of the digital agenda for europe (in particular with regard to the electronic submission of vat returns and lists), to abolish the payment of interest and penalties for vat-related errors where no vat revenue loss has been incurred by the individual legal person concerned in the member state, and to consider the eu-wide application of a common vat refund procedure, a common vat multiplier and a common electronic vat storage system. the highest priority at this stage is to address the lack of harmonisation and to meet the need for standardisation of procedures and to reduce language barriers, as well as to reduce the vulnerability of the system to fraud. i am convinced that the business community needs clear vat rules that increase legal certainty and increase the likelihood that they will be interpreted in the same way across the member states.
in writing. − a single vat system, when implemented across the european union in the future, will undoubtedly contribute to the promotion of trade between member states and to the eu's international competitiveness. however, in order to do so, we must not forget a number of key aspects that have been highlighted in our report. this is in particular the need to reduce the number of administrative obstacles faced by vat payers in the eu member states. second, the need to allow member states a certain degree of discretion in the application of the principle of subsidiarity, without prejudice to the rules on competition, in the establishment of justified exceptions or other advantages. thirdly, the single system must be designed and operated in such a way as to be able to prevent vat fraudsters operating in the eu.
in writing. − i support this resolution because the european union needs to develop and operate effectively a simpler, more stable and more efficient vat system, which benefits citizens, businesses and member states. vat plays an important role in ensuring economic stability and growth, which requires the prevention of vat fraud, the reduction of the bureaucratic burden on taxpayers and administrators, and the removal of obstacles to the smooth functioning of the internal market. i believe that in the current economic situation it would also be appropriate to apply a lower vat rate to energy-saving and environmentally friendly products and services. it is also essential to ensure that member states agree by the beginning of the following year on a common list of goods and services which should be exempt from vat or subject to a reduced rate of vat and that the commission reports on that list by the end of 2013.
in writing. − the european investment bank (eib), whose shareholders are the member states, is one of the eu's most important financial instruments. its loans outside the eu (eur 9 billion) accounted for more than 12% of its total loans in 2010. the european union shall provide a budgetary guarantee to the european investment bank (eib) covering certain risks of a public or political nature relating to eib lending and loan guarantee operations outside the eu in support of eu external policy objectives. this proposal aims to ensure the continuity of the eu guarantee for eib external financing for the remainder of the current financial perspective 2007-2013, while providing for new elements of delegation. these new elements will allow for increased eib intervention in sectors that will promote the development of third countries, such as environmental infrastructure, including water and sanitation, and sustainable transport, as well as climate change mitigation.
in writing. − i have endorsed the document as, based on the findings of the mid-term review, the overall objective is to ensure the continuity of the eu guarantee for eib external financing for the remainder of the current financial perspective 2007-13 and at the same time to provide for new elements of delegation. the eib is a non-profit-making, public bank implementing eu policies, investing only in projects that deliver eu policy objectives. the eib provides financial support to the eu's external cooperation and development policy objectives, such as private sector development, infrastructure development, reliable energy supply and a sustainable environment. i believe these are important areas that require continuity of funding.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which would grant the european investment bank an eu guarantee for external lending for the period 2007-13. in particular, given the bank's importance in the implementation of eu policy objectives, it is essential to ensure the continuity of the eu guarantee in the eib's external financing. in providing the necessary political and financial support to countries and projects, i believe that greater attention should be paid to those sectors which promote the development of third countries. it is also necessary to strengthen the eib's capacity to support the eu's development objectives and to step up its activities in the fields of health and education.
in writing. − the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) was established in 1990 to support the development of market economies in the countries of central europe and central asia following the collapse of large-scale communist regimes. the european union, together with the european investment bank (eib) and 40 countries (including all the then eu member states), were founding members. the european bank for reconstruction and development is currently managed by 61 countries, the eu and the eib. the eib supports projects in 29 countries, mainly in the private sector, that cannot be financed by the market. the bank promotes entrepreneurship and fosters the transition to an open and democratic market economy. i have endorsed this proposal, which proposes to allow the eu to subscribe for additional early redemption shares in the erpb and thus increase the authorised capital accordingly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the purpose of the proposed legislation is to allow the european union to subscribe for additional early redemption shares in the escb in an amount proportional to the current share of the union in the capital (3,031%). in may 2010, the board of governors of the eib decided to increase the bank's capital by 50% from eur 20 billion to eur 30 billion in order to respond to the financial crisis and to step up its support to the countries in which the bank conducts its operations. the capital increase is eur 1 billion in newly paid-in capital and eur 9 billion in new early redemption capital. the proposal aims at creating new paid-in capital by converting accumulated distributed reserves into equity capital. the operation will therefore have no direct impact on the eu budget. the risk arises from the possible need to pay additional capital in the event of a significant negative development in the bank's investment portfolio, although this is unlikely. after the increase, the eu's share in the capital of the erpb will remain at 3,031%, the paid-up share will increase from eur 157,50 million to eur 187,81 million and the pre-emption capital from eur 442,5 million to eur 712,63 million.
in writing. − i support this resolution as it is appropriate to authorise the european union to subscribe for additional early redemption shares in the escb in an amount proportionate to the current share of the union's capital. it is noted that the eu's participation in the capital of the esrb is an effective way to contribute to the achievement of the eu's objectives and to help mitigate the impact of the crisis in the countries in which the esrb operates and to maintain a high level of activity in the esrb. it should be noted that this operation will not have an immediate impact on the eu budget, as it aims to create new paid-in capital by converting the accumulated distributable reserves into share capital. moreover, the subscription of this capital should not lead to any actual cash payments from the eu budget, unless very large and unforeseen losses are incurred. i believe that there is no reason to doubt the financial sustainability of the bank, as the escb has a long track record of success, a prudent borrowing policy and good financial performance.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, lithuania and the erdf are closely linked by a close cooperation. according to the ebrd, our cooperation covers 78 projects with a total value of eur 1.8 billion and a net turnover of eur 590.6 million. i consider that i am asking the eu to sign the decision on these additional shares in the capital of the eib. in particular, it is understood that this will have no direct impact on the eu budget. the purpose of the proposed legislation is to allow the eu to subscribe for additional early redemption shares in the erdf countries in proportion to the current eu capital shares. this decision would allow the eib to expand its activities in the countries where it operates, including lithuania, thus providing valuable support to the economies of countries with limited capital at the time. although the activities of the ebrd have decreased since lithuania became a member of the eu, it continues to play an important role in our country. for example, the ebs may encourage commercial banks to continue lending to businesses, especially smes. more importantly, the erdf can help strengthen corporate governance in lithuania's local enterprises, promote investment in renewable energy and support the development of electricity connections.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the regulation which transposes into eu law the implementation of article 10 of the united nations protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition (unfp). this protocol, which supplements the un convention against transnational organized crime, is the first binding instrument relating to small arms adopted at global level. the proposed regulation introduces an ‘export procedure’ to be applied by member states to exports to third countries. the adoption of the regulation under the usual legislative procedure enables article 10 of the unfp to be applied in all the member states, which finally establishes a uniform system for trade in firearms. we, members of the european parliament, support this regulation, which encourages more transparency, helping to combat illegal trafficking in firearms by encouraging and strengthening cooperation amongst states, an objective which has grown in importance since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty on 1 december 2009.
in writing. − the stockholm programme on 'clear and safe europe for the benefit and security of its citizens' underlines that arms trafficking is one of the illicit activities that continues to pose a challenge to the eu's internal security and that the union must therefore continue to promote the ratification of international conventions (and their protocols), in particular those drawn up with the support of the united nations. i have endorsed this proposal as the union needs to take concrete action to complete the transposition into union law of the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, supplementing the united nations convention against transnational organised crime (unfccc) ('unfccc firearms protocol').
in writing. − i voted in favour of the regulation as it proposes an export procedure that member states could apply to exports to third countries. the adoption of the regulation would allow the application of article 10 of the unfpa (un firearms protocol) in all member states, thus finally establishing a uniform system for the trade in firearms, their parts, components and ammunition in the european union. this offer is limited to non-automatic weapons, their parts and ammunition for civilian (non-military) use and to trade or transport to third countries, including countries that are not signatories to the un firearms protocol, as appropriate.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. the proposed regulation will close the gap in the eu's exclusive competence in the area of the common commercial policy by harmonising and simplifying the procedures for the trade in arms with third countries in all eu member states. since, 10 years after the adoption of the un firearms protocol (unfp) by the un general assembly, the application of its provisions in the member states is highly uneven (the protocol has been ratified by 13 eu member states, signed by 9 and not joined by 5, including major arms exporters), this transposition of article 10 of the unfp into eu law will allow for the creation of a single eu system for the trade in small arms with third countries. the regulation does not seek to impose an additional financial burden on businesses (providing for appropriate simplifications of procedures), but encourages cross-border cooperation and strengthens the fight against the illicit trade in arms. i also welcome the rapporteur's initiative to include a reference to article 2 (2) of the council framework decision on the european arrest warrant and the surrender procedures between member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because a uniform, effectively functioning system of trade and export authorisations for firearms, their parts, components and ammunition must be established within the european union and import and transit measures must be introduced to prevent the illicit trade in firearms and to strengthen cooperation between states. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the proposed export procedure to exports to third countries. in order to speed up administrative and bureaucratic procedures and to enable exporters to plan their activities more efficiently, i believe it appropriate to reduce the maximum period allowed for examining the issue of an export authorisation. i also support the proposal to extend the period of validity of export licences for multiple shipments, as this extension reduces the administrative burden for member states and exporters who carry out shipments on a regular basis and for a long period of time.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on exceptional trade measures for countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union’s stabilisation and association process. the european union has granted unlimited duty-free access to the eu market for nearly all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process. the key aim of these measures is to revitalise the western balkan economies through a privileged access to the eu market. in turn, economic development is to foster political stability in the entire region. the termination of the trade preferences would take from the beneficiaries an objective economic advantage in their trade with the eu. this could have negative consequences on the overall economic performances for countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union’s stabilisation and association process; their economic recovery could be seriously jeopardised. as such i support this proposal which aims to amend some elements of this regulation in order to permit the extension of its validity to 31 december 2015.
in writing. − by regulation (ec) no 2007/20001, the european union has allowed duty-free entry on the eu market of almost all goods originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process, in exceptional and unlimited quantities. the main objective of these measures is to stimulate the economies of the western balkan countries by facilitating their access to the eu market. economic development is also promoted by political stability throughout the region. these trade preferences are granted for a period ending on 31 december 2010 and are currently applicable to all products originating in bosnia and herzegovina, serbia and kosovo. the cessation of trade preferences would result in the beneficiaries losing objective economic advantages in trade with the eu. this could have a very significant negative impact on the overall economic performance of the western balkans and adversely affect the internal reform and transition processes in that region. in addition, it could be a major obstacle to the recovery of the western balkans economy. i have endorsed this proposal to extend the provisions of the regulation until 31 december 2015.
in writing. − the regulation enabled the european union to grant duty-free access to the eu market to virtually all goods originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process, in exceptionally unlimited quantities. the main objective of these measures is to stimulate the economies of the western balkan countries by facilitating their access to the eu market. in turn, economic development is promoted by political stability throughout the region. i have endorsed this document as amending certain provisions of the regulation with a view to extending its validity until 31 december 2015 and making certain amendments which have become necessary following the entry into force of the bilateral agreements with bosnia and herzegovina and serbia.
in writing. − the eu has given the balkan countries a clear membership perspective and is actively promoting internal reforms in these countries through the stabilisation and association agreements, as the largest donor in the region, helping to gradually establish a free trade area between the eu and the balkan countries. the autonomous trade preferences have been in place since 2000, were renewed in 2007 and allow almost all goods produced in these countries to be exported to the eu without customs duties in unlimited quantities until the beginning of 2011. the eu is thus currently the largest trading partner of the balkan countries. trade is one of the main instruments for promoting development. a sudden end to trade preferences, especially now in the context of the economic crisis, would be a severe blow for the eu, not only to the economies of the balkan countries, but also to the political stability of the region. on the other hand, the commission is given sufficient leverage to take restrictive measures in the event of serious market distortions in the agricultural and fisheries sectors. i therefore voted in favour of extending the concessions until the end of 2015, with the necessary modifications.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to revive the economies of the western balkan countries by extending trade preferences and further facilitating their access to the eu market. it should be noted that economic development is of great importance as it promotes political stability throughout the region. in the meantime, the withdrawal of trade preferences would have a very significant negative impact on the western balkan economy, internal reforms and transition processes. moreover, the beneficiaries would lose objective economic advantages in trade with the eu. given the very sensitive and vulnerable nature of agricultural and fisheries markets, i support the proposal to empower the commission to adopt appropriate measures by means of delegated acts to protect the european union's markets and regulatory mechanisms in cases where their functioning is seriously disturbed by imports of agricultural and fisheries products.
in writing. − the forthcoming european council is very important and must decide the final course of action. the focus will be on the economic policy guidelines, strengthening europe's global competitiveness, the eu's position on the g20 and the eu's final position on the climate change conference. i support the proposals in the resolution that the president of the commission should present a comprehensive strategy on economic governance, including elements such as the recapitalisation of european banks, the resolution of the european financial stability facility (efsf) and the european stability mechanism (esm) at community level and the evaluation of existing and planned measures, a plan for a meaningful european growth, investment and jobs agenda, proposals to complete the review of the financial markets regulation and ensure that the eu economy can be better managed in the event of a future crisis.
in writing. - i have endorsed this document because the forthcoming european council is of great importance and must be the final and decisive decision on the future path to be taken. i consider that the following key aspects of the meeting are of great importance: the eu plan for the recapitalisation of european banks; the resolution of the european financial stability facility (efsf) and the european stability mechanism (esm) at community level and the assessment of existing and planned measures in terms of whether these measures will be sufficient to control the sovereign debt crisis; a meaningful european plan for growth, investment and job creation, including project bonds; the efforts of member states to coordinate and harmonise elements of their tax systems, including measures to combat tax fraud, tax avoidance and evasion; the need to complete the revision of the financial markets regulation and ensure that the eu economy is more resilient in the event of a future crisis. the report on solidarity is also important for the preparation of a common european system for the issuance of government bonds (european securities) by the end of 2011. these european securities would help to ensure greater fiscal discipline and stability in euro area market participation, and would also ensure that higher-credit-rated member states are not affected by higher interest rates by taking advantage of increased liquidity.
