in writing. − the european council is of unquestionable importance, since it will be the final and decisive decision on the way forward. given the importance of this meeting, i believe that economic policy should be given special attention. in this context, the president of the commission must present a detailed plan at the meeting, including a clear strategy listing the individual stages of its implementation. in particular, the eu plan for the recapitalisation of european banks, which would allow for an operational response to recapitalise the euro area lenders affected by the credit crisis and organise new phases of financial assistance, needs to be discussed in detail. another important topic for discussion at the meeting was the european plan for growth, investment and jobs, which also needs to include project bonds. it is also necessary to consider ways of improving the efforts of member states to coordinate and harmonise the elements of their tax systems, including measures to combat tax fraud, tax evasion and avoidance. in order to make the eu economy more resilient in the event of a future crisis, it is necessary to consider the proposals as soon as possible and to complete the review of the financial markets regulation. in addition, particular attention shall be paid to the report on the development of the european system of state bonds.
in writing. − i support the resolution on the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area, as they have fulfilled all the criteria set out in the schengen evaluation process. both countries have redesigned and reorganised their integrated border management systems through a substantial investment in their law enforcement authorities. bulgaria and romania have continuously proved their support and solidarity and sustained commitment to be reliable partners in south-eastern europe, through a consistent contribution to border security in these parts of the eu. it is of grave importance that we do not impose any additional criteria on member states that are already in the process of joining the schengen area and that we include bulgaria and romania solely on the basis of the schengen acquis and procedures. it is now up to the member states to honour their commitments under the eu legal framework as regards the schengen accession criteria and not give the priority to national populism, and accordingly uphold the fundamental right of the free movement of persons guaranteed to eu citizens by the treaties.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the creation of the schengen area is one of the greatest achievements of the european integration process, which enshrines a fundamental right of eu citizens, namely the free movement of persons. the european parliament in its resolution of 8 june 2011 and the council in its conclusions of 9 june 2011 confirmed that romania and bulgaria fulfil all the criteria of the schengen acquis assessment process for a successful accession to the area. i support the call in the resolution for all member states to take the decision to extend the schengen area and to accept bulgaria and romania in accordance with the schengen acquis and procedures alone, as no additional criteria can be provided for member states that have already started the process of accession to the schengen area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because i believe that the free movement of persons is a fundamental right of eu citizens enshrined in the treaties. the creation of the schengen area and the integration of the schengen acquis into the eu system are among the major achievements of the european integration process. romania and bulgaria fulfil all the criteria of the schengen acquis assessment process in order to successfully join the area. both countries have substantially restructured and reorganised their integrated border management systems and have significantly strengthened their institutional and legal systems through significant investment in their law enforcement institutions, as well as through training and the provision of state-of-the-art technology, and this is recognised in all schengen evaluation reports. there is some doubt that romania and bulgaria have failed to adopt all the provisions of the schengen acquis on the fight against corruption and organised crime, and that bulgaria has not adopted measures to help manage the expected increase in migrant flows at the borders with greece and turkey. however, i do not think that additional criteria can be provided for member states which have already started the process of joining the schengen area. the schengen area should therefore be extended to include bulgaria and romania, and the european council should act in accordance with the eu treaty and take all necessary measures to allow romania and bulgaria to join that area.
in writing. − it is worth noting that the creation of the schengen area and the integration of the schengen acquis into the eu system are among the greatest achievements of the european integration process. it is clearly an ideal expression of the free movement of persons. it should be noted that joining the schengen area is not easy, as the legal criteria of the schengen system are very strict. each member state wishing to join the schengen area must be adequately prepared to secure all the eu's external borders and to issue visas valid throughout the schengen area, as well as to ensure data protection and effective police cooperation. in order to strengthen the protection of the eu's external borders and the security of all eu citizens, the obligations laid down in the eu legal framework in relation to the criteria for accession to the schengen area must therefore apply equally to all member states, with the exception of bulgaria and romania.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let me begin by congratulating you and the rapporteur, mr kósa, on your report on the mobility and integration of disabled people and the european disability strategy 2010-2020. in this report, the european parliament once again demonstrates its longstanding commitment to making equality and inclusion a reality for the some 80 million disabled people living in europe. disability issues have entered the field of law and legislation. on 22 january, for the first time in its history, the european union became a party to an international human rights treaty. this is the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, which has entered into force in the european union. this key step for the rights of disabled people was achieved thanks to the unwavering support of the european parliament throughout the complex procedure leading to the conclusion of the convention. your legislative resolution of april 2009 sent a strong political message in this regard and helped pave the way for a unanimous agreement of member states in the council. the commission is committed to making the rights enshrined in the convention a reality, in cooperation with the council and parliament. as regards the european disability strategy, i want to assure you that the emphasis today on a human rights-based approach and citizen-centred disability policies is far from a semantic shift. it is based on very concrete actions, as also detailed in the european disability strategy. the overall objective of this strategy is that persons with disabilities should be able to exercise all their rights and participate fully in all aspects of social and economic life, as individuals, consumers, students, workers and political actors. our strategy focuses first on removing obstacles. it provides the means to implement the un convention at union level by adopting an ambitious programme of action. although aspects of everyday life such as education, health care and employment are primarily the responsibility of the member states, we are convinced that action by the european union is necessary to support and complement efforts at national level. we will use the europe 2020 strategy and its instruments to encourage the full economic and social participation of people with disabilities. this approach to inclusion will ensure that no action excludes disabled people. rest assured that we will be following very closely the measures taken by the member states to improve the employment situation of these people. we will learn from the reports on the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy submitted as part of the annual national reform programmes; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the reform programme and will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. i am pleased to announce that the commission will be placing the conference organized on the occasion of the european day of persons with disabilities under the heading of 'out of the crisis'. the conference will focus in particular on the contribution of the flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy and on union financing for inclusive growth. as regards the european legislative act on accessibility, the council in june expressed broad support for the european disability strategy and invited the commission to review the framework currently in place to ensure accessibility. this theme is at the heart of the strategy and the adoption of a european legislative act on accessibility is one of the priority actions decided in this area. accessibility means enabling all persons with disabilities to enjoy the same access facilities as everyone else, whether in their physical environment, access to transport, information and communication. accessibility is an essential prerequisite for the exercise of the right recognised by the treaty on european union, the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the united nations convention. studies and complaints from citizens indicate that there is still insufficient accessibility to goods and services in the european market. moreover, accessible goods and services are often expensive, a situation which clearly arises from the fact that this is a small market where competition is still limited. these gaps constitute barriers to the participation of people with disabilities in the economic, social and political life of our society. with the ageing of the population, a potential market is clearly emerging for products and services with a high degree of accessibility. companies often seem to ignore the economic potential of people with disabilities in terms of consumption. many member states have undertaken to improve accessibility by developing national guidelines and standards to comply with the obligations of the un convention. however, if we are content to provide purely national responses to the problem of lack of accessibility, the 27 member states will each find themselves with different laws, regulations, standards and technical requirements, ultimately resulting in a fragmented market with very little competition. we believe that a european market for accessible goods and services would be much more attractive to businesses. the adoption of a european legislative act on accessibility should aim to foster economies of scale for accessible goods and services, to address market gaps and to increase competition. the european commission plans to present a proposal for a european legislative act on accessibility in the autumn of 2012. the many issues relating to this initiative, its content, scope and legal form are currently being considered. the preparation process has indeed begun and will be supported by a substantial impact assessment. we would like to hear from all the stakeholders concerned, but of course, and above all, from people with disabilities and the organisations that represent them. we are naturally also keenly interested in the views of businesses, service providers and public authorities in the member states. we also hope that you will be willing to take part in this process and we invite you to give us your impressions on this subject for the proper preparation of these legislative acts.

people using public buildings, public services. i would like to point out that in the committee on employment and social affairs we decided to call on the member states to adopt the proposal for an in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. more than 80 million people, or about 16% of the eu's total population, are disabled. the eu's legal acts are designed to ensure equal rights for all eu citizens, including people with disabilities. and among these are the inalienable rights to dignity, to equal treatment, to independent living and to full participation in society. the ep has repeatedly expressed its support for improving the lives of people with disabilities. the parliament, which is elected by eu citizens under the treaties, plays an important role in representing the public interest. the ep has therefore a duty to continue to support people with disabilities in their fight for a decent life and to guarantee them greater rights. this should be done through the full inclusion of people with disabilities in society. promoting the employment of disabled people, enabling them to exercise their voting rights by removing administrative, legal or technical barriers, harmonising the rules for disabled people's use of public transport and facilitating access to education at all levels of education should be our priorities. most importantly, the ep must ensure that the needs of people with disabilities are taken into account in the eu 2020 strategy, its flagship initiatives and development programmes, with particular attention to the needs of people with disabilities in central and eastern european countries where a system of care for people with disabilities has been neglected or has been largely non-existent for decades.
in writing. mr president, commissioner, colleagues, public procurement is undoubtedly one of the most important factors determining the competitive functioning of the single market. billions of euros are spent each year on public works and services, and this raises the need to revise the current public procurement rules to reflect the main objective of public procurement policy, which is to meet the needs of citizens while ensuring the efficient use of public funds. in my many speeches on this subject, i have stressed the need to develop a public procurement system based on common principles at eu level and to move towards a more efficient electronic procurement system. this would allow the human factor, which makes the current public procurement system inefficient, opaque, complex and inflexible, to be eliminated at certain stages. i believe that the establishment and implementation of common principles at eu level would open up much greater opportunities to purchase works, goods or services at significantly lower prices, leading to a more transparent, clearer and more efficient public procurement system.
youth unemployment is 30 to 40 per cent in some member states and in some places almost half of young people are out of work. this is a huge problem. what do we have to do, and what can we do, at european union and national level to change this? i believe that, in particular, the preparation and implementation of national employment programmes should pay particular attention to youth problems and provide for measures to encourage young people to be employed without reducing their employment and social guarantees. improve labour market research and forecasting to identify professions with a shortage of workers and to inform young people preparing for studies as widely as possible. increase the involvement of young people in educational studies and retraining programmes, promote entrepreneurship among young people through a variety of measures ranging from teaching the basics of business in secondary schools to applying tax incentives to start-ups, and increase the awareness of young people about european union programmes in this field. the arrangements for the completion of traineeships should be regulated in more detail.
first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr ungureanu, for this important report, which reflects the main idea that we must promote the mobility of workers - one of the fundamental values of the european union - but we must do so responsibly. in other words, we need to promote value, not just any movement of workers. in encouraging people to move, we must ensure that their rights as workers are not violated and that they are not exploited in a foreign country. for these reasons, it is essential that law enforcement and labour inspectorates in different countries cooperate more closely. we need to ensure that people who go to work in other countries are not forced to squander their education, skills and work experience on lower-skilled jobs. this requires further strengthening of the recognition of professional qualifications in the european union. it is also necessary to assess the situation in countries where migration rates are very high for economic and social reasons and where many highly educated skilled workers leave. such mass emigration could have a huge economic and social cost for these countries in the future. i would therefore like to call again on the european commission and the member of the commission here and on the member states to look for solutions to this problem now.
in writing. the current demographic situation in europe is very complex, with declining birth rates in almost all member states, and we need to take measures to give mothers the best possible opportunity to raise their children and to have a real chance of returning to the labour market. it is also essential to ensure that women can achieve the best possible balance between work and family life. i would like to stress that we cannot discriminate against pregnant women or new mothers in the labour market simply because of their biological role in becoming mothers. we must protect the career prospects of mothers and not create any obstacles to their return to their workplace. improvements to the revised directive would improve the protection of mothers' rights, help ensure good working conditions and allow more time to be invested in family life. it is indeed regrettable that the council still lacks a common position on this important directive and that negotiations between member states have continued for so long without any positive progress. i therefore strongly hope that the member states, and in particular the presidency, will continue negotiations as soon as possible and make every effort to find a common solution so that this directive can move from the deadlock as quickly as possible. the crisis in this area should not lead to delayed decisions and savings, since the future of the european union depends on it.
mr president, i would like to move the following oral amendment to paragraph 7: ‘calls on the member states to remove obstacles to workers’ mobility by offering persons (the majority of whom are women) who follow their spouses or partners to another member state, appropriate services such as courses to facilitate their integration into their new social and cultural environment, for example language courses and vocational courses’.
last year, the european disability strategy was adopted. accessibility and health are among the priority areas of action envisaged in this strategy. we are constantly adopting new measures to make common infrastructure more accessible to people with disabilities. unfortunately, the pace of action taken by member states to improve infrastructure is still too slow to ensure adequate integration of people with disabilities into the labour market and access to the healthcare services they need. in particular, member states should therefore step up their efforts to ensure that, in the approval and implementation of various infrastructure projects, the infrastructure facilities under construction, whether new or being renovated, whether privately or publicly owned, are also accessible to persons with disabilities.
the modernisation and harmonisation of the existing public procurement system at european union level is an integral part of the proper future of the european union. the challenges for modernisation proposed by the commission are: a path towards greater transparency and administrative clarity; both the opportunities for small businesses and the improvement of efficiency, savings and time in procurement itself. it is also a pathway to the environment and to greater use of energy-saving measures. i welcome this comprehensive approach and i urge the member states to apply modern procurement principles now, before the end of the reform, as they prepare to implement the changes proposed by the commission.
the proper functioning of the free movement of workers as one of the fundamental principles of the european union has unfortunately had a negative impact on the demographic situation of some economically weaker member states, such as lithuania. however, while respecting this principle and the rights of our own citizens who have chosen to benefit from it, we must ensure that workers from any member state are not discriminated against in the european union. in some member states, disproportionate and often discriminatory barriers to entry for migrant workers remain, both in terms of access to the labour market and in terms of access to social guarantees for them and their family members. i am convinced that a citizen of the european union who has chosen to work in a member state other than his own must be treated equally in all eu member states. the commission and the member states therefore have a long way to go before this equality is truly achieved.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on alternative dispute resolution (adr) in civil, commercial and family matters. i welcome the recent commission consultation on adr. compared to courts, adr schemes are cheaper, quicker and less formal, offering practical solutions. as adr forms part of a general ‘justice-for-growth’ agenda across sectors, we, members of the european parliament, believe that any approach to adr should go beyond consumer disputes so as to include disputes about business-to-business, civil and commercial transactions, irrespective of whether they are carried out between private or public undertakings, as well as family disputes and cases of defamation or cases involving parties whose legal status differs. moreover, on-line shopping is increasing and adr could play a more relevant role here because the scope for judicial action is sometimes limited when dealing with new technologies. parliament stresses the need to ensure that european consumers can access adr systems for transnational as well as national disputes, especially in the on-line market, which is growing rapidly in the eu. i support the rapporteur’s position that the use of adr systems affords a higher level of protection of consumer rights, while also promoting cross-border trade and increased prosperity for all operators in the eu market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document because the legal procedures in cases of this kind are more complex, more expensive and more time-consuming. i believe that legal measures adopted at european union level will help to promote the use of alternative dispute resolution (adr) and encourage more individuals and legal entities to use them, especially in cross-border disputes. the commission is therefore invited to submit a legislative proposal on the application of the ags in the eu by the end of 2011 and the importance of its swift adoption is underlined. i am convinced that there is a need to promote the use of adr methods: they are easily accessible, easy to use, effective and inexpensive, and they can be used to establish and maintain commercial, economic, social and neighbourly relations based on quality and trust and contribute to a high level of consumer protection on mutually favourable terms, which, unlike the current case law, are mutually beneficial. the commission, on the basis of the data collected and a serious impact assessment and in line with better regulation, should explore the possibility of setting minimum standards for adr across sectors, while developing existing systems and encouraging member states and sectors eligible for the systems to increase funding, bearing in mind that adr, while being a low-cost alternative for the parties, must not become 'cheap justice'.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because it is necessary to extend the scope of the alternative dispute resolution (adr) methods. in particular, this approach must be applied to civil, commercial and family matters. in this context, i support the proposal to call on the commission to present a proposal by the end of this year on the application of ags in the eu and to set at least minimum ags standards in different sectors. it should be noted that the ags must be applied as a flexible, efficient and at the same time fair enough method of dispute resolution, and that the implementation of this method in the various sectors must be adequately financed so that such dispute resolution does not become 'expensive justice'.

in writing. − the proposal aims to amend directive 2000/25/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2000 on action to be taken against the emission of gaseous and particulate pollutants from engines for agricultural or forestry tractors. the provisions of this directive aim to ensure the free movement of agricultural and forestry tractors while reducing the emission limit values of engines in order to protect the health and well-being of citizens and the environment. the directive sets emission limit values which are gradually reduced. the independent experts and interested parties agree that the limit values for the types of agricultural tractors referred to in the proposed amendment are technically not feasible. therefore, if the entry into force were not postponed, the functioning of the internal market and the agricultural sector using those tractors would be completely disrupted. i have agreed to the commission's proposal to postpone the application of the requirements for the category of tractors concerned for three years.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because one of the main sources of air pollution is transport and its emissions. the emission limits for carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter are set and will be regulated in the future by several directives (entering into force on 1 january 2012 and 1 january 2014 respectively). the emissions control directives apply to engines for farm tractors in order to limit their emissions. one of the biggest problems at the moment is that if tractor manufacturers equipped engines with an exhaust system, they would not be able to ensure that the vehicles meet the operational requirements related to their size and manoeuvrability. this document therefore calls for narrow gauge tractors to be either excluded from the scope of the new directives altogether or to be deferred for five years. the introduction of an exemption would be a better solution, as the directive on the limitation of transport pollution, which is coming into force, would help to reduce air pollution and noise.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this document because this proposal to amend directive 2000/25/ec would postpone the t2, c2 and t4 obligations for three years. for tractors of category 1, the requirements of stages iiib and iv shall be met. this directive concerns positive ignition engines intended for agricultural and forestry tractors. this directive lays down limit values for the emission of pollutants carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen, hydrocarbons and particulate matter from engines. the directive sets progressively lower thresholds for the adjustment of the maximum emission of gases and particulate matter for subsequent phases corresponding to different dates. the strict requirements for stages iii and iv include the installation of the exhaust treatment systems in the engine compartment compared to the engine itself, which takes up a lot of space. furthermore, the possibility of installing such systems is severely limited by the operational requirements of the engine. narrow-track tractors use the same type of engines as other tractors, but there is one key difference: the small engine compartment and the limited space around it. tractor manufacturers cannot equip engines with exhaust treatment systems and at the same time ensure that vehicles meet the performance requirements in terms of size and manoeuvrability of the most important design aspects of these vehicles. it should be noted that this was the conclusion of various studies commissioned by the commission, which recommended that narrow gauge tractors be exempted from the requirements of stages iiib and iv altogether or that this requirement be deferred for at least five years.
in writing. − i voted against this resolution because i believe that it is appropriate to impose strict requirements for the installation of exhaust systems in the engine compartment of narrow-track tractors. in particular, in order to ensure a high level of environmental protection and the well-being of european citizens, we need to set requirements that encourage the reduction of emissions from engines fitted to agricultural and forestry tractors. it should be noted that narrow-track tractors currently in use cause a lot of pollution and a threat to the safety of workers. in view of this, the industry sector should seek to replace old, polluting tractors with modern, low-emission technologies as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the need to limit emissions of carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particulate matter from vehicles. the current emissions directive and the procedures it lays down will be tightened up from 2012 (with a transitional period until 2013). these restrictions will apply to approximately 1500 companies in the european union, and the installations covered include a wide range of ground installations for purposes such as construction, forestry and agriculture. the objective of this directive is to reduce emissions from vehicles with very high emission levels. this directive would also make it possible to combat unfair competition with third country producers whose production process is not yet subject to such strict restrictions.
in writing. − directive 97/68/ec regulates the maximum emission levels for carbon monoxide (co), hydrocarbons (hc), nitrogen oxides (nox) and particulate matter (pm) from diesel engines for non-road mobile machinery. the 2004 revision of directive 2004/26/ec established the current stage iii a thresholds and the dates and thresholds for the subsequent stage iii b. these stricter values will be phased in from january 2011 depending on the power category. the installations covered by this directive include a wide range of ground-based installations for purposes such as construction, forestry and agriculture. the directive also applies to locomotives, motor vehicles and inland waterway vessels. the directive covers a wide range of equipment manufacturers (around 1500 companies), most of which do not produce the engines used in this installation. the engines are produced by only a few large companies. i believe that the crisis will make it impossible for companies to meet the requirements, so it is proposed to allow the production of engines until 2014 with an increase in the flexibility percentage, i.e. the commission proposes to increase the current 20% to 50%. i have agreed to these proposed flexibility measures, which will be valid until 13 december 2013.
in writing. − i support this resolution as it is appropriate to extend the scope of the flexibility scheme. the global financial and economic crisis has, after all, had a severe impact on most industrial companies. in this context, it will be particularly difficult for companies to implement the requirements of the directive that are currently applicable. in order to ensure that the industry continues to develop and to remain competitive and to protect the environment, it is appropriate to apply flexibility measures until 2014 and to allow a certain number of engines to be placed on the market under a flexibility scheme. the implementation of these measures will mitigate as far as possible the impact of the current economic crisis on engine and machine manufacturers and will maintain the competitiveness and employment of the sector.
in writing. − i am strongly in favour of increased long-term investment and support for people with disabilities, as it is imperative that they are provided with the necessary means to enjoy equal rights, equal treatment and full participation in education, employment, social life and public life, in particular in relation to the right to vote. parliament has adopted significant decisions for the recognition and protection of the rights of people with disabilities, calling for legal standards and legislation at eu level. however, it is important that the new generation of human rights of people with disabilities be upheld through active and targeted policies ensuring the practical application of all human rights and guaranteeing equal opportunities and full access to services and products. one of the most important objectives is to improve the level of employment among the almost 80 million people with disabilities who live in the eu. an increased rate of poverty results in limited access to employment, training, healthcare and appropriate treatment, so disability benefits must therefore be guaranteed to those in need. states must develop national policies and strategies on disability, in harmony with the european disability strategy (eds), while at the same time introducing detailed deadlines and mechanisms for the implementation of the eds, particularly with regard to strengthening the role of parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. more than 80 million people, or about 16% of the total population of the european union, have a disability, and their unemployment rate is twice that of people without a disability. the disabled are thus among the most vulnerable and their poverty rate is over 70% above the average. the economic crisis has led to a reduction in the funding of measures and benefits for disabled people in some member states, which has further increased the social exclusion of this group. i believe that austerity measures that unduly reduce funding for services for people with disabilities or for projects that include them socially cannot be justified by the problems of the disabled. i agree that more use of the european structural funds, in particular the european regional development fund, is necessary to ensure that european funds improve access to goods and services for people with disabilities, reduce discrimination and exclusion against them and guarantee the right to a life of dignity and worth.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the mobility and inclusion of people with disabilities, as it covers many of the issues that affect people with disabilities, such as education, employment, integration, appropriate adaptation of the environment, assistance to family members. in my view, the report quite appropriately highlights the importance of increasing the mobility of disabled people by removing the physical and social barriers that prevent disabled people from accessing public buildings, public services such as public transport, information technology and other facilities and services. i also support the idea put forward in the report that specific data should be collected on disability problems and disability-related services in the member states, including data on care institutions and the quality of services provided in them. i would like to point out that the main obstacles to the integration of disabled people into society are high unemployment rates, and that disabled people's unemployment is due to insufficient preparation for the labour market. in addition, it is necessary to assess the situation of disabled people in the labour market in each member state, explaining the reasons why they lose the incentive to take up employment, to help them integrate into the labour market through the european social fund (esf) and to facilitate the creation of jobs for disabled people by employers. this report emphasises that member states should provide general information to families raising children with disabilities, financial support, social and health services, psychological support, and more flexible working conditions for parents or one of them raising children with disabilities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because more than 80 million people, or about 16% of the eu population, have a disability, including people with mental disabilities, particularly autism, and because their unemployment rate is twice that of people without disabilities. disabled people are vulnerable and live in poverty 70% above the average. the employment rate for disabled people is only around 45%, and we are well aware that quality jobs provide economic independence and personal achievement. unemployment is known to increase the risk of poverty and social exclusion, as at least one in four people will experience mental health problems at least once in their lives and one in ten may develop chronic mental health problems. it is important to stress that an active and targeted policy is needed to deal with this unchanging situation. the increased risk of poverty is not only due to the often limited access to employment and education, but also to the often limited access to health care and adequate treatment. the europe 2020 target of 75% employment for people aged 20-64 will not be achieved without the inclusion of people with disabilities.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the european commission's objectives to modernise the public procurement system in the european union. the current directives were adopted relatively recently, in 2004, and although a number of innovations were introduced into the previous public procurement system at that time, the situation has changed again in the last 6 years. one of the key issues in the public procurement system has always been the simplification of procedures to make them more efficient for buyers with limited resources, as well as the regulation of the issue of service concessions at eu level, the mandatory inclusion of social criteria in procurement procedures, the value thresholds for transactions, beyond which eu directives would automatically apply. in this document, the european parliament reaffirmed its position that there is no need for regulation of service concessions at eu level at present and that the inclusion of social criteria in procurement procedures should always remain voluntary, but recognised that the european commission should develop better procurement guides in this respect.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it aims to improve public procurement by simplifying procedures and giving more opportunities to small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the scope of the directives should be clarified to cover public procurement activities which, according to recent judgments of the court of justice, are intended to provide direct economic benefits to contracting authorities. i welcome the european commission's efforts to involve public procurement bodies more effectively in the pursuit of common social objectives, but i also point out that the main obstacle lies in the public procurement directives themselves. as long as the criterion of the cheapest tender is as important in the directives as the criterion of the most economically advantageous tender, given the considerable economic problems faced by contracting authorities in this area, little will change. this will only change if it is stated that contracts must be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender (for example, according to the principle 'apply or explain') and if the criteria for determining the most economically advantageous tender can be applied more easily. simpler eu public procurement rules and greater access to flexible procedures will help to promote sustainable and innovative purchasing practices. there are various options, such as continuous market monitoring, greater use of the negotiated procedure after they have been announced, and other additional measures that increase transparency or allow for the submission of substantive alternative proposals, in particular with regard to proposals based on the principle of sustainable development.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because public procurement activities must provide direct economic benefits to contracting authorities, and not the other way around. simplified procurement rules and more flexible procedures are necessary to ensure a sustainable and modern procurement operation. i do not think it is appropriate for public procurement authorities to include environmental costs in the assessment of the most economically advantageous tender. in this context, i support the proposal to allow the decision-making authorities to decide for themselves whether or not to apply criteria other than those relating to public procurement. attention should be drawn to the need to strengthen the provisions for the conclusion of subcontracting contracts in order to provide the public authorities with all information relating to subcontractors in advance, before the conclusion of the contract. it is also necessary to ensure that sme subcontractors are not treated less favourably than the main contractor. in order to facilitate the participation of non-profit, social and smes entities in public procurement, the thresholds for supply and service contracts should be increased.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur that eu rules should be simplified to make it easier for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) to bid on public contracts. smes are the backbone of lithuania's economy. these enterprises account for 76% of labour market employment in the business economy, which is 9% higher than the eu average. nevertheless, according to the statistics of the european commission, and compared to the eu average (28% versus 21%), the majority of lithuanian smes are experiencing financial problems. in lithuania, small enterprises receive only a small proportion of public procurement contracts than they should in view of their share of the economy. this is because today's procurement rules make tendering for contracts difficult and expensive. much remains to be done to create a fair and transparent eu regulatory framework for public procurement and to help smes to have better access to public procurement contracts both in the eu and in third countries. i agree with my alde colleagues that the 'once only' principle should apply, whereby the institutions should not ask for evidence that has already been provided in other procedures again. this should avoid burdensome bureaucratic obstacles.
in writing. − i support this report, which aims to reaffirm the european commitment to reinforcing the right of free movement for workers. member states must facilitate the exercise of this right, implementing existing legislation fully whilst bringing national legislation into line with the european provisions, in order to eliminate possible direct or indirect barriers, notably with regard to discriminatory behaviour based on nationality, refusal of rights for family members, and social security scheme rules, as well as other barriers that can prevent workers from moving freely in search of a job or can create disincentives to their doing to. in an era of globalised markets, the free movement of workers can address the problem of finding a profitable fit between labour demand and supply. the commission must strengthen its efforts in enforcing and supporting labour mobility, must conduct more in-depth analysis in relation to infringement procedures for non-compliant member states, and must present a long-term, comprehensive, multidisciplinary mobility strategy for analysing and removing all existing legal, administrative and practical barriers to the free movement of workers. over-protectionism in terms of labour mobility will induce a mistrust that could affect the eu’s performance as a world player. member states need to work and grow together.
in writing. − the right to live and work in another eu country is one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu and an essential component of eu citizenship as recognised by the treaties. however, some eu member states still have administrative and bureaucratic obstacles that prevent eu citizens from fully enjoying their rights, and insufficient efforts are being made to combat discrimination and exploitation of migrant workers. i agree with the calls for member states to simplify the administrative procedures relating to the right of free movement of workers in order to avoid unjustified, unnecessary or complex administrative procedures that restrict the exercise of that right. the commission should carry out a comprehensive study identifying the obstacles faced by european union workers wishing to exercise their right to free movement and assessing the action taken by the member states in this regard. the commission should also assess the current economic situation of member states in terms of labour markets and monitor member states to better align migration policies with labour aspects, to better address labour shortages and to stimulate domestic production and growth in their economies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i was appointed rapporteur for the opinion and i believe that the text put to the vote in plenary reflects the main idea i proposed - that the mobility of workers must be encouraged, but that this must be done in a responsible way. this means that when we encourage people to move, we must ensure that their rights as workers are not violated and that they are not exploited in a foreign country. we also need to ensure that people who go to work in other countries are not forced to squander their education, skills and work experience on jobs that are better paid but with lower qualifications. finally, i called for an assessment of the situation in countries where, especially recently, emigration is very high for purely economic reasons and where a large number of highly educated and highly skilled workers leave. such mass migration in the future could cost these 'donor states' a great deal not only economically but also socially. the commission and the member states should therefore start looking for solutions to this problem now.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because living and working in another member state is one of the fundamental freedoms of the eu, regardless of a person's ethnic origin, and an essential constituent of eu citizenship recognised by the treaties, yet statistics show that too few people still make use of this right, despite concrete initiatives to support labour mobility. the free movement of workers is a positive social and economic example for both the eu and the member states, as it is an important stage in eu integration, economic development, social cohesion, personal professional development, the fight against prejudice, racism and xenophobia, and can help to reverse the negative effects of the economic crisis and better prepare for the challenges of global change by engaging in dialogue with all stakeholders in decision-making and civil society. the commission must continue to promote labour mobility and present a long-term, comprehensive, multidisciplinary mobility strategy aimed at removing all existing legal, administrative and practical obstacles to the free movement of workers. consistent, effective and transparent policies are needed to respond to labour market and economic trends. it should be noted that mobility should remain voluntary, and that the negative side effects of increased mobility, which lead to 'mind drain' and the departure of young people, as well as the negative impact on family life and children when one or both parents work abroad, should be more effectively mitigated at eu level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the obstacles still existing throughout the european union to the exercise of the right to free movement of workers must be removed and the conditions for integration into the new social and cultural environment must be created. all member states must properly implement equal treatment of workers and ensure adequate protection of labour rights, and active labour market policy programmes to promote mobility must be developed. in addition, eu policies to combat direct and indirect discrimination and to remove legal and administrative barriers need to be strengthened. it should be noted that in order to facilitate the mobility of workers, we need to ensure that this right is not abused for the purposes of inequality, wages and social dumping.
in writing. − the free movement of workers is a very sensitive issue. it will shape the economic and social future of the eu. the free movement of workers is a right that all member states agreed upon, yet many member states have introduced or reintroduced restrictions. approximately one third of workers in the eu are in precarious job situations, and this leads to an increase in workers seeking jobs in other countries. the commission provided figures proving that eastern european workers, in particular, did not hinder the economy but in fact brought economic growth. there is a single market for capital and goods, but there are still limitations on the single labour market. western companies can operate without restrictions in eastern europe, and do so with varying degrees of success, but eastern european workers face restrictions in western europe. this is economically, politically and morally wrong. people have a right to jobs: a right that is granted by the eu. i voted in favour of this report because it emphasises that the eu must guarantee european values, including freedom and mobility, for all. comprehensive mobility for workers must be promoted, the rights of workers in foreign countries must be protected and such workers must not be exploited. it is vital to reaffirm the principle of job mobility and to promote geographic mobility.
in writing. − the services directive was adopted in 2006 and remains a key instrument for the creation of a fully functioning single market for services. member states have made a great deal of effort to implement it. nevertheless, efforts should be stepped up to ensure full and proper implementation of the services directive and to establish fully functioning common information points. the functioning of the common market for services is a prerequisite for promoting economic growth, decent employment and innovation in europe and for maintaining europe's competitiveness in the world. the mutual evaluation provided for in the services directive is an important tool for identifying further initiatives to improve the internal market for services. i agree that the commission should continue and strengthen its cooperation with each member state individually in order to ensure that the services directive is fully and correctly transposed and implemented in all member states and that the remaining obstacles to businesses taking full advantage of the single internal market are removed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it provides the european parliament with its assessment of the functioning of one of the mechanisms established by the mutual evaluation procedure in the services directive adopted in 2006. this is a new instrument, used for the first time in eu law, and its main objective is to assess the situation of the internal market in services following the implementation of this directive. the report therefore not only provides an overview of the results but also suggests ways of improving this process in the future, including by providing parliament with its assessment of the application of such a measure in other policy areas. the mutual evaluation process has been applied only to those provisions of the directive which leave a certain degree of discretion to the member states, such as certain provisions relating to the establishment of undertakings and the cross-border provision of services. the european parliament considers that the objectives of mutual evaluation are still not sufficiently defined, which has led to misunderstandings between member states, and that more should be done to make the process more transparent. although a certain degree of confidentiality is an important condition for building trust between member states, the report proposes to ensure that stakeholders are regularly provided with feedback on the progress of the process.
in writing. − this report summarises the experience of peer review with regard to the services directive and expresses general but conditional support for the application of this method in other policy areas. this report also discusses the results of the mutual evaluation and the next steps towards a better functioning of the internal market for services. i agreed with the view that the mutual evaluation provided for in the services directive is an important tool for identifying further initiatives to improve the internal market for services. the remaining regulatory obstacles, such as the rules on reservation of activities, insurance requirements, legal form and capital ownership requirements, should be removed. it is necessary to focus on unjustified or disproportionate requirements which should be abolished in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the single market and the maximum added value of the functioning of the single market for services. the commission must therefore continue and strengthen its cooperation with each member state individually in order to ensure the full and correct transposition of the services directive into national law and its implementation in all member states. in the meantime, member states must ensure that new and existing requirements are non-discriminatory, necessary and proportionate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the experience of mutual evaluation in relation to the services directive should be applied to other policy areas. it should be noted that the mutual evaluation process contributes to greater confidence among member states and provides an opportunity for member states to share best practices. the mutual evaluation process contributes to the improvement of the internal market for services and creates better conditions for its functioning. this assessment will help to identify the true state of the internal market after the implementation of the services directive, the impact of this directive on economic activity and employment, unjustified and disproportionate requirements. it should be noted that in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the single market, priority should be given to targeted actions that deliver the greatest added value from the functioning of the single market for services, and particular attention should be paid to those sectors and professions that promote the growth of cross-border provision of services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on global economic governance and i support the position of the rapporteur that global imbalances constitute a potential threat to financial and macro-economic stability. therefore, global economic governance has to be reformed in order to help rebalance the world economy and avoid another slump. we, members of the european parliament, supported the need for a global understanding and a common approach in relation to monetary policy, international trade, sustainable public finances and flexible currencies, on the basis of economic fundamentals. the global economy should be characterised by open markets, in which high social and environmental standards are vital, and the international monetary fund and the world trade organization should play a core role. alongside the completion of the single market, the economic governance framework in the eu must be strengthened.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it contains european parliament recommendations on global economic governance to the international monetary fund, the g20 and the world trade organisation (wto), as well as to the commission and the council. i believe that the european parliament's involvement in the debate on how the global economy should be managed in the future is crucial to preventing a repetition of a similar crisis in the future and to managing the current crisis and mitigating its effects as much as possible. in its report, the european parliament reiterated the importance of a responsible monetary policy and strong financial regulation and supervision at this time. parliament also stressed that the reform of global economic governance should ensure that global markets are integrated into a comprehensive institutional framework and that favourable conditions for long-term investment are created.
in writing. − the key to the rebalancing of the global economy is two-fold: increased competitiveness and wide-ranging reforms to stimulate growth in deficit countries, and market opening and sound monetary policy in surplus countries. there are many international organisations dedicated to managing the world economy, such as the imf, the world bank, the wto, the un conference on trade and development (unctad) and the international finance corporation (ifc), as well as the intergovernmental forums of the g7 and g20, of which the imf and g20 are the most effective, although both still need to be improved and global markets need global rules. there is a global recognition that some sectors of the financial industry contributed to the global financial crisis and exposed financial mismanagement, reinforced the sovereign debt crisis and a general consensus that the financial sector needs to be made more accountable, including to cover some of the losses incurred as a result of the crisis. i have endorsed this document because the lack of coordinated and effective regulation and supervision of the global financial system has exposed the financial sector to weaknesses that have subsequently further increased the vulnerability of the global economy and i believe that decisive action is needed to avoid similar crises in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the current global turmoil has forced us to urgently re-shape the global economic governance model. in particular, it is necessary to develop globally common, robust and effectively functioning rules for global financial markets to ensure coordinated and effective regulation and supervision. open markets for all market participants should be ensured, with the promotion of increased competitiveness and wide-ranging reforms. i think that the possibility of using special borrowing rights instead of the dollar as the world's reserve currency would help stabilize the global financial system. it is also essential to have a common approach to monetary policy, international trade, sustainable public finances and flexible currencies, based on key economic indicators. trade policy must focus on fair trade, democracy, human rights, working conditions and sustainable development.
in writing. − i strongly support this proposal, which aims to combat the inequalities that single mothers face in europe. member states must invest and must promote research into the issue, taking advantage of the newly created european institute for gender equality in vilnius, while also initiating dialogues with other member states in order to develop implementation strategies. policies towards single mothers differ across europe. the high unemployment rate for single mothers – combined with the gender pay gap – results in their being torn between taking on debt and caring for their children. we must encourage national policies that will guarantee indirect subsidies for the purchase of food. we must provide tax credits for single parents, along the lines of the arrangements that exist in austria, belgium, the netherlands and the uk. a european incentive to member states that provide healthcare for mothers and children where the family is below the national average would be a positive step. flexible job opportunities, including part-time work, teleworking, and e-jobs, should be offered at local, national and eu level to enable single mothers to reconcile their private and professional lives. germany can be used as a model in relation to increasing unemployment benefits for single mothers with dependent children.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and i am glad that the european parliament has paid a great deal of attention to single mothers, whose number is unfortunately increasing in europe. single mothers now account for 5% of european women. single mothers are not to be forgotten, but still in europe, about 85% of all single-parent families are single mothers. i would like to emphasise that poverty was most acute for single mothers in almost all of europe during the economic crisis. as regards the risk of poverty, it is important to recognise that children in single-mother care experience higher levels of poverty than children in traditional families where both parents are usually working. it should also be remembered that not all single mothers can work full-time if their children are very young. the number of children in a single-mother family also needs to be considered. in order to enable single mothers to balance their careers and family life, flexible working conditions such as remote working, part-time work and flexible working arrangements should be provided for them. tax breaks for single-parent families, reimbursement of medical expenses, the establishment of family centres and the initiation of special training programmes for single mothers are all necessary. they must also be given priority access to places in crèches and nurseries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document because it calls for greater attention to be paid to the situation of single women. member states are required to implement public policies, including education policy, care provision, health policy, employment policy, social security systems, housing policy, to meet the needs of and take into account the reality of single-parent families, in particular the real situation of single-parent families. i believe that the aim should be to increase the autonomy and independence of single mothers, to reduce their feelings of passivity and loneliness, to increase their social awareness, to improve their childrearing skills and to provide them with better access to information on their rights and employment opportunities. the european commission and the member states must take into account the specific situation of single mothers in different european countries and provide special support to single mothers belonging to the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. − at present, up to 5% of the total female population in the eu are single mothers, i.e. mostly women aged 25 to 40. in latvia and estonia, the figure is as high as 9%. this is a relatively new social phenomenon. the growing number of single mothers is associated with a devaluation of the family as a basic social unit. i believe that this new and difficult to define social category should be included in the social security system. however, we should find the optimal basket of support measures - the good proposals set out in the report should not be an incentive to put the traditional family in a less advantageous position, since we are interested in the fact that as many children as possible grow up in full families. this report is not only about single mothers, but also about child poverty, and i support the suggestions it makes to help children escape the cycle of poverty. moreover, in the current economic situation, particularly for those member states suffering from emigration, it is necessary to promote the inclusion of all social categories in economic growth. single mothers and parents are one of the important categories that should receive support and facilitate their entry into the labour market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because a common policy in this area is necessary, as unmarried mothers make up a large proportion of the population. it is noteworthy that this family model is often characterised by poverty and social exclusion. to solve the problems and make life easier for single mothers, we need to develop their independence and autonomy. in particular, the european structural funds should be used to promote maternal employment, the activities of family centres and other informal networks that care for single mothers, and the exchange of best practices. only by working together can we ensure that single mothers are not doomed to failure, but are empowered and happy mothers.
in writing. − in the eu, 5% of women are single mothers. this group is difficult to identify as it is categorised differently across the eu, yet these women need help. in some parts of europe, a woman’s extended family helps to bring up a child or children, but in other areas social benefits are of great help to single women. these women have to cope with a task often shared by two parents. single mothers and their children are at a high risk of poverty. among single-parent families, every third child lives below the poverty line or is in danger of being in poverty. the current economic crisis has not helped the situation. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for a change in policy – particularly in public policies involving education, health care, employment, social assistance and housing – to benefit single mothers. member states should promote appropriate models to support single mothers: models that help these women enter the labour market. there must also be an exchange of good practice among member states. only then can strong policies in support of single mothers be developed and implemented.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, this is a very important announcement. according to eurostat, lithuania has one of the highest rates of single mothers with children in the eu: 6% in lithuania, compared with 2% in greece, finland or romania. one of the most worrying is the poverty of children raised by single mothers. the high employment rate of single mothers is a barrier to protecting children from poverty. lithuania's child poverty rate is almost 22%, which is above the eu average (20,3%). children who grow up with only one parent are at greater risk of poverty. according to lithuanian national statistics, 44% of single-parent families are at risk of poverty. in lithuania, high levels of child poverty are partly due to low family allowances, which are well below the eu average. lithuanian single mothers find it very difficult to balance work and child rearing. according to the european commission, lithuania is not fully implementing the barcelona targets, which cover 9% of children under 3 years of age and 62% of children from three years of age to school age. i support the rapporteur's proposal to make use of the recently established european institute for gender equality in vilnius.
in writing. − i fully support this proposal, which aims to tackle organised crime at eu level. organised crime is a key threat to the internal security of the eu, polluting the legal economy, infringing human rights, subverting the rules of democracy and hindering implementation of the eu’s commitments to its citizens. the institutions must therefore make a concrete political effort to counter it. organised crime now has a transnational basis and it has to be fought using the same approach. the eu legislative framework in this regard must be improved and member states must ensure effective ratification and/or transposition of all european and international legal instruments relating directly or indirectly to action to combat organised crime. entrenched mafia-style organised crime in the eu must be eradicated, and the function of the european bodies involved in various ways in fighting organised crime must be strengthened. of utmost importance is full compliance with the principle of the mutual recognition of criminal decisions, with a view to combating organised crime and to improving judicial cooperation between member states and with third countries. it is stressed that measures countering organised crime must be consistent with respect for fundamental rights and proportionate to the objectives pursued.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because organised crime groups are becoming increasingly politically active in the european union and the trafficking of drugs, international arms trafficking, human trafficking and exploitation, financial crime of all kinds, counterfeiting, environmental crime, cybercrime, fraud, extortion (trafficking), misappropriation of public funds - most of these crimes are becoming targets for money laundering - is on the rise. the reports estimate the turnover of the italian mafia alone at around eur 135 billion, which, in cooperation with the mafia in other countries, is increasingly profitable and economically advantageous. organised crime is international in scope and has a high cost to society, as well as human rights violations. the report sets out ambitious objectives for the formulation of appropriate proposals to combat crime, to create greater freedom, security and justice in the european union and to combat crime.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, as is well known, the objective of organised crime (corruption, racketeering, drug trafficking, money laundering, etc.) is to obtain economic benefits, and therefore effective action to prevent and combat this phenomenon must focus on identifying, freezing, seizing and confiscating the assets acquired through criminal means. the current regulatory framework at eu level does not sufficiently ensure serious counter-measures, and therefore a regulatory framework is needed that allows for, for example, so-called extended asset seizures and lawsuits for assets registered in the name of others. member states should strengthen judicial authorities and law enforcement agencies on the basis of best available experience, by comparing legislation and instruments to support their activities and by allocating adequate human and financial resources. measures should be taken to help combat this recognised threat to the european union and its citizens, such as the establishment of a special commission of inquiry into the spread of transnational criminal organisations, including the mafia, the preparation of an impact assessment of the additional benefits of the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, the improvement of practical cooperation between police and judicial authorities in the member states, the exclusion of enterprises linked to organised crime and the mafia from participation in public tenders and the management of public procurement and similar measures.
in writing. −the need to strengthen the response to organised crime in the european union and beyond requires joint action and better coordination between the relevant eu institutions and between member states. i voted in favour of the report because it contains a series of specific proposals on how to increase the deterrent effect and make penalties more effective, while respecting fundamental rights and freedoms. the report also takes into account the external dimension of organised crime. in some third countries, corruption is deeply rooted as part of the culture of social relations. in addition to making full use of the instruments available to promote the fight against corruption in third countries, the eu should monitor the procedures for the allocation and use of eu funds in third countries to ensure that they meet the eu's high standards of transparency and publicity. it should be noted that, in addition to the maximum transparency of procedures and the publication of all information on public finances, the availability to the public of data on criminal offences and persons involved in them would be an effective tool. corruption is linked to organised crime and member states and the eu should make additional efforts to reduce the tolerance of even 'small' corruption in their societies.
in writing. − colleagues, based on the 2011 europol report on the assessment of organised crime the sudden surge in organized crime in lithuania is a serious problem. my country is mentioned 24 times in the report, compared to latvia, which is mentioned only once, or estonia, which is mentioned three times. europol claims that the assets of lithuanian criminal groups have increased their recruitment, infiltration and investment opportunities. the report describes the important role of lithuanian groups in the trafficking of drugs (including amphetamines, methamphetamines and ecstasy) with eu countries. they are also involved in counterfeiting euro banknotes and smuggling cigarettes. as the ep report says, organised crime is a multi-billion dollar business in europe and growing. the spread of illicit trafficking, as well as the opportunities offered by the global economic crisis, have made organized crime even more dangerous. the rapporteur proposes a number of measures, including improving the european legal framework, to help strengthen the fight against organised crime at eu level. we also need to fight political forces that look the other way and sometimes indirectly support the problem.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the high-level forum on aid effectiveness through which the european parliament stresses the necessity for the eu to adopt a strong position in busan in order to achieve global consensus on an effective and truly inclusive partnership for development and identify clear and measurable aims in order to increase aid effectiveness, supplemented by an effective follow-up mechanism. the report underlines that future success will depend on factors such as engaging stronger national parliaments in the monitoring of aid as well as local authorities and civil society organisations; enhancing efforts towards political, administrative and fiscal decentralization in partner countries and better coordination of activities between donor countries. we, as members of the european parliament, stated that aid effectiveness requires poor countries to be able to mobilise domestic revenues; therefore, we urge the eu to make the fight against tax havens and tax evasion its utmost priority, while promoting alternative sources of development finance. i am also in favour of the eu advocating, in busan, the introduction of binding measures which will ensure that aid provision complies with human rights agreements, as all governments – donor and recipient – are bound by human rights obligations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it sets out the european parliament's recommendations for the 4th high-level forum on aid effectiveness to be held in south korea in november this year. indeed, the european union and its member states provide more than half of the world's official development assistance, and the eu therefore plays an important role in the implementation of the aid effectiveness agenda. the document notes that, according to the latest monitoring and evaluation studies, recipient countries have done more than donor countries in implementing commitments under previously adopted development assistance declarations and agendas. the parties are therefore invited to further discuss in the forthcoming forum how to increase transparency and accountability in the provision of assistance and to reduce fragmentation of assistance. the document also expresses the belief that the eu must take an ambitious stance in the forum, as this would help to discuss in more detail and fully implement the commitments in the area of aid effectiveness.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the success of the fourth high-level forum will depend on a firm commitment to increase the effectiveness of assistance, i.e. by setting clear and measurable objectives and precise deadlines for their implementation. the paris declaration and the accra agenda for action are not being sufficiently implemented. the importance of bottom-up governance of development, consistency of support and the establishment of robust, effective and independent monitoring mechanisms involving parliaments and civil society at both national and international level is emphasised. support should be leveraged to promote inclusive and sustainable growth by taking into account the specificities of each country, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of support in countries that need it most, with a view to reducing poverty and aid dependency, promoting job creation and self-sustaining sustainable economic growth in developing countries. i believe that development aid is not enough to eradicate poverty and that aid should be directed at the causes of poverty rather than the consequences. more effective support through engagement in the development process is needed to build a strong and environmentally sound economy in the beneficiary countries, ensuring access to basic social services for all citizens and reducing dependency on support over time.
in writing. − a recent report published by the oecd shows that only one target out of 12 set by the paris declaration for 2010 has been met. another study shows that more ambitious application of the principles of the declaration could have saved the eu and its member states billions. against the background of the economic difficulties the eu and its member states currently face, the real challenge lies not so much in reaching the quantitative target level of oda, but in achieving the biggest impact with the money we spend. the procedures and practices to achieve this are there, the thing lacking is strong leadership and sustained political commitment to accelerate implementation. china, a signatory of the paris declaration as a recipient, has actively expanded its aid programme at a rate of around 30% per year for the past five years. now is a good time to find ways to involve china in the aid architecture, as it seeks to enhance the impact of its policies and aid. both donors and recipient countries have received a sobering signal, and the 4th high level meeting in busan is a forum to draw conclusions and look for a way forward to achieve mdgs.
