in writing. today's debate on the 2012 budget is very similar to last year's debate. the arguments of both the council and the parliament have not changed. the economic crisis is still ongoing, so the council's aim of cutting all spending as much as possible is understandable. i think that this has been taken into account in parliament's position. the budget is growing by only 1.9 percent, which is less than inflation, and some budget cuts have also been made. i agree that strict budgetary discipline is necessary, but we must not forget the financial commitments that are made and the consequences of not fulfilling them in the long term. i want to emphasize again what i have said many times: to get out of the crisis we must invest in the future. adequate funding is needed for priority programmes that promote economic growth and job creation. we must strive to deliver effectively on our own targets set out in 'strategy 2020'. the proposed cuts by the council to the 7th research programme, to small and medium-sized enterprises and to programmes promoting the competitiveness of enterprises are therefore unjustified. i believe that parliament's position maintains a responsible approach to the 2012 budget and i am convinced that the efficient and balanced use of eu funds will help to speed up the recovery of the european economy and create additional incentives for the creation of new jobs, thus creating conditions for social and economic well-being.
unemployment in the european union is a particularly painful and worrying problem. this report proposes a number of good measures to reduce unemployment, particularly among young people. however, i would like to point out that during this term of office we have already discussed a number of strategies and proposals to reduce unemployment. this includes the creation of green jobs and the promotion of youth employment and the problem of employment of certain social groups. if all these proposals were put into practice, rather than left on the table, i believe that the european union would already have achieved its 2010 targets in 2015. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's proposals, but i would also point out that, in particular, better coordination of the implementation of the measures already adopted is needed, both to reduce unemployment and to save money for other priorities.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and its member states and the kingdom of norway on cooperation in the field of satellite navigation, as this issue is of importance to both parties to the agreement. this decision will allow for the establishment and maintenance of better relations with the kingdom of norway, located in the western part of the scandinavian peninsula, which is considered to be one of the most successful examples of a prosperous capitalist state. the country is considered the world's third largest oil exporter after saudi arabia and russia, and, although it contributes heavily to the eu budget, it refuses to become a full member of the union. cooperation thus has a positive impact on the european union's economy and one of the main objectives is to further strengthen cooperation between the parties by supplementing the provisions of the agreement on satellite navigation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because of all the non-eu countries, the eu has the closest cooperation with norway in the implementation of the european gnss programmes galileo and egnos. as a member of the european space agency and an informal participant in the ec galileo management systems for many years, norway has contributed politically, technically and financially to all stages of galileo's implementation. this agreement formalises cooperation between norway and the european union in the field of satellite navigation. the agreement lays down general principles for cooperation and the rights and obligations of norway in the areas referred to above. the agreement is necessary because two important ground installations will be installed in norway to help ensure the proper functioning of the system. in this context, norway commits to support the future union policy aimed at protecting the european gnss.
in writing. − i believe that it is particularly appropriate and useful to conclude an agreement with the kingdom of norway on cooperation in the field of satellite navigation. in particular, as a member of the european space agency and through its long-standing informal involvement in the esa's galileo governance systems, norway has contributed politically, technically and financially to all stages of galileo's implementation. in addition, two important ground installations are planned in norway to help ensure the proper functioning of the system. in this context, norway commits to support the future union policy aimed at protecting the european gnss. it should be noted that the eu should formally establish close cooperation on all aspects of the european gnss programmes in order to ensure an adequate level of protection of the services provided.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament recommends that the council conclude an agreement between the european community and its member states and the united states of america on the promotion, supply and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and associated applications. one of the main objectives of this agreement is to establish a framework for cooperation between the parties in the promotion, provision and use of gps and galileo navigation and timing signals. gps signals are a public positioning system for a given object, managed by the us department of defence and made available free of charge to its member states, while galileo signals, managed by the eu, are competitors to gps signals, which are expected to improve the quality of the service of this navigation system, strengthening the economic stability of the european union. the other main objectives of the galileo programme are to facilitate the use of these signals, services and equipment for commercial, peaceful, civil and scientific purposes.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the agreement between the european union and the european community and its member states on the promotion, provision and use of galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and associated programmes is being concluded on behalf of the european union. gps and galileo, if their radio frequencies are coordinated and interoperate at user level, could increase the number of satellites visible from any location on earth and improve access to navigation signals for civilian users worldwide. i am convinced that cooperation is needed to achieve the full benefits of this important technology in all relevant application areas.
in writing. − i agree to the conclusion of this eu-us agreement on the promotion, provision and use of the galileo and gps satellite navigation systems and related programmes. i believe that close cooperation in this area is essential to ensure that the benefits of these important technologies are available in all relevant fields of application. it is noted that the agreement will ensure full compatibility and interoperability between the existing global navigation satellites and positioning systems. in addition, markets will be opened, trade growth will be encouraged, and users of satellite navigation systems and equipment suppliers will be given favourable opportunities to extend their services by ensuring compatibility of radio frequencies with existing systems and equipment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. as early as 1 april 1987, the commission decided that all acts which had been amended not more than ten times should be codified in order to make their provisions clear and easy to understand (all the acts governing a given area are combined into one document). this proposal will codify council directive 90/435/eec of 23 july 1990 on the common system of taxation applicable in the case of parent companies and subsidiaries of different member states, which will replace the various acts whose provisions were incorporated into it and will provide greater clarity for the parties concerned.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because social inequalities are increasing in europe and there is a need for concrete initiatives to tackle this phenomenon. individuals and companies are subject to different tax systems in each european union country. national tax bases are almost always illegal. to prevent this, the existing directive should be supplemented as soon as possible with stricter provisions to combat abuse. one of the main objectives of amending this directive is therefore to facilitate as far as possible the conditions for multinational mergers. to seek to limit the erosion of the tax base by eu companies and to apply minimum requirements to dividend income from subsidiaries established in third countries. another problem that will have to be solved in the future is double taxation. the commission has already put forward a proposal for a common consolidated corporate tax base, which already solves part of the problem. however, this measure can only be effective if the possibilities of avoiding corporate tax in the eu are limited in the future.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because, in the opinion of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, the proposal does not contain any substantive changes other than those mentioned and because, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the previous acts and of the amendments mentioned, the proposal seeks only to codify the existing texts without changing their substance.
in writing. − i support this resolution because a common eu tax system for parent companies and subsidiaries in different member states will facilitate multinational mergers. the tax obstacles faced by companies from different member states in comparison with companies from the same member state will also be removed. such legislation will thus protect national tax revenues and, in addition, prevent misuse and double taxation by the very stringent measures provided for in the directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the revision of the eu financial regulation. the regulation lays down the budgetary principles and financial rules governing the establishment and implementation of the general budget, ensures sound and efficient management, control and protection of the financial interests of the union and enhances the transparency to which all legislative acts must conform and which all institutions must observe. i believe that the draft regulation proposed by parliament duly simplifies and clarifies the eu's financial rules, taking account of the current circumstances of the eu and the challenges ahead, and also ensures greater transparency of the eu budget, improves its efficiency and effectiveness.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the 2002 council regulation on the financial regulation applicable to the general budget of the european communities has been substantially amended several times and now requires further amendments to take account of the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon. this regulation lays down the budgetary principles and financial rules applicable to the establishment and implementation of the general budget, ensuring sound and efficient management, control and the protection of the financial interests of the union, and enhancing the transparency to be observed in all legislative acts and to be complied with by all institutions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the agenda for new skills and jobs. the economic, financial and social crisis now affecting europe highlights the weaknesses of the european economic and social model. the draft adopted by the commission in november 2010 entitled ‘an agenda for new skills and jobs: a european contribution towards full employment’ is part of the europe 2020 strategy, representing the commission’s contribution towards achieving the member states’ ambitious goal of 75% employment for the 20-64 age group by 2020. in attaining this goal, the commission proposed action in four main areas: furthering labour market reform, updating people’s skills in line with labour market requirements through training programs, improving the quality of labour legislation and action to ensure labour market conditions. i support this proposal, which suggests several improvements; the reduction of administrative burdens and red tape for smes, measures to improve the work-life balance, the need to improve the directive on the temporary posting of workers, the need for further progress on the mutual recognition of qualifications as between the eu and third countries and closer cooperation between educational institutions and the world of business.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because in the europe 2020 strategy member states agreed to reach the employment target of 75% for the 20-64 age group by 2020, which is closely linked to economic growth and the sustainability of social protection systems and public finances. i believe that national measures to balance labour market flexibility and employment guarantees need to be revised in the light of new socioeconomic conditions. the need to stimulate labour demand and create jobs is urgent. i also believe that there is room for improvement, particularly in the following areas: reducing the administrative burden on smes and red tape to create jobs; better monitoring and forecasting of future skills needs, thus allowing for better matching with supply and targeting of skills development to ensure greater lifelong employment opportunities. take into account the need to strengthen the rules on the balance between labour market flexibility and employment guarantees and to adapt them to the social and economic conditions of each member state in order to ensure a flexible labour market, proactive labour market policies, lifelong learning and modern welfare systems; to pursue closer cooperation between educational institutions and business enterprises and similar measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the new skills and jobs agenda is one of the key drivers of progress, sustainable and inclusive growth, which ensures full employment and prosperity. it should be noted that in order to improve competitiveness and working and living conditions, it is necessary to develop and implement more effective employment, education and work organisation strategies at eu level. this will ensure the creation of decent jobs, and provide opportunities for lifelong learning, qualifications and skills development for all age groups. attention should be drawn to the need to involve employers more actively in the activities of educational establishments and to promote more active social dialogue throughout the eu. in order to respond promptly to the challenges facing the european labour market, i support the creation of a european employment observatory and the planned eu skills panorama. the key components of the balance between labour market flexibility and employment guarantees need to be revised and strengthened in order to achieve the objectives set.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it calls on eu member states to better coordinate their economic policies in order to create jobs and facilitate effective competition. throughout europe, there are various inequalities within employment policies. while maintaining budgetary discipline is crucial to avoid debt, spending cuts in areas such as education and the labour market would increase the shortage of skilled workers in europe. competitiveness and employment must be promoted to move towards a sustainable, stronger and greener economy. to improve competitiveness in the eu, as well as create new jobs, there must be better education and employment strategies. i support the rapporteur, who urges the eu to combat discrimination of any kind, whether based on gender, age or nationality, more effectively. the flexicurity arrangements that exist must be strengthened and adapted to each member state. member states must improve workers' rights. even at a time of economic problems, social and unemployment protection can not be sacrificed. additionally, member states should help workers integrate their jobs and their family life. innovation is necessary to further boost employment. pursuing full employment must go hand-in-hand with improving working conditions.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, lithuania's youth unemployment rate (34%) is one of the highest in the eu. only greece and spain have higher rates. one of the reasons for this unjustifiably high rate is the incompatibility between the requirements of the labour market and the qualifications of young people. last year, 52% of all young unemployed people who registered at the labour exchange had no vocational training. the best way to combat unemployment is still through vocational training and education. according to this report, improving workers' knowledge and skills in line with labour market requirements will increase employability and help europe recover in the long term. the labour market needs to be further restructured to provide greater flexibility and security in the labour market. eu governments, including mine, should do more to provide businesses with the right incentives to invest in training. in my view, the area requiring more attention is longterm unemployment. according to the second quarter of 2011, 52% of registered unemployed in lithuania have been looking for work for a year or more. the new jobs and skills agenda should target this group.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank all the participants in this debate. what can i say? i am greatly invigorated by the comments that i have heard from all sides of this chamber and i can say that at present we are finalising the communication that will be presented to the european parliament and to the council – unless we find unexpected hitches – on 17 november. i hope that will lead to a creative debate and a concrete plan of action that will see us fight and reduce antimicrobial resistance. basically – and i am not going to repeat the various comments that have been made in this house – the issue is prudent use and research. prudent use in the human health sphere, both through the discipline of practitioners in prescribing (and i totally agree that we have to move to prescription-only antibiotics) and in the case of patients, who have to be educated in how to use antibiotic medicines. the misuse of antibiotics, even if prescribed, can lead to a continuation of this hazard. concerning animal husbandry, i believe that we are realising that this is a key issue and that the abuse of antibiotics in veterinary medicinal products and medicated feed is one cause of the problems that we are facing today. therefore i believe that concrete action in this regard is also going to be called for. concerning research, what i can say is that the commission is fully committed to exploring, with all relevant stakeholders, how to ensure the development of new effective antimicrobials, stimulate antimicrobial development and promote and support research and innovation in this area. we are already in preliminary discussions on this issue, and i hope that we can pull together all european resources to really concentrate and focus on fighting this and creating new medicines as new antibiotics. but i have to remind this house – and i have to remind everybody – that creating new molecules, new medicine, is not the solution. it is the appropriate use of antibiotics that is the solution to this problem.
acting president of the council. - mr president! - what are you doing? members of the european parliament! thank you very much for a very productive discussion on antibiotic resistance. antibiotic resistance affects all microorganisms and all antibiotics, but the most dangerous is a group called the alarm pathogens. therefore, all possible measures should be taken to ensure that the activity of the antibiotics available today is maintained for as long as possible. i agree with mrs grossetête, the ppe member, who believes that controlling the use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine and medicine is one of the most important steps and actions in reducing the problem of drug resistance. i also agree with what mrs mcavan, the socialist member, said, and with what mr skylakakis, the liberal member, said, and with what mr wojciechowski, the conservative member, said, about the poor conditions of production on large-scale industrial farms. the other statements you have made also build a strategy, show the way forward and are undoubtedly the basis for further action by the council, i think, and by the european commission. ladies and gentlemen! member states should strengthen the cross-sectoral mechanism for coordinating the implementation of the national strategy for the prevention and spread of antimicrobial resistant strains of bacteria, as well as the exchange of information and coordination with the european commission, the european centre for disease prevention and control and other member states. further coordination of the work of laboratories monitoring infections with drug-resistant bacteria and the creation of a platform for the exchange and processing of monitoring data is also necessary. to this end, it is necessary to establish a european network of reference laboratories for monitoring antibiotic resistance and conducting molecular typing for epidemiological purposes. ladies and gentlemen! the intensification of basic research on drug resistance, cooperation between basic and reference laboratories and continuous training of doctors and allied professionals in rational antibiotic therapy and infection control are of great importance. given the importance of the situation, action within the european union should take place at several different levels, such as: monitored intensification of infections with resistant bacteria and consumption of antibiotics, testing of reservoirs of resistance in humans and farmed animals in the natural environment, development of basic research, educational activities among those involved in medicine and the general public. in conclusion, i am confident that the danish presidency will enable a serious and in-depth discussion on this subject and that the solutions it proposes will take the form of council conclusions and be adopted at the health ministers' meeting in june 2012. we are waiting for the very important document announced by commissioner dalli, which will also be the basis for further intensive work for the good of society as a whole.
in writing. the rapid growth of bacterial resistance to antimicrobials is a real concern. this is clearly illustrated by the fact that at least 25 000 patients die every year in the eu from infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria and that the eu suffers additional healthcare costs and losses of around eur 1.5 billion every year as a result of infections caused by these bacteria. there is a clear need for a set of measures to address antimicrobial resistance, including strengthening the monitoring and control of the use of authorised antimicrobials in humans and animals, increasing the incentives to seek new antimicrobials and reducing the likelihood of the spread of antimicrobial resistance from animals to humans through the food chain or through direct contact. this is clearly a transnational phenomenon and, while acknowledging this concern about antimicrobial use, i would like to highlight the many shortcomings and gaps in the promotion of prudent antimicrobial use identified in the latest eurobarometer survey and encourage the european commission to examine trends in the misuse of antimicrobials and to come forward as soon as possible with a legislative package to combat antimicrobial resistance that would encourage initiatives for responsible use and adequate consumer information.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the qualification and status of third country nationals or stateless persons as beneficiaries of international protection. the proposal from the commission for the recast of the original directive forms part of the move towards a common european asylum policy by 2012. after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the parliament is now in a position of co-decision. the existing directive has two key elements: the grounds on which someone qualifies for refugee status or subsidiary protection, and the content of that protection. it is clear that there are considerable variations in practice between member states in their implementation of the current directive. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for clarification in the legislative framework - the directive itself - to provide a clearer framework for the implementation process. i support this proposal, which aims to approximate the two categories of protection more closely and thus to generally refer to beneficiaries of international protection. the proposal also aims to ‘approximate the entitlements of the content of protection more closely’: access to the labour market is perhaps the most significant.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the directive on beneficiaries of international protection should be further developed, which is the main objective of this report. the monitoring of the application of the directive in the member states has revealed considerable differences and, while some of the identified shortcomings can be addressed by encouraging closer cooperation between member states, there is also a need for greater clarity in the legal framework. the main amendments proposed by the european parliament are to bring the two different categories of beneficiaries of protection, which have different rights related to the nature of the protection, closer together. however, in the areas of social security, integration measures and residence permits, member states will be able to continue to apply different regimes to people falling within these two categories of protection. the amendments to the directive also aim to clarify the concept of the best interests of the child by providing a set of guiding principles. another important issue addressed by the amendments during the examination of the document concerned the protection providers. the european parliament strongly advocated that only states could be considered as providers of protection, since international organisations do not have the characteristics of a state.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the important amendment proposed here is to bring the two categories of protection closer together and thus to speak in general about beneficiaries of international protection. this will allow implementing authorities to be reminded that the two categories of protection are complementary: the additional protection is no less important for persons who are at risk of serious harm if they return to their country of origin. the proposal also aims to bring closer protection-related rights, of which access to the labour market is perhaps the most important. most member states no longer differentiate between the two groups. however, these groups may continue to be treated differently in the following areas: social security, integration measures and residence permits, although some progress has been made in the latter (for holders of supplementary protection status, the extension of the permit after one year must be for at least two years, several member states currently apply such a distinction). the european parliament considered that this was important in order to integrate the individual and to ensure that he or she felt more stable.
in writing. - i voted yes. i believe that the trialogue reached the right compromise on the amendments to the directive. it was necessary to clarify certain elements of the directive in order to eliminate the duplication of provisions of the directive which has led to the divergent application of its provisions in the member states. the rapporteur has successfully achieved many of the objectives set, and i congratulate her on that. the eu has set itself the objective of creating a common area of protection and solidarity by 2012, based on a common asylum procedure and a uniform status for persons granted international protection. the so-called qualifications directive is one of the five key pieces of legislation that make up the first stage of the common asylum system (ceas). while there is no doubt that effectiveness in this area can only be achieved by acting at european union level, i believe it is necessary to leave to the member states all the means to deter, investigate and defend themselves against possible abuses of the european asylum system.

in writing. − i support this resolution as it is appropriate to refer the matter to the court of justice for an opinion on the matter in question, as the eu-australia agreement on the processing and transfer of passenger name record data by air carriers to the australian customs and border protection agency raises legal uncertainty. in particular, the proper implementation of the agreement in both the eu and australia requires that the provisions of the agreement, in particular those relating to passenger data, comply with the requirements of the eu data protection legislation and are compatible with the provisions of the eu treaties. it is essential that the condominium agreement establishes and applies strict conditions for the transfer and use of pnr data, as well as conditions governing data protection. it is also necessary to ensure legal certainty for air carriers, passengers and data protection authorities, while guaranteeing the protection of citizens' privacy and physical security.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is of the utmost importance to reach an agreement as soon as possible between the european union and australia on the issue of passenger name record (pnr) by carriers. pnr is a data collection, processing and transmission system for travel by air or other public transport where passenger data is recorded for the purpose of ticketing, reservation and registration by the carrier. the current agreement is based on australian border protection laws and one of the main objectives of this eu-australia agreement would be to align the transfer of passenger data with the personal data protection laws in force in europe. the conclusion of this agreement would not only facilitate the transfer of passenger data to carriers, but would also centralise the analysis of pnr data and ensure the protection of passenger data.
in writing. − the european union is negotiating three international agreements with australia, canada and the usa on the processing and transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data by air carriers. pnr data are provided by passengers and collected by air carriers and used by them in their ticketing, reservation and registration systems. given the commercial nature of the pnr, this data includes several types of information, ranging from names, addresses, passport numbers and credit card information to information on other passengers, travel itineraries and travel agents. as airlines comply with these australian requirements, problems arise with european data protection laws. in order to address these concerns, the commission has entered into negotiations with australia to establish the conditions under which access to pnr data is granted. i abstained in voting in favour of this document because we have to decide whether we are in favour of the collection of personal data, i.e. names, flights, passport details, credit card details, because there is no 100% guarantee as to what they will be used for. i believe that the need for mass collection and storage of pnr data must be demonstrated, based on factual evidence for each of the purposes for which it is published. the proportionality of the measure must be demonstrated (i.e. it must be demonstrated that the same objective cannot be achieved by less dissuasive means). the objective must be clearly and strictly defined on the basis of clear legal and reasoned definitions.
in writing. − the processing of pnr data involves the processing of personal data, which raises serious questions about the fundamental rights to privacy and the protection of personal data. it is therefore necessary to ensure that the comprehensive storage and processing of pnr data for all passengers ensures high data protection safeguards and respect for the privacy of eu citizens in accordance with the relevant eu rules. in this context, both existing and future eu agreements require legal certainty and objective factual evidence to support the assertion that the storage and processing of pnr data is necessary and proportionate. in addition, appropriate legal safeguards must be included, including provisions on the use of pnr data for law enforcement and security purposes only and the prevention of the use of data for data mining and classification.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that it is necessary to develop new and better antimicrobials and at the same time to improve the conservation of existing antibiotic stocks. each year, around 25 000 patients die in the european union from diseases caused by drug-resistant microorganisms, resulting in at least eur 1.5 billion in additional healthcare costs. people take antimicrobials (medicines that inhibit the growth and reproduction of microorganisms) because they can kill bacteria, viruses and other microorganisms, but improper and irrational use of these drugs kills vital human cells and suppresses the resistance of the immune system. indeed, the use of antimicrobials in food-producing animals and their feedingstuffs is a major factor in the spread of these substances through food, which may weaken the antibacterial effects of medicinal products used in the future. antimicrobial resistance is a growing public health threat not only in europe but also worldwide.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it is a matter of concern that, despite the actions taken at european and international level, antimicrobial resistance is a growing public health threat in europe and worldwide. i believe that the fight against antimicrobial resistance in human medicines needs to be stepped up, focusing on the following priorities in order of importance: prudent use of antimicrobials in humans and animals, ensuring that they are used only for effective treatment of diseases, with appropriate doses, intervals and duration; monitoring and control of antimicrobial resistance; the need for research and development of new antimicrobials and their substitutes; and links with measures to combat antimicrobial resistance in veterinary medicines, animal feed and plant feed. the commission is invited to propose without delay a legislative framework to combat amr by promoting initiatives on responsible use and supporting the dissemination of such initiatives and information.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the world is facing an increase in antimicrobial resistance, which affects not only humans but also animals. this is a consequence of frequent or inappropriate use of antibiotics and is a very serious problem requiring a coordinated solution at eu level. only by working together can we prevent infections from spreading and reduce the need for antibiotics. the pharmaceutical innovation sector is currently dominated by a patent-oriented r&d model, which has led to market failures and a decline in r&d. in this context, there is a need for eu-wide innovation incentive premiums or other measures to boost investment in research. we also need to ensure that antimicrobials are used strictly and only when necessary. the increasing antimicrobial resistance is leading to a decline in the effectiveness of antimicrobial treatment, increased morbidity and mortality, and rising healthcare costs. in order to achieve the objectives effectively and as rapidly as possible, an integrated system for the monitoring of antimicrobial resistance and its use in europe should be established to prevent threats to human health.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i share the concern about the rise in antimicrobial resistance in pathogens. the misuse, unnecessary and often ineffective use of antimicrobials and antibiotics in human or animal health care leads to the emergence of antimicrobial resistant bacteria. this is how we're building a time bomb that can take us back to a time before antibiotics. at that time, a simple cold could have resulted in death. i support the call for increased funding for the development of new antibiotics. but the most important thing is to educate the public about the problems that arise from the misuse of antimicrobials at the wrong time and for the wrong purpose. i would particularly urge a change in the established practice in animal husbandry, where antibiotics are now used as a preventive measure rather than a therapeutic one. the prevention of disease is better achieved by improving animal housing conditions rather than by feeding animals medicines. certain types of antimicrobials for which no possible substitute has yet been identified should be completely banned for use in animal husbandry.

in writing. − currently, air services between the eu and jordan are provided under bilateral agreements between individual member states and jordan. the european commission has recently negotiated a comprehensive and much more ambitious agreement, replacing all bilateral agreements and creating a euro-mediterranean airspace between the eu and jordan. this agreement establishes uniform standards for air carriers in all 27 member states of the union and allows these carriers to operate them, irrespective of their country of origin. accordingly, eu air carriers will be able to provide air services between all points in the eu and jordan, which have been subject to various conditions until now. i have endorsed this document as the conclusion of a euro-mediterranean aviation agreement with jordan has long been an eu priority and an important step in the development of the european neighbourhood policy. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with jordan was signed on the basis of the agreements with ryanair and ams, which were signed on the basis of the agreements with ryanair and ams.

in writing. − the kingdom of spain has requested, on behalf of the autonomous community of the canary islands, the temporary suspension of the application of the common customs tariff to certain industrial goods imported into the canary islands in order to strengthen the competitiveness of local economic operators and to ensure more stable employment in these outermost regions of the union. to ensure that imports of goods raw materials, parts, components or non-tariffed means of production do not distort competition, they will be subject to end-use control. this will ensure that they are used only by local businesses operating on the islands. the local companies operating on the islands will have to use the production facilities for at least two years before they can sell them freely to companies operating elsewhere in the union. in addition, those wishing to benefit from the temporary exemption will have to use the raw materials, parts and components for the processing and preservation of the industry in the canary islands. it is not possible to carry out an impact assessment of these measures as they are part of a number of other measures to address the specific problems of these islands. however, these measures will have an impact on the union's own resources and revenue. i have endorsed this document because, in the context of the current economic downturn, it is considered that the need for concrete measures to stimulate economic activity and stabilise employment in the medium term is compatible with the european economic recovery plan and the measures needed to address the specific problems of the outermost regions of the union.

in writing. − the persisting disparities between national insolvency laws create difficulties for companies with cross-border activities and are an obstacle to a successful restructuring of insolvent companies am fully in favour of this report which identifies areas in national insolvency laws that are accessible and eligible for harmonization and issues that should be revised in the insolvency regulation. i am in favour of this report which invites the commission to incorporate the following recommendations into future legislative proposals on an eu corporate insolvency framework: harmonise the opening of insolvency proceedings, revise the insolvency regulation with regard to its scope and certain definitions ( e.g. ‘centre of main interest’, ‘establishment’ in the context of secondary proceedings) and make the communication between the relevant courts obligatory, improve the cooperation of liquidators and cooperation in general on administrative level in cases where enterprises that are part of a group of companies become insolvent and create of an eu registry for insolvency case.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that we need to create the best possible legal environment for business and to eliminate the shortcomings that are hampering competitiveness in the european union. indeed, differences in national insolvency laws create difficulties for companies operating in several countries and may hinder the successful restructuring of insolvent companies. in this document, the european parliament sets out its recommendations on areas of insolvency law that could be harmonised at eu level and which could help to prepare future legislative initiatives in this area. the parliament therefore proposes to harmonise certain aspects of the opening of insolvency proceedings, including the procedure for the lodging of claims, the harmonisation of the aspects of actions for annulment, the qualification and working conditions of liquidators and the drawing up of restructuring plans. the european parliament also proposed the creation of an eu insolvency register listing all insolvency cases opened cross-border and making the transmission of data to the courts mandatory.
in writing. − i supported this proposal because differences in national insolvency laws create competitive advantages or disadvantages and difficulties for companies operating in several countries and can hinder the successful restructuring of insolvent companies. these discrepancies allow for the search for a more favourable legal position. i believe that the internal market would benefit from a level playing field for all businesses and from no distortion of competition. the commission is therefore invited to submit to parliament one or more legislative proposals on the eu corporate insolvency legal framework in accordance with the detailed guidelines set out in the annex to this proposal, in order to ensure a level playing field, on the basis of a detailed analysis of all possible alternatives.
in writing. - i support this resolution because the differences in national rules place many firms in an unequal competitive position and make it difficult for them to operate. in addition, the restructuring of insolvent companies is made more difficult. it should be noted that a common and effective insolvency system is a very important market economy instrument. it not only helps to preserve business and production capacity, but also promotes change, redistribution of operational resources and plays a crucial role in credit and investment. i therefore believe that the insolvency system should function as a common tool in the european crisis management system. in this context, it is necessary to harmonise at eu level the conditions under which insolvency proceedings and claims may be brought, as well as certain aspects of actions for annulment and other claims. only through these measures will an effective competitive environment be created for business operators and the possibility be created for them to survive in the face of temporary financial difficulties.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report which depicts how demographic change clearly impacts the provision of social infrastructure, such as pension systems, nursing care and healthcare and calls for proactive measures to prevent its negative consequences. demographic change is producing new challenges in many regions of the eu. as demographic change can bring both risks and opportunities, it is imperative that each region has its own strategy. as such members call on the commission to include demographic change as a horizontal objective in the future cohesion policy and also encourages the regions to use structural funds to help address demographic challenges and to improve access to social and administrative services. as europe will, for demographic reasons, remain dependent on migration for skilled labour, this report calls for member states to recognise the integration of migrants as a strategically important policy measure. it also believes that the regions should use esf funds in a decisive manner to combat youth unemployment by supporting training measures for young people, while continuing support to raise the female employment rate. lastly, the report considers that demographic developments in the regions should be statistically measured, so that data can be evaluated at european level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because demographic change will bring new challenges for many regions of the european union. not all eu regions have yet realised the threat of demographic change, but they must now realise that each region and city needs its own strategy. in principle, such strategies are the responsibility of the member states, but the regions themselves must also take the initiative, and at the same time they must develop guidelines and outline future prospects. demographic change, in particular population ageing, has an undeniable impact on the provision of social infrastructure services such as pension systems, care and healthcare, and regional authorities need to respond to the changing needs of different population groups. moreover, the impact of demographic change varies widely across regions, depending on whether it is rapid or slow, whether people are migrating to or from a region, and therefore requires different strategic adaptation plans for regions and therefore needs to be managed in a coordinated manner by all eu, national and regional authorities. it should also be noted that regions with declining populations, especially in rural areas, define quality of life differently from regions with growing populations, and therefore require different strategic support plans for the regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the european union is undergoing demographic change and one of the main challenges for the future is to find a way to deal with its consequences. europe is an ageing society, with the oldest population and the lowest population growth rates in the world. in most member states, fertility rates are below the level needed to maintain the current population, and in some cases even fall further, and life expectancy is increasing. demographic change is rightly seen as the major trend of the 21st century, which will fundamentally change the political, social, societal and economic landscape in europe. the problem is not demographic change itself, but the delay in responding to it by politicians and society. the multifaceted demographic challenges are primarily the responsibility of the member states, but the regions must also play an active role in this area and therefore need to be supported at european level. the erdf and the esf can contribute to addressing the challenges posed by demographic change in the eu, namely the increase in the number of older people and the decline in the number of young people. if we can shape demographic change and find the right responses not only at european, but also at national and regional levels, it will be an opportunity for europe, not a threat.
in writing. − i support this resolution because europe is currently undergoing demographic changes of unprecedented scale and with certain risks, especially in cohesion policy. in this context, i believe that structural policy reforms must be actively implemented at eu level. in particular, the allocation of eu structural funds should take account of the level of development of each region and other demographic indicators. the erdf and esf must provide more funding for urban and infrastructure development. it should be noted that the commission has a special role to play in this area, as it must ensure that the effects of demographic change are managed in an effective and coordinated manner. in addition, in view of the increasing problem of ageing populations, pension systems need to be strengthened, generational cohesion promoted and high quality care and nursing at home ensured.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased that the report addresses demographic issues, but more attention should be paid to those challenges that affect rural and urban areas. one third of lithuania's population lives in rural areas. at the same time, young people are emigrating and rural populations are ageing - one in four rural residents is over 60. the statistics are alarming. the rural birth rate is 30% higher than in the cities, but this percentage is decreasing every year, and the mortality rate in rural areas is very high (75% higher than in the cities). this has a negative impact on natural population growth. demographic change also highlights differences in the quality of life of those living in rural areas and those living in cities. children, farmers and the elderly are the most affected by demographic change in lithuania. lithuanian rural residents are at risk of poverty three times more often than those living in large cities. i agree with the rapporteur that the eu structural funds should be better adapted to the challenges of demographic change. for example, low-interest loans from the erdf would greatly help the rural poor in lithuania.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because, in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, to improve the conditions under which it operates, particularly in financial markets, and to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection, a common framework for the regulation of requirements and powers relating to the sale of debt securities and credit default swaps should be established and better coordination and consistency between member states should be ensured. it is therefore proposed to provide for provisions in the form of a legal regulation to ensure that provisions directly imposing obligations on private parties to provide and disclose information on net short positions in relation to certain instruments and not to agree to sell securities on borrowing are applied uniformly throughout the european union. the regulation is also necessary to empower the authority to coordinate the measures taken by the competent authorities or to take those measures itself.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report, which welcomes the commission proposal to update the legal framework for european statistics on permanent crops, in line with current user and market requirements. the report stresses the objective of achieving simplification and recognises the efforts made by the commission to reduce the administrative burden on respondents and ensure that statistical data on permanent crops provide a reliable basis for taking judicious decisions in relation to production and the european market. the report indicates that the administrative burden may be reduced by amending the precision requirements, excluding from the scope of the provisions all small holdings of less than 0.2 hectares, and no longer requiring a breakdown by nuts 3 region for certain data on vines for purposes other than the production of table grapes. with regard to the delegation of power to the commission to amend certain aspects of this regulation through delegated acts, the rapporteur stresses that the principles laid down in parliament’s resolution of 5 may 2010 on the power of legislative delegation (2010/2021(ini)) must be strictly applied.

in writing. − under the euratom treaty, research programmes may not exceed five years. the current euratom seventh framework programme (2007-2011), which consists of two specific programmes (one for indirect actions and one for direct actions of the jrc), will run until the end of 2011. the proposal for a council decision extending the specific programme of direct actions for 2012-13 as requested is attached to this memorandum. i have endorsed this document because the main objective is to ensure that eu-funded research in these areas continues for another two years after the end of the 2007-2011 programme period. to this end, the proposal sets out in detail the objectives of research and technological development. this specific programme of direct actions identifies three thematic priorities: nuclear waste management, environmental impact and basic knowledge, nuclear safety and nuclear security control measures and nuclear security. i therefore believe that it is necessary to continue this programme.

in writing. − professional mobility is a key factor for economic development and sustainable economic recovery. however, one of the main reasons for difficulties in relation to the recognition of professional qualifications is a lack of confidence in the criteria used for accreditation and granting academic qualifications in the country of origin. so there is an urgent need to establish automatic recognition measures by removing prejudice and formal national obstacles to recognition. while the automatic recognition procedure has been successful, the recognition process under the general system based on professional experience is excessively time-consuming both for the competent authorities and for professionals. i am in favour of this report, which calls for simplification, a reduction in the duration of procedures through the use of modern communication technologies, the centralisation of information and the clarification of definitions. it also urges that the classification of economic activities be upgraded in line with scientific and technical developments, and that public health and safety be improved through the introduction of a proactive alert mechanism and through restrictions on the principle of partial access in relation to health professions. it underlines the importance of language skills, of integrating professionals and of injecting confidence into the system through the mandatory introduction of the internal market information (imi) system, and it calls for the introduction of a voluntary professional card.
in writing. − the changing demographic situation will make the mobility of professionals in the european union increasingly important. the mobility of professionals is a key factor in restoring economic development and a sustainable economy. based on the findings of the european centre for the development of vocational training (cedefop), the demand for highly qualified workers is expected to grow in the european union between now and 2020, creating more than 16 million jobs, and the rules for the recognition of professional qualifications need to be made more transparent, simpler and more flexible. one of the main reasons for the difficulties in the recognition of academic titles and professional qualifications is the lack of confidence in the criteria for accreditation and award of degrees in the country of origin, which requires the urgent introduction of automatic recognition measures by removing formal national barriers to recognition and abandoning the prior negative opinion. i support the call to lay the foundations for an ambitious system of recognition of the professional qualifications of all workers, with the aim of enabling workers to obtain all or some of the certificates (diploma, certificate of completion of vocational training or certificate of professional qualification) in the light of their professional experience, to be assessed by the commission for the recognition of acquired knowledge and competences.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because highly qualified workers still face obstacles to finding employment in another eu member state. the european parliament therefore proposes the creation of a voluntary european professional certificate attesting academic and professional experience. this certificate could be a useful tool to promote the mobility of certain professionals, simplify administrative procedures and increase worker safety. the european parliament also calls on the member states, the competent authorities and the commission to ensure that diplomas and certificates are recognised on the same basis as professional qualifications, in order to create a genuine single market at european and international level and to avoid regulating what is already regulated. member states, competent authorities and the commission should ensure greater transparency so that the person making the request or receiving a negative reply receives a full explanation of the reasons for the non-recognition of his or her diploma or professional qualification. thus, all workers must be provided with information both about their rights and about the procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications in order to ensure the rights of all workers and to prevent their exploitation.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as one of the main reasons for the difficulties in the recognition of academic titles and professional qualifications is the lack of confidence in the criteria for accreditation and award of degrees in the country of origin, and the urgent need to introduce automatic recognition measures by removing formal national barriers to recognition and abandoning the negative prior opinion. the increasing free movement of highly qualified persons and workers is one of the greatest advantages of european cooperation and a competitive internal market, a vital factor in the economic development of the eu as a whole and a right of all eu citizens. i believe that the mobility of workers who are eu citizens should be encouraged and that indirect barriers should be removed, provided that the balance between mobility and the quality of professional qualifications is maintained and that any potential outflow of minds from the member states is prevented.
in writing. − the proposals set out in the communication aim to address the problems and shortcomings identified in the recognition of professional qualifications since 2005, when the directive on the full implementation of the right to take up employment or to provide services in another member state, as enshrined in the treaties, entered into force. this requires simplification of regulation, increased availability of information, increased coordination and trust in the system. on the other hand, a balance must be struck between the right to employment and the rights of consumers, including patients. i hope that the ep's proposals will be duly reflected in the commission's legislative proposal. we need to ensure that everyone who is entitled to it can benefit from the not too complex, flexible and accessible system of recognition of qualifications that professionals across the eu expect from us. healthcare professionals are the most mobile in the eu (around 57 200 professional qualifications for healthcare professionals were recognised in 2007-2010). of the 800 regulated qualifications, 43% are in the healthcare system and 9% in the social sector, including education. countries such as lithuania, which have been experiencing negative trends in the emigration of highly qualified professionals for several years, should reform the most sensitive sectors accordingly. studies show that most professionals would prefer to work in the country of qualification, even for relatively lower pay, if there were sufficient opportunities to obtain a job after graduation in the field of their specialty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential to take effective measures at eu level to simplify the process of recognition of professional qualifications and to ensure the proper implementation of the freedom of movement of persons and the freedom to provide services. the envisaged automatic recognition measures will remove the current formal national barriers to recognition and will open the way to a competitive internal market. this will create favourable conditions for promoting the mobility of professionals, since the refusal to recognise qualifications acquired in another member state is often one of the main obstacles to the free movement of services and persons. furthermore, the implementation of the provisions of the directive will ensure confidence between member states in the criteria for accreditation and award of degrees in the country of origin.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, this report proposes to simplify the system to make it easier for doctors to work in the eu. i agree with the rapporteur that this would stimulate economic growth and provide flexibility for the labour market, but this should be done without creating serious labour shortages in countries such as lithuania. according to a lithuanian report published earlier this year, the percentage of doctors and nurses in lithuania per 10 000 inhabitants is one of the highest in europe. however, to visit a doctor, especially a specialist, the average lithuanian has to wait several weeks or longer for a ticket. this is because lithuania has one of the largest numbers of doctors migrating within the eu. the most worrying aspect is that many of the young, talented narrowly specialised doctors, such as interventional cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, and vascular surgeons, are emigrating. last year, doctors' salaries were cut three times, cutting some specialists' salaries by several thousand litas. according to the lithuanian medical association, half of medical students go to germany, the united kingdom, and scandinavia to look for work. we need to provide more incentives to stop doctors from migrating.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report through which the european parliament welcomes the consumer agenda, to be set by the commission by may 2012 which will include all initiatives for consumers, emphasizing the need for the proper implementation and enforcement of existing legislation (in particular the latest consumer rights directive). this report indicates how the agenda must ensure safe food, health and product safety as well as aiming to lower inequalities between consumers in europe, how it can contribute to a low carbon economy as decided in the eu 2020 strategy and how it must protect children from advertising. it must also address globalisation of our markets, the digitalisation of the economy and ageing population as well as the importance of enforcement/redress instruments and support to consumer organisations. this report invites the commission to propose ‘consumer friendly’ legislation and, together with ms, to provide adequate support and capacity building to consumer organisations, with a view to strengthen their role and means thereby enhancing consumer empowerment.
