in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the need to increase consumer protection while ensuring the free movement of services and goods. the consumer agenda should cover all relevant topics and issues faced in the field of consumer affairs. ensuring food safety, health and product safety should be the top priority of the consumer agenda. consumer information is an essential and important tool in all financial services sectors. in particular, protection should be provided to vulnerable categories of persons who are considered as such because of their mental, physical or psychological disability, age or vulnerability, such as children, adolescents, elderly people, or certain persons who are vulnerable because of their social and financial situation (e.g. those with excessive debts). it is therefore essential to inform consumers of their rights and obligations and to ensure that consumers' rights are fully respected when using the internet and by protecting intellectual property rights, while protecting personal data and privacy. in order to implement consumer rights, the commission should continue to support and draw attention to the work of the european consumer centres, which play a key role in informing consumers about their rights.
in writing. - i agree with the view that consumers must be empowered. consumer empowerment depends on their knowledge of consumer rights and information, on the existence of well-known and effective non-governmental organisations and public institutions, on active media and on simple and accessible redress mechanisms. ensuring food safety, health and product safety should be the top priority of the consumer agenda. but we also need a consumer agenda that reduces inequalities between european consumers, contributes to a low-carbon economy as decided in the europe 2020 strategy and protects children from advertising. more broadly, new challenges facing modern societies such as the globalisation of our markets, the digitalisation of the economy, an ageing society need to be addressed, and the importance of enforcement and redress mechanisms and support for consumer organisations need to be incorporated. finally, a strong representation of consumer interests is an integral part of a strong civil society. it is necessary to ensure that such representation is possible and promoted not only at eu level but also at national level in all member states. many years after joining the eu, this is not the case in all our countries, so measures to strengthen consumer mobility are inevitably needed in these countries.
in writing. − the consumer is the essential pillar of the single market. however, unconsciously promoted consumption is destructive both economically and environmentally, and ultimately violates the rights of consumers themselves. the new eu consumer strategy should promote responsible and sustainable consumption. this requires greater attention to consumer awareness, the provision of useful, accurate and understandable information, clear labelling, and the dissemination of knowledge about consumer rights. much remains to be done to ensure consumer rights and protection in the financial services, e-commerce and energy sectors. there must be a system of dispute resolution and redress, protection of minors from misleading advertising and consumer rights for vulnerable groups elderly people, people with low incomes, people with disabilities, children and women and migrants. further research is needed on the health effects of chemicals, nanotechnologies and antibiotics used in the food, cosmetics and other industries on consumers. these and other proposals set out in the report will help to create a consumer culture in the eu, so that a generation of consumers is born who are aware of their rights, who know how to defend them, who use them responsibly, who do not waste resources, who do not exploit them, who try to contribute as little as possible to environmental damage. this will, in turn, encourage producers of goods and service providers to take more account of consumer expectations.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report, which considers the growing economic importance of the online gambling industry and through which members welcome the commission’s initiative to launch public consultation in connection with its green paper on online betting and gambling. the report indicates that efficient regulation of the online gambling sector must combat illegal gambling by strengthening technical and legal instruments for identifying and penalising illegal operators; guarantee effective protection for gamblers; preclude risks of gambling addiction; guarantee the integrity of sporting competition; ensure that part of the value of bets goes to sports and horse-racing bodies; ensure that a considerable proportion of government revenue from gambling is used for publicly beneficial and charitable purposes; and ensure that gaming is kept free from crime, fraud and any form of money laundering. although we reject any european legislative act uniformly regulating the entire gambling sector, we nonetheless take the view that, in some areas – given the cross-border nature of online gambling services – there would be clear added value from a coordinated european approach in addition to national regulation. we also believe that a pan-european code of conduct for online gambling should address the rights and obligations of both service providers and consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the online gambling sector is constantly growing and some aspects of this growth are not controlled by national governments, which poses risks to consumer protection and organised crime. although gambling services are covered by various eu legislation, such as the audiovisual media services directive, the unfair commercial practices directive, the distance selling directive, the anti-money laundering directive, the data protection directive, the privacy and electronic communications directive and the directive on a common value added tax system, there is no specific european legislation in the eu to regulate online gambling. different regulation of the sector in the member states makes it difficult for regulated service providers to provide legal cross-border gambling services, while regulators have to protect consumers and combat illegal gambling. i agree that in order to protect consumers, especially vulnerable and young players, from the negative aspects of online gambling, the eu needs to adopt common consumer protection standards and ensure that eu-wide principles are established for online gambling.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is essential to limit the growth of the online gambling sector, to strengthen the protection of minors from online gaming, and to combat money laundering and other gambling-related crimes. at present, there is no specific european legislation regulating online gambling in the european union, and the online gambling sector is growing and the market is worth more than eur 10 billion. it is noteworthy that more and more people are suffering from the risks of addiction, fraud, deception and underage gambling. excessive online gambling can lead to mental disorders that can take over a person's life and force him to give up many important work, social, family and material obligations. in order to reduce the number of legal and illegal gambling in europe, it is necessary to adopt uniform laws for all member states concerning gambling licences and their regulation.
in writing. − the online gambling sector is growing steadily. currently, around 10% of all gambling in europe takes place online or through similar distribution channels. the increasing supply and the growing number of players in this field make the fragmentation of the current european market more and more apparent. in many member states, online gambling is banned altogether or with certain restrictions, while in others the market is fully open and liberalised. however, the very different traditions in this sector make the principle of subsidiarity particularly important. member states are largely free to decide how to regulate their gambling sector. however, such a wide variation in regulation on the internet also distorts the market. gambling service providers from member states with an open market and low tax rates are also available in countries where online gambling is prohibited or compete with licensed online gambling service providers. the latter, like the providers of gambling services in the real world, are hardly competitive in these countries. there is also a large unregulated black market online. i agree that an independent and strong national regulatory authority is necessary to ensure that the online gambling market is open and orderly. it must establish and implement the general conditions for gambling. national regulatory authorities should therefore be given the necessary powers to punish infringements and to take action against illegal service providers.
in writing. − we recently discussed in the european parliament the issue of more active action to properly regulate online gambling, and today we have already expressed a stronger position. it is worth noting that the online gambling sector is constantly growing. according to the latest figures, about 10% of all gambling in europe is now online. the market size is over eur 10 billion. these trends have also given rise to related problems, such as the risks of gambling addiction. the social group of minors - young players and other socially sensitive sections of society - is particularly vulnerable. studies show that since the advent of online gambling, there has been a marked increase in the number of people who seek help from gambling-addicted centres. compulsive gambling has been identified as a behavioral disorder that affects up to 2 percent of the population in some countries. so while we are talking about public health, we should not forget the specifics of online gambling. online gambling is also often associated with criminal activity, fraud. the cross-border nature of the internet means that these games are not hindered by national borders. this is one of the reasons why member states alone are not able to protect consumers from the risks they face. i am convinced that the national authorities responsible for supervision in the member states need to cooperate as much as possible, to exchange information and to exchange good practice. only by working together will we be able to prevent the exploitation of existing regulatory gaps in online gambling and the inefficiencies of national regulatory authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. as an economic and social activity, beekeeping is of crucial importance for sustainable rural development, the creation of economic and social public goods, food security and the conservation of biodiversity. recently, increased mortality has led to a significant decline in bee populations in the eu and globally, with negative impacts on agriculture, food production and security, biodiversity, environmental sustainability and ecosystems. i support the call to increase the amount of support for research on honeybee health under the next financial framework (fp8) and to focus research on technological development and disease prevention and control.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the increasingly visible decline in bee populations in the european union. bees make a major contribution to the conservation of biodiversity and to economic and social public goods. in the european union, 84% of plant species and even 76% of food production depend on pollination by bees, but their pollination is being steadily suppressed. the economic value of bees is of great importance in the european union and action is urgently needed to reduce the causes of bee mortality. pesticide use, climate change, air pollution, and the electromagnetic fields produced by human equipment are thought to be the main factors contributing to the increase in bee mortality. to reduce these factors, action is needed to improve environmental quality and reduce the use of biocides and pesticides.
in writing. − the beekeeping sector is an integral part of european agriculture. beekeeping also provides an important ecosystem service through pollination, which contributes to the enhancement of biodiversity by maintaining plant genetic diversity and ecological balance. the exact causes of the recent increase in bee mortality are still unclear. there are several obstacles to the development of new bee health products. the market for such products is relatively small compared to other livestock sectors and the return on investment is low. therefore, veterinary manufacturers are not interested in developing new medicines for bees. i agree that one of the main obstacles to effective action on excessive bee mortality is the lack of reliable and comparable data on the number of hives, beekeepers and families lost in the eu. there is a strong need for an effective harmonised surveillance system to identify the extent and causes of bee mortality. a harmonised system of surveillance at european level is needed, but member states must also take action to reduce the risks to bee health. scientific research needs to be coordinated and scientific results shared at european level to avoid duplication of effort. member states' authorities shall support the dissemination of appropriate scientific and technical knowledge on bee health among beekeepers. a permanent structured dialogue between beekeepers, farmers and the relevant institutions is needed.
in writing. - in my country, bees have long been held in high esteem for their industriousness. more than three quarters of europe's food quality depends on the work of bees. unfortunately, industrial society and chemical fertiliser-based agriculture pose a major threat to bee health, and modern science is not yet able to combat the dangers of pesticides and other chemicals to bees. the document we adopted today deals in great detail with the threats to the beekeeping sector and proposes ways of tackling them. strengthening scientific research, reviewing animal health requirements and giving due consideration to beekeeping in the context of the cap reform actions necessary to maintain the current level of the beekeeping sector and to avoid new problems in the food chain.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report regarding the reform of the eu state aid rules on services of general economic interest (sgei) in response to the commission communication on the same subject. i am in favour of this report which notes the aims of the reform proposed by the commission in seeking to clarify the application of the rules on aid for sgei, demanding the commission to provide clarification of the relationship between the rules of the internal market, and the provision of public services and that it ensures that the principle of subsidiarity is applied in the definition, organisation and financing of public services. accordingly, it calls for provisions to be framed in such a way as to ensure that they can be applied correctly and that they place no unnecessary burden on the public authorities. committee calls on the commission to come up with special de minimis arrangements for ssgi that can be assumed to entail no substantial detriment to trade between ms; to include investment costs for infrastructure necessary to the functioning of sgei within the costs that compensation payments may cover, while emphasising the importance that sgei be of high quality and universally accessible.
in writing. − services of universal economic interest (sesi) are important among the common values of the union and promote social, economic and territorial cohesion, and are therefore crucial in combating inequalities in society and in creating sustainable development. the emu makes a major contribution to the economic capacity and competitiveness of the member states, thus helping not only to prevent and overcome economic crises but also to build shared economic prosperity. the cfp can contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular in the areas of employment, education and social inclusion, with a view to ensuring high levels of productivity, employment and social cohesion. i agree that the commission must provide an explanation of the relationship between the internal market rules and the provision of public services and ensure the application of the principle of subsidiarity in the definition, organisation and financing of public services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is very important to ensure legal certainty on the rules on funding for public service providers. the european commission decision setting out the rules for the granting of state aid to public service providers is still valid until the end of this year and the commission is currently deciding whether the new decision, which will come into force on 1 january next year, should change these funding rules. indeed, the content of these rules has been the subject of much debate in recent years, and the european parliament has today put forward its proposals on this matter. in particular, parliament called on the commission to simplify these rules in order to avoid placing an unnecessary administrative burden on service providers. secondly, the parliament called on the commission to clarify certain aspects of the rules which are not sufficiently clear in the current decision, and which require the constant intervention of the european court of justice in the interpretation of these rules, which do not provide any legal certainty either for municipalities or for public service providers. finally, parliament called for an increase in the prices for the provision of services above which it would be compulsory to inform the commission of the granting of state aid. i am convinced that all these efforts are essential to ultimately improve the quality and accessibility of public services to citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because services of general interest are important not only for the well-being of individual citizens but also for the well-being of society as a whole. these are services which the state or public authorities consider to be of particular importance to all citizens and which would not be provided or would be provided inadequately without state intervention. the state intervention must ensure that these services are available to all citizens or that they are of high quality and affordable to all citizens. the provision of these services is a successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular in the fields of employment, education and social inclusion. the legal measures should be clearer, simpler, more proportionate and more effective. the administrative burden of applying the rules is too great, especially for small local authorities. the food is often completely out of proportion to the effect of the measure. there is a need to achieve greater clarity and to ensure a more diversified and proportionate approach to the different types of services of general economic interest. the aim of simplifying the aid rules so that the burden on the administrative authorities is proportionate to the impact of a particular measure on competition in the internal market could also help to improve the application of the rules. services of general economic interest must be of high quality and universal access to them must be promoted.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. 116 million or more people in the european union are at risk of poverty and about 42 million people live in conditions of severe material deprivation. in some member states, social inequalities are increasing, arising from economic differences in income and wealth, differences in the labour market and the resulting social insecurity, and different access to social functions of the state, such as social protection, health care, education, etc. the european poverty action plan is one of the seven flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to reduce the number of people living in poverty and to reduce social exclusion. the programme for food distribution to the poorest in the union, launched in 1987, currently provides food aid to 13 million people and involves some 240 food banks and charities in the distribution chain. i welcome the council's agreement to lift the funding cuts for this important programme.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the commission's proposals on combating poverty and social exclusion have some shortcomings which could be remedied by the european parliament's proposals. i am particularly pleased that the report has drawn attention to the problem of the impoverished workers. the main reason for this phenomenon is, in my view, the excessively low level of minimum wages in the member states. in the future, this should be discussed much more widely both in brussels and in the member states, as it is the first and most effective way to reduce poverty levels across the eu. i am also pleased that the report has drawn attention to the problem of poverty among older women. in this context, the proposal to consider the possibility of legalising family leave for carers across the eu seems to make sense. this would help to solve the problem of calculating the length of working life of women, as women currently caring for dependent relatives and family members are unnecessarily losing years of work experience and consequently their pensions. i also support the idea of considering the issue of minimum pensions throughout the eu.
in writing. − over the past few years, despite the commitments of the union, poverty and social exclusion have increased. the crisis and its aftermath have exacerbated this problem, with the most vulnerable people feeling the strain. i believe that this situation is incompatible with the eu's values of justice and solidarity. in order to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth, the european project must focus on the most vulnerable, as poverty reduction is the engine of this future growth. poverty is a multi-factor phenomenon and therefore requires an integrated response from all levels of government, from the eu to the local level, in cooperation with local actors. i voted in favour of this report, which is based on the considerable contribution made by the actors concerned, particularly in the light of the proposals contained in this report, to overcome this problem of poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. − the fight against poverty must not end with the end of the european year against poverty. poverty and social exclusion, as well as the fight against them, are complex issues requiring complex solutions not only in the fight against unemployment but also in other areas of budgetary balance, health care, reduction of discrimination, protection of human rights . as with many social protection issues, the fight against poverty is primarily a matter for the member states, so the role of the eu institutions is often only advisory. this report by us will not alleviate poverty itself. however, i hope that the governments of the member states will take note of the measures proposed and, by coordinating their actions with each other, take measures that will contribute to poverty reduction, even in economically difficult times.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which provides for measures that will make a significant contribution to the eu's priority target of reducing by 20 million the number of people at risk of poverty or exclusion by 2020. we must make every effort to ensure that the main objective of income support programmes in each member state is to protect people from poverty and social exclusion. the greatest assets of the state are not land and factories. the greatest asset is its people, and the state must take care of them first. it is the state that must ensure the right business conditions in the country, take care of public employment. the minimum wage must guarantee a decent standard of living. the steady rise in the cost of food, energy and housing is one of the main causes of poverty, poverty, homelessness. in view of the current situation and the achievement of the objectives envisaged, i support the proposal for the commission to draw up as soon as possible guidelines and principles for a framework directive on the quality and accessibility of social services of general interest and on the adequacy and sustainability of european pension systems.

president of the commission. − mr president, many issues were raised during the debate. these issues are, in a way, interlinked. that is why, when we put forward our roadmap for stability and growth, we mentioned the need to combine growth and stability. during the debate, one specific issue that was referred to in some statements was taxation. it is important to look at this in more detail at european level. the truth is that, after the united states, the european union is the richest region in the world. yet some are suggesting that we should depend on emerging economies, countries which are much poorer than us, to rescue the european union. i find this rather strange, to be honest. the reality is stark. we have the resources in europe to respond, provided there is the political will. the reality is that our member states spend more than they receive from taxpayers. this is the reality. when the point has been reached where you can no longer cut expenditure, you need to think about raising revenue. this is unavoidable. this means appropriate, fair taxation. this taxation, i want to make clear, should not be dependent on labour – because we need more employment, not less – but should be dependent on, for instance, resource consumption, on excessive consumption of energy or on considerable fortunes and patrimony. the commission has made proposals on the fight against tax evasion through the request for a mandate to negotiate with third countries. so far we have not received a mandate from the council to negotiate with third countries to fight tax evasion. we have made proposals in the energy tax directive. we have made proposals on the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) as a first step to some kind of coordination. we have made proposals for a financial transaction tax. so let us be honest. it is not necessary to bring forward yet another package. it is time for the council and the member states to act, and to act quickly, also in the field of taxation. let us speak in very concrete terms. some governments have said that their country is very rich. the state is poor because people do not collect taxes, but the country is very rich. so, if the country is very rich, it will probably be the right moment to ask the rich country to contribute to stabilising the situation, rather than putting itself and the euro area as a whole at risk because it does not have a proper taxation system. regarding the more general debate about economic governance, the treaty requires that member states regard their economic policies as a matter of common concern – all the member states, not only the euro area countries –and that their budgetary policies are guided by the need for sound public finances. the treaty further requires that member states’ economic policies do not risk jeopardising the proper functioning of economic and monetary union. these are the guiding principles for the package of proposals for deeper economic integration which the commission is finalising for next week. we aim to find a package with the right balance between substantial reinforcement of economic governance, on the one hand, and assessing options for stability bonds, on the other. such bonds could, if well designed, strengthen financial stability and fiscal discipline in the euro area, and thus facilitate sustainable growth and job creation in europe as a whole. let us be very honest about this. there are no miracle solutions. we have to have some kind of instruments to fight the current financial instability in europe. if we want to keep a common currency, something more is needed in terms of the common instruments to fight this financial instability. we have to make a decision on this as a matter of urgency, even before any revision of the treaty. as demonstrated by the current crisis, and in particular by the need to put in place common financial backstops, euro area member states are liable to experience spillovers. they should come up with more concrete responses to possible spillovers from their policies. therefore, member states in the euro should consider their budgetary plans to be of common concern. that is why we think that draft budgetary plans should be assessed at european level before they become binding. we will, of course, assess budgetary plans with regard to both fiscal sustainability and macroeconomic imbalances. this is why we have been discussing governance today. governance is not just an objective issue regarding the substantive issues of economic policy. as we have seen during this crisis, what investors – and our citizens, of course – are asking is ‘are you in the euro area ready to take decisions?’ ‘are you in the euro area able to sustain a common currency?’ so the governance issue is a substantive issue. it is not a formal issue. this is the reality all over the world. just today, the president of the united states, speaking in the pacific, asked the european union to take bolder decisions in terms of structure and governance. i think our partners are right to ask us to have a clearer, streamlined way of taking decisions. this is why it is important to discuss these matters of governance. they should not be seen in terms of turf – if matters are decided at european or national level, if they go to brussels, to this institution or another. an indispensable pre-condition for a strong common currency is to have some kind of integration in terms of the governance of the euro area. without this increased integration, convergence and discipline, we will not be able to sustain a common currency. that moment of truth is coming. either member states accept this and complete what was initiated in maastricht, by supplementing monetary union with an economic union that requires further discipline, further convergence, and further integration, or they do not accept it, which would jeopardise our goal. this is the truth. these coming weeks will see very important decisions being taken. the commission is coming with proposals which i hope will enable us to achieve our goal and i have seen the determination in many of our member states. we know that it will be extremely difficult; let us be fair to all our member states. there are 17 democracies in the euro area and 27 democracies in the european union. the rhythm of democracy is slower than the rhythm of markets. we now need to show, also through increased community governance, that we are able to respond to the immediate and longer-term concerns. we can only achieve that through stability and growth, only through responsibility and solidarity. this is the pact at the core of our response. some just want to speak about discipline and responsibility. they should also think about solidarity. others just want to speak about growth. they should also speak about discipline. we need this pact to be achieved so that we can have a consistent, coherent, credible response to this crisis. we can come out of this crisis stronger, but, in order to do this, some important decisions have to be taken.
president of the european council. - mr president, i will be very brief. i have come here at the invitation of the president of parliament to speak about economic governance. this was the subject of preparation for the european council on 9 december, including the report i was to deliver in cooperation with the president of the commission and the president of the eurogroup. that was the subject of this debate and so i have stuck to it. in my introduction, i was very cartesian. what have we done and what are we going to do? it's as simple as that. and so i've made the enumeration, the synthesis, in fact, of what we've done. is it self-sufficient to say what we do? no, i'm not going. it is a very factual report of what has been achieved, and also of what should have been done long before the eurozone crisis. we didn't do it, we didn't ask for it, and we're paying the price today. after the chapter of what we did, what we have to do. i will again give the topics to be discussed, chapter by chapter. these are the themes that will be central to the interim report i will be presenting in december with josé manuel barroso and jean-claude juncker. these are the subjects of budgetary discipline, budgetary integration, in fact economic union, and economic convergence. and in each theme, i've specified the questions we should ask. this is not the time for me to come up with a plan. i am very respectful of the community method. the commission should be making proposals, not me! the commission has therefore made proposals and will continue to make them. my role is to try to find a consensus among the 17 and the 27 in the european council. that's my role, that's why i was asked to take on this role. and i will. but i think i asked the right questions earlier and i thank some of you who have been kind enough to give your views on the issues on the agenda today and on economic governance. as regards the three main subjects - budgetary discipline, budgetary integration and economic convergence - i would just like to make one comment. what we are experiencing is a private debt crisis, made very much worse by what banks and financial institutions have done not only in europe, but also around the world, and in a way, i would say by a global policy of very low interest rates. and this has created a debt bubble in some countries, which has resulted in a loss of competitiveness and current account deficits. and that's where a lot of our problems come from. and this, alongside a sovereign debt crisis. private and public debt are thus at the root of the problems we face today. often in this house i hear a great deal about the effects of austerity policy, but too seldom do i hear that this policy of budgetary discipline is inevitable in many countries. there are countries that are not attacked by the financial markets, and there's a reason for that: they have had a fairly healthy fiscal, economic policy. if all countries had a good ratio of, say, private and public debt, we wouldn't be in this eurozone crisis. so first things first, we need to put order in every home. i know it comes at a price, but it's absolutely essential. and even to pursue a policy of fiscal integration, and we have spoken of stability bonds, eurobonds, a form of debt mutualisation. this cannot be done without budgetary discipline. it goes with it. the two go together! yes, we say that, i agree, but we don't really emphasize it. that's the least we can do. if we want to go down the road of fiscal and financial integration, we have to go step by step, because today we are not ready to have full-fledged fiscal integration because there are too many economic, social and fiscal differences within the euro area. when youth unemployment is 8% in some countries and 48% in others, we are not ready; the divergence is far too great. so if we want budgetary integration, we must choose the means and instruments, and then see whether we need to amend the treaty in some ways and whether we need to amend it in others. we will work on these three pathways and we will discuss them in december. i am sure that we will discuss this again in this parliament and in the european council in the coming months. i would like to make two small comments on the division in europe. ladies and gentlemen, the greatest division we could have - which we will not have - would be the failure to guarantee the stability of the euro area. by then, we'd have the largest division. we must therefore give the 17 countries all the instruments and means to safeguard the stability of the euro area. i believe that this objective is a priority. i do not care at this stage whether one or the other is frustrated or whether one or the other would like to have this or that. everything has to be done to be together in the same boat: the seventeen first, then the twenty-seven. but the primary objective is to safeguard the financial stability of the euro area. a final word on economic growth. this is not just a european problem. we must, of course, make our contribution to growth and the first condition is to restore confidence in our own area because the recession, or rather the stagnation of these days comes, in the first place, not from austerity policies but from the lack of confidence of investors and consumers in the euro area. this explains much of the present stagnation. there is of course the united states which also suffers from the debt problem and which also suffers from a structural problem in its economy. i have just been there in september, and the speech given by business leaders there is virtually the same as in europe. there is of course also a loss of growth in emerging countries. they must also accept - and i am speaking in terms of the prudence of sioux - greater flexibility in their exchange rates so that the problems they are facing are not exported to other parts of the world. growth is a whole. it is not just europe and in europe, it is not just a question of austerity, it is also a question of trust. we need to work on economic growth. it is also necessary to work on this through non-financial means, which is why the single market is so important. we have not yet fully exploited the possibilities of the single market and by far. we must work on different levels and not just in europe but across the world. these are some of the things i wanted to explain to you in this debate on economic governance. in writing. mr president, commission president, colleagues, we are discussing today the long-term reforms to the eu's economic governance, which will determine the way and the principles on which the economic governance and surveillance system will be based. the adopted european economic governance mechanism is the largest body of legislation since the establishment of economic and monetary union on economic and financial regulation. this set of documents sets economic priorities, regulates stricter supervision of national fiscal policies, provides for measures to ensure greater economic stability and address regulatory weaknesses in the financial sector. mr president, you have expressed your support for the economic governance model that has been chosen, which leaves many people in doubt about the fragmentation of europe into a so-called two-speed europe. while all countries will be able to participate in the mechanism and comply with the criteria set out therein, only euro area countries will have decision-making rights. those member states which have already pegged their currency to the euro and have transferred their monetary policy to the european central bank, but which for some reason have not yet adopted the euro (e.g. lithuania), are directly affected in all respects by decisions taken in the euro area, even though they cannot influence them. i think that it is necessary to consider in detail the principles of the economic model chosen and to ensure that those member states whose currency is pegged to the euro also have decision-making rights in the economic governance mechanism. this principle might also provide a stronger incentive for non-euro area countries to link their currency to the euro in the first place, thus strengthening their aspirations to integrate into the euro area and at the same time participate in decision-making.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support for workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 22 september 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the allocation of the egf to austria to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. i have agreed to this document because in this particular case it concerns a reduction of 30 to 50% in the volume of freight business in july 2009. the traffic of lorries with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3,5 tonnes decreased by 17% in the first half of 2009 compared to the same period of the previous year. these downward trends continued in 2010 and led to a number of redundancies in austrian road transport companies. according to austria, the crisis, which affected the behaviour of european consumers and led to a decline in goods production, had a particularly negative impact on the transport sector, which only became apparent later than in the case of the main secondary industries. the commission therefore proposes to mobilise an amount of eur 3 643 770.
in writing. − i support the decision to grant aid to the austrian transport sector, which has been hit hard by the economic and financial crisis and has led to the redundancies of hundreds of workers. it should be noted that the crisis has affected small and very small transport companies the most. i believe that the amount allocated is sufficient to facilitate reintegration into the labour market and to implement other active labour market measures to encourage the self-employment and earlier employment of the beneficiaries. the aid must therefore be dynamic and effective in order to cover the costs of job search, training and retraining, as well as the costs of promoting entrepreneurship, and to prevent the spread of unemployment in the country.
in writing. - i voted for financial aid to greece. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. greece applied for aid in respect of 642 redundancies in 2 enterprises operating in the retail trade. this application qualifies for financial assistance and i therefore approve the allocation of eur 2 918 500.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support for workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. on 22 september 2011, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in greece to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. i have endorsed this document because in this particular case greece indicates that the economic and financial crisis has had a devastating effect on the greek economy. the average private sector income also decreased. the decrease in revenue had a direct consequence in the decrease in consumption. the trend in private final consumption expenditure in greece in 2009 is negative, as is the eu-27 average. in 2010, private consumption increased in the eu-27 and decreased even more in greece compared to the previous year. the decrease in private consumption had a significant impact on the retail sector and in particular on shopping centres. the commission therefore proposes to mobilise an amount of eur 2 918 500.
in writing. − in order to mitigate the negative effects of globalisation, it is necessary to target the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund. it is essential to ensure that the assistance to redundant workers is dynamic and delivered as quickly and efficiently as possible. i support the decision to grant aid to these greek companies operating in the retail sector, as hundreds of workers have been made redundant as a result of the financial and economic crisis. i believe that the amount allocated is sufficient to mitigate the effects of the collective redundancies in this sector and to facilitate the return to the labour market of the workers affected. this support will cover the costs of job search, training and retraining, as well as the promotion of entrepreneurship and will effectively prevent the spread of unemployment in the country.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because of the need to pay greater attention to the results of the work of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp) and the eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) and to ensure consistency between its resolutions and those of the european parliament. the jpa has done a good job of making north-south cooperation count. at present, national and regional strategy papers are submitted by the european commission to the european parliament and the national parliaments of the acp countries for parliamentary scrutiny. it is important that the development committee and the jpa monitor the situation and ensure that this instrument of parliamentary control is used effectively. the assembly has played and continues to play a key role in overseeing the negotiation of economic partnership agreements. the hearings of the main negotiators from both sides, the meetings with economic and social actors (in formal meetings and accompanying events) and the interaction between members of the european and southern parliaments have helped to increase the transparency of the process and to take account of local concerns. whatever the outcome of the negotiations, the assembly's activities have undoubtedly had an impact on this process.

in writing. − given that the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly is the largest parliamentary body covering both the north and the south, greater attention should be paid to its performance. it is worth noting that the assembly has played and continues to play a key role in overseeing the negotiation of economic partnership agreements. the opening of an open and democratic dialogue between the european union and the acp countries on the cotonou partnership agreement is welcome. i believe that the acp parliaments need more support to enable them to exercise effective democratic control. we also need to do more to achieve the millennium development goals as soon as possible.
in writing. − i fully support this report, which welcomes the commission’s proposal to use the european heritage label as a tool, among other more efficient ways, to bridge the gap between the european union and its citizens. the report suggests that, whereas the commission proposed to award the label each year, members consider that selecting sites every two years would ensure better quality of the selection process and of the selected sites. it states that transnational sites should be favoured, as they promote commonalities, and they should feature prominently in all member states’ ordinary quota of two proposed sites per year. the report insists that the new label should not be a mere transformation of the old one: no transitional provisions should be needed but the new, well defined criteria must be the object of future negotiations with the council. the commission is also asked to inform parliament, the council and the committee of the regions at each stage of the selection process.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation as the council has already adopted its position at first reading, which is based on the agreement reached after the first reading in the european parliament. the commission proposal for a european heritage label focuses on the added value of this label compared to other initiatives in the field of cultural heritage. the label is awarded not because of the beauty of the site or its architectural features, but in recognition of its symbolic value for european integration and the history of the union. it is not inherently linked to conservation but to the activities that can be carried out in the sites concerned and to their educational dimension, especially if it is important for the education of young people. finally, the labelled sites will be able to function more efficiently through cooperation. the european parliament and the council agreed that each member state may pre-select a maximum of two heritage sites every two years one domestic and one international. the coordinating country shall apply the quota for international heritage sites only in order to maintain the commitment of the member states to participate in these initiatives. the panel of independent experts shall select no more than one proposed heritage site per country that may be eligible for the label.
in writing. − the european heritage label is an attempt to make european citizens feel more connected to the european union and to value diversity through a shared history and heritage, and to strengthen the dialogue between cultures themselves. i think it's a beautiful initiative that should be nurtured.
in writing. − we need to ensure that this initiative does not conflict with initiatives already underway, such as the unesco world heritage list project. i believe that the european countries should be given the right to propose the most significant cultural heritage objects and sites, which bear witness to the identity of each country as an integral part of europe, to outstanding personalities and historical events that have played an important role in the development of that country and of european history and culture. in this context, clear and rigorous criteria must be established for the selection of heritage sites on the basis of their symbolic importance for europe and their educational work, rather than on the basis of their beauty or architectural quality. it is also essential to ensure that participation is based on a voluntary and equal basis.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which is important for the whole european rail system. in this context, i have consistently stressed the need to assess the specificities of the baltic states, where the dominant railways with wider track gauge than those of most eu countries are technologically and commercially integrated into the railway network of third countries. this was reflected in the amendments i made. it is good that the rapporteur and other members of the european parliament have listened to the differences in the baltic states and made the appropriate exceptions in the draft report of the parliament. parliament approved a compromise amendment to the communication on infrastructure charges, including a very important amendment for the baltic states on the possibility of imposing higher charges for the transport of goods to third countries. this will ensure that the baltic states do not have to subsidise rail freight from third countries and that all costs incurred by the infrastructure manager in providing the transport service are covered.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is of the utmost importance to pursue the development of a rail transport system in the european union that is as sustainable and environmentally friendly as possible. one of the main modes of transport that is expanding and has the potential to grow is trains. over a period of 12 years, from 1996 to 2008, the market share of the road haulage market increased by around 2%. these figures are not high because of increased competition, but looking ahead, the european union is committed to reducing its carbon emissions and is also concerned about making the most efficient use of resources. in order to expand the single european railway area and increase the efficiency of trains, measures such as stricter railway safety rules, the development of railway infrastructure and its more efficient use are proposed.
in writing. − the need to separate rail infrastructure from freight and passenger transport activities is expected to contribute to the creation of a more efficient eu single transport market, to the development of the railway sector, and to the improvement of service quality. lithuania is clearly in favour of an integrated railway management model. we take the principled position that the 'lithuanian railways' need not be split up, as their current management model is more beneficial for lithuania. i was and am convinced that the provisions of the directives cannot be applied blindly throughout the community. conditions allowing member states to address their specific problems are necessary. this position has led the commission to reconsider its proposal for the separation of different activities in the railway sector and to prepare a new draft directive by the end of next year. legislative changes are needed to ensure a more liberal, competitive railway market. however, these changes should not have the opposite effect and should be adopted in the light of the experience of hospitals not only in the eu but also in other countries. it shows that integrated railway management is often more efficient. in countries where the railway sector is fragmented, there are no more efficient operators, competition between them has not made the railway sector more attractive, and railways have not won a larger share of the transport market. the issues in the lithuanian railway sector are made even more complex by the specific situation in lithuania. the railway company does not comply with european standards and remains mainly integrated into the cis market. the close link between the infrastructure and the freight transport operator is therefore crucial for the transport of goods from third countries.
in writing. - i support the initiative to create a common european railway area. however, i do not support the proposals for the separation of infrastructure managers and operators and transport services. i believe that the implementation of these proposals will make it more difficult to open up the railway market. in addition, the quality of rail transport services will be negatively affected. it should be noted that the reservation provided for in the proposal, which applies to 1520 mm mesh, will be available to a limited number of operators. meanwhile, countries such as lithuania, which have integrated companies operating on a network linked to third countries, will be prevented from applying the above exemption, as the railway lines of these countries belong to the ten-t network. such legal regulation will have a particularly negative impact on lithuania and its rail transport sector as a whole.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, rail transport is one of the leading transport sectors in lithuania. according to statistics for the previous year, lithuanian railways carried 4.4 million passengers and more than 40 million tonnes of freight. however, the technical level of infrastructure in the lithuanian railway sector is still below that of europe. modernisation and technical interoperability between lithuanian and european railways is essential to linking europe. one of the main tasks of lithuania's transport policy should be to promote rail transport, with particular attention to the passenger transport sector. the freight transport sector is currently much better developed in lithuania than the passenger transport sector, while the number of passengers is decreasing. lithuania and the eu should do more to promote rail passenger transport and try to make it more attractive remember that rail travel is much safer and more environmentally friendly than road travel. i support the rapporteur's call for greater financial transparency and agree that national regulatory authorities should monitor rail-related services more closely. i also think that the european commission should be more involved in coordinating the rail baltic project. this is an important strategic project which is being developed to connect the railways of the baltic states and western europe. we can't let the lack of funds get in the way of this project.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. climate change is one of the major challenges of the 21st century that requires international action. in the absence of an international agreement, it is necessary to conclude a legally binding international agreement as soon as possible, in accordance with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, recognising that developed countries have a key role to play and developing countries have a proper role to play in this process. the current commitments and pledges under the copenhagen accord and formally endorsed by the cancún agreement are insufficient to achieve the overall objective of limiting the global annual average surface temperature increase to 2oc (the 2oc target). european countries face crucial choices to safeguard their future prosperity and security and to meet their co2 reduction commitments. i support the call for the world's heads of state and government to take a genuine political leadership role in the negotiations and to demonstrate the will to reach a comprehensive, international, impartial, ambitious and legally binding agreement to ensure that global temperatures do not rise above 2°c and that greenhouse gas emissions are capped as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because one of the biggest problems of this century is climate change and its impact not only on europe but also on the whole world. increased climate change is leading to more frequent storms and floods, colder winters, more rainfall, and earlier seasons. without the necessary action to reduce the global annual surface temperature increase to 2°c and to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the damage to nature and wildlife will be severe and our normal lives may be irreversibly altered. the european commission has put forward proposals to reduce these problems by 2050, but it is necessary to achieve all this by 2020. climate change is caused by human lifestyles, by poor forest management, i.e. deforestation, and by many other factors. to ensure our future security, action to mitigate climate change is urgently needed.
in writing. − i voted for this document because there is a great deal of scientific evidence that climate change is happening and having an impact, and that international action is therefore needed to tackle one of the greatest challenges of the 21st century and beyond. the general objective of concluding a legally binding international agreement in accordance with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities should be pursued further, recognising that developed countries have a key role to play and that developing countries should contribute appropriately to this process. account should be taken of the fundamental geopolitical changes in the world over the past decades, with a number of developing countries becoming major economic and political players and new balances of power and influence emerging, fostering new roles and responsibilities. i believe that it is necessary to urge the conference to ensure that a comprehensive, impartial, ambitious and legally binding international agreement on post-2012 activities is reached on the basis of the international rules-based framework provided for in the kyoto protocol, in order to ensure that global temperatures do not rise by more than 2°c and that greenhouse gas emissions are reduced as quickly as possible.
in writing. − i support this resolution because climate change is one of the major global challenges facing the world today, and its solution requires concerted and coordinated action at international level. i believe that the eu must publicly commit itself to continue to meet its commitments under the kyoto protocol. all eu institutions must take a strong stand at the durban conference and take a broader and more effective eu climate diplomacy. in addition, every effort should be made to ensure that the eu's other global partners follow its example by setting binding emission reduction targets. i support the plan to create a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050. i believe that the target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050 is realistic and can help to preserve prosperity and security for the future. innovative financing mechanisms and revenues from the future financial transaction tax must be used internationally to achieve the objectives set. it is worth noting that the durban conference is to adopt concrete actions to implement the cancún agreements on long-term financing.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in recent years, member states have devoted only 0.43% of gdp to official development assistance (oda), despite the millennium commitment of 0.7% by 2015 and the intermediate target of 0.56% by 2010. if the eu fails to meet its aid commitments, this could seriously damage the trust and credibility of its partners in the developing world. the financial and economic crisis has put increasing pressure on national budgets and requires measures to make development aid more effective and to help eliminate the causes of impeding the development of poor countries. i agree that a change in policies is needed in all industrialized and developing countries to address the structural causes of poverty, and that it is therefore essential to focus local resources in partner countries for sustainable development. priority should be given to improving tax administration and transparency, ensuring accountability of each country, and to combating tax evasion and illicit capital flight, if necessary by adopting appropriate legislation. i support the call to make the fight against tax havens, tax evasion and illicit capital flight a priority for development policy and to ensure that mining companies in developing countries pay proper taxes and produce in a way that respects social and environmental standards.
in writing. − in recent years, member states have allocated only 0.43% of gnp to official development assistance, despite the millennium commitment of 0.7% by 2015 and the intermediate target of 0.56% by 2010. member states committed 50% of all new aid to sub-saharan africa in 2005, but only half of this was committed. eu countries also failed to meet their commitment to allocate 0.15% of gdp to the least developed countries (ldcs) in 2010. i agree that failure to meet its aid commitments could seriously damage the trust and credibility of its partners in the developing world, and that compliance with the commitments would send a clear and unambiguous signal to poor countries and other aid providers. member states are urged to take immediate measures to implement the commitment of 0.7% of gnp and the specific commitments to africa and the octs, and are recommended to adopt fully transparent, multiannual, binding measures, including legislation. at the same time, i am convinced that more effective, more cost-effective aid is needed, since ineffective aid wastes up to eur 6 billion a year.
in writing. - i support this resolution. it should be noted that in recent years, member states have significantly reduced their support in defiance of the millennium commitment. in addition, around eur 6 billion is wasted every year on ineffective aid. there is therefore a real risk that the eu will not be able to meet its aid commitments. such a situation would cast doubt on the credibility of the eu among partners in the developing world. to dispel such doubts and to strengthen its image as a reliable and stable partner, the eu must go beyond the oda in its aid and implement other instruments for financing international development. in addition, the commission should include the issue of land grabbing as one of the most pressing issues of the moment in its policy dialogue with developing countries.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report. it aims to support and sustain european cinema – which is an important branch of european industry – both in terms of its richness and with regard to granting the widest possible access, in the interests of unity and freedom of thought. through this resolution, members call on the member states and the commission to provide financial support for the full digitisation of equipment in eu cinemas, to establish european and national programmes to support the transition to digital technologies as quickly as possible, and to encourage the circulation of european films in an audiovisual sector that is globally very competitive. members recommend the standardisation of systems based on iso standards in the areas of production, distribution and film screening, and also emphasise the need for public and private investment as the cinema sector enters the digital era. they stress that, in order to ease the digitisation process, diversified financing, both public and private, should be made available at local, regional, national and european level, particularly to support small and independent cinemas. they recommend that the financing of digitisation projects from the eu structural funds should be linked to a commitment on the part of supported cinemas to screen european films.

for the efd group in the european digital agenda, broadband and the internet are particularly important factors for economic growth, job creation and strengthening europe's global competitiveness. europe will only be able to fully exploit the potential of the digital economy when it has a well-functioning internal market in this area. i believe that transparency, quality of service and easy switching are essential for a neutral network, while ensuring freedom of choice for end-users. it is important to underline the need to preserve an open internet while providing high quality services in compliance with legislation that promotes and respects fundamental rights such as intellectual property rights, freedom of expression and freedom of establishment. the obstacles to switching operators, the blocking and capping practices and the discrimination against dominant market participants need to be removed.
for the efd group i fully agree with the author, mrs gallo, and i think that the honourable commissioner's position is a little too cautious in this case. the different value added tax applied to digital and physical goods is indeed a major problem today, preventing the potential of growth and the large supply of goods and services offered by the digital market from being properly exploited. in addition, discriminatory conditions are created when the benefits of the single market are granted only to physical goods. in this context, i believe that the commission should take immediate action to apply a reduced rate of vat to cultural goods and services supplied in the form of physical media or online, and to simplify and harmonise the vat rules. particular attention should be paid to electronic books, which are currently subject to the normal vat rate and to physical books, which are subject to a lower rate of 15% and 5% respectively. i believe that the implementation of these measures will facilitate the development of a culture of digital resources and the effective functioning of the digital single market. this market is of vital importance and is necessary for the development of more modern businesses and better services for citizens in the community countries, it contributes strongly to the further development of electronic commerce, electronic services and it is therefore necessary to remove as soon as possible the existing barriers to the digital single market.
member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank you for this opportunity and to welcome the interest and engagement demonstrated by the european parliament as regards the negotiations on an association agreement with georgia. we had an intensive and regular exchange with the rapporteurs, which, i believe, has helped in preparing a well-structured and balanced report. the recommendations of this report will be very helpful in our further negotiations with georgia. successful negotiations and conclusion of the agreement will be a major step towards georgia’s political association and economic integration with the eu and will bring our relations to a new level. we acknowledge the importance georgia attaches to its european identity. as you know, any reference to article 49 remains controversial among member states and is therefore impossible to offer, but what is important for georgia at this stage is to seize a maximum of the many opportunities which political association and economic integration will offer to change relations now: in short, to create more of europe within georgia. using this opportunity, let me briefly inform you about the state of play in the negotiations. together with our georgian counterparts, we are working intensely to advance the negotiations. since the launch of these negotiations in july 2010, talks have been conducted in plenary sessions covering political dialogue and foreign and security policy, justice, freedom and security issues, and economic and sectoral cooperation. seven plenary sessions have already taken place and the eighth round is due to take place soon. good progress was made on the preamble, the objectives and general principles of the agreement. we have been able provisionally to agree on a large part of the text. provisional agreement was also reached on a number of elements relating to political dialogue and foreign and security policy. it is not surprising that security and stability, as a result of a peaceful resolution of the existing conflicts over south ossetia and abkhazia, are the core issues for georgia. we have achieved substantial progress on justice, freedom and security as well. the sides also advanced on economic and sectoral cooperation – 19 chapters have been provisionally closed out of 28. the eu is committed to starting the negotiations with georgia on a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta), as an integral part of the future association agreement, as soon as possible. this commitment was also made at the eastern partnership summit of 29-30 september in warsaw. the launch of negotiations is conditional upon georgia making sufficient progress in the implementation of certain ‘key recommendations’. the eu appreciates all the efforts that georgia has undertaken to address the issues and take the necessary steps to prepare for the negotiations. we are now in the final stages of the process, which should allow the commission to make its formal recommendation to the eu member states before the end of the year. last week, an important agreement was reached between georgia and russia on russia’s accession to the world trade organization. the eu welcomes and appreciates georgia’s acceptance of a compromise. it is in everyone’s interests – including those of the eu and georgia – to have russia inside the rules-based wto system. the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, catherine ashton, is visiting georgia today and meeting president saakashvili. the main aim of this visit is to reinforce the message of the eu’s continuing commitment to georgia, and to demonstrate that the political and economic ties between the eu and georgia are being further strengthened.
in writing. this communication on the negotiation of an eu-georgia association agreement is an important document for the european union and the state of georgia. this is a step towards the country's membership of the european union. we support georgia's european perspective and the course of the negotiations. it is important that the eu continues to actively mediate in the resolution of the 2008 territorial conflict between russia and georgia. we call on georgia to cooperate more closely with the international criminal court in its investigation of the 2008 war crimes. i agree with the rapporteur that an agreement between russia and georgia on russia's wto membership should be reached as soon as possible. we trust that the georgian authorities will take all measures to ensure that all eu standards are respected in the country's consolidation of the rule of law, the social market economy and human rights. i join the rapporteur in calling on the georgian government to engage more widely in constructive dialogue with the opposition forces and to continue to create a democratic environment for freedom of expression, in particular by allowing all political parties to use the state media. i also call on the georgian authorities to make stronger commitments in the areas of employment policy and social cohesion and to continue to create an environment conducive to the implementation of eu social market economy standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, because of its universal nature, justice must be applied equally to all, without exceptions and without double standards. the international criminal court is the first permanent international judicial institution with the power to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes, and it makes a major contribution to the promotion of human rights and international law by combating impunity, thus playing an important deterrent role and making clear that impunity for these crimes will not be tolerated. moreover, no place should become a safe haven for perpetrators of genocide, crimes against humanity, summary executions, war crimes, torture, mass rape or crimes related to enforced disappearances. parliament stressed that the international criminal court must not only address the problems of armed conflict, but also investigate more actively human rights violations that amount to crimes against humanity and cases where national authorities are clearly unwilling to investigate, prosecute or punish suspected offenders. despite the strong support of the eu and its member states to the icc, much remains to be done at political and diplomatic as well as at practical level to help the icc overcome the challenges and difficulties it currently faces.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the international criminal court (icc) has been successfully implementing its exceptional universal mandate to prosecute persons for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide since its establishment on 1 july 2002, when the rome statute entered into force. since its establishment, the eu has supported the icc through a wide range of political, diplomatic, financial and logistical actions, thus promoting the universality and integrity of the rome statute and contributing to the independence and effective functioning of the court. in addition to the political and diplomatic challenges currently faced, the main problem hampering the court's work is inadequate funding. it is continuously working on new cases, but the funding does not increase as new cases are brought. it is essential that the eu member states continue to provide the court with the resources it needs to carry out its mandate. more financial and logistical support than is currently available should be provided to ensure that the court's current funding shortfall is successfully addressed. the eu and its member states should ensure adequate financial support for the court's budget.
in writing. − i believe that the eu must give greater support to the international criminal court, which, as a permanent international judicial institution, prosecuting individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes, contributes in particular to the proper implementation of human rights and international law, and to the maintenance of peace and the strengthening of international security. serious crimes falling within the jurisdiction of the icc are of concern to all member states. every effort should therefore be made to promote the most active cooperation possible in order to prevent these crimes and to overcome the impunity of the perpetrators. it is also essential that the court be protected from possible political pressure in order to properly implement the principle of impartiality and to administer justice based on the law rather than on political motives.

in writing. − i support this resolution, which aims to further develop the programme to support the further development of an integrated maritime policy, to define the objectives of this programme, to set clear funding conditions and to strengthen the involvement of legislators in the adoption of delegated acts and in reporting. i believe that it remains essential to maximise sustainable development, economic growth and social cohesion in the eu's coastal, island and outermost regions. to achieve these objectives, it is necessary to implement coherent and coordinated policy measures relating to maritime affairs and to develop international cooperation. in addition, adequate and appropriate funding must be allocated to this programme.
