in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls for a ban on the use of cluster munitions in post-conflict countries, where they cause many tragic injuries and deaths among civilians, leaving children and other unsuspecting innocents injured by unexploded secondary munitions. cluster munitions are aerial or ground-launched container containing from a few dozen to a few hundred secondary munitions, spread over an area roughly the size of a football field. the un convention on cluster munitions, which prohibits the use, development, manufacture, acquisition, stockpiling, storage or transfer of cluster munitions, entered into force in 2010, but has not yet been signed by all eu member states. the purpose of this resolution is to draw attention to and to call on all eu member states not to accept and ratify the recently concluded protocol to the convention on certain conventional weapons, which is not compatible with the convention on cluster munitions, as it would allow the use of cluster munitions.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because cluster munitions pose a serious threat to civilians due to their high lethal impact and because the use of these munitions in post-conflict countries has been the cause of many tragic injuries and deaths among civilians, as unexploded secondary munitions are often found by children and other unsuspecting innocent people. the support of eu member states, parliamentary initiatives and the activities of civil society organisations were crucial to the successful conclusion of the oslo process and the entry into force of the convention on cluster munitions (ccm). the cwc prohibits member states from using, developing, manufacturing, otherwise acquiring, stockpiling, possessing or transferring cluster munitions, directly or indirectly, or from aiding, abetting or inducing any person to engage in any activity prohibited under the convention. the cwc establishes a new humanitarian standard of assistance to victims, including those directly affected by cluster munitions and their families and communities. therefore, this document invites eu member states and candidate countries that are not parties to the convention on cluster munitions to join the cwc as a matter of urgency and the signatory parties to the cwc to ratify it as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for a total ban on the use of cluster munitions, as they pose a lethal threat to the civilian population. member states must strictly respect the obligation not to accept or ratify any protocol to the convention on certain conventional weapons authorising the use of cluster munitions. it should be noted that such a protocol is legally incompatible with the provisions of the convention on cluster munitions. i also believe that the commission should include a ban on cluster munitions as a standard clause in agreements with third countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the financial and economic crisis has seriously damaged the potential for economic growth and the digital economy can make a major contribution to europe's future prosperity. the european union can exploit the opportunities of the single market by facilitating online and cross-border trade between member states. the european parliament calls on the commission to consider the possibility of revising directive 2008/8/ec by 1 january 2015 in order to provide for value added tax (vat) to be paid in the member state of the customer. in addition, the revision of vat legislation, which would give member states greater flexibility to apply lower vat rates, should be carried out in conjunction with the application of the principles laid down in directive 2008/8/ec. in order to ensure that all member states benefit equally from the digital single market, the principle of charging in the customer's member state should be introduced as early as possible. the european union must therefore do more than simply correct the inconsistencies in the existing legal framework. in addition, the revision of vat rules should give priority to encouraging businesses to develop and offer new pan-european internet services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the digital distribution of cultural, journalistic and creative content gives authors and content providers the opportunity to reach more new consumers. i believe that the eu must continue to promote the creation, production and distribution (across all platforms) of digital content and that a lower vat rate for online cultural content could really boost growth. a revision of the vat legislation is necessary to allow member states greater flexibility to apply lower vat rates, and this should be carried out in conjunction with the application of the principles laid down in directive 2008/8/ec. in order to ensure that all member states benefit equally from the digital single market, the principle of charging in the member state of consumption should be introduced as early as possible. finally, any revision should simplify the vat system, for example by introducing the single window principle for vat and eliminating double taxation.
in writing. − i support this resolution because the digital market is very important and vital for modern business and eu citizens. this market is a major contributor to the further development of e-commerce services and it is therefore necessary to remove the existing barriers to the digital single market as soon as possible. the difference between vat on digital and physical goods is a major problem today, preventing the potential of growth and the large supply of goods and services offered by the digital market from being exploited. in addition, discriminatory conditions are created when the benefits of the single market are granted only to physical goods.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union is the world's largest importer of fishery products and one of the world's largest fisheries operators. it therefore has a major responsibility to play a key role in mobilising the international community's efforts to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. unfortunately, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is a major environmental and economic problem in both fishing seas and freshwater fishing areas worldwide, undermining fisheries management, threatening the sustainability of fish stocks and food security. it also distorts the market and has unpredictable consequences for society as a whole, including developing countries. such illegal fishing and related commercial activities create unfair competition for fishermen and others who operate in accordance with the law and cause economic hardship for fishing communities, consumers and the sector as a whole. in the fight against illegal fishing, there is therefore a need to increase coordination between the commission, the community fisheries control agency and the member states in order to improve the collection and exchange of information and to promote the rigorous and transparent application of european union fisheries legislation. in addition, member states and the commission should ensure the fight against illegal fishing at sea and in inland waters.
in writing. − fishing is a global industry, and so is inevitably illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. as we know, global cooperation is needed to combat iuu fishing. the world's oceans are the common heritage of mankind, and it is the common duty of mankind to preserve them. i agreed that a global ocean governance system is essential for fisheries management, especially in the high seas, and that the current approach is completely wrong. it is necessary to negotiate international agreements to ensure that fishing rights are subject to the necessary criteria relating to transparency of ownership, operations and catches, traceability of products, etc., and that states that fail to fulfil their obligations lose fishing rights. finally, it should be noted that many of these recommendations will require significant resources to implement. many developing countries would have difficulty finding such resources, so ways of providing aid must be found. it's a common situation these days. however, such aid cannot be unconditional; in the event of failure, the beneficiary countries should suffer the same consequences as other countries, such as export bans.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards repayable assistance and financial engineering. the proposal defines a countervailable grant as a direct financial contribution which is granted as support and which can be partially or fully reimbursed without interest. it specifies that the structural funds may finance expenditure incurred in carrying out activities linked to the contributions to be reimbursed. it also specifies that the funds returned to the granting authority or to another competent authority of the member state must be kept in a separate account and reused for the same purpose or in accordance with the objectives of the operational programme. legal certainty and clarity should be ensured with regard to repayable assistance and financial engineering instruments. i agree with the rapporteur that proper monitoring of financial engineering instruments is necessary, but that new additional reporting obligations for member states should not apply. the ep amendments aim to clarify the text, to include a definition of a credit line, to amend the reporting requirements and to clarify the obligations relating to the declaration of expenditure.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1260/1999 specifies the different forms of support that could be provided as a contribution from the structural funds. member states have introduced these forms of support during the 2000-2006 programming period and have set up special funds, as well as providing repayable support through other instruments. on the other hand, council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 does not provide for the definition of both repayable and non-repayable aid. it contains provisions on financial engineering measures, but their scope is rather narrow. the regulation does not appear to cover repayable aid. however, member states continued to apply forms of reimbursable support, building on the positive experience of the previous programming period. i have endorsed the document as it is necessary to provide in regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 that the aid to be recovered may be co-financed by the structural funds. the commission proposal aims to clarify the legality of the existing legal practice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because we must make every effort to ensure that the money returned is properly invested and that the aid provided is used as efficiently as possible. in particular, the structural funds should be used to finance expenditure incurred in carrying out activities linked to the contributions to be reimbursed. in order to ensure a transparent and expeditious implementation process, it is necessary that the refunded aid is held in a separate account and used for the same purpose. particular attention should be paid to financial engineering as an innovative way of using eu structural funds resources. the commission and the member states should therefore ensure the monitoring of the application of those measures. it is also essential to ensure that administrative costs or charges are proportionate to the overall effectiveness of the financial engineering instrument.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 as regards certain provisions on financial management applicable to certain member states experiencing or threatened with severe financial stability difficulties. the european commission's proposal sought to provide additional financial resources to eu member states facing particular difficulties in managing their public debt/deficit and to ensure financial stability in order to continue implementing programmes. a balanced compromise was reached in the negotiations with the council on the retroactive application of the proposed measures, as well as on a temporary suspension allowing all the countries participating in the programme to benefit from the increased co-financing rate. it will also allow for rapid assistance to those member states that have been severely affected by the crisis. the temporary increase in co-financing rates will facilitate the concentration of resources on specific projects and reduce the pressure on national budgets.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the commission proposal amending council regulation (ec) no 1083/2006. the aim is to provide additional financial resources to eu member states facing particular difficulties in managing their public debt/deficit and to ensure financial stability in order to continue implementing programmes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, as the national budgets of the member states have been particularly badly affected by the prolonged financial and economic crisis, and measures are therefore needed to help ensure the financial stability of the member states and the continued implementation of the programmes. in this context, it is necessary to provide temporary additional financial assistance to those member states which are facing significant difficulties in administering their public debt or deficit. i therefore support the proposal to increase the overall funding rates for a certain period. it is also essential to ensure that support is provided only in exceptional cases where the problems encountered cannot be solved by other means.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and in favour of the commission proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards its period of application. council decision 2002/546/ec of 20 june 2002 authorises spain to apply or exempt certain locally produced products in the canary islands from the reduced so-called aiem tax (which is normally levied on products imported into and purchased in the canary islands) until 31 december 2011. decision 2002/546/ec gives the reasons for adopting specific measures to strengthen the local industry by increasing its competitiveness. the global economic crisis of 2009, which led to a drop in travellers, had a significant impact on the canary islands' economy, which is heavily dependent on tourism revenues. on 16 november 2010, spain submitted to the european commission a request for an extension of the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec for two years. the commission assessed the request in the light of the extent of the difficulties encountered by the canary islands. it concluded that the data available justified the granting of the request. the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards the period of application of that decision will allow for an extension of its period of application until 31 december 2013.
in writing. − the provisions of the eu treaty do not, in principle, allow for a differential taxation between local products from the canary islands and products from spain or other member states. by council decision of 20 june 2002, spain was authorised to apply a reduced rate of the so-called aiem tax or to exempt certain locally produced products in the canary islands until 31 december 2011. the decision sets out the reasons for adopting the specific measures to strengthen the local industry by increasing its competitiveness. the global economic crisis of 2009, which led to a drop in travellers, had a significant impact on the canary islands' economy, which is heavily dependent on tourism revenues. as a result, unemployment increased to 26,2% in 2009, whereas the unemployment rate ranged from 10,4% to 12% between 2001 and 2007. on 16 november 2010, spain submitted to the european commission a request to extend the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec by two years in order to bring its expiry date into line with the expiry of the guidelines on national regional aid for 2007-2013. the commission assessed the request in the light of the extent of the difficulties encountered by the canary islands. it concluded that the data available justified the granting of the request. i have endorsed the document as a proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards the period of application of that decision, allowing for an extension of its period of application until 31 december 2013.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this decision because, in view of the extent of the difficulties faced by the canary islands, it is appropriate to extend the tax exemption currently applicable to the canary islands. it should be noted that the canary islands derive most of their income from tourism. the prolonged economic and financial crisis has had a particularly severe impact on the canary islands' economy, with an increase in unemployment. i believe that the eu should give its outermost regions as much support as possible, through specific measures, thus enabling the economies of these regions to develop. in view of the unfavourable market situation of the canary islands, it is necessary to improve their competitiveness by strengthening the domestic industry by granting certain tax incentives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and supported the commission proposal for a council decision amending decision 2007/659/ec as regards its period of application and the annual quota for the application of the reduced rate of excise duty. taking into account the special conditions, particularities and limited possibilities of the outermost regions of the eu, including the french overseas departments, the council, on a proposal from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, will establish specific measures aimed at establishing the conditions for the application of the treaties and the common policy to these regions. these specific measures relate in particular to tax policy. however, those measures will not affect the integrity and consistency of the union legal order.
in writing. − france is authorised to apply a reduced rate of excise duty to traditional rum produced in its overseas departments and sold on the mainland. the reduced rate of excise duty shall apply only to an annual quota of 108 000 hectolitres of pure alcohol. the derogation expires on 31 december 2012. the french authorities have submitted the required report to the commission with two requests. first, it is requested that the annual quota of 108 000 hectolitres of pure alcohol be increased to 125 000 hectolitres in order to reflect the evolution of the eu rum market. secondly, the extension of the period of application of decision 2007/659/ec by one year, i.e. until 31 december 2013, is requested in order to coincide with the expiry of the period of application of the commission decision of 27 june 2007 on state aid in the same field (state aid no 530/2006). i voted in favour of the motion to approve the commission proposal.
in writing. - i support this resolution which provides for the extension of the period of application of the reduced rate of excise duty on rum produced in the french overseas departments and sold on the mainland and for a corresponding increase in its quotas. it should be noted that the application of the reduced excise duty is of particular importance for these regions and their development. it should be noted that their remoteness, isolation, small size and difficult topographical and climatic conditions make the social and economic situation of the overseas departments particularly difficult. in view of the particular characteristics and limited possibilities of these regions, it is therefore necessary to maintain the reduced rate of excise duty on traditional rum produced in the overseas departments in order not to jeopardise their development and to ensure economic and social stability.
in writing. - i voted for this important document. the european central bank plays an important role in maintaining price and financial stability and adequate liquidity in financial markets. the prolonged financial crisis in the eu and the widening gap in economic convergence between the euro area and the countries whose currencies are pegged to the euro remain one of the most serious challenges for the single monetary policy. i believe that the european union needs a common fiscal area, which includes not only the euro area countries but also those member states whose national currencies are linked to the euro and are directly affected by all decisions taken by the ecb. i have repeatedly proposed the establishment as soon as possible of a european credit rating agency, which would enable the economies of the member states to be assessed objectively and independently on the basis of clear and transparent rating criteria. i also support the call in the report for the commission to take all the necessary steps to create a european monetary fund, which would remove the need for the international monetary fund to participate in european credit policy and reduce the dependence of the member states on other international institutions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it welcomes the fact that the ecb has so far managed very well to keep hicp inflation at around 2%, despite several macro-financial shocks and volatile commodity prices, and in a period of low average gdp growth in the union. the ecb's primary objective is to maintain price stability and that this contributes to maintaining financial stability and adequate liquidity in financial markets. financial instability poses a serious threat to price stability over the medium term, which makes the functioning of the monetary policy stance more difficult. i believe that the ecb has played a crucial role in the emergency measures it has taken to maintain market stability.
in writing. − i agree with the 2010 annual report of the european central bank (ecb). the ecb has done a very good job, especially at a time of very low gdp growth and volatile commodity prices, which was difficult for europe as a whole. despite these factors, the ecb, through its contingency measures, has played a key role in preserving market, price and financial stability, and adequate liquidity in financial markets. the ecb has maintained a steady and active stance throughout the crisis. however, the ecb must ensure greater transparency in the performance of its tasks. i believe that the creation of a european credit rating fund is appropriate in order to break the current oligopoly in credit ratings and to promote fair competition. the commission must also make every effort to ensure that the european monetary fund is set up and operational as soon as possible. only by implementing these measures will the dependence of the member states on other international institutions and the imf be reduced, without the involvement of the imf in the future european credit policy.

in writing. − the european union's ambition to become the most competitive economy in the world is particularly influenced by the education of its citizens. one of the aspects of education is the number of people who are not leaving school. my country, lithuania, is one of the few that has already achieved its goal of reducing this figure to less than 10 percent. it would be nice to suggest that other countries take lessons from countries like lithuania, but the education system in each country is unique, reflecting cultural and social characteristics. in line with the general principles set out in the resolution, i would like to stress that, in the field of education, we must nevertheless take account of the specific features of each country and seek to find attractive individual solutions for each of them. at the supranational level, however, we can only encourage member states and the eu institutions to cooperate more closely and to exchange good practices.
in writing. − i support this resolution because school leaving is a major factor in unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. i believe that the implementation of appropriate measures at european union level can solve this problem and prevent the spread of poverty. it is worth noting that most member states still have a fragmented and poorly coordinated approach to tackling this problem. in particular, certain school reforms and the creation of a pupil advisory fund are needed. schools should be encouraged to abandon the traditional testing model so that a student's future prospects are not dependent on a one-day mark. evaluation should be an ongoing, ongoing process. it is also essential that member states continue to develop educational opportunities, innovate and diversify national education programmes through a variety of means. i support the idea of second chance schools, which would enable people who have left school to reintegrate into the education system, creating favourable conditions for them to reconcile their commitments to the educational institution with their work and family commitments.

in writing. − on 21 april 2009, the commission adopted a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1394/2006 establishing a financing instrument for cooperation with industrial and other high-income countries and territories (the instrument regulation). the proposal is part of the mid-term review of the external financing instruments. main objective to extend the scope of the regulation to include cooperation with developing countries falling within the scope of regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 of 18 december 2006 establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation in the field of geographical cooperation with developing countries in asia, central asia and latin america, and iraq, iran, yemen and south africa. the amended instrument regulation will provide an appropriate legal basis for (financing) activities which do not meet the criteria for official development assistance as set out by the development assistance committee of the organisation for economic cooperation and development and which, on this basis, do not fall within the scope of the instrument regulation. i supported the proposal as the amended regulation will further strengthen relations with countries that are both developing countries and important partners in the global economy, such as china, brazil and mexico, as well as with regions such as the middle east and central asia, asia, latin america and south africa.

in writing. − the customs union is one of the main pillars of the free movement of goods, economic development and growth of the internal market. customs play an important role in protecting the eu's financial interests, as the import of counterfeit and pirated goods into the eu leads to lost revenue and infringements of intellectual property rights, and counterfeit products can pose a serious risk to the safety and health of european consumers. customs today are primarily faced with increasing import, export and transit volumes, although resources remain limited, and it is therefore of particular importance to ensure the efficient and effective management of customs procedures. i agree that the modernised customs code adopted in 2008 is essential to improve the current situation and to ensure a smooth, well-functioning and simple customs system. i believe that e-customs, and in particular centralised customs clearance, is one of the most important aspects of customs modernisation and simplification, which would enhance the eu's economic competitiveness and allow for the development of reliable trade relations with third countries.
in writing. − in 2013, all member states' customs authorities must introduce uniform it equipment and, as they cannot do so, it is proposed to postpone this date. companies also claim that it will be difficult for them to adapt to the new rules so quickly. the commission has made such a proposal. i think this is an important measure to simplify and really harmonise customs procedures in order to contribute to strengthening the european economy. i also agree that the widespread application of simplified customs procedures for imports, which aims to reduce customs formalities and controls before goods are released, is one of the most important components of eu customs policy. more than 71% of all customs procedures were simplified, but these procedures resulted in unjustified losses to the eu budget and in irregularities related to eu trade policy. the competitiveness of the european economy is of paramount importance, especially if the internal market is to be revived. customs has an important role to play in improving and influencing competitiveness, as simplification of customs legislation and promotion of electronic customs facilitate economic growth. to fulfil its full potential, customs must be modern, cooperative, responsive and active.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the right to information in criminal proceedings. the european union has set itself the objective of fostering and developing an area of freedom, security and justice. in accordance with the conclusions of the european council in tampere on 15 and 16 october 1999, the principle of mutual recognition should become the basis for judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters in the european union, as enhancing the mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions and ensuring the necessary harmonisation of legislation would facilitate cooperation between public authorities and the judicial protection of the rights of individuals. the degree of implementation of the principle of mutual recognition depends to a large extent on various criteria, including mechanisms for safeguarding the rights of suspects or accused persons and common minimum standards necessary to facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition. this is one of the foundations of the rule of law and i therefore agree with the rapporteur that this directive should apply to suspects and accused persons irrespective of their legal status, nationality or citizenship. the specific conditions and rules for the provision of information on an arrest or detention should be laid down by member states in their national law, subject to the proviso that the exercise of this right should not interfere with the proper conduct of criminal proceedings.
in writing. − this proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council aims to establish common minimum standards for the right to information in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. the proposal aims to improve the rights of suspects or accused persons. the establishment of common minimum requirements for these rights should facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition, thereby improving judicial cooperation between the member states of the eu. on 30 november 2009, the council adopted an action plan to strengthen the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, which calls for the adoption of measures relating to the right to interpretation and interpretation, the right to information on rights and information on charges, the right to legal advice and legal aid, the right to information of relatives, employers and consular authorities and the specific measures for the protection of vulnerable suspects or accused persons. i voted in favour of this document, which is the second measure of the action plan (the first measure concerned the right to interpretation and translation), which will help to better ensure the rights of suspects or accused persons throughout the eu and will help to strengthen judicial cooperation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because suspects and accused persons must know their procedural rights and they must be respected, as this is the only way to ensure a fair and impartial trial. both suspects and accused persons shall be given all necessary information concerning the charges against them, the nature and the grounds of the charges. all member states should therefore cooperate as effectively as possible to ensure common standards of the right to information in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. the provisions of this directive set out minimum requirements. member states may grant more rights than those provided for in this directive in order to ensure a higher level of protection in cases not specifically provided for in this directive. this directive therefore aims, in particular, to promote the right to liberty, the right to a fair trial and the rights of the defence. the proper implementation of the main provisions of this directive will significantly improve the effectiveness of the rights of suspects and accused persons by ensuring that they are informed of their rights.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as an example of a guideline for the communication on the rights of persons detained under a european arrest warrant. the sole purpose of this example is to show what a rights notice could look like, in order to make it easier for national authorities to draw up such a notice at national level. member states are not obliged to use this model. when drawing up their rights notice, they may amend this template to comply with the applicable national rules and add additional useful information. i agree that the competent authorities should inform the suspect or accused person without delay, orally or in writing, of the rights under national law which are essential to ensure a fair trial, as provided for in the directive. in order to ensure that the suspect or accused person exercises those rights effectively in practice, that information should be provided without delay during the proceedings and at the latest before the first formal questioning of the suspect or accused person by the police or another competent authority.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because this directive will ensure that every suspect and accused person, regardless of his or her legal status, nationality or citizenship, has the right to a fair trial in criminal proceedings in all eu countries. it should be noted that the right to information in criminal proceedings is one of the many means of ensuring a fair trial that aims to increase confidence in the common eu area of justice. in this context, i consider it appropriate to lay down at least minimum requirements which would facilitate the application of the principle of mutual recognition and improve judicial cooperation between the member states.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european protection order (epo) which is a new legal instrument that will provide continuous protection of victims of violence when they move from one member state to another. i support the position of the rapporteur that the new legal instrument will significantly help those who suffer from violence and wish to lead a normal life. the epo was first conceived to be a tool to protect victims of gender violence, but it will also cover victims of any crime, such as victims of human trafficking, genital mutilation, organised crime and terrorism, as long as they have an identified perpetrator. an epo may also be requested to safeguard relatives of a beneficiary of a protection order. an epo would only apply to protection measures taken on criminal matters, but it will be complemented by separate legislation on the mutual recognition of protection afforded by civil law. i agree that this instrument has to be further developed but it is a very important first step to show that the eu stands strongly against gender violence or any other type of violence, and will continue to do so in the future.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the draft european protection order directive is based on the initiative of 12 eu member states. the adoption of this directive will establish measures that will enable the executing state to continue to ensure the protection of individuals against the criminal activities of another person that may endanger their life, physical and psychological integrity, dignity, personal freedom or sexual integrity. the main objective is to prevent new criminal activity, as well as to reduce the consequences of previous criminal acts and to provide better protection for victims. this directive focuses on protection measures applicable in criminal matters and, in view of the different legal traditions of the member states in this field, it will need to be complemented in the future by a similar mechanism for the mutual recognition of protection measures applicable in civil matters. the council has undertaken to ensure that the provisions of this directive complement those of the european protection order directive and that the common scope of these two instruments allows member states to cooperate, irrespective of the nature of their national systems, in order to provide victims with the maximum possible protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it represents a major step forward in the european parliament towards the creation of a uniform system of protection for victims of crime throughout the european union. the european protection order is a document that commits law enforcement authorities in all eu countries to cooperate in the future in the protection of victims or potential victims of crime. this means that, if law enforcement authorities decide that potential victims of crime or victims of crime are in need of special protection to prevent an imminent or even greater danger in the future, the decision would be valid throughout the european union. thus, for example, if lithuanian law enforcement authorities decide that a person's life, physical, psychological or sexual integrity is in real danger and therefore grant him protection, their decision would also be valid in another eu member state. therefore, if a person travels or is threatened with relocation to another eu country, the foreign law enforcement authorities would take over and provide protection for that person in their own country.
in writing. − i have endorsed the document because this directive will establish measures which will enable the executing state to continue to ensure the protection of individuals against the criminal activities of another person which may endanger their life, physical and psychological integrity, dignity, personal freedom or sexual integrity. the main objective is to prevent new criminal activity, as well as to reduce the consequences of previous criminal acts and to provide better protection for victims. our main objective is to strengthen the rights of victims in the eu.
in writing. − criminal law is essentially a matter for the member states. however, the implementation of a single area of justice inevitably requires the harmonisation of certain measures, in particular those relating to the safeguarding of the rights of individuals. the european protection order is precisely what will ensure adequate protection for victims not only in the country of the proceedings but also in other eu countries. i welcome the agreement reached by the european parliament and the council on the document and look forward to its swifter implementation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, due to the transnational nature of the cases, their scale or their potential impact, individual member states are not in a position to adequately protect persons at risk. however, in a common area of justice without internal borders, the victim must be protected against a new criminal offence or the consequences of a previous criminal offence must be reduced in relation to him. therefore, in order to protect the life, physical and psychological integrity, dignity, personal freedom and other rights of the victim, it is necessary to establish a legal framework to ensure that eu protection orders are issued and enforced in all member states. in particular, the level of protection granted to a person in one member state must be maintained and granted accordingly in the other member state to which he moves. to achieve this, it is necessary to establish a common set of measures applicable at eu level, which establish obligations and sanctions for the person who poses a risk.
in writing. − this proposal is part of the eu's efforts to develop a comprehensive immigration policy. the european council of tampere on 15 and 16 october 1999 stressed that the european union should ensure a level playing field for third-country nationals legally residing in the territory of the member states and that they should be granted rights and obligations similar to those enjoyed by eu citizens. in view of the demographic challenges facing the eu, legal migration and a well-managed migration policy should help member states to meet current and future labour needs and contribute to the economic expansion and sustainable development of the eu member states. to achieve these objectives, this proposal aims to ensure equal rights for all third-country workers legally resident in a member state but not yet entitled to long-term resident status and to introduce a single application procedure for a single residence and work permit. such a single authorisation will enable member states to better manage and control the presence of third-country nationals on their territories for work purposes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the single residence and work permit directive is one of the first and most important steps forward in the european union's migration policy. we tried to find the best possible solution that would be acceptable to all third-country workers legally living and working in the european union, and this led to a fairly long discussion and negotiation with the council. unfortunately, we cannot find a common position within the european parliament itself on the inclusion of certain categories of workers in the content of this directive, i.e. seasonal workers, intra-corporate transferees, asylum seekers. for this reason, this directive will not be a framework directive, which was intended to simplify administrative procedures and regulate the entry and work of all third-country workers in the eu member states. this directive does not therefore fully enshrine the principle of legal equality for all third-country workers. although it was not possible to reach agreement on all the points, the final agreement on this directive managed to include a provision on the transferability of pensions and on the right of third-country workers to vocational training.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal, as one application procedure and one permit (to live and work) should be established for third-country nationals wishing to reside in a member state for work purposes, in order to reduce red tape, and it is also necessary to provide for common rights for all third-country workers legally resident in a member state. the general rights of third-country workers should be ensured by establishing areas where they are treated on an equal footing with nationals.
in writing. −when we admit workers from third countries, especially highly qualified professionals, to the european union, we must also provide them with the right conditions for authorisation and employment. reducing bureaucracy throughout the process and simplifying the process is therefore a positive step. i am glad that the council agrees with him.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution and supported the european parliament's position at second reading. currently, micro-entities are subject to the same rules as larger companies. the reporting rules applicable to micro-entities have been found to be disproportionate to their specific accounting needs, resulting in a cost burden that may interfere with the proper use of capital for production purposes. the commission proposal for a directive aims to simplify the business environment of micro-entities, and in particular the requirements for financial reporting, in order to promote their competitiveness and enable them to develop. the amendments to the directive should reduce the administrative burden, while still ensuring adequate protection and information for stakeholders, and allowing the reporting requirements of micro-entities to be aligned with the real needs of users and promoters. i agree with parliament's position that the commission should present a report on the situation of micro-entities no later than five years after the entry into force of the directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which confirms the european parliament's position on the council's position on the amendments to the fourth enterprise directive. the amended directive lays down provisions for the annual accounts of certain types of companies relating to micro-entities. the european commission proposed amendments to this directive as early as 2009. the position adopted today by the european parliament proposes to clarify the provision allowing member states to exempt micro-entities from the general requirement to publish annual accounts, provided that balance sheet information is properly submitted to at least one designated competent authority under national law and provided that the information is transmitted to the business register. the european parliament also adopted a compromise agreement with the council which establishes new, higher thresholds for the criteria for classifying enterprises as small and medium-sized enterprises or micro-enterprises, respectively. thus, for undertakings whose balance sheet total does not exceed eur 350 000 per year and whose net turnover is eur 700 000 per year, the directive allows the derogation from the disclosure of balance sheet information provided for therein.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as it can be and sometimes is difficult for micro-entities to publish annual reports. at the same time, member states need to ensure that the requirements laid down in this directive are complied with. therefore, member states should be allowed to exempt micro-entities from the general requirement to publish annual accounts, provided that the balance sheet information is properly submitted to at least one designated competent authority under national law and provided that the information is transmitted to a business register where a copy of the document can be obtained on request. in this case, the obligation to publish all accounting documents under article 47 of directive 78/660/eec in accordance with article 3 (5) of directive 2009/101/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 16 september 2009 on the coordination of safeguards which, for the protection of the interests of members and third parties, are required by member states of companies within the meaning of the second paragraph of article 48 of the treaty, with a view to making such safeguards equivalent does not apply. member states may, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3, provide for exemptions from certain requirements of this directive for companies which, at the balance sheet date, do not exceed the thresholds of two of the following three criteria (micro-entities): balance sheet total eur 350 000, net turnover eur 700 000, average number of employees in the financial year 10. in my view, it is necessary to reduce the administrative burden on micro-entities in accounting, as these entities are overburdened in some eu member states.
in writing. − i think it is appropriate to allow member states to exempt micro-entities from the general requirement to publish annual accounts, provided that the balance sheet information is properly presented under national law and that these companies do not exceed certain established criteria. the application of such an exemption will reduce the administrative burden on smes and simplify the business environment. furthermore, the relaxation of financial reporting requirements, taking into account the needs of smes, will increase the competitiveness of micro-entities and allow them to exploit their growth potential more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the financial management provisions applicable to certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. the financial and budgetary crisis has led some member states to limit their budgets and may result in their failure to meet their commitments under the community's co-financing programmes (the structural and cohesion funds, the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european fisheries fund). these member states risk losing community support from the eafrd unless they provide evidence that they are allocating adequate national funding. i therefore supported the commission's proposal to temporarily increase the maximum eu co-financing rate for programmes implemented in member states receiving support under the european financial stability facility (currently greece, ireland and portugal) and in non-euro area member states under the balance of payments facility (currently latvia and romania). this temporary increase in community co-financing, granted at the request of the member state concerned, would help to reduce the amount of appropriate national financing needed for the financial years 2011 and 2012. i am convinced that this funding model would help to allocate the funds allocated to the rural economy and contribute to the overall economic recovery in these member states and, at the same time, in the eu as a whole.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution and supported the european parliament's position at first reading. in its proposal for a regulation, the commission proposes to temporarily increase the maximum union co-financing rate (up to 95%) for programmes implemented in member states benefiting from the european financial stability facility (greece, ireland and portugal) and in non-euro area member states under the balance of payments facility (latvia, hungary, romania). there is a risk that member states benefiting from financial assistance programmes may default due to budgetary constraints and lose community support (unless they provide evidence that they are allocating adequate national funding, at the latest 2 years after the initial payment year). the measure proposed by the commission will allow these member states to reduce their contribution to projects co-financed by the european union. this will allow earlier disbursement of funds already committed from the eu cohesion fund, the rural development fund or the fisheries fund, and the start of programmes delayed due to a lack of national funding.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it supports the commission's proposal to temporarily increase the co-financing rate of the union for the support from the european agricultural fund for rural development to those member states which, as a result of the current economic and financial crisis, are unable to meet their commitments under the community co-financing programmes. without these temporary measures, member states such as greece, ireland, portugal, latvia and romania and their economies would be at risk of losing their long-term competitiveness. the european parliament therefore supported the commission's proposal to temporarily increase the co-financing rate of the union until 2013 in order to maintain the necessary level of investment in these countries and thus ensure their further economic development. such temporary measures will not affect the overall rural development allocation.
in writing. − the financial and budgetary crisis has led some member states to limit their budgets and may prevent them from meeting their commitments under community co-financing programmes (structural and cohesion funds, european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the edf). these member states risk losing community support from the eafrd unless they provide evidence that they are allocating adequate national funding as provided for in article 70 of regulation (ec) no 1698/2005 no later than 2 years after the year of initial payment (n+2 rule). in the light of these circumstances, the commission proposes to temporarily increase the maximum union co-financing rate for programmes implemented in member states benefiting from the european financial stability facility (currently greece, ireland and portugal) and in non-euro area member states under the balance of payments facility (currently latvia and romania). this temporary increase in community co-financing, granted at the request of the member state concerned, would help to reduce the amount of adequate national financing needed for the financial years 2011 and 2011. i have supported this document because it would help to allocate the funds allocated to the rural economy and contribute to the general economic recovery in these member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because some countries, because of the financial and economic crisis, are unable to meet their obligations in the implementation of community co-financing programmes and are therefore at risk of losing the support they are entitled to. in order to protect those states, i believe it is appropriate to increase the maximum rate of union co-financing at least temporarily. this would not only reduce the amount of national funding but also provide a significant contribution to the restoration of economic stability in countries experiencing or threatened with serious financial stability problems.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on barriers to trade and investment. open and fair trade is the best way to ensure and maintain a level playing field for european companies competing at global level. the commission must take the initiative to eliminate or at least reduce the restrictive effects of non-tariff barriers on the ability of european firms to enter foreign markets. i agree with the rapporteur that this must be a key priority for eu trade policy under the europe 2020 strategy. the commission should raise the issue of non-tariff barriers with all the eu's trading partners, and it is particularly important that it addresses this issue with the strategic partners with whom the eu has the largest trade. the eu also needs to carefully review its own trade measures in order to remove all illegal barriers to open and free trade and to become a true leader in tackling non-tariff barriers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. eu companies still face significant obstacles when operating in third countries. one of the main problems remains non-tariff barriers, which encompass all trade restrictive measures on imports other than customs duties (tariffs). non-tariff barriers include direct factors affecting prices (such as export subsidies or rebates, countervailing or anti-dumping duties, currency manipulation, import valuation methods, additional customs duties, unjustified standards and verification procedures) and indirect factors affecting prices (such as the granting of import licences, import quotas and so-called voluntary export restrictions). the eu's trade policy should, in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, give regulatory priority to the removal or reduction of unjustified non-tariff barriers and other regulatory barriers applied by countries that are key strategic partners of the eu through regulatory dialogue. it is also necessary to resolve the accessibility of public procurement to eu companies in third countries. the procurement procedures of the eu's strategic partners are generally not open to foreign participants and still have relatively few international commitments, with the eu being much more open than other countries in this area. eu law allows european and foreign companies to participate in public procurement without discrimination, and the eu needs to step up its efforts to reach agreements with the union's main trading partners to allow european companies to participate in public procurement in third countries on fair and impartial terms.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to draw attention to the trade and investment barriers that prevent european union companies from entering third country markets. this report focuses in particular on so-called non-tariff barriers which have a direct or indirect impact on the prices of goods. such barriers may include export subsidies or rebates, manipulation of the exchange rate, lengthy customs procedures, unjustified standards and verification procedures, as well as the setting of import licences, import quotas or export restrictions. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission, which is responsible for international negotiations on behalf of the eu, to step up its fight against non-tariff barriers in the world trade forums. parliament also called on the commission to pay greater attention to ensuring that free trade agreements concluded between the eu and third countries respect the principle of reciprocity in relation to market access, i.e. that they are mutually beneficial for both parties to the agreement.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as the eu should actively defend its industry against violations of agreed rules, wto standards and principles by its trading partners, where necessary, using all the means at its disposal, including multilateral and bilateral dispute settlement systems and trade defence measures compatible with the wto. one of the regulatory priorities of the new eu trade policy under the europe 2020 strategy should be the removal or reduction of unjustified non-tariff barriers and other regulatory barriers imposed by countries that are key strategic partners of the eu through regulatory dialogue. i believe that any obstacles arising from inconsistent application of bilateral and multilateral trade rules are not justified. the regulatory dialogue should take into account the right of all states to strengthen human rights, environmental rules, social rules and public health. the commission should clearly distinguish between non-tariff barriers that lead to unfair distortions of competition and those that reflect legitimate public policy objectives, in particular those relating to public health and the environment. requiring the application of the principle of reciprocal market access to industrialized and developing countries should be an integral part of the eu's trade strategy as much as the removal or reduction of non-tariff barriers.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. i believe that the trade and investment barriers faced by the european services sectors need to be given special attention in the light of the current economic situation. it should be noted that non-tariff measures and various crisis measures are of particular importance in view of the higher value added of the services sector and the eu's position as the largest exporter of services. it is essential that the eu actively defends its industry and demands that the eu's main strategic partners remove or at least reduce the scope of unjustified non-tariff barriers and other regulatory measures.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, tomorrow the sakharov prize for freedom of thought will be awarded to representatives from the arab spring, from tunisia to egypt, from libya and syria. unfortunately not all of them will be with us tomorrow. our syrian friends are still fighting for their rights and therefore cannot be with us here in strasbourg. but honourable members, the arab spring is a good example of the universality of human rights and of peoples’ aspiration to live in democratic systems. this year’s winners embody the dramatic changes that have defined the past 12 months, and i wish to pay tribute to them now. whether through dramatic acts of self-sacrifice, endurance in prison, or daily confronting injustice, they remind us of the true meaning of courage. by drawing cartoons or organising online they remind us that courage manifests itself in many different ways. it is about speaking the truth and refusing to be intimidated. this is the case, too, for this year’s nobel prize winner from yemen, mrs karman, whom i had the opportunity to meet with just a few days ago. she deserves all the recognition she is now receiving as a result of her struggle for women’s rights. it is also the case of the group of afghan women whom i met at the beginning of the international afghanistan conference in bonn and who are a real inspiration to us. speaking out fearlessly is something that has defined the careers of many in this house, and none more so than president buzek. under him, parliament’s work on human rights has significantly increased and i would like to take this opportunity to thank him for his dedication. 2011 has been a particularly active year for human rights in parliament. the subcommittee on human rights, chaired first by heidi hautala, and now by barbara lochbihler, has developed a great number of activities, including the de keyser report on democracy, which inspired me, in particular on the idea of the global and coherent approach to human rights and to democratisation and civic participation. the historic developments in our neighbourhood have significantly advanced human rights. the bringing down of longstanding repressive regimes has led to the formation of new governments and to free and fair elections. the continuing violent crackdowns in syria, repression in belarus, and protracted conflicts, including in the middle east, require us to keep up the pressure. the events of this year have served to highlight the vital links between human rights and democracy. it has led to a new approach for the european union, which aims to provide greater support to partners engaged in building what i have termed ‘deep democracy’. that is where the right to vote is accompanied by effective freedom of thought, freedom of speech, freedom of expression, freedom of association and freedom of religion or belief, underpinned by impartial justice, public security from accountable protection forces, and access to a competent and non-corrupt civil service. we have also continued using our financial instruments to promote and protect human rights. in 2011 the european instrument for democracy and human rights funded more than 1 200 operations in more than 130 countries. even in the toughest environments, where basic rights and freedoms are the most repressed, we have been able to provide assistance to civil society. to give just a few examples: our funding has been used to fight media and cyber censorship to keep information flowing out of syria or north korea; in uzbekistan, belarus and egypt it provided legal defence for hundreds of political opponents arbitrarily imprisoned. it also supported their families and their lawyers, who risked imprisonment for taking up their case. it supported the rehabilitation victims, those having undergone torture in zimbabwe or sri lanka, and those affected by the campaigns of mass rape in east congo or libya. and it supported democratic transition in morocco, tunisia, ivory coast, burma myanmar and libya, also helping in the support and observation of elections in niger, peru and zambia. we have also kept up its work to advance human rights on the multilateral stage in 2011. the un special session on libya, which made the historic recommendations to suspend libya from the human rights council, was a turning point in allowing this to respond to emergencies. several times this year the eu raised the human rights situation in syria, in the hrc and in the general assembly, building an alliance of countries from all regions, including the arab world. our role was instrumental in establishing the independent commission of inquiry on the human rights situation in syria. in june, we secured the adoption of a human rights council resolution on the human rights situation in belarus, with whom we have tried to engage to improve its human rights record. i continue to highlight the human rights situations in north korea and in burma myanmar, reflecting the developments on the ground. i expect the new civilian government in burma myanmar will push ahead with political reforms and re-engage with the international community. i hope aung san suu kyi will finally be able to come to this parliament to receive the sakharov prize that she was awarded 21 years ago. we continue our efforts to build consensus on freedom of religion or belief. i have also maintained my focus on promoting the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people through the implementation of the eu’s toolbox. promoting and protecting the universal rights of freedom of religion, belief and sexual orientation are central to the eu’s approach. we have also begun work on the campaign on forced marriages, which destroy the lives of so many young people, girls and boys. when i was engaged in taking legislation through on forced marriages in the country i know best and come from, i was surprised to learn that 15% of those who ring the helplines on forced marriages are boys. either young boys forced into marriage with a girl they have never met, or young gay men forced into marriage for what reasons i do not know. in brussels, we have been working to put in place the arrangements foreseen by the treaty of lisbon to put human rights firmly at the centre of our policy. we are committed not only to guarantee but also to promote their universal respect by all. the charter of fundamental rights has contributed to promoting consistency between the eu’s internal and external policies, and the eu accession to the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms will be a cornerstone for future developments. with the creation of the eeas, we have begun to work more closely with parliament, with member states and with civil society. the department created within the eeas on human rights and democracy is currently being reviewed to make it more effective. we have established a network of focal points in all eu delegations that contribute to delivering our eu human-rights policy goals. ms lochbihler gave us the privilege of meeting with all heads of eu delegations recently, at the beginning of this month, and i hope that the honourable member was able to see that human rights are at the core of the activities of the people on the ground. each of our member states have played their own part in bringing their national legislation in line with eu standards of full compliance with all the relevant treaties and conventions on human rights in the wider un framework. but the indivisibility and universality of human rights is increasingly being challenged globally. we will continue to counter this. the ongoing economic crisis should not be used as a pretext for those who want to dilute certain rights. all that i have just said has helped me to inform the review of the eu human rights policy that was first announced before this house and i am pleased that my contribution will be tabled very shortly. i want to outline some main points from that now. the text i will table this week is a contribution to an ongoing debate. it is necessarily concise, meaning that not every detail is reflected, but i hope that it offers a good basis for future work with this parliament and with the council. a number of meps have been involved in the process from the beginning, as when the chair of the subcommittee on human rights attended the eu ngo forum in july, which produced a first set of recommendations for inclusion. since then there have been various informal meetings and contacts with parliament, including of course with the human rights subcommittee, which contributed greatly to the process, and i want to thank particularly richard howitt for the work that he has done. though much of the discussion about the review of our policy has centred on the process, i also want to say something about the substance. crucially, i want the outcome of the review to deliver a strong reaffirmation of what the eu stands for: the universality of human rights as binding international commitments and norms. the message must go out that human rights are not negotiable and are inviolable. against that backdrop, i have identified four main priority areas for action. first, overhauling the eu’s delivery mechanisms. i want to make our policy more effective, adapting it better to the specific circumstances of each country, coupled with a global campaign-based approach. a key element here is the strengthening of relations with civil society, so that ngos are better engaged as full partners with the european union. second, achieving a joined-up approach in our policies. this is the idea i have spoken of often, to break down traditional silos, and have human rights running as a silver thread throughout a truly integrated range of external policies. third, building strong partnerships encompassing the whole world: multilaterally working through the un and the icc; regionally developing work, for example with the arab league; and bilaterally through our dialogues. fourth, speaking as one, which does not mean with a single voice but rather a coordinated and consistent message from everyone, ensuring that the invaluable work of parliament and the member states is brought together for the benefit of the whole. i propose to use thematic campaigns to deliver on specific cross-cutting themes. this has already been done to great effect in support of the icc and the abolition of the death penalty. i believe that approach can be extended, for example to promote the rights of women, by setting realistic, time limited, achievable, objectives. i am keen to make the best possible use of tailor-made country strategies on human rights, which should be driven by recommendations made locally. whilst they should stand firm on the universality of human rights and the global standards that apply to all, i believe this will allow us to deliver more across the board than a one-size-fits-all approach for 150 countries. it should allow us, too, to make the most effective use of the assorted tools we have, while engaging with due respect with the views of our partners on the ground. eu delegations are well placed to take this forward. i want to work closely, too, with all my commission colleagues, to bring human rights fully into the key community policies, such as development and trade, building on recent communications on the future of development, budget support, corporate social responsibility and the neighbourhood policy. i agree with ms lochbihler when she says that parliament has a key role to monitor, assess and provide political accountability for the eu’s actions in the human rights field. our financial support for human rights must go beyond the european instrument for democracy and human rights and should be reflected in other eu financial instruments. i will work to ensure that human rights are taken into account consistently in the programming of all eu external financial assistance. it is clear that in order to be credible when we raise human rights concerns with others, we have to make sure that our own house is in order too. so i am determined to instil a human rights culture in the eu’s emerging diplomatic structures. we already have an active eu training policy, but there is much more to be done in this direction and we are ready to take that forward. and i am very open-minded on the idea of appointing an eu special representative for human rights, to act as a catalyst and to raise our profile internationally. i look forward to discussing these proposals with members of this house over the coming weeks and months and to getting their views as we take this issue further forward. this parliament, this house of democratically elected representatives from all over the european union, is a champion of human rights, in the european union and in the world. your reports and your opinions inspire us and help to guide the work that we do. it is for this reason that being in front of you today on this topic is not merely my obligation, but it is also my privilege.
