i am pleased to welcome the rapporteurs for their profound review of the european neighbourhood policy and for their valuable proposals. the arab spring showed that seemingly stable regimes are crumbling like a house of cards in the internet age. many colleagues referred to the successful statement of the report as 'more for more' and 'more for more'. i think that principle is important for the belarusian regime. the european union is right to impose tough sanctions on the persons in charge of the companies they control, but sanctions and trade restrictions should not harm the already difficult lives of ordinary belarusians, who are suffering from hyperinflation. it is regrettable that the belarusian authorities have not responded to the initiative of brussels to facilitate the visa regime. the commission is also proposing to extend the visa waiver to all non-eu citizens of the european union.
the european parliament has repeatedly expressed the view that information plays a crucial role in ensuring that consumers consume only safe food. only by receiving complete and non-misleading information about the products consumed will the consumer be able to make an informed choice. this year we took a step further in this direction with the adoption of the regulation on food information to consumers, and now we are taking it further by introducing additional requirements for specific food groups. today, many stores sell drinks called fruit juices. however, it is often unclear what fruit is used to make them, how much sugar or sugar substitutes are used, whether the juice is the actual fruit, or what ingredients are used to make the drink. the document we are discussing today is another step towards clarity, defining what can be called fruit juices. it is of particular importance that the same requirements apply to all juices marketed in the european union. therefore, no derogation should be granted for juices imported into the european union. the european union is a market large enough for producers to adapt to our requirements. we can vote on this directive tomorrow at the first reading. this is important in view of the length of the procedure in an otherwise case. although i am somewhat disappointed that the text agreed at the trilogue does not reflect all the amendments adopted by the committee, i nevertheless believe that the agreement of all parties is more important in this case, which i believe will contribute to legal clarity and consumer protection.
the regulation we voted on today is of great importance for the european union's water bodies. this is also very important news for the baltic sea, whose waters are suffering from phosphorus compound pollution, which causes algal blooms that are becoming more intense and active every year. according to the helkom commission, if phosphates were to be phased out, the bloom of the baltic sea would be reduced by 24%. today, we took the first step, setting the half-gram limit on washing machines. the fact that a directly applicable act has been adopted will not allow countries which have not regulated the use of phosphates to rely solely on the goodwill of household chemical manufacturers and the awareness of consumers, as has been the case up to now. the maximum phosphate levels used in the eu vary widely, resulting in about 16 000 tonnes of phosphorus entering the baltic sea each year. i hope that the member states will support our position and that the entry into force of this regulation and the acceleration of waste water treatment will bring about a significant improvement in the situation of the baltic and other seas.
in writing. − in its conclusions of 17 june 2010, the european council stressed that iceland meets the political criteria set by the copenhagen european council of 1993 and endorsed the commission's opinion on iceland's application for eu membership. the european council therefore decided to open negotiations with iceland. iceland is therefore a candidate country. on 16 and 17 december 2010, the european council endorsed the council conclusions of 14 december 2010 on enlargement and agreed to grant montenegro candidate status. i voted in favour of this document as the commission proposes to the council and parliament to amend council regulation (ec) no 1085/2006 of 17 july 2006 establishing a pre-accession facility in order to move iceland and montenegro from the list of potential candidate countries to the list of candidate countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which proposes to move iceland and montenegro from the list of potential candidate countries to the list of candidate countries. it is good to see that both countries have made great progress towards eu integration and have fulfilled the political requirements, the copenhagen criteria. it is worth noting that the decision to move these countries to the candidate list will have a positive impact on the eu enlargement processes, which are one of the eu's top priorities. it should be noted that iceland is an exceptional candidate country in terms of its alignment with eu law through the application of the agreement on the european economic area and in terms of its economic and social development. the eu has also made progress in the area of the protection of the environment. however, in order for further processes and negotiations to proceed smoothly and efficiently, both sides must continue to make every effort to implement internal reforms and to properly implement the requirements of membership and to assume the obligations associated with eu membership.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. the sector of these products is a sufficiently important part of the industry of the european union. however, taking only one example orange juice, it should be noted that more than 82% of the eu consumption of juice is produced mainly in brazil and the united states, i.e. juice produced in the eu territory accounts for less than 20% of the eu consumption of orange juice. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is important to support the european sector by aligning the directive with international law and the code and by establishing the same rules for all products marketed in the community. as stated in the recitals in the preamble to the directive, the aim is to facilitate the free movement of those products. the european union produces high-quality fruit juices that help to maintain a healthy and balanced diet. they are produced to the sustainability standards that our laws promote. it is therefore fair for eu companies to require that the same quality standards apply to all products traded in the eu. we also need to take into account environmental aspects: local products do not have to be transported over long distances, which results in high co2 emissions. it should be stressed that this document is not about european protectionist measures, but about the continuing commitment to sustainability in all sectors of our economy. the overall quality of the product shall also be assessed in the light of the ethical, ecological and qualitative aspects of the product.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution and supported parliament's position at first reading. the commission proposal aims to amend for the second time the 2001 council directive on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. the rules laid down in the directive governing the composition, use of traditional descriptions, production specifications and labelling of such products are designed to ensure their free movement within the european union. the proposal reaffirms the distinction between fruit juices and fruit juices from concentrate, simplifies the provisions on the return of taste and aroma, provides for the removal of sugars from the list of authorised ingredients and adds tomatoes to the list of fruits used in the production of fruit juices. i agree that the commission and the member states should carry out targeted information campaigns to inform consumers of the different categories of juices and similar products provided for in this directive and to help them distinguish, for example, between juices and nectars.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that we must create the conditions for further development of the european union's fruit juice and similar products industry. the eu directive adopted in 2001 already introduced a major and important change in industrial regulation and, above all, in consumer protection. in other words, it was under this directive that producers were obliged to indicate on the labels whether the juice was made from a concentrate or whether it was genuine squeezed fruit juice. at this stage of the review of the said directive, it is proposed to maintain this division. another key feature of the revised directive is that it is more consistent with the provisions of the food code and it is decided whether the juice produced in the european union can be subject to certain techniques that are applicable to the juice produced in other regions of the world. for example, the addition of tangerine juice to orange juice, which the european parliament does not object to, not only enhances the colour and flavour of the juice but also, in some cases, meets the needs of certain categories of consumers. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it requires the maintenance of the double labelling system which distinguishes pressed fruit juices from those made from concentrate. it is difficult for consumers to distinguish clearly between the different categories of products covered by the directive. there is a lot of confusion, especially when it comes to the difference between juices and nectars. it is very important to clarify this difference in the presence or absence of sugar in these products, as this is particularly important for groups of consumers with special needs (diabetics, children, overweight people, etc.). all fruit juices and related products traded in the eu would be subject to the same legislation and particular attention should be paid to harmful practices. it is important to support the european sector by aligning the directive with international law and the code and by establishing the same rules applicable to all products traded within the community. the current directive will provide an opportunity for third country producers to improve product quality through more sustainable production processes. the same rules for all will help to avoid fraud and unfair competition and will help to provide clearer information to consumers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is appropriate to maintain the double labelling to distinguish pressed fruit juices from those made from concentrate. the implementation of the provisions of this directive will create the right conditions for consumers to choose a product that is as unprocessed as possible and as natural as possible. the dual classification will ensure that consumers are provided with accurate information and that the illustrations on the packaging do not mislead them as to the true composition of the juices. it should be noted that uniform rules throughout the community will allow the free movement of these products and will help to avoid fraud and unfair competition. in addition, in line with the provisions of this directive and with a view to more sustainable production processes, producers in third countries will be encouraged to improve the quality of their products.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household detergents. the aim of the current commission proposal for a regulation is to reduce the phosphorus content of detergents for household washing machines. phosphates enter our water system, rivers, streams, lakes, especially the danube basin and the baltic sea. phosphorus promotes excessive algal growth, which deprives other living organisms of oxygen and can produce toxins that kill fish, plants and other living species, as well as impairing water quality. so to clean up europe's waters, we need to reduce the amount of phosphorus that enters our continent's waters, and we need to do that globally. i therefore believe that the first priority should be to encourage the use of biological detergents with a minimum phosphate content and to limit the phosphate content of various household detergents by law. i therefore urge all eu member states to implement this regulation immediately and to make every effort to prevent the unnecessary large-scale use of phosphates. otherwise, we will leave future generations not the baltic sea, the danube basin or other bodies of water with diverse flora and fauna, but swamps.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution and supported parliament's position at first reading. the commission proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 648/2004 as regards the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household detergents aims to reduce the phosphorus used in household washing machine detergents. phosphorus is found in large quantities in household detergents and is directly released into our water systems, rivers, streams, lakes, especially the danube basin and the baltic sea. this leads to eutrophication excessive algal growth, which deprives other organisms of oxygen and can produce toxins that kill fish, plants and other species of organisms, as well as deteriorate water quality. the commission proposal aims to set limits on the content of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in detergents and to ensure that the proposed ban on the use of phosphates cannot be easily circumvented. i agree that it is appropriate to extend the restrictions on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household washing detergents to household automatic dishwasher detergents and to include them in the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. − i have supported the proposal as it aims to amend regulation (ec) no 648/2004 on detergents by setting limits on the levels of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household detergents in order to reduce the impact of detergents on the overall eutrophication of eu surface waters, taking into account the evaluations and impact assessment carried out by the commission in accordance with article 16 of regulation (ec) no 648/2004.

in writing. − i have voted in favour of this document because, in order to comply with international law, economic activities relating to the exploitation of natural resources in a non-self-governing territory must be of benefit to the people living in that territory and must take account of their wishes. it is essential that the legal representatives of the people of western sahara be consulted on any agreement envisaging the use of the natural resources of that territory. it is necessary to ensure that the future protocol fully respects the rules of international law, benefits the people of western sahara and takes into account their wishes. the fisheries partnership agreement itself must pursue economic and social objectives, based on close scientific and technical cooperation, in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. each protocol shall be economically, ecologically and socially sustainable and mutually beneficial.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the impact of the financial crisis on the defence sector in the eu member states, which calls for increased cooperation in the field of defence. member states collectively spend about eur 200 billion a year on defence, which represents only about a third of the us defence budget alone. european countries are already incapable of carrying out military operations (example recent libya intervention) without us support, whose share of all defence spending within nato has risen to 75%. i agree with the rapporteur that the financial crisis is a global phenomenon and it has also touched the defence sector. there is a common tendency to cut spending on defence in the member states, which is the subject of our concern. it is true that maintaining these expenditures, when we are in a financial crisis, where there are social pressures, is not an easy task. at the same time it is important to stress, thinking about our future, we simply cannot afford to neglect basic needs such as security and defence in such turbulent times.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the impact of the financial crisis on the defence sectors of the eu member states. eu member states spend a total of around eur 200 billion a year on defence. the reliance of member states on uncoordinated national defence planning decisions for a large proportion of defence spending leads not only to persistent capacity shortfalls but also to often unnecessary overcapacity and duplication, unprecedented industries and markets. most eu member states have recently seen their defence budgets cut as a result of the financial, economic and debt crises. this may have a negative impact on the military capabilities of countries and the eu's ability to effectively implement commitments related to peacekeeping, conflict prevention and strengthening international security. i share the parliament's position that member states must seek to offset the negative impact of the financial crisis on the defence sectors of the eu member states through greater european cooperation and coordination. without coordinated cuts in defence budgets, europe could lose some of its military capabilities altogether. member states therefore need to exchange information effectively and increase transparency on current and future defence budget cuts. it is also necessary to make effective use of the potential economies of scale offered by cooperation projects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that attention should be paid to the way in which member states finance their defence sector in times of crisis and economic hardship. this owninitiative report by the european parliament was drawn up in the light of the recent trend towards a major crisis-related reduction in the defence budgets of most eu member states, without any coordination at eu level. as the european parliament's report notes, the security situation is becoming increasingly complex and unpredictable both in europe and worldwide, and it is therefore proposed to maintain the pre-crisis level of european defence capabilities, as well as to rely less on the financing of defence spending by the united states in the north atlantic alliance. it is the latter aspect that is emphasised in the report, as it is believed that a strengthened european defence capability will increase the eu's strategic autonomy and make a major contribution to the collective security pursued by nato and other partnerships.
in writing. − i supported this document because defence is a public good, linked to the security of all european citizens, and all member states must contribute to it, in accordance with the principles of cooperation, burden-sharing and cost-effectiveness. the financial, economic and debt crises are reducing the defence budgets of most eu member states, with the potential for adverse effects on the military capabilities of countries and on the eu's ability to effectively implement its commitments to peace-keeping, conflict prevention and strengthening international security, in line with the principles of the united nations charter, unless member states are able to offset these adverse effects through increased european cooperation and coordination. member states need to urgently improve the transparency and openness of their defence markets. the competitiveness of the european defence industry needs to be enhanced, while ensuring that taxpayers' interests are properly protected.
in writing. − in times of economic upswing, not all nato countries spent 2% of gdp on defence. the defence budgets of eu member states will continue to decline following the economic crisis, with austerity measures and cuts in public spending. the situation has developed where one nato member country contributes as much as 75% of the total nato defence expenditure. while it is true that large-scale financing does not necessarily guarantee efficiency, it is necessary to seek new ways of cooperation between eu member states to avoid the negative impact of defence spending cuts on defence capabilities. european countries need to pool and share capacities in a coordinated way, and there is much to be done through joint european programmes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, in order to strengthen the european union's role in the world and preserve europe's technological capacity, while taking into account the specificities of each member state, a common defence industrial policy based on an economic approach is needed. it is worth noting that the enhanced european defence capability will contribute to the collective security pursued by the various partnerships, including nato. i believe that member states should implement permanent structured cooperation and define the conditions for the application of the solidarity and mutual defence provisions, improving the transparency and openness of their defence markets. i support the proposal that the eu should jointly purchase the most expensive and modern equipment and set up an eu headquarters for civil and military operations, which will help to maintain not only international peace and security but also provide opportunities for saving national budgets. it is worth noting that research and innovation play a crucial role in the security and defence sector. in this context, it is essential to maximise the synergies, development and independence of european defence and civil security research programmes. i believe that the european defence industry and the technological base will contribute to the creation of new jobs in this industrial sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the eu-russia summit of 15 december 2011. closer eu-russia cooperation, good neighbourly relations and a genuine strategic partnership are crucial to ensuring stability, security and prosperity in europe and beyond. i agree that the security of energy supply is one of the eu's key priorities and one of the main areas of cooperation with russia. the supply of natural resources should not be used as a political tool. it is important to strengthen the energy partnership with russia and to ensure that the eu speaks with one voice and shows strong internal solidarity in its relations with russia. i agree with parliament's position that the eu must ensure a reliable energy supply based on uniform standards for all eu member states. the diversity of energy suppliers and supply channels must also be ensured.
in writing. − you voted on this resolution as the european parliament reiterated its position on cooperation with russia and at the same time expressed its deep concern about the irregularities in the duma elections on 4 december 2011: on the day of the elections, numerous irregularities were reported in russia, including multiple votes, interference with party observers and falsification of ballots. the organisation of the elections has demonstrated that russia does not comply with the election standards set by the organisation for security and cooperation in europe (osce). parliament also expressed serious concern about the reports of falsification and the preliminary findings in the osce office for democratic institutions and human rights report on procedural irregularities, lack of media impartiality, obstruction of independent observers and insufficient separation of party and state. the european parliament therefore calls on the russian authorities to take account of the findings of the osce election observation report on democratic institutions and human rights, and in cooperation with the venice commission, to reform electoral laws to bring them into line with osce and council of europe standards and to implement these standards in practice, in order to ensure free and democratic presidential elections in 2012, with equal opportunities for opposition candidates.
in writing. − the russian people want the right to vote freely in fair elections and to feel in control of their country's future, and the european union to develop a strategic partnership with a democratic, secure and stable country that respects fundamental rights and freedoms and the sovereignty of its neighbours. we have to admit to ourselves that russia is moving selectively forward in its relations with the eu - what helps economic development is accepted, and concerns about democracy and human rights violations are simply dismissed. we may seek friendship with russia, but how far are we willing to go to gain it? i find it difficult to imagine a visa-free regime with a state whose government structures shelter people accused of crimes against humanity, such as in the case of mr golovatov, while russia refuses to cooperate in cases of this category, such as the january 13 and medinsky murders, while there is no substantial progress in the magnitsky case, while mr khodorkovsky is imprisoned. the movement of the russian people after the duma elections is a signal not only to democracy in russia, but also to us that civil society in the country is alive, people know their rights and are ready to demand them. we cannot let down the democratically minded section of russian society.
in writing. − the eu and russia are economically and politically interdependent. it is one of the eu's most important partners. in this context, i believe that the negotiations on a new partnership and cooperation agreement should proceed at a faster pace. it should cover in detail political, economic and social issues and security issues. particular attention should also be paid to strengthening the energy partnership in order to ensure the security of energy supply. russia's accession to the wto is welcome, which will create a more favourable environment for businesses in both countries and help to liberalise trade in the global economy.
in writing. − i am pleased that this resolution has been adopted, which recalls that russia is a permanent member of the council of europe, the osce and the un security council and is therefore committed to implementing and respecting the principles of democracy. following repeated warnings from the osce and european union institutions about the critical human rights situation in the country, electoral laws and politically motivated court decisions, the european court of human rights this year criticised the cumbersome registration procedure for political parties in russia. however, the december 4 russian state duma elections and the repressive response of the authorities to the ensuing widespread popular protests have once again highlighted the serious situation of democracy and human rights in the country, as evidenced by reports of widespread violations by the osce office for democratic institutions and human rights. the european parliament resolution sends a clear and damning signal to the russian leadership, which is why i have supported it. however, i do not agree that the visa-free regime with russia should be supported and continued. first, the state of democracy and human rights in russia does not meet the standards of a democratic state and the criteria for a visa-free regime. secondly, the number of russian citizens entering the eu is three times higher than the number of eu citizens going to russia, where they face various administrative and movement restrictions. third, the results and contribution of the visa facilitation regime to the dynamics of eu-russia relations have not yet been assessed. any discussion on visa-free travel between the eu and russia is therefore premature.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on european neighbourhood policy. its main objective is the absolute necessity of advocating our fundamental values in relations with our neighbouring countries. a new strategy with regard to the european neighbourhood policy (enp), aimed at empowering citizens, people and their organisations, as well as the regional and local authorities, will be put into practice by the eu, adapted to the socio-economic and political realities of each of the eu’s neighbouring countries. i agree with the rapporteur that it is essential to defend a bottom-up approach, stronger conditionality and stronger differentiation of this policy, ensuring a better targeted assistance to each eu neighbouring country and guaranteeing that funding matches political ambition. the eu should increase its support for institution-building, civil society and the will to start democratisation processes, supporting organised movements striving for positive democratic changes in their countries: in advancing women’s and children’s rights – in particular the civic and political participation of women, building and deepening the democratic principles of freedom, fair elections and the rule of law. the immediate economic assistance in order to foster socio-economic changes, which are preconditions for long-term stabilisation and prosperity, is also necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the review of the european neighbourhood policy. in may 2011, the european external action service and the european commission announced a new ambitious european neighbourhood policy (enp). the proposal sets out the main priorities and directions of the renewed esf strategy aimed at strengthening the eu's individual and regional relations with its neighbours by allocating more resources to wider reforms and increasing mutual accountability. i welcome the proposal to create a new european neighbourhood instrument and to increase the funding of the esf. i agree with parliament's view that it is important to strengthen the energy cooperation aspect of the european neighbourhood policy. it is necessary to ensure security of energy supply through diversification of sources and demand management, to take effective measures to respect the principle of solidarity in the energy sector and to promote the construction, modernisation and development of modern energy networks and infrastructure interconnections with the eu's neighbours. the strengthening of the eastern partnership will be a key factor in the development of the eu's border regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the position it expresses that the guidelines for the revision of the european neighbourhood policy, drawn up by the european commission, are moving in the right direction. in particular, the european parliament's report supports the 'more for more' and 'less for less' principle proposed by the commission, which means closer cooperation with the european union for those neighbouring countries which are successfully and actively implementing democratic reforms in their countries and, conversely, a cooling-off in relations with the eu for those countries which refuse or delay the implementation of these reforms. as a general rule, i also support the idea that such a tool of diplomatic pressure is appropriate to promote the development of democratic processes in neighbouring countries, but we must be very careful not to harm the ordinary citizens of those countries by such means. i believe that any aid and measures aimed at strengthening civil society in these countries, while putting pressure on the leadership of non-democratic regimes, will enable us to achieve the best results in strengthening democracy in neighbouring countries.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy needed to be revised in the light of the dramatic changes in the south, in order to achieve mutually beneficial cooperation between the eu and its partners, in accordance with the principle of 'more for more'. i welcome the commission's proposal to increase the financing of the esf by 23% in the new multiannual financial framework. however, a proper balance must be found between the two esa flanges. the arab spring has been a political focus for a year. the eu must support the development of countries, the development of civil society, help rebuild infrastructure, and promote the processes of democracy and the rule of law, so as not to close the windows of opportunity for democracy. however, the eu should play the role of promoter, not implementer, of the relevant reforms. the revolutions have given more voice to the citizens, and they need to feel that they are the owners of the reforms. we must not leave our eastern neighbours to their own devices. many of them are pursuing a european perspective and making progress in european reforms - efforts that must be recognised and valued. we must not forget that in the eastern neighbourhood many aspects are linked to the eu-russia dialogue, such as the visa-free regime, decisions must be taken only on the basis of objective criteria and real progress.

uzbekistan, like the other central asian countries, is rich in resources and an important partner for the european union. it is the fifth largest cotton producer and the third largest cotton exporter in the world. the european union is the world's largest importer of uzbek cotton. these facts give us the opportunity and the duty to positively influence the development of uzbekistan and bilateral cooperation, to promote progress in both the economic and human rights fields. however, we must avoid overly educational rhetoric that can achieve the opposite. the people of uzbekistan have a positive attitude towards the european union and i believe that the european union delegation in tashkent will be important in strengthening cooperation. the work on parliament's position on the protocol was not easy, in particular because of the human rights concerns that existed. both the report and the opinion of the foreign affairs committee severely condemn any form of forced labor. looking at the facts, i have come to two main conclusions. first, uzbekistan must ensure the free functioning of the international labour organisation in the country. at the same time, it should be noted that uzbekistan has already taken significant steps to address the problems by ratifying 13 wto conventions and most un human rights conventions, and these principles are enshrined in the constitution. forced labour of children is a criminal offence. secondly, it is essential to modernise the agricultural sector. it is therefore important to conclude a textile trade protocol with uzbekistan, which should be concluded without undue delay as soon as the international labour organisation confirms that specific reforms have been implemented and that forced labour is effectively eliminated.
i agree with the rapporteur that the agreement on trade in textile products with uzbekistan should not be based on purely economic arguments. taşkent denies that child labour is used in the country, but the refusal to allow the international labour organization and other observers to enter is another story. the european union should use all its influence to change the situation. the government is failing to manage agriculture, to prevent the destruction of nature, to prevent the waste of water. eu firms, buying up to a quarter of the country's cotton, are supporting this failed system, whether they like it or not. i would suggest, half-jokingly, half-seriously, that we require all eu companies buying uzbek cotton to label their products as 'probably produced with child labour'. could this help to accelerate change in the country?
i cannot in any way support the fact that bulgarian and romanian citizens of the european union are discriminated against in the labour market and subject to certain restrictions. some say that this poses a threat to the labour market in certain countries of the european union, but no one has proved that this is the case. on the contrary, the communication issued by the european commission last month shows that in those countries where romanian and bulgarian workers are employed, they contribute to economic prosperity, to better living conditions, they are useful, and not the other way around. in fact, the commission's spokesman said today that the commission has no power to put forward certain uniform criteria, which is a major threat to one or another country in the european union if romanian or bulgarian citizens come to work there without any restrictions. i do not see why there cannot be such a uniform criteria and who will be hindered by it. the biggest threat i see is that we in the european union have started to divide everything into several areas: there are european union countries, there are eurozone countries and non-eurozone countries, freelance people and those who cannot work freely. this is the real threat, not the free movement of workers without any restrictions.
the author. − indeed, the 'advanced energy for europe' programme has provided a very favourable environment for companies and public authorities in the member states of the community to prepare feasibility and market studies, business plans for reducing energy consumption and changing the way it is used. this is a major step forward in reducing the climate change footprint, limiting and minimising pollution, and using energy resources more efficiently and rationally. but if we were really talking about really advanced energy, we should be talking about different principles today, like a european energy without fossil fuels. it could be wind, it could be solar, it could be hydro. the search for new forms of energy should be the focus of all programmes to promote smart energy in europe. it is necessary to encourage and finance member states' investments in new and advanced technologies in the field of energy efficiency and renewable energy sources. today, the path to smart energy requires new and bold steps in principle. let us design our future in new forms of energy, such as hydrogen energy, the next generation of nuclear technology. we are the generation whose actions will determine whether we preserve the earth for future generations or condemn it to a slow but inevitable death in 100 or 200 years. let us choose such actions, let us choose only such principles, that they do not give the slightest incentive to destroy what we have not created.
the 'smart energy for europe' programme has attracted a lot of interest from european union citizens and businesses since it was launched in 2003. to date, more than 500 eu-wide projects have been implemented, making a significant contribution to the european union's capacity for innovation, the development of a knowledge society, and greater energy efficiency, including the development of renewable sources. i agree with all the concerns expressed about the future of this programme and its prospects and i believe that it must be maintained in the next financial period. it must be adequately funded to enable the participation of as many research institutes and smes as possible from all member states in the projects, thus contributing to the creation of real added value throughout the european union.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on budgetary control of eu financial assistance to afghanistan which points out that currently no direct budget support is granted to this country. i agree with the rapporteur that budget support remains the most appropriate channel to foster capacity building and, therefore, the commission should be invited to consider sectoral budget support, where appropriate, with rigorous and well-defined conditions. we, members of the european parliament, call on the commission to insist on the establishment of full financial and operational independence of the control and audit office of afghanistan. moreover, the ep also urges the commission to further strengthen coordination with member states and the donor community in general. i want to stress that the own-initiative report of 15 january 2009 on the control of eu funds in afghanistan had already asked the commission to provide a comprehensive annual report including shortcomings identified and measures taken to remedy these shortcomings. regrettably, until now the commission has not prepared such a report, therefore, we, members of the european parliament, strongly urged the commission – once more – to implement the recommendation.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as the european commission has allocated 2 billion and disbursed over eur 1.8 billion in development and humanitarian aid to afghanistan since 2002, and parliament has a monitoring role to play, and it is therefore requested that the commission transparently apply and make public the following measures: agreements with the government of the islamic republic of afghanistan; baseline values, indicators, targets, calculation methods and sources of verification to assess progress and to take decisions on disbursement of the variable-rate components of possible future budget support based on performance; clear and standardised reports assessing progress in an objective and transparent manner, based on established criteria and, if necessary, giving reasons why the planned progress could not be achieved initially.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the commission's 2010 report on competition policy. i agree that the commission must take effective action to promote the harmonisation of competition rules across the board. in energy policy, the commission should monitor more closely the competition in energy markets and improve the integration of energy from renewable sources into electricity grids. it is important that the commission strengthen its efforts to open up the credit rating agency sector to competition and to ensure the quality of credit ratings. the commission should determine whether the distortion of competition is due to differences in the application of public procurement rules in the eu member states. i also agree that an interoperable and efficient cross-border transport infrastructure network is essential to ensure a competitive and efficient internal market in the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because competition policy is an essential tool for the european union to create a dynamic, efficient and innovative internal market and to be competitive on the global stage. the european parliament welcomes the commission's prompt and reasonable response to the crisis by adopting specific state aid rules and using competition policy as a crisis management tool. large amounts of state aid during the crisis, such as in the form of guarantee schemes, recapitalisation schemes and additional liquidity support provided by banks, contributed to the large imbalances in public finances. the commission should further investigate the competitive situation in the retail sector, in particular in relation to the alleged abuse of market power by dominant retail chains, which is detrimental to small retailers and producers in the agri-food market. the european parliament also believes that competition policy should contribute to the promotion of open standards and to the application and interoperability of activities, in order to avoid that the small number of market participants prevents consumers and customers from participating in the development of technologies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for france, with a view to allocating eur 24.5 million in commitment and payment appropriations. the european globalisation adjustment fund shall provide support for and facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns linked to globalisation and as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis. in october 2009, france submitted an application and requested assistance for 4 445 redundancies (of which 3 582 were foreseen) from renault sa and its seven automotive suppliers. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the aid granted to the company in question. this led to a decline in demand for renault cars and a deterioration in the company's economic situation. the commission has assessed the application to be eligible under the egf regulation. i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the egf in accordance with the request made by france for financial assistance to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis.
in writing. − on 9 october 2009, france submitted an application to mobilise the egf, in respect of redundancies in the company 'renault s.a.s.' and seven of its suppliers. the application concerns 4 445 redundancies, of which 3 582 are redundancies, in the enterprises of renault s.a.s. and its seven suppliers during the reference four-month period from 1 april 2009 to 31 july 2009. this application complies with the requirements for financial support as laid down in article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006. i therefore supported the commission's proposal to mobilise an amount of eur 24 493 525.
in writing. − i voted against the resolution on public access to european parliament, council and commission documents as it goes far beyond the goal to create more transparency by better access to documents for the citizens. moreover, the report takes on issues that cannot be the subject of the regulation at all. i supported the position of the epp group, that the report does not only transgress the law and interinstitutional agreement in force but violates as well the safeguarding of competition proceedings, sensitive and personal data. the report defines as a ‘document’ all data and content which is somehow linked to the politics, the measures and the decisions of all institutions of the eu; this includes in a broad way also preparative, confidential and classified documents. therefore this definition includes not only documents but also pieces of information. as a consequence the citizens would have access to procedures, which goes far beyond the normal access to documents and which would open the floodgates to public influence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is our task as meps, as representatives of the citizens, to ensure that the right of citizens to have access to documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies in any form, as conferred on them by the treaty of lisbon, is properly implemented. i therefore support parliament's position and the amendments, which would, in particular, combine the proposals submitted by the commission in 2008 and this year into a single document, thus simplifying it. the european parliament also added to the commission's proposal provisions on supplementary requests for information, the implementation of the principle of good administration and transparency during the transitional period, and provisions prohibiting any discrimination, as well as provisions prohibiting the refusal to provide information to citizens on the grounds of possible technical failures or discrepancies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because, with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the commission is being asked to make it clearer to citizens that it is prepared to provide information in a more transparent way on the functioning of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. legislators should seize this opportunity and try to make this regulation a genuine and exclusive legal basis for public access to all documents of the eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, taking into account that citizens are the end-users. we have a duty to make it as easy and simple as possible to have access to european parliament, council and commission documents.
in writing. − we often complain about the lack of public interest in the activities of the european union institutions. however, one reason for this is that citizens do not know what is happening in these institutions, how decisions are taken, they cannot access the working documents of the institutions and only see the final document, sometimes without understanding when a provision was introduced during the deliberations. of course, there are some areas where it is not possible to disclose all the data. for example, in cases of infringement of competition law, i believe that the citizens' interest lies more in ensuring fair competition than in access to documents. so, while i support the document in principle, i do not agree with all the amendments that have been adopted, and i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the european maritime safety agency (emsa). the commission proposal aims to amend regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 on the european maritime safety agency in order to clearly define the current tasks and role of the eeas, in order to extend the tasks of the eeas to new areas to be developed at international and eu level. i agree that the ejsa should be more involved in eu marine research in the field of research. it is also necessary to clarify the definition of the eeas' assistance to the commission and the member states in the various international and regional organisations, to harmonise and interlink the different supervisory systems of the eeas operational services and to simplify the legal framework for the activities of the eeas in order to expand the possibility of technical cooperation between the eeas and neighbouring countries. the mandate of ejsa should cover not only the activities of ships but also those of offshore oil installations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it proposes long-term changes by establishing a european maritime safety agency (emsa). the european maritime safety agency, set up in 2002 and operational since march 2003, aims to ensure effective and uniform maritime safety and to protect and support pollution control mechanisms. the european maritime safety agency also provides scientific and technical assistance to the member states and the european commission for the application of community legislation. the agency's activities are important, since it has already carried out more than 100 investigations of all kinds in the field of safety, security and prevention of pollution from ships since its inception. the agency has also organised numerous events in its field of work and produced detailed technical reports. the european maritime safety agency is thus recognised as a well-functioning organisation, which is efficient and helps member states to save a great deal of money.
in writing. − offshore oil and gas exploration and production activities pose a threat to maritime transport and the marine environment. the european maritime safety agency plays an important role in this area by ensuring a high, uniform and effective level of maritime safety and prevention of pollution from ships. i believe that the agency should act in the interests of the european union. this includes the freedom of action of the agency outside the territory of the european union in the areas of its competence, in promoting the implementation of the european union's maritime security policy, in cooperation with third countries on technical and scientific matters. the tasks of the enlarged agency should be clearly and precisely defined in order to avoid duplication and any confusion. i believe that it is necessary to ensure a high, uniform and effective level of safety and security at sea, to use available capacities for assistance, to prevent and respond to marine pollution, including from offshore oil and gas installations, and to create a european maritime area without barriers. that is why i voted in favour of this document.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the commission's white paper 'a roadmap for a common european transport area'. developing a competitive transport system based on the efficient use of resources. the european commission's white paper adopted in march 2011 sets out a comprehensive strategy for the development of a competitive transport system and the main objectives to be achieved by 2050. i agree with parliament that the eu's high dependence on imported fossil fuels poses a serious risk to the eu's economic security and may limit the flexibility of the eu's foreign policy choices. i believe that it is necessary to ensure the successful development of the trans-european transport network (ten-t), to effectively connect the transport networks of all eu regions and to eliminate the differences in the level of infrastructure development between the eu member states. i agree that member states should commit themselves to eliminating the main known problematic sections of roads for all modes of transport by 2020 and to bringing the transport infrastructure of the new member states up to the level of other member states by 2025. the commission should increase the stability of the financing of ten-t projects. eu co-financing should be based on the 'use it or lose it' principle. we must take decisive action in clearly defining, developing and implementing the objectives of a future efficient and competitive eu transport policy. since the main objectives of the 2001 white paper have been only partially or not at all achieved, we need to analyse and learn from past mistakes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because one of the main sectors in the european union is transport, which provides some 10 million jobs and accounts for 5% of gross domestic product (gdp). the transport sector is of great importance and has a lot of potential to develop and innovate in areas such as transport, logistics and mobility. transport can also be beneficial in other areas in the european union, such as innovation, research, the environment, sustainable economy, growth and energy. the sector also has a significant potential to contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the european union's europe 2020 strategy for growth. taking into account economic, employment, environmental, social and territorial aspects, the european internal transport market should be completed by further opening up transport networks and markets. the european commission should ensure that proposals for the opening up of services in all transport markets do not lead to social dumping, do not reduce the quality of services, and do not create the conditions for the emergence of private monopolies or oligopolies. an integrated transport policy covering the entire transport and logistics value chain is needed to adequately address transport and mobility problems, especially in urban areas. the coordination of activities among policy-makers in the european institutions should be strengthened, as well as the ongoing dialogue and consultation with representatives of the logistics industry, transport service providers and customers in the european logistics and mobility forum.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as the transport sector is of vital importance for the development of the european union, its regions and cities, and also for european citizens, because it provides jobs for many europeans and creates the european internal market. transport has a significant contribution to make to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular in the areas of employment, sustainable economic growth, research, energy, innovation and the environment. i agreed with the rapporteur that member states underestimate the added value of transport policy for europe and delay its implementation, implementing directives and projects incorrectly or late. in times of economic and financial crisis, there is little incentive to invest in ten-t projects. it is necessary to effectively connect the transport networks of the new and old eu member states and to eliminate the differences in the level of infrastructure development in the eu member states in order to create a common european transport area. europe needs to develop a competitive transport system based on the efficient use of resources.
in writing. − i fully support the provisions of the communication on the common transport area, as the proper functioning of the transport sector is also essential for the proper functioning of the single market. i would also like to draw attention to two provisions relating to the acceleration of infrastructure development. first, there is still a need to improve the connectivity between eu member states, especially by rail. it is therefore necessary to pay particular attention to the projects included in the list of ten-t priority projects. secondly, the promotion of environmentally friendly transport also requires improving the infrastructure associated with it, in particular the distribution points of energy (gas stations, charging stations for electric vehicles, etc.). this also requires action in other areas, in particular urban planning.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it can bring about tangible positive changes for the european parliament in uzbekistan's path towards strengthening democracy and better protection of human rights. the european parliament has received a request from the council of ministers of the european union to give its consent to the conclusion of a protocol amending the eu-uzbekistan partnership and cooperation agreement. in this case, parliament stated that it would consider the issue of consent only after the uzbek authorities had granted the international labour organisation's observers permission to carry out a comprehensive and unhindered monitoring and after they had confirmed that concrete reforms had been implemented and had produced tangible results in order to effectively prohibit forced and child labour at national, provincial and local levels. the european parliament considered that the conclusion of such a protocol could benefit european union textile exporters, but suspended its signature, considering that the economic aspect of the agreement should not be overestimated in the face of serious violations of democratic principles and human rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because textiles are not covered by the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) and the sector is regulated by a bilateral agreement which expired in 2005, and this has created legal uncertainty for union exporters, as uzbekistan (not being a wto member) can increase import tariffs at any time, while the union grants the most favourable treatment (in terms of customs tariffs) to all countries in the world. the objective of this protocol is to include textile products in the sps, thereby granting each other the status of a most favourable treatment and ending the legal uncertainty for union exporters of textile products. in line with the principles and objectives of the union's external action, i believe that the union, as one of its main trading partners and the largest importer of cotton from uzbekistan, has a moral obligation to use its leverage to put an end to forced child labour in that country. for this reason, the protocol cannot be considered as a mere technical agreement as long as human rights issues are raised.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because free movement of workers is one of the fundamental values of the european union and one of the greatest achievements guaranteed by eu law, which allows citizens of one eu member state to work in another eu member state under the same conditions as nationals of that member state. this is perhaps the most important right granted to individuals, which is an essential component of both the internal market and european citizenship. although the european commission communication of 11 november 2011 found that workers from romania and bulgaria had and have a positive impact on the economies of all member states where workers from these countries are employed, some eu member states currently apply work restrictions to romanian and bulgarian nationals. thus, member states wishing to extend restrictions on the access of nationals of those countries to the labour market must give specific, detailed and duly substantiated reasons for such extension. those member states should clearly identify the threats and labour market disturbances in their countries, as the reports by the member states and the commission show only positive effects on the economy of the bulgarian and romanian workers and no labour market disturbances. the commission must also take measures to ensure that there are no restrictions on fundamental freedoms and that there are no obstacles to the free movement of workers throughout the european union.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the right to health is a fundamental right and all workers must have the same legal guarantees and working conditions that protect their health, safety and dignity at their workplace. it should be recognised that the characteristics and activities of the workplace are constantly changing as a result of technological developments and changing economic and social conditions, and that a rapid solution of political, administrative and technical issues is essential to ensure a high level of health and safety at work. in addition, great attention should be paid to risk prevention, which is essential to reduce the number of work-related accidents and diseases. good management of the occupational health and safety system has positive effects at national and european level, as well as on individual companies. at european and national level, it is therefore necessary to harmonise occupational health and safety policies and to integrate them fully into other types of public policy: health, employment, industry, environment, transport, education, energy, regional development, public procurement and the internal market. in addition, the gender dimension should be implemented in all policy areas in order to better take into account the specific risks faced by women workers. the adoption, design and implementation of national strategies should take into account the specific situation in each member state, focusing on those sectors and undertakings where the highest number of accidents at work occur.
in writing. − the 1989 framework directive and other directives (including reach) for specific threats or sectors set out in detail all the acquis communautaire relating to occupational health and safety. these legislative acts enable the implementation of the european treaties and the charter of fundamental rights in the field of occupational health and guarantee the fundamental right to health protection. however, the strategy indicates that this is not enough. it is necessary to adapt this legislation to new threats. the promotion and implementation of occupational health policy has positive results in four areas: economic, social, personnel and corporate image, which is why i voted in favour of this document.
in writing. − in support of this document, i would like to draw attention to one aspect: to ensure adequate health and safety at work, much more attention than is currently needed is needed to ensure adequate training of workers. often, especially where the workforce is predominantly unskilled, such as in construction, training is not provided or is provided very superficially, leading to a number of tragic accidents. therefore, company representatives responsible for the safety of workers should take active action in training workers, and occupational safety supervisory authorities should pay more attention to explaining the importance of adequate and timely training of workers.
